chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.summary: Nest (NestJS) is a framework for building efficient, scalable Node.js server-side applications.

blocks.md: Nest (NestJS) is a framework for building efficient, scalable [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) server-side applications. It uses progressive JavaScript, is built with and fully supports [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) (while still letting you write plain JavaScript), and combines elements of OOP (object-oriented programming), FP (functional programming), and FRP (functional reactive programming).
blocks.text: Nest (NestJS) is a framework for building efficient, scalable Node.js server-side applications. It uses progressive JavaScript, is built with and fully supports TypeScript (while still letting you write plain JavaScript), and combines elements of OOP (object-oriented programming), FP (functional programming), and FRP (functional reactive programming).
blocks.zh: Nest(NestJS）是构建高效、可扩展的框架 [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 服务器端应用程序。它使用渐进式 JavaScript，内置并完全支持 [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)（同时仍然让你用简单的方式写作 JavaScript），并结合了 OOP（面向对象编程），FP（函数式编程），以及 FRP（函数式反应编程）。

blocks.md: Under the hood, Nest uses robust HTTP server frameworks such as [Express](https://expressjs.com/) (the default), and can optionally be configured to use [Fastify](https://github.com/fastify/fastify) instead.
blocks.text: Under the hood, Nest uses robust HTTP server frameworks such as Express (the default), and can optionally be configured to use Fastify instead.
blocks.zh: 在底层，Nest 使用稳健 HTTP 服务器框架，例如 [Express](https://expressjs.com/)（默认值），并且可以可选地配置为使用 [Fastify](https://github.com/fastify/fastify) 反而。

blocks.md: Nest provides a level of abstraction above these common Node.js frameworks (Express and Fastify), but also exposes their APIs directly to the developer. This gives you the freedom to use the myriad third-party modules available for the underlying platform.
blocks.text: Nest provides a level of abstraction above these common Node.js frameworks (Express and Fastify), but also exposes their APIs directly to the developer. This gives you the freedom to use the myriad third-party modules available for the underlying platform.
blocks.zh: Nest 提供了高于这些常见的抽象级别 Node.js 框架（Express 和 Fastify），但也将它们的 API 直接暴露给开发人员。这使您可以自由地使用底层平台可用的无数第三方模块。

blocks.md: Philosophy
blocks.text: Philosophy
blocks.zh: 哲学

blocks.md: In recent years, thanks to Node.js, JavaScript has become the "lingua franca" of the web for both frontend and backend applications. This has given rise to projects like [Angular](https://angular.dev/), [React](https://github.com/facebook/react), and [Vue](https://github.com/vuejs/core), which improve developer productivity and enable the creation of fast, testable, and extensible frontend applications. However, while plenty of excellent libraries, helpers, and tools exist for Node.js (and server-side JavaScript), none of them effectively solves the main problem of **architecture**.
blocks.text: In recent years, thanks to Node.js, JavaScript has become the "lingua franca" of the web for both frontend and backend applications. This has given rise to projects like Angular, React, and Vue, which improve developer productivity and enable the creation of fast, testable, and extensible frontend applications. However, while plenty of excellent libraries, helpers, and tools exist for Node.js (and server-side JavaScript), none of them effectively solves the main problem of architecture.
blocks.zh: 近年来，得益于 Node.js,JavaScript 已经成为前端和后端应用程序的 web“通用语言”。这催生了诸如 [Angular](https://angular.dev/),[React](https://github.com/facebook/react)，和 [Vue](https://github.com/vuejs/core) 这提高了开发人员的工作效率，并支持创建快速、可测试和可扩展的前端应用程序。然而，尽管存在大量优秀的库、助手和工具 Node.js（和服务器端 JavaScript)，都没有有效解决**架构**的主要问题。

blocks.md: Nest provides an out-of-the-box application architecture that lets developers and teams create highly testable, scalable, loosely coupled, and maintainable applications. The architecture is heavily inspired by Angular.
blocks.text: Nest provides an out-of-the-box application architecture that lets developers and teams create highly testable, scalable, loosely coupled, and maintainable applications. The architecture is heavily inspired by Angular.
blocks.zh: Nest 提供了一个开箱即用的应用程序架构，允许开发人员和团队创建高度可测试、可伸缩、松耦合和可维护的应用程序。该建筑深受 Angular 的启发。

blocks.md: To get started, you can either scaffold the project with the [Nest CLI](/cli/overview) or [clone a starter project](#alternatives). Both produce the same outcome.

They create a new project directory and populate it with the initial core Nest files and supporting modules, giving your project a conventional base structure. We recommend the **Nest CLI** for first-time users, and the [First steps](/first-steps) chapter continues with this approach.

chapters.title: First steps
chapters.summary: This set of articles covers the core fundamentals of Nest.

blocks.md: This set of articles covers the **core fundamentals** of Nest. To introduce the essential building blocks of a Nest application, we'll build a basic CRUD application whose features cover a lot of ground at an introductory level.
blocks.text: This set of articles covers the core fundamentals of Nest. To introduce the essential building blocks of a Nest application, we'll build a basic CRUD application whose features cover a lot of ground at an introductory level.
blocks.zh: 这组文章涵盖了 Nest 的**核心基础**。为了介绍 Nest 应用程序的基本组成部分，我们将构建一个基本的 CRUD 应用程序，其特性涵盖了入门级别的许多内容。

blocks.md: Language
blocks.text: Language
blocks.zh: 语言

blocks.md: Nest is written in [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) and runs on [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/), and it supports both TypeScript and plain JavaScript. Because Nest relies on the latest language features, using it with plain JavaScript requires [Babel](https://babeljs.io/).
blocks.text: Nest is written in TypeScript and runs on Node.js, and it supports both TypeScript and plain JavaScript. Because Nest relies on the latest language features, using it with plain JavaScript requires Babel.
blocks.zh: Nest 是用 [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) 编写的，在 [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/) 上运行，它支持 TypeScript 和普通 JavaScript。因为 Nest 依赖于最新的语言特性，所以将其与普通 JavaScript 一起使用需要 [Babel](https://babeljs.io/)。

blocks.md: Most examples in this documentation use TypeScript, but you can **switch any code snippet** to plain JavaScript syntax with the language toggle in the upper-right corner of the snippet.
blocks.text: Most examples in this documentation use TypeScript, but you can switch any code snippet to plain JavaScript syntax with the language toggle in the upper-right corner of the snippet.
blocks.zh: 本文档中的大多数示例使用 TypeScript，但您可以将任何代码片段**切换为普通代码片段 JavaScript 语法与代码片段右上角的语言切换。

blocks.md: Prerequisites
blocks.text: Prerequisites
blocks.zh: 先决条件

blocks.md: Make sure that [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) is installed on your operating system. Running a Nest application requires **v20.19 or later** (or **v22.12+** on the 22.x line). The Nest CLI's generators (such as `nest new` and `nest generate`) require **v22.22.3+, v24.15+, or v26+**. We recommend the latest active LTS release, which satisfies both requirements.

The Nest CLI's generators (such as nest new and nest generate) require v22.22.3+, v24.15+, or v26+. We recommend the latest active LTS release, which satisfies both requirements.
blocks.zh: 确保 [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 安装在您的操作系统上。运行一个 Nest 应用程序需要**v20.19 或更高版本**（或 22.x 行上的**v22.12+**）。这个 NestCLI 的生成器（例如 `nest new` 和 `nest generate`) 需要**v22.22.3+、v24.15+或 v26+**。我们推荐最新的活动 LTS 释放，满足这两个要求。

blocks.md: The quickest way to set up a new project is with the [Nest CLI](/cli/overview). With [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/) installed, run the following commands in your terminal:
blocks.text: The quickest way to set up a new project is with the Nest CLI. With npm installed, run the following commands in your terminal:

blocks.md: The CLI asks which module system to use: ESM (the default), which uses Vitest as the test runner, or CommonJS, which uses Jest.
blocks.text: The CLI asks which module system to use: ESM (the default), which uses Vitest as the test runner, or CommonJS, which uses Jest.
blocks.zh: CLI 询问使用哪个模块系统：ESM（默认值），它使用 Vitest 作为测试运行器，或者 CommonJS，它使用 Jest。

blocks.md: It also asks whether to set up [NestJS Observe](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/ 'NestJS Observe'), the official observability platform for Nest. If you answer yes, the generated project includes the `@nestjs/observe` SDK, already wired into `AppModule` and `NestFactory.create()`. In an interactive terminal, the prompt defaults to yes; in non-interactive environments, such as CI, it is skipped and Observe is not added. Pass `--observe` or `--no-observe` to skip the prompt either way. See the [Observability](/observability/overview) chapter for what Observe covers.
blocks.text: It also asks whether to set up NestJS Observe, the official observability platform for Nest. If you answer yes, the generated project includes the @nestjs/observe SDK, already wired into AppModule and NestFactory.create(). In an interactive terminal, the prompt defaults to yes; in non-interactive environments, such as CI, it is skipped and Observe is not added. Pass --observe or --no-observe to skip the prompt either way. See the Observability chapter for what Observe covers.
blocks.zh: 它还询问是否设置 [NestJS Observe](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/) 官方可观测性平台 Nest.如果回答是，则生成的项目包括 `@nestjs/observe` SDK，已经连接到 `AppModule` 和 `NestFactory.create()` 在交互式终端中，提示默认为是；在非交互式环境中，例如 CI，它被跳过，并且没有添加观察。通过 `--observe` 或者 `--no-observe` 以任何方式跳过提示。参见 [Observability](/observability/overview) 观察涵盖的章节。

blocks.md: If you set up Observe, the CLI then offers to link the new project to it, once the dependencies are installed. Accepting prints a code to approve at [observe.nestjs.com/link](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/link 'Link a project to NestJS Observe') (signing up first if you don't have an account; the free plan needs no payment details), and the CLI then writes the app key and secret into `.env` and makes every `nest start` script (`start`, `start:dev`, and `start:debug`) load it. Requests, background jobs, errors, and distributed traces start reporting the next time you start the application. To link later, or when the CLI doesn't offer it (without a terminal, or with `--skip-install`), run `npx @nestjs/observe link` in the project directory - see [Linking from the terminal](/observability/sdk#linking-from-the-terminal).

Accepting prints a code to approve at observe.nestjs.com/link (signing up first if you don't have an account; the free plan needs no payment details), and the CLI then writes the app key and secret into .env and makes every nest start script (start, start:dev, and start:debug) load it. Requests, background jobs, errors, and distributed traces start reporting the next time you start the application. blocks.md: New projects are generated with TypeScript's [strict](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig#strict) mode enabled. To opt out, set `"strict": false` in the generated `tsconfig.json`.

blocks.md: The project structure generated by the Nest CLI encourages the convention of keeping each module in its own dedicated directory.

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: By default, if an error occurs while the application is being created, the process exits with code `1`. To have the error thrown instead, disable the `abortOnError` option (e.g., `NestFactory.create(AppModule, { abortOnError: false })`).
blocks.text: By default, if an error occurs while the application is being created, the process exits with code 1. To have the error thrown instead, disable the abortOnError option (e.g., NestFactory.create(AppModule, { abortOnError: false })).
blocks.zh: 默认情况下，如果在创建应用程序时发生错误，进程将退出代码 `1`。要引发错误，请禁用 `abortOnError` 选项（例如，`NestFactory.create(AppModule, { abortOnError: false })`）。

blocks.md: Platform
blocks.text: Platform
blocks.zh: 平台

blocks.md: Nest is designed to be platform-agnostic. Platform independence lets you create reusable logical parts that can be used across several different types of applications. Nest can work with any Node.js HTTP framework once an adapter is created for it. Two HTTP platforms are supported out of the box: [Express](https://expressjs.com/) and [Fastify](https://www.fastify.io). Choose the one that best suits your needs.
blocks.text: Nest is designed to be platform-agnostic. Platform independence lets you create reusable logical parts that can be used across several different types of applications. Nest can work with any Node.js HTTP framework once an adapter is created for it. Two HTTP platforms are supported out of the box: Express and Fastify. Choose the one that best suits your needs.
blocks.zh: Nest 被设计成与平台无关。平台独立性允许您创建可重用的逻辑部件，这些部件可以在几种不同类型的应用程序中使用。一旦为任何 Node.jsHTTP 框架创建了适配器，Nest 就可以与它一起工作。开箱即用支持两个 HTTP 平台：[Express](https://expressjs.com/) 和 [Fastify](https://www.fastify.io)。选择最适合你需求的。

blocks.md:
|                    |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `platform-express` | [Express](https://expressjs.com/) is a well-known, minimalist web framework for Node.js. It is a battle-tested, production-ready library with extensive community resources. Nest uses the `@nestjs/platform-express` package by default, so no setup is required. |
| `platform-fastify` | [Fastify](https://www.fastify.io/) is a high-performance, low-overhead framework focused on efficiency and speed. To learn how to use it, see [Performance (Fastify)](/http/performance).                                                                    |
Each platform exposes its own application interface: `NestExpressApplication` and `NestFastifyApplication`, respectively.
blocks.text: Each platform exposes its own application interface: NestExpressApplication and NestFastifyApplication, respectively.
blocks.zh: 每个平台都公开了自己的应用程序界面：`NestExpressApplication` 和 `NestFastifyApplication`，分别。

blocks.md: When you pass a type to the `NestFactory.create()` method, as in the example below, the `app` object exposes methods that are available only on that platform. You don't **need** to specify a type **unless** you want to access the underlying platform API.
blocks.text: When you pass a type to the NestFactory.create() method, as in the example below, the app object exposes methods that are available only on that platform. You don't need to specify a type unless you want to access the underlying platform API.
blocks.zh: 当您将类型传递给 `NestFactory.create()` 方法时，如下例所示，`app` 对象将公开仅在该平台上可用的方法。您不需要**指定类型，除非**您想要访问底层平台 API。

blocks.code: const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule);

chapters.title: Controllers
chapters.summary: Controllers are responsible for handling incoming requests and sending responses back to the client.

blocks.md: Controllers are responsible for handling incoming **requests** and sending **responses** back to the client.
blocks.text: Controllers are responsible for handling incoming requests and sending responses back to the client.
blocks.zh: 控制器负责处理传入的**请求**并将**响应**发送回客户端。

blocks.md: A controller's purpose is to handle specific requests for the application. The **routing** mechanism determines which controller handles each request. A controller often has multiple routes, and each route can perform a different action.
blocks.text: A controller's purpose is to handle specific requests for the application. The routing mechanism determines which controller handles each request. A controller often has multiple routes, and each route can perform a different action.
blocks.zh: 控制器的目的是处理应用程序的特定请求。**路由**机制确定哪个控制器处理每个请求。一个控制器通常有多条路由，每条路由可以执行不同的动作。

blocks.md: To create a basic controller, you use classes and **decorators**. Decorators associate classes with the required metadata, which Nest uses to build a routing map that connects requests to their corresponding controllers.
blocks.text: To create a basic controller, you use classes and decorators. Decorators associate classes with the required metadata, which Nest uses to build a routing map that connects requests to their corresponding controllers.
blocks.zh: 要创建基本控制器，您可以使用类和**装饰器**。装饰器将类与所需的元数据相关联，Nest 用于构建路由映射，该映射将请求连接到其相应的控制器。

blocks.md: The following example uses the `@Controller()` decorator, which is **required** to define a basic controller, with an optional route path prefix of `cats`. A path prefix in the `@Controller()` decorator groups related routes and reduces repetitive code. For example, to group the routes that manage cat entities under the `/cats` path, specify the `cats` prefix in the `@Controller()` decorator. You then don't need to repeat that portion of the path for each route in the file.

blocks.md: The `@Get()` HTTP request method decorator placed before the `findAll()` method tells Nest to create a handler for a specific endpoint. An endpoint is defined by the HTTP request method (GET in this case) and the route path. The route path of a handler combines the (optional) prefix declared for the controller **and** any path specified in the method's decorator. Since the example sets a prefix (`cats`) and no path in the method decorator, Nest maps `GET /cats` requests to this handler.
blocks.text: The @Get() HTTP request method decorator placed before the findAll() method tells Nest to create a handler for a specific endpoint. An endpoint is defined by the HTTP request method (GET in this case) and the route path. The route path of a handler combines the (optional) prefix declared for the controller and any path specified in the method's decorator. Since the example sets a prefix (cats) and no path in the method decorator, Nest maps GET /cats requests to this handler.
blocks.zh: 这个 `@Get()`HTTP 请求方法装饰器放置在 `findAll()` 方法告诉 Nest 为特定端点创建处理程序的步骤。端点由 HTTP 请求方法（GET 在这种情况下）和路由路径。处理程序的路由路径结合了为控制器声明的（可选）前缀**和**方法的装饰器中指定的任何路径。因为示例设置了前缀（`cats`) 并且方法装饰器中没有路径，Nest 地图 `GET /cats` 对此处理程序的请求。

blocks.md: If the method decorator also specified a path, such as `@Get('breed')`, the resulting route would be `GET /cats/breed`.
blocks.text: If the method decorator also specified a path, such as @Get('breed'), the resulting route would be GET /cats/breed.
blocks.zh: 如果方法装饰器还指定了路径，例如 `@Get('breed')`，则结果路由将是 `GET /cats/breed`。

blocks.md: When a `GET /cats` request arrives, Nest routes it to the user-defined `findAll()` method. The method name is arbitrary: you must declare a method to bind the route to, but Nest attaches no significance to its name.
blocks.text: When a GET /cats request arrives, Nest routes it to the user-defined findAll() method. The method name is arbitrary: you must declare a method to bind the route to, but Nest attaches no significance to its name.
blocks.zh: 当一个 `GET /cats` 请求到达，Nest 将其路由到用户定义的 `findAll()` 方法。方法名是任意的：必须声明一个方法来绑定路由，但是 Nest 不重视它的名字。

blocks.md: This method returns a 200 status code along with the associated response, which in this case is a string. To explain why, we need to introduce the two **different** options Nest provides for manipulating responses:
blocks.text: This method returns a 200 status code along with the associated response, which in this case is a string. To explain why, we need to introduce the two different options Nest provides for manipulating responses:
blocks.zh: 该方法返回 200 状态代码以及相关的响应，在本例中，响应是一个字符串。为了解释原因，我们需要介绍两个**不同**的选项 Nest 提供操作响应：

blocks.md:
Standard (recommended) With this built-in method, when a route handler returns a JavaScript object or array, it is automatically serialized to JSON. When it returns a JavaScript primitive type (e.g., string, number, boolean), Nest sends the value without attempting to serialize it. Response handling is therefore straightforward: return the value, and Nest takes care of the rest.

The response's status code is 200 by default, except for POST requests, which use 201. You can change this behavior by adding the @HttpCode(...) decorator at the handler level (see Status code).
Library-specific You can use the library-specific (e.g., Express) response object, injected with the @Res() decorator in the route handler signature (e.g., findAll(@Res() response)). This approach lets you use the native response handling methods exposed by that object. For example, with Express, you can construct responses with code like response.status(200).send().

blocks.title: Warning
blocks.md: Nest detects when a handler uses either `@Res()` or `@Next()`, which indicates that you have chosen the library-specific option. If both approaches are used at the same time, the standard approach is **automatically disabled** for that route and no longer works as expected. To combine them (for example, to inject the response object only to set cookies or headers while leaving the rest to the framework), set the `passthrough` option to `true` in the `@Res({ passthrough: true })` decorator.
blocks.text: Nest detects when a handler uses either @Res() or @Next(), which indicates that you have chosen the library-specific option. If both approaches are used at the same time, the standard approach is automatically disabled for that route and no longer works as expected. To combine them (for example, to inject the response object only to set cookies or headers while leaving the rest to the framework), set the passthrough option to true in the @Res({ passthrough: true }) decorator.
blocks.zh: Nest 检测处理程序何时使用 `@Res()` 或者 `@Next()`，这表明您选择了特定于库的选项。如果同时使用这两种方法，标准方法将被**自动禁用**该路线，并且不再按预期工作。若要组合它们（例如，注入响应对象仅用于设置 cookies 或头，而将其余的留给框架），请设置 `passthrough` 选项 `true` 在 `@Res({ passthrough: true })` 装修师。

blocks.md: Request object
blocks.text: Request object
blocks.zh: 请求对象

blocks.md: Handlers often need access to the client's **request** details. Nest provides access to the [request object](https://expressjs.com/en/api.html#req) of the underlying platform (Express by default). To access it, add the `@Req()` decorator to the handler's signature, which instructs Nest to inject it.
blocks.text: Handlers often need access to the client's request details. Nest provides access to the request object of the underlying platform (Express by default). To access it, add the @Req() decorator to the handler's signature, which instructs Nest to inject it.
blocks.zh: 处理程序通常需要访问客户端的**请求**详细信息。Nest 提供对 [请求对象](https://expressjs.com/en/api.html#req) 底层平台（Express 默认情况下）。要访问它，请添加 `@Req()` 装饰器到处理程序的签名，它指示 Nest 注射它。

blocks.md: To take advantage of `express` typings (as in the `request: Request` parameter above), install the `@types/express` package.
blocks.text: To take advantage of express typings (as in the request: Request parameter above), install the @types/express package.
blocks.zh: 利用 `express` 打字（如 `request: Request` 上面的参数），安装 `@types/express` 包装。

blocks.md: The request object represents the HTTP request and has properties for the query string, route parameters, HTTP headers, and body (see the [Express documentation](https://expressjs.com/en/api.html#req)). In most cases, you don't need to access these properties manually. Instead, use dedicated decorators such as `@Body()` or `@Query()`, which are available out of the box. The following table lists the provided decorators and the platform-specific objects they represent.
blocks.text: The request object represents the HTTP request and has properties for the query string, route parameters, HTTP headers, and body (see the Express documentation). In most cases, you don't need to access these properties manually. Instead, use dedicated decorators such as @Body() or @Query(), which are available out of the box. The following table lists the provided decorators and the platform-specific objects they represent.
blocks.zh: 请求对象表示 HTTP 请求并具有查询字符串、路由参数， HTTP 标题和正文（参见 [Express documentation](https://expressjs.com/en/api.html#req)).在大多数情况下，您不需要手动访问这些属性。相反，使用专用的装饰器，如 `@Body()` 或者 `@Query()` 开箱即用。下表列出了所提供的装饰符及其所代表的特定于平台的对象。

blocks.md:
@Request(), @Req() req
@Response(), @Res()* res
@Next() next
@Session() req.session
@Param(key?: string) req.params / req.params[key]
@Body(key?: string) req.body / req.body[key]
@Query(key?: string) req.query / req.query[key]
@Headers(name?: string) req.headers / req.headers[name]
@Cookies(name?: string) request cookies / the cookie named name (see Cookies)
@SignedCookies(name?: string) verified signed cookies / the signed cookie named name
@Ip() req.ip
@HostParam() req.hosts

<sup>\* </sup>For compatibility with typings across underlying HTTP platforms (e.g., Express and Fastify), Nest provides the `@Res()` and `@Response()` decorators. `@Res()` is an alias for `@Response()`. Both directly expose the native `response` object of the underlying platform. When using them, also install the typings for the underlying library (e.g., `@types/express`) to take full advantage of them. When you inject either `@Res()` or `@Response()` in a route handler, you put Nest into **library-specific mode** for that handler, and you become responsible for managing the response. You must then send a response by calling a method on the `response` object (e.g., `res.json(...)` or `res.send(...)`); otherwise, the request will hang.

Both directly expose the native response object of the underlying platform. When using them, also install the typings for the underlying library (e.g., @types/express) to take full advantage of them. When you inject either @Res() or @Response() in a route handler, you put Nest into library-specific mode for that handler, and you become responsible for managing the response. You must then send a response by calling a method on the response object (e.g., res.json(...) or res.send(...)); otherwise, the request will hang.
blocks.zh: <sup>\* </sup>为了与跨底层 HTTP 平台(例如，Express 和 Fastify]) 的类型兼容，Nest 提供 `@Res()` 和 `@Response()` 装饰器。`@Res()` 是 `@Response()` 的别名。两者都直接公开底层平台的本机 `response` 对象。使用它们时，还要安装底层库的类型（例如，`@types/express`），以充分利用它们。当您将 `@Res()` 或 `@Response()` 注入路由处理程序时，您将 Nest 置于该处理程序的**特定库模式**，并且您将负责管理响应。然后，您必须通过调用 `response` 对象上的方法（例如，`res.json(...)` 或 `res.send(...)`）来发送响应；否则，请求将挂起。

blocks.md: `@Body()`, `@Query()`, `@Param()`, and `@RawBody()` also accept an options object with `schema` and `pipes` properties. This lets you attach [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev/) compatible schemas, such as those created with Zod, Valibot, or ArkType, directly to route parameters.

blocks.md: Nest provides decorators for all standard HTTP methods: `@Get()`, `@Post()`, `@Put()`, `@Delete()`, `@Patch()`, `@Options()`, `@Head()`, and `@QueryMethod()`. The last one maps to the `QUERY` method; it is named `QueryMethod` to avoid a clash with the `@Query()` parameter decorator. In addition, `@All()` defines an endpoint that handles all of them.

The last one maps to the QUERY method; it is named QueryMethod to avoid a clash with the @Query() parameter decorator. In addition, @All() defines an endpoint that handles all of them.
blocks.zh: Nest 为所有标准 HTTP 方法提供装饰器：`@Get()`、`@Post()`、`@Put()`、`@Delete()`、`@Patch()`、`@Options()`、`@Head()` 和 `@QueryMethod()`。最后一个映射到 `QUERY` 方法；它被命名为 `QueryMethod`，以避免与 `@Query()` 参数装饰器发生冲突。此外，`@All()` 定义了一个处理所有这些问题的端点。

blocks.md: Route wildcards
blocks.text: Route wildcards
blocks.zh: 路线通配符

blocks.md: Nest also supports pattern-based routes. For example, an asterisk (`*`) at the end of a path acts as a wildcard that matches any combination of characters. In the following example, the `findAll()` method is executed for any route that starts with `abcd/`, regardless of the number of characters that follow.
blocks.text: Nest also supports pattern-based routes. For example, an asterisk (*) at the end of a path acts as a wildcard that matches any combination of characters. In the following example, the findAll() method is executed for any route that starts with abcd/, regardless of the number of characters that follow.
blocks.zh: Nest 还支持基于模式的路由。例如，星号（`*`) 在路径的末尾充当匹配任何字符组合的通配符。在下面的示例中，`findAll()` 方法对以 `abcd/`，不管后面有多少个字符。

blocks.md: The `'abcd/*'` route path matches `abcd/`, `abcd/123`, `abcd/abc`, and so on. In string-based paths, the hyphen (`-`) and the dot (`.`) are interpreted literally.
blocks.text: The 'abcd/*' route path matches abcd/, abcd/123, abcd/abc, and so on. In string-based paths, the hyphen (-) and the dot (.) are interpreted literally.
blocks.zh: 这个 `'abcd/*'` 路线路径匹配 `abcd/`,`abcd/123`,`abcd/abc`，等等。在基于字符串的路径中，连字符（`-`）和点（`.`）是字面解释的。

blocks.md: This approach works with both Express and Fastify. Express v5, however, made its routing stricter: in plain Express, a wildcard must be named for the route to work (e.g., `abcd/{*splat}`, where `splat` is an arbitrary name for the wildcard parameter with no special meaning). Because Nest provides a compatibility layer for Express, you can still use an unnamed asterisk (`*`) as a wildcard.
blocks.text: This approach works with both Express and Fastify. Express v5, however, made its routing stricter: in plain Express, a wildcard must be named for the route to work (e.g., abcd/{*splat}, where splat is an arbitrary name for the wildcard parameter with no special meaning). Because Nest provides a compatibility layer for Express, you can still use an unnamed asterisk (*) as a wildcard.
blocks.zh: 这种方法适用于 Express 和 Fastify。然而，Expressv5 使其路由更加严格：在普通的 Express 中，必须为要工作的路由命名通配符（例如，`abcd/{*splat}`，其中 `splat` 是通配符参数的任意名称，没有特殊含义）。因为 Nest 为 Express 提供了一个兼容层，所以您仍然可以使用一个未命名的星号（`*`）作为通配符。

blocks.md: For asterisks in the **middle of a route**, Express requires named wildcards (e.g., `ab{*splat}cd`), while Fastify does not support them at all.
blocks.text: For asterisks in the middle of a route, Express requires named wildcards (e.g., ab{*splat}cd), while Fastify does not support them at all.
blocks.zh: 对于**路线中间**中的星号，Express 需要命名通配符（例如，`ab{*splat}cd`），而 Fastify 根本不支持他们。

blocks.text: Route conflicts and resolution order

blocks.md: Nest registers routes in declaration order. On order-sensitive adapters, such as the default Express adapter, a parametric route can therefore silently shadow a more specific one:
blocks.text: Nest registers routes in declaration order. On order-sensitive adapters, such as the default Express adapter, a parametric route can therefore silently shadow a more specific one:
blocks.zh: Nest 按声明顺序注册路由。在区分顺序的适配器上，例如默认值 Express 适配器，因此参数路由可以静默地覆盖更特定的路由：

blocks.md: This is easy to miss: the application boots without a warning, and the problem only surfaces at runtime, when a request is dispatched to the wrong handler. Pipes such as `ParseIntPipe` do not help here, because routing selects the handler *before* any pipe runs.
blocks.text: This is easy to miss: the application boots without a warning, and the problem only surfaces at runtime, when a request is dispatched to the wrong handler. Pipes such as ParseIntPipe do not help here, because routing selects the handler *before* any pipe runs.
blocks.zh: 这很容易被忽略：应用程序在没有警告的情况下启动，并且问题只在运行时出现，当请求被分派给错误的处理程序时。管道，例如 `ParseIntPipe` 这里没有帮助，因为路由会在任何管道运行之前选择处理程序。

blocks.md: NestJS v12 adds two opt-in `NestApplicationOptions` properties that guard against this. Both default to the previous behavior, so existing applications are unaffected unless you set them.
blocks.text: NestJS v12 adds two opt-in NestApplicationOptions properties that guard against this. Both default to the previous behavior, so existing applications are unaffected unless you set them.

blocks.md: **`routeConflictPolicy`** enables bootstrap-time diagnostics. For each kind of conflict, it takes a severity of `'off'` (the default), `'warn'`, or `'error'`:
blocks.text: routeConflictPolicy enables bootstrap-time diagnostics. For each kind of conflict, it takes a severity of 'off' (the default), 'warn', or 'error':

blocks.md:
duplicate Two routes share an identical method, path, host, and version.
shadow Two route patterns can match the same request (e.g., /users/me and /users/:id).

With `'error'`, all offending pairs are aggregated into a single `RouteConflictException`, thrown when the application initializes (in `app.init()`, or in `app.listen()` if you don't call `init()` explicitly). This way, you see every conflict at once rather than one per restart.
blocks.text: With 'error', all offending pairs are aggregated into a single RouteConflictException, thrown when the application initializes (in app.init(), or in app.listen() if you don't call init() explicitly). This way, you see every conflict at once rather than one per restart.
blocks.zh: 和 `'error'`，所有违规对聚合为一个 `RouteConflictException`，在应用程序初始化时抛出（在 `app.init()`，或在 `app.listen()` 如果你不打电话 `init()` 明确）。这样，您可以一次看到每个冲突，而不是每次重新启动一次。

blocks.md: State sharing
blocks.text: State sharing
blocks.zh: 状态共享

blocks.md: Developers coming from other programming languages may be surprised to learn that in Nest, nearly everything is shared across incoming requests. This includes resources such as the database connection pool, singleton services with global state, and more. Node.js doesn't follow the request/response multi-threaded stateless model, in which each request is handled by a separate thread. As a result, using singleton instances in Nest is fully **safe**.
blocks.text: Developers coming from other programming languages may be surprised to learn that in Nest, nearly everything is shared across incoming requests. This includes resources such as the database connection pool, singleton services with global state, and more. Node.js doesn't follow the request/response multi-threaded stateless model, in which each request is handled by a separate thread. As a result, using singleton instances in Nest is fully safe.
blocks.zh: 来自其他编程语言的开发人员可能会惊讶地发现 Nest 几乎所有内容都由传入的请求共享。这包括数据库连接池、具有全局状态的单例服务等资源。Node.js 不遵循请求/响应多线程无状态模型，其中每个请求由单独的线程处理。因此，在 Nest 是完全**安全**的。

blocks.md: That said, some edge cases may require request-based lifetimes for controllers, such as per-request caching in GraphQL applications, request tracking, or multi-tenancy. To learn how to control this, see [Injection scopes](/fundamentals/injection-scopes).
blocks.text: That said, some edge cases may require request-based lifetimes for controllers, such as per-request caching in GraphQL applications, request tracking, or multi-tenancy. To learn how to control this, see Injection scopes.
blocks.zh: 也就是说，一些边缘情况可能需要控制器基于请求的生命周期，例如 GraphQL 应用程序中的每个请求缓存、请求跟踪或多租户。要了解如何控制这一点，请参见 [Injection scopes](/fundamentals/injection-scopes)。

blocks.md: Before we proceed (if you're using TypeScript), we need to define the **DTO** (Data Transfer Object) schema. A DTO is an object that defines the shape of data sent over the network. You could define the DTO schema using **TypeScript** interfaces or plain classes, but **classes** are the recommended choice. Classes are part of the JavaScript ES6 standard, so they are preserved as real entities in the compiled JavaScript. TypeScript interfaces, by contrast, are removed during transpilation, so Nest can't reference them at runtime. This matters because features such as **pipes** rely on access to the metatype of variables at runtime, which is only possible with classes.

blocks.md: Observing routes in production
blocks.text: Observing routes in production
blocks.zh: 生产中的观察路线

blocks.md: A controller that behaves perfectly on your machine can behave very differently under real traffic. In production, the question is never "does this route work?" but "why did `GET /cats/:id` go from 40 ms to 900 ms after Tuesday's deploy, and is it every request or one unlucky tenant?"
blocks.text: A controller that behaves perfectly on your machine can behave very differently under real traffic. In production, the question is never "does this route work?" but "why did GET /cats/:id go from 40 ms to 900 ms after Tuesday's deploy, and is it every request or one unlucky tenant?"
blocks.zh: 在机器上表现完美的控制器在实际流量下可能会有很大不同。在生产中，问题从来不是“这条路线有效吗？”但是“为什么 `GET /cats/:id` 周二部署后从 40 毫秒增加到 900 毫秒，是每个请求还是一个不幸的租户？”

blocks.md: Route handlers are the natural unit for answering that question, and [NestJS Observe](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/ 'NestJS Observe') reports on exactly that unit. Because the `@nestjs/observe` SDK hooks into Nest's own request lifecycle rather than wrapping the HTTP server, every measurement is labeled with the route pattern you declared (`GET /cats/:id`, not 10,000 distinct URLs). Each route is therefore a single line you can sort, chart, and alert on:

chapters.title: Providers
chapters.summary: Providers are a core concept in Nest.

blocks.md: Providers are a core concept in Nest. Many of the basic Nest classes, such as services, repositories, factories, and helpers, can be treated as providers. The main idea behind a provider is that it can be **injected** as a dependency, which lets objects form relationships with each other. The Nest runtime takes care of "wiring up" these objects.
blocks.text: Providers are a core concept in Nest. Many of the basic Nest classes, such as services, repositories, factories, and helpers, can be treated as providers. The main idea behind a provider is that it can be injected as a dependency, which lets objects form relationships with each other. The Nest runtime takes care of "wiring up" these objects.
blocks.zh: 提供者是 Nest 中的一个核心概念。许多基本的 Nest 类，如服务、存储库、工厂和助手，可以被视为提供程序。提供程序背后的主要思想是，它可以作为依赖项被**注入**，这让对象之间形成关系。Nest 运行时负责“连接”这些对象。

blocks.md: In the previous chapter, we built a basic `CatsController`. Controllers should handle HTTP requests and delegate more complex tasks to **providers**. In their simplest form, providers are plain JavaScript classes listed in the `providers` array of a module. For more details, see the [Modules](/modules) chapter.

blocks.md: Dependency injection
blocks.text: Dependency injection
blocks.zh: 依赖注入

blocks.md: Nest is built around the **dependency injection** design pattern. For an introduction to the concept, see the [Angular documentation](https://angular.dev/guide/di).

blocks.md: Nest resolves dependencies by their type. In the example below, Nest resolves `catsService` by supplying an instance of `CatsService`. With the default (singleton) scope, Nest creates the instance once and shares it with every class that depends on it. Nest then passes the instance to the controller's constructor:
blocks.text: Nest resolves dependencies by their type. In the example below, Nest resolves catsService by supplying an instance of CatsService. With the default (singleton) scope, Nest creates the instance once and shares it with every class that depends on it. Nest then passes the instance to the controller's constructor:
blocks.zh: Nest 按类型解析依赖项。在下面的示例中，Nest 通过提供 `CatsService` 的实例来解析 `catsService`。使用默认（singleton）作用域，Nest 创建一次实例，并与依赖它的每个类共享它。Nest 然后将实例传递给控制器的构造函数：

blocks.code: constructor(private catsService: CatsService) {}

blocks.md: This single line does two things:
blocks.text: This single line does two things:
blocks.zh: 这行有两件事：

blocks.md:
- The `private` keyword makes `catsService` a TypeScript **parameter property**: it declares a `catsService` member on the class and assigns the constructor argument to it, so you don't have to write `this.catsService = catsService` yourself.
- The `CatsService` type annotation is what Nest resolves against. At compile time, TypeScript emits the constructor's parameter types as metadata, and the container reads that metadata to determine which provider to supply.
blocks.text: The private keyword makes catsService a TypeScript parameter property: it declares a catsService member on the class and assigns the constructor argument to it, so you don't have to write this.catsService = catsService yourself. The CatsService type annotation is what Nest resolves against. At compile time, TypeScript emits the constructor's parameter types as metadata, and the container reads that metadata to determine which provider to supply.
blocks.zh:
- 这个 `private` 关键词制作 `catsService` 一个 TypeScript**参数属性**：它声明一个 `catsService` 类上的成员，并将构造函数参数分配给它，因此您不必编写 `this.catsService = catsService` 你自己。
- 这个 `CatsService` 类型注释是什么 Nest 决心反对。在编译时，TypeScript 将构造函数的参数类型作为元数据发出，容器读取该元数据以确定提供给哪个提供程序。

blocks.title: Warning
blocks.md: Because resolution relies on the emitted type, the annotation must refer to something that exists at runtime, that is, a **class**. Interfaces and type aliases are erased during compilation. If `AppConfig` is an interface, `constructor(private config: AppConfig)` leaves Nest with no token to look up, and the application fails at startup with a "Nest can't resolve dependencies" error. The same happens when you import a class with `import type`, because the import is erased as well. To inject something that isn't a class, register it under a token and inject it explicitly with `@Inject()`, as described in [Custom providers](/fundamentals/custom-providers#interfaces-and-abstract-classes).

If AppConfig is an interface, constructor(private config: AppConfig) leaves Nest with no token to look up, and the application fails at startup with a "Nest can't resolve dependencies" error. The same happens when you import a class with import type, because the import is erased as well. To inject something that isn't a class, register it under a token and inject it explicitly with @Inject(), as described in Custom providers.
blocks.zh: 因为解析依赖于发出的类型，所以注释必须引用运行时存在的东西，即**类**。接口和类型别名在编译过程中被删除。如果 `AppConfig` 是一个接口， `constructor(private config: AppConfig)` 叶子 Nest 没有要查找的令牌，并且应用程序在启动时失败，显示“Nest 无法解析依赖项”错误。导入类时也会发生同样的情况 `import type`，因为导入也被删除了。要注入不是类的东西，请在令牌下注册它，然后用 `@Inject()` 如中所述 [Custom providers](/fundamentals/custom-providers#interfaces-and-abstract-classes).

blocks.md: Scopes
blocks.text: Scopes
blocks.zh: 范围

blocks.md: By default, a provider's lifetime ("scope") matches the application lifecycle. When the application bootstraps, Nest resolves every dependency, which means every provider is instantiated. Likewise, when the application shuts down, every provider is destroyed. You can also give a provider a different scope, for example, make it **request-scoped** so that its lifetime is tied to an individual request. See the [Injection scopes](/fundamentals/injection-scopes) chapter for details.
blocks.text: By default, a provider's lifetime ("scope") matches the application lifecycle. When the application bootstraps, Nest resolves every dependency, which means every provider is instantiated. Likewise, when the application shuts down, every provider is destroyed. You can also give a provider a different scope, for example, make it request-scoped so that its lifetime is tied to an individual request. See the Injection scopes chapter for details.
blocks.zh: 默认情况下，提供程序的生命周期（“范围”）与应用程序生命周期相匹配。当应用程序引导时，Nest 解析每个依赖关系，这意味着每个提供程序都被实例化。同样，当应用程序关闭时，每个提供程序都会被销毁。您还可以给提供程序一个不同的作用域，例如，使其具有**请求作用域**，以便其生命周期与单个请求绑定。参见 [Injection scopes](/fundamentals/injection-scopes) 详情见章节。

blocks.md: Custom providers
blocks.text: Custom providers
blocks.zh: 定制提供者

blocks.md: Nest has a built-in inversion of control (IoC) container that manages the relationships between providers. The container underpins dependency injection and supports more than the class-based providers shown so far: you can also define providers with plain values, classes, and synchronous or asynchronous factories. For examples, see the [Custom providers](/fundamentals/custom-providers) chapter.
blocks.text: Nest has a built-in inversion of control (IoC) container that manages the relationships between providers. The container underpins dependency injection and supports more than the class-based providers shown so far: you can also define providers with plain values, classes, and synchronous or asynchronous factories. For examples, see the Custom providers chapter.
blocks.zh: Nest 有一个内置的控制反转（IoC）容器，用于管理提供程序之间的关系。该容器支持依赖注入，并且支持的不仅仅是目前为止显示的基于类的提供程序：您还可以使用纯值、类以及同步或异步工厂来定义提供程序。例如，请参见 [Custom providers](/fundamentals/custom-providers) 篇章。

blocks.md: Optional providers
blocks.text: Optional providers
blocks.zh: 可选提供者

blocks.md: Some dependencies are not always required. For example, a class might depend on a **configuration object** but fall back to default values when none is provided. Such a dependency is optional, and its absence should not cause an error.
blocks.text: Some dependencies are not always required. For example, a class might depend on a configuration object but fall back to default values when none is provided. Such a dependency is optional, and its absence should not cause an error.

blocks.text: To mark a dependency as optional, apply the @Optional() decorator to the constructor parameter:

The previous examples used constructor-based injection, where each dependency is identified by its class in the constructor signature. For more on custom providers and their tokens, see the [Custom providers](/fundamentals/custom-providers) chapter.
blocks.text: This example injects a custom provider, so it passes the HTTP_OPTIONS custom token to @Inject(). The class is therefore responsible for the fallback, typically by merging the injected value, if any, over a set of defaults.

The class is therefore responsible for the fallback, typically by merging the injected value, if any, over a set of defaults.

blocks.md: Property-based injection
blocks.text: Property-based injection
blocks.zh: 基于属性的注入

blocks.md: The examples so far use constructor-based injection, where providers are injected through the constructor. In some cases, **property-based injection** is more convenient. For example, if a base class depends on one or more providers, passing them up through `super()` from every subclass becomes cumbersome. Instead, you can apply the `@Inject()` decorator directly to a property:

For example, if a base class depends on one or more providers, passing them up through super() from every subclass becomes cumbersome. Instead, you can apply the @Inject() decorator directly to a property:

blocks.title: Warning
blocks.md: If your class doesn't extend another class, prefer **constructor-based** injection. The constructor states explicitly which dependencies the class requires, which makes the code easier to follow than properties annotated with `@Inject()`.
blocks.text: If your class doesn't extend another class, prefer constructor-based injection. The constructor states explicitly which dependencies the class requires, which makes the code easier to follow than properties annotated with @Inject().

chapters.title: Modules
chapters.summary: A module is a class annotated with the @Module() decorator.

blocks.md: A module is a class annotated with the `@Module()` decorator. The decorator provides metadata that **Nest** uses to organize and manage the application structure.
blocks.text: A module is a class annotated with the @Module() decorator. The decorator provides metadata that Nest uses to organize and manage the application structure.
blocks.zh: 模块是一个类，注释为 `@Module()` 装修师。装饰器提供的元数据是**Nest**用于组织和管理应用程序结构。

blocks.md: Every Nest application has at least one module, the **root module**. It is the starting point from which Nest builds the **application graph**, the internal structure Nest uses to resolve relationships and dependencies between modules and providers. A very small application may have only a root module, but most applications have multiple modules, each encapsulating a closely related set of **capabilities**. Modules are the **recommended** way to organize your components.
blocks.text: Every Nest application has at least one module, the root module. It is the starting point from which Nest builds the application graph, the internal structure Nest uses to resolve relationships and dependencies between modules and providers. A very small application may have only a root module, but most applications have multiple modules, each encapsulating a closely related set of capabilities. Modules are the recommended way to organize your components.
blocks.zh: 每一 Nest 应用程序至少有一个模块，即**根模块**。这是起点 Nest 构建**应用程序图**，即内部结构 Nest 用于解决模块和提供程序之间的关系和依赖关系。一个非常小的应用程序可能只有一个根模块，但大多数应用程序都有多个模块，每个模块都封装了一组密切相关的**能力**。模块是组织组件的**推荐**方式。

blocks.md: The `@Module()` decorator takes a single object with properties that describe the module:
blocks.text: The @Module() decorator takes a single object with properties that describe the module:
blocks.zh: 这个 `@Module()`decorator 获取一个具有描述模块的属性的单个对象：

blocks.md:
|               |                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `providers`   | the providers that will be instantiated by the Nest injector and that may be shared at least across this module                                                                                          |
| `controllers` | the set of controllers defined in this module that must be instantiated                                                                                                                                  |
| `imports`     | the list of imported modules that export the providers required in this module                                                                                                                           |
| `exports`     | the subset of `providers` that this module provides and that should be available to other modules importing it. You can use either the provider itself or its token (the `provide` value)                |

A module **encapsulates** its providers by default: you can inject only providers that are part of the current module or that are explicitly exported by an imported module. A module's exported providers form its public interface, or API.
blocks.text: A module encapsulates its providers by default: you can inject only providers that are part of the current module or that are explicitly exported by an imported module. A module's exported providers form its public interface, or API.
blocks.zh: 默认情况下，模块会**封装**其提供程序：您只能注入当前模块的一部分或由导入模块显式导出的提供程序。模块的导出提供程序形成其公共接口，或 API。

This becomes more important as the application or team grows, and it aligns with the [SOLID](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SOLID) principles.

blocks.text: Shared modules
blocks.zh: 共享模块

blocks.md: In Nest, modules are **singletons** by default, so you can share the same instance of any provider between multiple modules.
blocks.text: In Nest, modules are singletons by default, so you can share the same instance of any provider between multiple modules.
blocks.zh: 在 Nest 默认情况下，模块是**单例**，因此您可以在多个模块之间共享任何提供程序的相同实例。

blocks.md: Every module is automatically a **shared module**: once created, it can be reused by any other module. Suppose you want to share an instance of `CatsService` between several other modules. To do so, first **export** the `CatsService` provider by adding it to the module's `exports` array:

blocks.md: Registering `CatsService` directly in every module that needs it would also work, but each module would then get its own separate instance of the service. Multiple instances increase memory usage and can cause unexpected behavior, such as inconsistent state if the service holds internal state.
blocks.text: Registering CatsService directly in every module that needs it would also work, but each module would then get its own separate instance of the service. Multiple instances increase memory usage and can cause unexpected behavior, such as inconsistent state if the service holds internal state.

blocks.md: Encapsulating `CatsService` in a module such as `CatsModule` and exporting it ensures that every module importing `CatsModule` reuses the same instance. This reduces memory consumption and makes behavior more predictable, because shared state and resources are managed in one place. Sharing services efficiently across the application is one of the key benefits of modularity and dependency injection.

This reduces memory consumption and makes behavior more predictable, because shared state and resources are managed in one place. Sharing services efficiently across the application is one of the key benefits of modularity and dependency injection.

blocks.text: Global modules

blocks.md: Importing the same set of modules everywhere can become tedious. In [Angular](https://angular.dev), `providers` are registered in the global scope and, once defined, are available everywhere. Nest, by contrast, encapsulates providers inside the module scope: you can't use a module's providers elsewhere without first importing the module that encapsulates them.

Nest, by contrast, encapsulates providers inside the module scope: you can't use a module's providers elsewhere without first importing the module that encapsulates them.

In the example above, the `CatsService` provider is available everywhere, and modules that inject it don't need to add `CatsModule` to their `imports` array.

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: Making everything global is not a recommended design practice. Global modules reduce boilerplate, but the `imports` array makes a module's API available to other modules in a controlled, explicit way. This keeps the application structure maintainable, shares only the parts of a module that others need, and avoids unnecessary coupling between unrelated parts of the application.

chapters.title: Middleware
chapters.summary: Middleware is a function that is called before the route handler.

blocks.md: Middleware is a function that is called **before** the route handler. Middleware functions have access to the [request](https://expressjs.com/en/4x/api.html#req) and [response](https://expressjs.com/en/4x/api.html#res) objects, and to the `next()` middleware function in the application's request-response cycle. The **next** middleware function is commonly denoted by a variable named `next`.
blocks.text: Middleware is a function that is called before the route handler. Middleware functions have access to the request and response objects, and to the next() middleware function in the application's request-response cycle. The next middleware function is commonly denoted by a variable named next.
blocks.zh: 中间件是一个在路由处理程序之前调用的函数。中间件函数可以访问 [请求](https://expressjs.com/en/4x/api.html#req) 和 [回应](https://expressjs.com/en/4x/api.html#res) 对象，以及应用程序的请求-响应周期中的 `next()` 中间件函数。**next**中间件函数通常由名为 `next` 的变量表示。

blocks.md: By default, Nest middleware is equivalent to [Express](https://expressjs.com/en/guide/using-middleware.html) middleware. The official Express documentation describes the capabilities of middleware as follows:
blocks.text: By default, Nest middleware is equivalent to Express middleware. The official Express documentation describes the capabilities of middleware as follows:
blocks.zh: 默认情况下，Nest 中间件相当于 [Express](https://expressjs.com/en/guide/using-middleware.html) 中间件。官方 Express 文档描述了中间件的功能如下：

blocks.md:
Middleware functions can perform the following tasks:
  • execute any code.
  • make changes to the request and the response objects.
  • end the request-response cycle.
  • call the next middleware function in the stack.
  • if the current middleware function does not end the request-response cycle, it must call next() to pass control to the next middleware function. Otherwise, the request will be left hanging.

You implement custom Nest middleware either as a function or as a class with the `@Injectable()` decorator. A class should implement the `NestMiddleware` interface, while a function has no special requirements. Let's start by implementing a simple middleware class.
blocks.text: You implement custom Nest middleware either as a function or as a class with the @Injectable() decorator. A class should implement the NestMiddleware interface, while a function has no special requirements. Let's start by implementing a simple middleware class.

blocks.md: Dependency injection
blocks.text: Dependency injection

blocks.md: Nest middleware fully supports dependency injection. Like providers and controllers, middleware classes can **inject dependencies** that are available within the same module. As usual, dependencies are injected through the `constructor`.

blocks.md:
- **The stack trace comes with source code.** The frame is resolved through your source maps back to `src/orders/orders.service.ts:35`, and the surrounding lines are shown inline, so you can read the failing code in the error card without cloning anything.
- **Occurrences are grouped into defects.** Errors with the same class and stack shape collapse into one fingerprinted group with a count, first-seen and last-seen timestamps, and the release that introduced it. "New since v2.4.1" is a fact you read off the page rather than infer.
- **The failure keeps its context.** The trace it belonged to, the user who hit it, the logs written during that request, and the spans that ran before the throw are all attached, so you can see what the request was doing when it failed.

blocks.md: The built-in exception filter handles many cases automatically, but you may want **full control** over the exceptions layer, e.g., to add logging or to use a different JSON schema based on dynamic factors. **Exception filters** are designed for exactly this purpose. They let you control the exact flow of execution and the content of the response sent back to the client.

To do this, we need access to the underlying platform `Request` and `Response` objects. We'll use the `Request` object to extract the original `url` and include it in the response, and the `Response` object to take direct control of the response that is sent, using the `response.json()` method.

chapters.title: Pipes
chapters.summary: A pipe is a class annotated with the @Injectable() decorator that implements the PipeTransform interface.

blocks.md: A pipe is a class annotated with the `@Injectable()` decorator that implements the `PipeTransform` interface.
blocks.text: A pipe is a class annotated with the @Injectable() decorator that implements the PipeTransform interface.
blocks.zh: 管道是一个类，注释为 `@Injectable()` 实现 `PipeTransform` 接口。

blocks.md: Pipes have two typical use cases:
blocks.text: Pipes have two typical use cases:
blocks.zh: 管道有两种典型用例：

blocks.md:
- **transformation**: transform input data to the desired form (e.g., from string to integer)
- **validation**: evaluate input data and, if valid, pass it through unchanged; otherwise, throw an exception
blocks.text: transformation: transform input data to the desired form (e.g., from string to integer) validation: evaluate input data and, if valid, pass it through unchanged; otherwise, throw an exception
blocks.zh:
- **转换**：将输入数据转换为所需形式（例如，从字符串到整数）
- **验证**：评估输入数据，如果有效，则将其不变地通过；否则，抛出异常

blocks.md: In both cases, pipes operate on the arguments being processed by a controller route handler. Nest interposes a pipe immediately before a method is invoked; the pipe receives the arguments destined for the method and operates on them. Any transformation or validation takes place at that point, after which the route handler is invoked with the (potentially) transformed arguments.
blocks.text: In both cases, pipes operate on the arguments being processed by a controller route handler . Nest interposes a pipe immediately before a method is invoked; the pipe receives the arguments destined for the method and operates on them. Any transformation or validation takes place at that point, after which the route handler is invoked with the (potentially) transformed arguments.
blocks.zh: 在这两种情况下，管道都对由控制器路由处理程序处理的参数进行操作。Nest 在调用方法之前立即插入管道；管道接收指定用于方法的参数，并对其进行操作。任何转换或验证都发生在该点，之后用（潜在的）转换的参数调用路由处理程序。

blocks.md: Nest comes with a number of built-in pipes that you can use out of the box, and you can also build your own. This chapter introduces the built-in pipes and shows how to bind them to route handlers. It then walks through several custom pipes to show how to build one from scratch.
blocks.text: Nest comes with a number of built-in pipes that you can use out of the box, and you can also build your own. This chapter introduces the built-in pipes and shows how to bind them to route handlers. It then walks through several custom pipes to show how to build one from scratch.
blocks.zh: Nest 带有许多内置管道，您可以开箱即用，也可以自己制作。本章介绍了内置管道，并展示了如何将它们绑定到路由处理程序。然后，它通过几个自定义管道来展示如何从头开始构建一个。

blocks.md: Pipes run inside the exceptions zone. An exception thrown by a pipe is handled by the exceptions layer (the global exception filter and any [exception filters](/exception-filters) applied to the current context). When a pipe throws an exception, the route handler is not executed. This makes pipes the recommended place to validate data that enters the application from external sources, at the system boundary.

blocks.md: Next, we use the class-transformer function `plainToInstance()` to transform the plain JavaScript argument object into a typed object so that we can apply validation. This is necessary because the incoming POST body, when deserialized from the network request, does **not have any type information** (this is how the underlying platform, such as Express, works). blocks.md: Transformation use case
blocks.text: Transformation use case

blocks.md: Validation isn't the only use case for custom pipes. As mentioned at the beginning of this chapter, a pipe can also **transform** input data to the desired format. This is possible because the value returned from the `transform()` method replaces the previous value of the argument.
blocks.text: Validation isn't the only use case for custom pipes. As mentioned at the beginning of this chapter, a pipe can also transform input data to the desired format. This is possible because the value returned from the transform() method replaces the previous value of the argument.
blocks.zh: 验证并不是自定义管道的唯一用例。正如本章开头提到的，管道还可以将输入数据**转换**为所需的格式。这是可能的，因为从 `transform()` 方法替换参数的先前值。

blocks.md: When is this useful? Sometimes the data passed from the client needs to be changed (for example, converted from a string to an integer) before the route handler can process it. Some required fields may also be missing, and you may want to apply default values. **Transformation pipes** perform these functions by interposing a processing function between the client request and the route handler.
blocks.text: When is this useful? Sometimes the data passed from the client needs to be changed (for example, converted from a string to an integer) before the route handler can process it. Some required fields may also be missing, and you may want to apply default values. Transformation pipes perform these functions by interposing a processing function between the client request and the route handler.
blocks.zh: 这什么时候有用？有时，从客户端传递的数据需要更改（例如，从字符串转换为整数），路由处理程序才能处理它。某些必填字段也可能缺失，您可能希望应用默认值。**转换管道**通过在客户端请求和路由处理函数之间插入处理函数来执行这些功能。

chapters.title: Guards
chapters.summary: A guard is a class annotated with the @Injectable() decorator that implements the CanActivate interface.

blocks.md: A guard is a class annotated with the `@Injectable()` decorator that implements the `CanActivate` interface.
blocks.text: A guard is a class annotated with the @Injectable() decorator that implements the CanActivate interface.
blocks.zh: 守卫是一个类，注释为 `@Injectable()` 实现 `CanActivate` 接口。

blocks.md: Guards have a **single responsibility**: they determine whether a given request will be handled by the route handler, based on conditions present at runtime (such as permissions, roles, or ACLs). This is often referred to as **authorization**. In traditional Express applications, authorization (and its close relative, **authentication**, with which it usually collaborates) has typically been handled by [middleware](/middleware). Middleware is a good fit for authentication, because tasks such as validating a token and attaching properties to the `request` object are not tied to a particular route context (and its metadata).
blocks.text: Guards have a single responsibility: they determine whether a given request will be handled by the route handler, based on conditions present at runtime (such as permissions, roles, or ACLs). This is often referred to as authorization. In traditional Express applications, authorization (and its close relative, authentication, with which it usually collaborates) has typically been handled by middleware. Middleware is a good fit for authentication, because tasks such as validating a token and attaching properties to the request object are not tied to a particular route context (and its metadata).
blocks.zh: 守卫有一个**单一的职责**：他们根据运行时存在的条件（如权限、角色或 ACL）来确定给定的请求是否将由路由处理程序处理。这通常被称为**授权**。在传统 Express 应用程序、授权（以及它通常与之协作的近亲**身份验证**）通常由 [中间件](/middleware).中间件非常适合进行身份验证，因为诸如验证令牌和将属性附加到 `request` 对象不绑定到特定的路由上下文（及其元数据）。

blocks.md: Middleware, however, is context-blind by nature: it doesn't know which handler will be executed after it calls `next()`. **Guards**, on the other hand, have access to the `ExecutionContext` instance, so they know exactly what will be executed next. Like exception filters, pipes, and interceptors, guards let you interpose processing logic at exactly the right point in the request/response cycle, and do so declaratively. This helps keep your code DRY.

Guards, on the other hand, have access to the ExecutionContext instance, so they know exactly what will be executed next. Like exception filters, pipes, and interceptors, guards let you interpose processing logic at exactly the right point in the request/response cycle, and do so declaratively. This helps keep your code DRY.
blocks.zh: 然而，中间件本质上是上下文盲的：它不知道在调用 `next()` 后将执行哪个处理程序。另一方面，**守卫**可以访问 `ExecutionContext` 实例，因此他们确切地知道接下来要执行什么。像异常过滤器、管道和拦截器一样，防护允许您在请求/响应周期的正确位置插入处理逻辑，并且可以声明地这样做。这有助于保留您的代码 DRY。

blocks.md: Authorization guard
blocks.text: Authorization guard
blocks.zh: 授权卫士

blocks.md: As mentioned, **authorization** is a common use case for guards, because specific routes should be available only when the caller (usually a specific authenticated user) has sufficient permissions. The `AuthGuard` we'll build now assumes an authenticated user, and therefore a token attached to the request headers. It extracts and validates the token, and uses the extracted information to determine whether the request can proceed.

It extracts and validates the token, and uses the extracted information to determine whether the request can proceed.
blocks.zh: 如前所述，**授权**是守卫的常见用例，因为只有当调用者（通常是特定的经过身份验证的用户）具有足够的权限时，特定的路由才应该可用。这个 `AuthGuard` 我们现在将构建假设一个经过身份验证的用户，因此将一个令牌附加到请求头。它提取并验证令牌，并使用提取的信息来确定请求是否可以继续。

blocks.md: Each interceptor implements the `intercept()` method, which takes two arguments. The first is the `ExecutionContext` instance (exactly the same object as for [guards](/guards)). `ExecutionContext` extends `ArgumentsHost`, which we covered in the exception filters chapter. There, we saw that it's a wrapper around the arguments passed to the original handler, and that it contains different argument arrays depending on the type of application. See the [exception filters](/exception-filters#arguments-host) chapter for more on this topic.
blocks.text: Each interceptor implements the intercept() method, which takes two arguments. The first is the ExecutionContext instance (exactly the same object as for guards). ExecutionContext extends ArgumentsHost, which we covered in the exception filters chapter. There, we saw that it's a wrapper around the arguments passed to the original handler, and that it contains different argument arrays depending on the type of application. See the exception filters chapter for more on this topic.
blocks.zh: 每个拦截器实现 `intercept()` 方法，该方法接受两个参数。第一个是 `ExecutionContext` 实例（与 [警卫](/guards) 完全相同的对象）。`ExecutionContext` 扩展了 `ArgumentsHost`，我们在异常过滤器一章中介绍了这一点。在那里，我们看到它是传递给原始处理程序的参数的包装器，并且根据应用程序的类型，它包含不同的参数数组。有关此主题的更多信息，请参见 [异常筛选器](/exception-filters#arguments-host) 章节。

blocks.md: By extending `ArgumentsHost`, `ExecutionContext` adds several helper methods that provide additional details about the current execution process. See the [execution context](/fundamentals/execution-context) chapter to learn more about `ExecutionContext`.

blocks.md: The second argument is a `CallHandler`. The `CallHandler` interface exposes a `handle()` method, which you use to invoke the route handler method at some point in your interceptor. If you don't call `handle()` in your implementation of the `intercept()` method, the route handler method won't be executed at all.
blocks.text: The second argument is a CallHandler. The CallHandler interface exposes a handle() method, which you use to invoke the route handler method at some point in your interceptor. If you don't call handle() in your implementation of the intercept() method, the route handler method won't be executed at all.
blocks.zh: 第二个参数是 `CallHandler`。`CallHandler` 接口公开了一个 `handle()` 方法，您可以使用该方法在拦截器中的某个点调用路由处理程序方法。如果在实现 `intercept()` 方法时不调用 `handle()`，路由处理程序方法根本不会被执行。

blocks.md: This means that the `intercept()` method effectively **wraps** the request/response stream. As a result, you can implement custom logic **both before and after** the execution of the final route handler. Running code **before** the handler is straightforward: place it before the `handle()` call. To act on what happens afterward, use the `Observable` that `handle()` returns: you can apply [RxJS](https://github.com/ReactiveX/rxjs) operators to it to further manipulate the response. In Aspect Oriented Programming terminology, the invocation of the route handler (i.e., calling `handle()`) is called a [Pointcut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pointcut), indicating that it's the point at which our additional logic is inserted.
blocks.text: This means that the intercept() method effectively wraps the request/response stream. As a result, you can implement custom logic both before and after the execution of the final route handler. Running code before the handler is straightforward: place it before the handle() call. To act on what happens afterward, use the Observable that handle() returns: you can apply RxJS operators to it to further manipulate the response. In Aspect Oriented Programming terminology, the invocation of the route handler (i.e., calling handle()) is called a Pointcut, indicating that it's the point at which our additional logic is inserted.
blocks.zh: 这意味着 `intercept()` 方法有效地**包装**请求/响应流。因此，您可以在执行最终路由处理程序之前和之后实现自定义逻辑。运行代码**之前**处理程序很简单：将其放在 `handle()` 呼吁。要对之后发生的事情采取行动，请使用 `Observable` 那个 `handle()` 退货：您可以申请 [RxJS](https://github.com/ReactiveX/rxjs) 操作员对其进行进一步操纵响应。在面向方面的编程术语中，路由处理程序的调用（即，调用 `handle()`）称为 a[Pointcut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pointcut)，表示这是插入我们的附加逻辑的点。

blocks.md: Consider, for example, an incoming `POST /cats` request. This request is destined for the `create()` handler defined inside `CatsController`. If an interceptor that doesn't call `handle()` is invoked anywhere along the way, the `create()` method won't be executed. Once `handle()` is called and the `Observable` it returns is subscribed to (Nest subscribes to the stream your `intercept()` method returns), the `create()` handler is triggered. As the handler's result flows through the stream, you can apply additional operations to it before the final result is returned to the caller.

As the handler's result flows through the stream, you can apply additional operations to it before the final result is returned to the caller.
blocks.zh: 例如，考虑一个传入 `POST /cats` 请求。此请求发送给 `create()` 内部定义的处理程序 `CatsController`.如果拦截器不打电话 `handle()` 在路径的任何地方调用， `create()` 方法不会被执行。一次 `handle()` 被称为 `Observable` 它返回订阅到（Nest 订阅您的流 `intercept()` 方法返回）， `create()` 处理程序被触发。当处理程序的结果流经流时，您可以在最终结果返回给调用者之前对其应用其他操作。

blocks.md: Sometimes you may want to skip calling the handler entirely and return a different value instead. A typical example is a cache that improves response time. A realistic implementation would also need to consider factors such as TTL, cache invalidation, and cache size, which are beyond the scope of this discussion. The following basic example demonstrates the main concept.

blocks.md: Our `CacheInterceptor` has a hardcoded `isCached` variable and a hardcoded response `[]`. The key point is that it returns a new stream, created by RxJS's `of()` function, so the route handler **won't be called** at all. When someone calls an endpoint that uses `CacheInterceptor`, the response (a hardcoded, empty array) is returned immediately. To build a generic solution, use `Reflector` together with a custom decorator, as described in the [guards](/guards) chapter.

chapters.title: Custom providers
chapters.summary: Earlier chapters touched on various aspects of dependency injection (DI) and how Nest uses it.

blocks.md: Earlier chapters touched on various aspects of **dependency injection (DI)** and how Nest uses it. One example is [constructor-based](/providers#dependency-injection) dependency injection, which injects instances (often service providers) into classes. Dependency injection is built into the Nest core at a fundamental level. So far, we've explored only one main pattern. As your application grows more complex, you may need the full feature set of the DI system, so this chapter explores it in more detail.

One example is constructor-based dependency injection, which injects instances (often service providers) into classes. Dependency injection is built into the Nest core at a fundamental level. blocks.text: DI fundamentals

blocks.md: Dependency injection is an [inversion of control (IoC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inversion_of_control) technique in which you delegate the instantiation of dependencies to the IoC container (in our case, the NestJS runtime system) instead of instantiating them imperatively in your own code. Let's examine what happens in this example from the [Providers](/providers) chapter.

When it finds the `CatsService` dependency, it looks up the `CatsService` token, which returns the `CatsService` class, per the registration step (#3 above). Assuming `SINGLETON` scope (the default), Nest then either creates an instance of `CatsService`, caches it, and returns it, or, if an instance is already cached, returns the existing one.

blocks.md: \*This explanation is simplified to illustrate the point. In reality, analyzing the code for dependencies is a sophisticated process that happens during application bootstrapping. blocks.text: Custom providers

blocks.md: Sometimes your requirements go beyond what _standard providers_ offer. For example:
blocks.text: Sometimes your requirements go beyond what _standard providers_ offer. For example:

blocks.md:
- You want to create a custom instance instead of having Nest instantiate (or return a cached instance of) a class.
- You want to reuse an existing class in a second dependency.
- You want to override a class with a mock version for testing.

blocks.md: Use string or `Symbol` tokens when the runtime DI token should be decoupled from a class. `Symbol` tokens are especially useful for libraries and larger applications: each symbol has a unique runtime identity, which avoids the accidental collisions that can occur when unrelated providers use the same string token. chapters.summary: Sometimes the application start should be delayed until one or more asynchronous tasks complete.

blocks.md: Sometimes the application start should be delayed until one or more **asynchronous tasks** complete. For example, you may not want to start accepting requests until the connection to the database has been established. Asynchronous providers let you do this.
blocks.text: Sometimes the application start should be delayed until one or more asynchronous tasks complete. For example, you may not want to start accepting requests until the connection to the database has been established. Asynchronous providers let you do this.

blocks.md: Introduction
blocks.text: Introduction
blocks.zh: 介绍

blocks.md: Most code examples in the **Overview** section of the documentation use regular, or static, modules. Modules define groups of components, such as [providers](/providers) and [controllers](/controllers), that fit together as a modular part of an application. They provide an execution context, or scope, for these components. For example, providers defined in a module are visible to other members of the module without being exported. When a provider needs to be visible outside of a module, it is first exported from its host module, and then imported into its consuming module.
blocks.text: Most code examples in the Overview section of the documentation use regular, or static, modules. Modules define groups of components, such as providers and controllers, that fit together as a modular part of an application. They provide an execution context, or scope, for these components. For example, providers defined in a module are visible to other members of the module without being exported. When a provider needs to be visible outside of a module, it is first exported from its host module, and then imported into its consuming module.
blocks.zh: 文档**概述**部分中的大多数代码示例使用常规或静态模块。模块定义组件组，例如 [供应商](/providers) 和 [控制器](/controllers)，作为应用程序模块化部分装配在一起。它们为这些组件提供了执行上下文或范围。例如，模块中定义的提供程序对模块的其他成员是可见的，而不会被导出。当提供程序需要在模块外部可见时，首先将其从其主机模块导出，然后导入到其消费模块中。

blocks.md: Dynamic module use case
blocks.text: Dynamic module use case

blocks.md: With static module binding, the consuming module has no way to **influence** how the providers of the host module are configured. This matters for general-purpose modules that need to behave differently for each consumer, much like a "plugin" that requires some configuration before it can be used.
blocks.text: With static module binding, the consuming module has no way to influence how the providers of the host module are configured. This matters for general-purpose modules that need to behave differently for each consumer, much like a "plugin" that requires some configuration before it can be used.
blocks.zh: 使用静态模块绑定，消费模块无法**影响**如何配置主机模块的提供程序。这对于需要为每个消费者提供不同行为的通用模块很重要，就像一个“插件”需要一些配置才能使用。

blocks.md: As an example, consider a module that generates the public identifiers of your entities. Identifiers that start with a type prefix, such as `usr_` for users and `ord_` for orders, tell you at a glance what kind of entity they refer to. The generation logic is the same for every entity, and only the prefix differs. With static binding, an `IdGeneratorModule` could provide only one generator, configured one way for every module that imports it. What we need instead is for `UsersModule` and `OrdersModule` to each import the module with their own prefix.

With static binding, an IdGeneratorModule could provide only one generator, configured one way for every module that imports it. What we need instead is for UsersModule and OrdersModule to each import the module with their own prefix.
blocks.zh: 例如，考虑一个生成实体公共标识符的模块。以类型前缀开头的标识符，例如 `usr_` 对于用户和 `ord_` 对于订单，一目了然地告诉你他们指的是什么样的实体。每个实体的生成逻辑都是相同的，只有前缀不同。有了静态绑定，`IdGeneratorModule` 只能提供一个生成器，为每个导入它的模块配置一种方式。我们需要的是 `UsersModule` 和 `OrdersModule` 要导入带有自己前缀的模块。

blocks.md: This is where **dynamic modules** come into play. A dynamic module provides an API for importing one module into another and customizing the properties and behavior of that module at the time it is imported.
