blocks.text: Colors are also off by default when the NO_COLOR environment variable is set to any non-empty value.
blocks.zh: 默认情况下，颜色也会关闭 `NO_COLOR` 环境变量被设置为任何非空值。

blocks.md: To configure a prefix for each log message, pass a `ConsoleLogger` instance with the `prefix` property set:
blocks.text: To configure a prefix for each log message, pass a ConsoleLogger instance with the prefix property set:
blocks.zh: 要为每个日志消息配置前缀，请传递 `ConsoleLogger` 实例 `prefix` 属性集：

blocks.md: The following table lists all available options:
blocks.text: The following table lists all available options:
blocks.zh: 下表列出了所有可用选项：

blocks.md:
| Option            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Default                                        |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `logLevels`       | Enabled log levels.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `['log', 'fatal', 'error', 'warn', 'debug', 'verbose']` |
| `timestamp`       | If enabled, will print timestamp (time difference) between current and previous log message. Note: This option is not used when `json` is enabled.                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `false`                                        |
| `prefix`          | A prefix to be used for each log message. Note: This option is not used when `json` is enabled.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `Nest`                                         |
| `json`            | If enabled, will print the log message in JSON format.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `false`                                        |
| `colors`          | If enabled, will print the log message in color.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `true` (`false` if `json` is enabled or `NO_COLOR` is set) |
| `context`         | The context of the logger.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `undefined`                                    |
| `forceConsole`    | If enabled, will use `console.log`/`console.error` instead of `process.stdout.write`/`process.stderr.write`. Useful in test environments, such as Jest, that buffer console calls.                                                                                                                                                                     | `false`                                        |
| `compact`         | If enabled, will print the log message in a single line, even if it is an object with multiple properties. If set to a number, the most n inner elements are united on a single line as long as all properties fit into breakLength. Short array elements are also grouped together.                                                                 | `false` (`true` if `json` is enabled)          |
| `maxArrayLength`  | Specifies the maximum number of Array, TypedArray, Map, Set, WeakMap, and WeakSet elements to include when formatting. Set to null or Infinity to show all elements. Set to 0 or negative to show no elements. Ignored when `json` is enabled, colors are disabled, and `compact` is set to true as it produces a parseable JSON output.             | `100`                                          |
| `maxStringLength` | Specifies the maximum number of characters to include when formatting. Set to null or Infinity to show all elements. Set to 0 or negative to show no characters. Ignored when `json` is enabled, colors are disabled, and `compact` is set to true as it produces a parseable JSON output.                                                           | `10000`                                        |
| `sorted`          | If enabled, will sort keys while formatting objects. Can also be a custom sorting function. Ignored when `json` is enabled, colors are disabled, and `compact` is set to true as it produces a parseable JSON output.                                                                                                                                | `false`                                        |
| `depth`           | Specifies the number of times to recurse while formatting object. This is useful for inspecting large objects. To recurse up to the maximum call stack size pass Infinity or null. Ignored when `json` is enabled, colors are disabled, and `compact` is set to true as it produces a parseable JSON output.                                         | `5`                                            |
| `showHidden`      | If true, object's non-enumerable symbols and properties are included in the formatted result. WeakMap and WeakSet entries are also included as well as user defined prototype properties                                                                                                                                                             | `false`                                        |
| `breakLength`     | The length at which input values are split across multiple lines. Set to Infinity to format the input as a single line (in combination with "compact" set to true). Ignored when `json` is enabled, colors are disabled, and `compact` is set to true as it produces a parseable JSON output.                                                       | `Infinity` when `compact` is enabled, or when colors are off and `compact` isn't explicitly `false`; `80` otherwise |
blocks.zh:
| 选择 | 描述 | 默认的 |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `logLevels` | 启用日志级别。 | `['log', 'fatal', 'error', 'warn', 'debug', 'verbose']` |
| `timestamp` | 如果启用，将打印当前和以前的日志消息之间的时间戳（时间差）。注意：在以下情况下不使用此选项 `json` 已启用。 | `false` |
| `prefix` | 用于每个日志消息的前缀。注意：在以下情况下不使用此选项 `json` 已启用。 | `Nest` |
| `json` | 如果启用，将在 JSON 格式。 | `false` |
| `colors` | 如果启用，将以彩色打印日志消息。 | `true`(`false` 如果 `json` 已启用或 `NO_COLOR` 已设置） |
| `context` | 记录器的上下文。 | `undefined` |
| `forceConsole` | 如果启用，将使用 `console.log`/`console.error` 而不是 `process.stdout.write`/`process.stderr.write`。在缓冲区控制台调用的测试环境（如 Jest）中非常有用。 | `false` |
| `compact` | 如果启用，将在单行中打印日志消息，即使它是具有多个属性的对象。如果设置为数字，只要所有属性都适合 breakLength，最多 n 个内部元素就会合并在一条线上。短数组元素也被分组在一起。 | `false`(`true` 如果 `json` 已启用） |
| `maxArrayLength` | 指定格式化时要包含的 Array、TypedArray、Map、Set、WeakMap 和 WeakSet 元素的最大数量。设置为 null 或 Infinity 以显示所有元素。设置为 0 或负值以显示无元素。忽略时 `json` 启用，禁用颜色，并且 `compact` 设置为 true，因为它生成一个可解析的 JSON 产量。 | `100` |
| `maxStringLength` | 指定格式化时要包含的最大字符数。设置为 null 或 Infinity 以显示所有元素。设置为 0 或负值以不显示字符。忽略时 `json` 启用，禁用颜色，并且 `compact` 设置为 true，因为它生成一个可解析的 JSON 产量。 | `10000` |
| `sorted` | 如果启用，将在格式化对象时对键进行排序。也可以是自定义排序功能。忽略时 `json` 启用，禁用颜色，并且 `compact` 设置为 true，因为它生成一个可解析的 JSON 产量。 | `false` |
| `depth` | 指定格式化对象时要递归的次数。这对于检查大型物体很有用。要递归到最大调用堆栈大小，请传递无穷大或空。忽略时 `json` 启用，禁用颜色，并且 `compact` 设置为 true，因为它生成一个可解析的 JSON 产量。 | `5` |
| `showHidden` | 如果为真，对象的不可枚举符号和属性将包含在格式化结果中。还包括 WeakMap 和 WeakSet 条目以及用户定义的原型属性 | `false` |
| `breakLength` | 输入值在多行上分割的长度。设置为无穷大以将输入格式化为单行（结合设置为 true 的“紧凑”）。忽略时 `json` 启用，禁用颜色，并且 `compact` 设置为 true，因为它生成一个可解析的 JSON 产量。 | `Infinity` 当 `compact` 被启用时，或者当颜色关闭并且 `compact` 没有显式 `false` 时；`80` 否则 |

blocks.text: JSON logging is essential for application observability and for integration with log management systems. To enable it, create a ConsoleLogger instance with its json property set to true, and pass it as the value of the logger property when creating the application instance:

blocks.md: This configuration outputs logs in a structured JSON format, which makes it easier to integrate with external systems such as log aggregators and cloud platforms. For example, platforms like **AWS ECS** (Elastic Container Service) natively support JSON logs, enabling features like:
blocks.text: This configuration outputs logs in a structured JSON format, which makes it easier to integrate with external systems such as log aggregators and cloud platforms. For example, platforms like AWS ECS (Elastic Container Service) natively support JSON logs, enabling features like:

- **Log filtering**: narrow down logs based on fields like log level, timestamp, or custom metadata.

blocks.md: If you're using [NestJS Mau](https://mau.nestjs.com), JSON logging also lets you view logs in a well-organized, structured format, which is especially useful for debugging and performance monitoring.
blocks.text: If you're using NestJS Mau, JSON logging also lets you view logs in a well-organized, structured format, which is especially useful for debugging and performance monitoring.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.md: When `json` is set to `true`, the `ConsoleLogger` defaults `colors` to `false` and `compact` to `true`. With those two values, each entry is serialized with `JSON.stringify()`, so the output is valid JSON, free of formatting artifacts. For development, you can explicitly set `colors` to `true` (or `compact` to `false`). Entries are then rendered with Node's `util.inspect()`, which is easier to read during local debugging but is no longer strict JSON.
blocks.text: When json is set to true, the ConsoleLogger defaults colors to false and compact to true. With those two values, each entry is serialized with JSON.stringify(), so the output is valid JSON, free of formatting artifacts. For development, you can explicitly set colors to true (or compact to false). Entries are then rendered with Node's util.inspect(), which is easier to read during local debugging but is no longer strict JSON.
blocks.zh: 何时 `json` 设置为 `true`，这个 `ConsoleLogger` 默认值 `colors` 二 `false` 和 `compact` 二 `true` 使用这两个值，每个条目都序列化为 `JSON.stringify()`，因此输出有效 JSON，没有格式化工件。对于开发，可以显式设置 `colors` 二 `true` （或 `compact` 二 `false`).然后使用 Node's `util.inspect()`，这在本地调试期间更容易读取，但不再严格 JSON.

blocks.md: When JSON logging is enabled, the log output looks like this (on a single line):
blocks.text: When JSON logging is enabled, the log output looks like this (on a single line):
blocks.zh: 何时 JSON 日志记录已启用，日志输出如下所示（在一行上）：

blocks.code:
{
  "level": "log",
  "pid": 19096,
  "timestamp": 1607370779834,
  "message": "Starting Nest application...",
  "context": "NestFactory"
}

blocks.md: Each entry has the following fields:
blocks.text: Each entry has the following fields:
blocks.zh: 每个条目都有以下字段：

blocks.md:
- `level`: the log level.
- `pid`: the process id.
- `timestamp`: when the entry was written, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The `timestamp` and `prefix` options, and a [custom timestamp format](#extend-built-in-logger), apply to text output only.
- `message`: the message, as passed to the logger.
- `context`: the logger context, when there is one.
- `stack`: the stack trace passed to `error()`, when there is one.
- `params`: the [structured logging params](#structured-logging-params), when any were passed.
blocks.text: level: the log level. pid: the process id. timestamp: when the entry was written, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The timestamp and prefix options, and a custom timestamp format, apply to text output only. message: the message, as passed to the logger. context: the logger context, when there is one. stack: the stack trace passed to error(), when there is one. params: the structured logging params, when any were passed.
blocks.zh:
- `level`：日志级别。
- `pid`：进程 id。
- `timestamp`：写入条目的时间，以毫秒为单位，自 Unix 时代以来。这个 `timestamp` 和 `prefix` 选项，以及 [自定义时间戳格式](#extend-built-in-logger)，仅适用于文本输出。
- `message`：传递给记录器的消息。
- `context`：记录器上下文，如果有的话。
- `stack`：传递到的堆栈跟踪 `error()`，当有一个。
- `params`：[结构化日志记录参数](#structured-logging-params)，当任何通过时。

blocks.md: As in text mode, `error` entries are written to stderr and all other levels to stdout.
blocks.text: As in text mode, error entries are written to stderr and all other levels to stdout.
blocks.zh: 与文本模式一样，`error` 条目写入 stderr，所有其他级别写入 stdout。

blocks.md: Structured logging params
blocks.text: Structured logging params
blocks.zh: 结构化日志记录参数

blocks.md: Log messages often need to carry metadata: a user id, a request duration, a correlation id. Starting with NestJS v12, plain objects passed **after** the first message argument are treated as structured params and attached to the same log entry instead of being emitted as separate log records.
blocks.text: Log messages often need to carry metadata: a user id, a request duration, a correlation id. Starting with NestJS v12, plain objects passed after the first message argument are treated as structured params and attached to the same log entry instead of being emitted as separate log records.
blocks.zh: 日志消息通常需要携带元数据：用户 id、请求持续时间、相关性 id。从 NestJSv12，在**第一个消息参数之后**传递的纯对象被视为结构化参数，并附加到同一个日志条目，而不是作为单独的日志记录发出。

blocks.code:
const logger = new Logger('UserService');
logger.log('User created', { userId: 1, email: 'foo@bar.com' });

blocks.md: In text mode, the params are appended inline to the same formatted line:
blocks.text: In text mode, the params are appended inline to the same formatted line:
blocks.zh: 在文本模式下，参数内联附加到相同的格式行：

blocks.code: [Nest] 3785  - 02/26/2026, 10:04:41 AM     LOG [UserService] User created { userId: 1, email: 'foo@bar.com' }

blocks.md: When several plain objects are passed, they are merged into a single set of params:
blocks.text: When several plain objects are passed, they are merged into a single set of params:
blocks.zh: 当传递几个普通对象时，它们会合并到一组参数中：

blocks.code: logger.log('Request handled', { method: 'GET' }, { path: '/api', duration: 42 });
[Nest] 3785  - 02/26/2026, 10:04:41 AM     LOG [UserService] Request handled { method: 'GET', path: '/api', duration: 42 }

blocks.md: In JSON mode, params are nested under a `params` key by default:
blocks.text: In JSON mode, params are nested under a params key by default:
blocks.zh: 在 JSON 模式，参数嵌套在 `params` 默认密钥：

blocks.md: To spread them into the root of the JSON object instead (which some log aggregators prefer), enable `flattenParams`:
blocks.text: To spread them into the root of the JSON object instead (which some log aggregators prefer), enable flattenParams:
blocks.zh: 要将它们扩展到 JSON 对象的根目录（某些日志聚合器更喜欢这样），请启用 `flattenParams`：

blocks.code: new ConsoleLogger({ json: true, flattenParams: true });

{
  "level": "log",
  "pid": 3785,
  "timestamp": 1772089691769,
  "message": "User created",
  "context": "UserService",
  "userId": 1,
  "email": "foo@bar.com"
}

blocks.md: The relevant `ConsoleLogger` options are:
blocks.text: The relevant ConsoleLogger options are:
blocks.zh: 相关 `ConsoleLogger` 选项有：

blocks.md:
| Option             | Description                                                                                                   | Default |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `structuredParams` | If enabled, plain objects logged after the message are attached to the same entry as params.                  | `true`  |
| `flattenParams`    | If enabled, params are spread into the root of the JSON record instead of nested under `params`. A param whose key the record already uses (such as `message` or `level`) is dropped. JSON mode only; requires `structuredParams`. | `false` |
blocks.zh:
| 选择 | 描述 | 默认的 |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `structuredParams` | 如果启用，消息后记录的普通对象将附加到与参数相同的条目。 | `true` |
| `flattenParams` | 如果启用，参数将传播到 JSON 记录而不是嵌套在 `params`.记录已使用其键的参数（例如 `message` 或者 `level`）被丢弃。 JSON 仅模式；要求 `structuredParams`. | `false` |

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: Only **plain objects** are treated as params. Arrays, strings, numbers, class instances, and `null` are still logged as separate messages (a string passed as the *last* argument is still treated as the context), and a plain object passed as the *first* argument is still treated as the message itself. Set `structuredParams: false` to restore the pre-v12 behavior.
blocks.text: Only plain objects are treated as params. Arrays, strings, numbers, class instances, and null are still logged as separate messages (a string passed as the *last* argument is still treated as the context), and a plain object passed as the *first* argument is still treated as the message itself. Set structuredParams: false to restore the pre-v12 behavior.
blocks.zh: 只有**普通对象**被视为参数。数组、字符串、数字、类实例和 `null` 仍然被记录为单独的消息（作为*last*参数传递的字符串仍然被视为上下文），作为*first*参数传递的普通对象仍然被视为消息本身。设置 `structuredParams: false` 恢复 v12 之前的行为。

blocks.title: Note
blocks.md: In the example above, `bufferLogs` is set to `true` so that all logs are held in a buffer until a custom logger (`MyLogger` in this case) is attached. With `autoFlushLogs` enabled (the default), Nest flushes the buffer on its own: an HTTP application (or microservice) flushes it when it starts listening in `app.listen()`, and a standalone [application context](/standalone-applications) flushes it when you call `app.useLogger()`. If initialization fails, Nest flushes it right away. When Nest can't create a provider (for example, because its factory throws), it falls back to the original `ConsoleLogger` to print the buffer and the error. When a lifecycle hook such as `onModuleInit()` rejects, Nest prints the buffer through the logger you attached (or through the original one, if none is attached yet) but doesn't log the error: the call that started initialization, such as `app.listen()`, rejects with it. Set `autoFlushLogs` to `false` to flush the buffer yourself with `app.flushLogs()` (or the static `Logger.flush()`).
blocks.text: In the example above, bufferLogs is set to true so that all logs are held in a buffer until a custom logger (MyLogger in this case) is attached. With autoFlushLogs enabled (the default), Nest flushes the buffer on its own: an HTTP application (or microservice) flushes it when it starts listening in app.listen(), and a standalone application context flushes it when you call app.useLogger(). If initialization fails, Nest flushes it right away. When Nest can't create a provider (for example, because its factory throws), it falls back to the original ConsoleLogger to print the buffer and the error. When a lifecycle hook such as onModuleInit() rejects, Nest prints the buffer through the logger you attached (or through the original one, if none is attached yet) but doesn't log the error: the call that started initialization, such as app.listen(), rejects with it. Set autoFlushLogs to false to flush the buffer yourself with app.flushLogs() (or the static Logger.flush()).
blocks.zh: 在上面的示例中， `bufferLogs` 设置为 `true` 以便所有日志都保存在缓冲区中，直到自定义日志记录器（`MyLogger` 在这种情况下）是附加的。和 `autoFlushLogs` 已启用（默认值）， Nest 自行刷新缓冲区： HTTP 应用程序（或微服务）在开始侦听时刷新它 `app.listen()` 和一个独立的 [应用上下文](/standalone-applications) 打电话时刷新 `app.useLogger()`.如果初始化失败， Nest 马上冲洗。何时 Nest 无法创建提供程序（例如，因为它的工厂抛出），它会回落到原来的 `ConsoleLogger` 打印缓冲区和错误。当生命周期挂钩时，例如 `onModuleInit()` 拒绝， Nest 通过附加的记录器（如果还没有附加，则通过原始记录器）打印缓冲区，但不记录错误：启动初始化的调用，例如 `app.listen()`，用它拒绝。设置 `autoFlushLogs` 二 `false` 自己冲洗缓冲区 `app.flushLogs()` （或静态 `Logger.flush()`).

blocks.title: Warning
blocks.md: If a provider factory or a lifecycle hook calls `process.exit()` itself (for example, after a failed connection check), or a startup step never settles (such as a connection that keeps retrying), nothing in the buffer is printed, not even when you stop the process with `Ctrl+C`. Throw an error instead, so that initialization fails and Nest flushes the buffer.

Throw an error instead, so that initialization fails and Nest flushes the buffer.
blocks.zh: 如果提供者工厂或生命周期挂钩调用 `process.exit()` 本身（例如，在失败的连接检查之后），或者启动步骤从未解决（例如，不断重试的连接），缓冲区中不会打印任何内容，即使您使用 `Ctrl+C`.而是抛出一个错误，使得初始化失败，并且 Nest 刷新缓冲区。

blocks.md: When startup logs must always be visible, even if the process exits or stalls, don't buffer them: pass a logger instance as the `logger` option of `NestFactory.create()`, as shown in [Custom implementation](#custom-implementation), so that Nest hands each line to it as soon as it is logged. That instance is created outside the dependency injection system, so it can't inject providers such as `ConfigService`.

blocks.md: Correlating logs with requests
blocks.text: Correlating logs with requests
blocks.zh: 将日志与请求相关联

blocks.md: Centralizing logs solves storage, not investigation. Once every instance ships to the same place, the hard part becomes reconstructing a *single* request out of thousands of interleaved lines. That is why so much production debugging is really the work of inventing a correlation id, threading it through every log call, and hoping nothing on the path forgot to pass it along.
blocks.text: Centralizing logs solves storage, not investigation. Once every instance ships to the same place, the hard part becomes reconstructing a *single* request out of thousands of interleaved lines. That is why so much production debugging is really the work of inventing a correlation id, threading it through every log call, and hoping nothing on the path forgot to pass it along.
blocks.zh: 集中日志解决的是存储，而不是调查。一旦每个实例都发送到同一个地方，困难的部分就变成了从数千个交织行中重建一个*单个*请求。这就是为什么这么多的生产调试实际上是发明一个相关 id，在每个日志调用中穿过它，并希望路径上没有任何东西忘记传递它。

blocks.md: [NestJS Observe](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/ 'NestJS Observe') removes that bookkeeping. Turn on `forwardLogs` and every line written through Nest's `Logger` is captured with the trace it was written in already attached:
blocks.text: NestJS Observe removes that bookkeeping. Turn on forwardLogs and every line written through Nest's Logger is captured with the trace it was written in already attached:
blocks.zh: [NestJS Observe](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/) 删除了记账。打开 `forwardLogs` 每一行都被写下来 Nest 的 `Logger` 捕获了已附加的跟踪：

blocks.md: You keep calling `this.logger.log()` with an `orderId` param exactly as before: no correlation id to generate, no context object to thread through your service layer. On an execution page, the logs for that one request are then placed on the trace's own clock, each line sitting next to the span that was in flight when it was written, so "the retry warning fired *before* the timeout, not after" is something you can see instead of infer from timestamps across three log streams.
blocks.text: You keep calling this.logger.log() with an orderId param exactly as before: no correlation id to generate, no context object to thread through your service layer. On an execution page, the logs for that one request are then placed on the trace's own clock, each line sitting next to the span that was in flight when it was written, so "the retry warning fired *before* the timeout, not after" is something you can see instead of infer from timestamps across three log streams.
blocks.zh: 你一直打电话 `this.logger.log()` 用一个 `orderId` 参数和以前一模一样：不需要生成相关 id，不需要穿过服务层的上下文对象。在执行页面上，该请求的日志被放置在跟踪自己的时钟上，每一行都位于编写时正在飞行的跨度旁边，因此“重试警告是在超时之前发出的，而不是之后发出的”是您可以看到的，而不是从三个日志流的时间戳中推断出来的。

blocks.md: Structured logging params carry through as well, so `orderId` stays a queryable field rather than being flattened into the message text. Log lines are also alertable in their own right, for example: "tell me when `payment declined` appears more than 10 times in 15 minutes".
blocks.text: Structured logging params carry through as well, so orderId stays a queryable field rather than being flattened into the message text. Log lines are also alertable in their own right, for example: "tell me when payment declined appears more than 10 times in 15 minutes".
blocks.zh: 结构化日志参数也会继续执行，因此 `orderId` 保留一个可查询的字段，而不是被展平成消息文本。日志行本身也是可警报的，例如：“告诉我何时 `payment declined`15 分钟内出现 10 次以上”。

blocks.md: If you would rather keep log content in your own aggregator, you do not have to forward anything. Even with `forwardLogs` off, the SDK augments `ConsoleLogger` so every line written during a request carries that request's trace id: at the end of the line in the default format (`   Trace ID: <id>`, after the message), and as a `traceId` field with [JSON logging](#json-logging) enabled:

Even with forwardLogs off, the SDK augments ConsoleLogger so every line written during a request carries that request's trace id: at the end of the line in the default format ( Trace ID: , after the message), and as a traceId field with JSON logging enabled:
blocks.zh: 如果您希望将日志内容保留在自己的聚合器中，则不必转发任何内容。即使有 `forwardLogs` 关闭，SDK 增加 `ConsoleLogger` 因此，在请求期间写入的每一行都以默认格式在行尾携带该请求的跟踪 id：（` Trace ID: <id>`，在消息之后），并且作为 `traceId` 字段 [JSON 伐木作业](#json-logging) 启用：

blocks.code: {"level":"log","pid":66803,"timestamp":1789978166281,"message":"Payment captured","context":"OrdersService","traceId":"0199a3f2-7c1e-7b40-9d2a-5e8f1c3b7a64"}

blocks.md: That id is enough to jump from a line in your existing stack to the full trace in the dashboard. It is on by default and controlled by the `attachTraceIdToLogs` option (see [Trace correlation](/observability/sdk#trace-correlation)). Lines written outside a request (during bootstrap, for example) are left as they are. The augmentation applies to Nest's built-in `ConsoleLogger` only, so if you replace it with an [external logger](#use-external-logger), read the id yourself with `TracerService.currentTraceId()`. See the [SDK reference](/observability/sdk#logs) for forwarding and its redaction settings.

It is on by default and controlled by the attachTraceIdToLogs option (see Trace correlation). Lines written outside a request (during bootstrap, for example) are left as they are. The augmentation applies to Nest's built-in ConsoleLogger only, so if you replace it with an external logger, read the id yourself with TracerService.currentTraceId(). See the SDK reference for forwarding and its redaction settings.
blocks.zh: 该 id 足以从现有堆栈中的一行跳转到仪表板中的完整跟踪。默认情况下，它是打开的，由 `attachTraceIdToLogs` 选项控制（参见 [Trace correlation](/observability/sdk#trace-correlation)）。在请求外部写入的行（例如，在引导期间）保持原样。该扩展仅适用于 Nest 的内置 `ConsoleLogger`，因此如果您用 [外部记录器](#use-external-logger) 替换它，请自己用 `TracerService.currentTraceId()` 读取 id。有关转发及其编辑设置，请参见 [SDK 参考](/observability/sdk#logs)。

blocks.md: The trace id is not the only thing that lives for the length of a request. The SDK keeps an `AsyncLocalStorage` store for every request, job, and message it instruments, and `TracerService` exposes it through `setAttribute()` and `getAttribute()`. That is the natural place for the user or tenant a request is acting for, readable from anywhere downstream without threading it through every call. See [Request-scoped attributes](/observability/manual-instrumentation#request-scoped-attributes), and the [Async local storage](/recipes/async-local-storage) recipe for how it compares to a store you set up yourself.

blocks.md: Use external logger
blocks.text: Use external logger
blocks.zh: 使用外部记录器

blocks.md: As [Logging in production](#logging-in-production) shows, the built-in logger already covers structured, centralized logging for most applications. Some requirements still call for a dedicated library such as [Pino](https://github.com/pinojs/pino) or [Winston](https://github.com/winstonjs/winston): multiple in-process transports (files, syslog, HTTP), redaction of sensitive fields, custom serializers, or the lowest possible overhead on services that log at very high volume. As with any standard Node.js application, you can take full advantage of such modules in Nest: implement the `LoggerService` interface as described in [Custom implementation](#custom-implementation), or use a community integration.

Some requirements still call for a dedicated library such as Pino or Winston: multiple in-process transports (files, syslog, HTTP), redaction of sensitive fields, custom serializers, or the lowest possible overhead on services that log at very high volume. As with any standard Node.js application, you can take full advantage of such modules in Nest: implement the LoggerService interface as described in Custom implementation, or use a community integration.
blocks.zh: 作为 [Logging in production](#logging-in-production) 如图所示，内置记录器已经涵盖了大多数应用程序的结构化、集中式日志记录。有些需求仍然需要专用库，例如 [Pino](https://github.com/pinojs/pino) 或者 [Winston](https://github.com/winstonjs/winston)：多个进程内传输（文件、系统日志、HTTP)、敏感字段的编辑、自定义序列化程序或以非常高的卷记录服务的最低可能开销。与任何标准一样 Node.js 应用程序，您可以充分利用这些模块 Nest：实施 `LoggerService` 中所述的接口 [Custom implementation](#custom-implementation)，或使用社区集成。

chapters.title: Events
chapters.summary: The Event Emitter package (@nestjs/event-emitter) provides an observer implementation that lets you subscribe to and listen for events that occur in your application.

blocks.md: The [Event Emitter](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nestjs/event-emitter) package (`@nestjs/event-emitter`) provides an observer implementation that lets you subscribe to and listen for events that occur in your application. Events are a good way to decouple different parts of your application, since a single event can have multiple listeners that don't depend on each other.
blocks.text: The Event Emitter package (@nestjs/event-emitter) provides an observer implementation that lets you subscribe to and listen for events that occur in your application. Events are a good way to decouple different parts of your application, since a single event can have multiple listeners that don't depend on each other.

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: If an event listener belongs to a [request-scoped](/fundamentals/injection-scopes) provider, Nest creates a new instance of that provider for every event it handles. The event payload takes the place of the request object, so injecting `REQUEST` in that provider gives you the payload. If the payload you emit is the incoming request object itself (or carries its context ID), set the `inheritRequestContextId` option of `forRoot()` to `true` so that the listener reuses that request's DI sub-tree instead of creating a new one.

chapters.title: Task scheduling
chapters.summary: Task scheduling lets you run arbitrary code (methods or functions) at a fixed date and time, at recurring intervals, or once after a specified delay.

blocks.md: Task scheduling lets you run arbitrary code (methods or functions) at a fixed date and time, at recurring intervals, or once after a specified delay. In the Linux world, this is often handled at the OS level by tools like [cron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cron). For Node.js apps, several packages emulate cron-like functionality. Nest provides the `@nestjs/schedule` package, which integrates with the popular Node.js [cron](https://github.com/kelektiv/node-cron) package. This chapter covers the `@nestjs/schedule` package.
blocks.text: Task scheduling lets you run arbitrary code (methods or functions) at a fixed date and time, at recurring intervals, or once after a specified delay. In the Linux world, this is often handled at the OS level by tools like cron. For Node.js apps, several packages emulate cron-like functionality. Nest provides the @nestjs/schedule package, which integrates with the popular Node.js cron package. This chapter covers the @nestjs/schedule package.

name Lets you access and control a cron job after it's been declared.
timeZone Specifies the time zone for the execution. This modifies the actual time relative to your time zone. If the time zone is invalid, an error is thrown. You can check all available time zones on the Moment Timezone website.

blocks.md:
- `stop()` - stops a job that is scheduled to run.
- `start()` - restarts a job that has been stopped.
- `setTime(time: CronTime)` - stops a job, sets a new time for it, and then starts it.
- `lastDate()` - returns a JavaScript `Date` representing the last execution of the job, or `null` if it hasn't run yet.
- `nextDate()` - returns a `DateTime` representation of the date when the next execution of the job is scheduled.
- `nextDates(count: number)` - returns an array (of size `count`) of `DateTime` representations for the next set of dates that will trigger job execution. `count` defaults to 0, which returns an empty array.

- `stop()`- 停止计划运行的作业。
- `start()`- 重新启动已停止的作业。

blocks.md: The instances coordinate through a lock store they share, such as your PostgreSQL database or Redis. The first instance to fire the job takes a lease on it and keeps renewing it while it's up, and the other instances skip their ticks instead of queuing them. If the owner stops, another instance takes the job over at its next tick. A job that can take longer than its interval also gets `@WithoutOverlapping()`, which skips a tick while the previous run is still going. [Distributed locks](/reliability/locks) shows how to register the module and the store.

blocks.md: Knowing a cron job actually ran
blocks.text: Knowing a cron job actually ran
blocks.zh: 知道 cron 作业实际运行

blocks.md: A scheduled job that throws is a problem you will hear about. A scheduled job that silently *stops being scheduled* (the process crashed, the container was descheduled, a deploy shipped a `@Cron()` expression with a typo) is a problem nobody hears about until the report it generates is missing.

A scheduled job that silently *stops being scheduled* (the process crashed, the container was descheduled, a deploy shipped a @Cron() expression with a typo) is a problem nobody hears about until the report it generates is missing.
blocks.zh: 一个计划中的工作抛出是一个你会听说的问题。静默*停止调度*的调度作业（进程崩溃、容器取消调度、部署发送 `@Cron()` 带有错别字的表达式）是一个没有人听说过的问题，直到它生成的报告丢失。

blocks.md: This is the failure mode cron monitoring exists for, and [NestJS Observe](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/ 'NestJS Observe') covers it without a third-party ping service or a heartbeat URL for the job to call on its way out. Scheduled runs are reported as **jobs**, alongside queue consumers, each with its duration, outcome, and failure reason. A **job silence** alert rule fires when a named job hasn't reported within a tolerance you set, anywhere from 2 minutes to 7 days: *"alert me if `daily-invoices` has not reported in the last 26 hours"*.

Scheduled runs are reported as jobs, alongside queue consumers, each with its duration, outcome, and failure reason. A job silence alert rule fires when a named job hasn't reported within a tolerance you set, anywhere from 2 minutes to 7 days: *"alert me if daily-invoices has not reported in the last 26 hours"*.
blocks.zh: 这是 cron 监控存在的故障模式，并且 [NestJS Observe](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/) 无需第三方 ping 服务或心跳即可覆盖 URL 让工作在结束时呼叫。计划运行与队列使用者一起报告为**作业**，每个作业都有其持续时间、结果和失败原因。当指定作业未在您设置的容差范围内报告时（从 2 分钟到 7 天不等），**作业静默**警报规则将触发：*"如果出现以下情况，请提醒我 `daily-invoices` 在过去 26 小时内没有报告”*。

blocks.md: Two details make this practical rather than noisy. A scope that has never reported anything doesn't fire, so you can add the rule before the job ships without being paged for something that isn't integrated yet. And rules carry a recurring mute schedule, so a job that legitimately doesn't run at weekends doesn't wake anyone on Saturday.

blocks.zh: 两个细节让它实用而不是嘈杂。从未报告过任何内容的作用域不会触发，因此您可以在作业发布之前添加规则，而无需分页尚未集成的内容。规则有一个重复的静音时间表，所以一份在周末不运行的工作不会在周六叫醒任何人。

blocks.md: A handler that needs to report its own progress can inject `TracerService` and record spans or custom metrics from inside the run. Metrics in particular aren't tied to a trace, so they can be reported from cron jobs and lifecycle hooks alike. See [Manual instrumentation](/observability/manual-instrumentation) for that, and the [Observability](/observability/overview) chapter for setup.

chapters.title: Queues
chapters.summary: Queues are a design pattern that helps you deal with common application scaling and performance challenges.

blocks.md: Queues are a design pattern that helps you deal with common application scaling and performance challenges. Some examples of problems that queues can help you solve are:
blocks.text: Queues are a design pattern that helps you deal with common application scaling and performance challenges. Some examples of problems that queues can help you solve are:
blocks.zh: 队列是一种设计模式，可帮助您处理常见的应用程序扩展和性能挑战。队列可以帮助您解决的一些问题示例包括：

blocks.md:
- Smooth out processing peaks. For example, if users can initiate resource-intensive tasks at arbitrary times, you can add these tasks to a queue instead of performing them synchronously. Worker processes then pull tasks from the queue in a controlled manner. As the application grows, you can add queue consumers to scale up back-end task handling.
- Break up monolithic tasks that may otherwise block the Node.js event loop. For example, if a user request requires CPU-intensive work like audio transcoding, you can delegate this task to other processes, so user-facing processes remain responsive.
- Provide a reliable communication channel across services. For example, you can queue tasks (jobs) in one process or service and consume them in another. By listening for status events, any process or service can be notified of completion, errors, or other state changes in the job lifecycle. When queue producers or consumers fail, their state is preserved, and task handling can resume automatically when nodes restart.
blocks.text: Smooth out processing peaks. For example, if users can initiate resource-intensive tasks at arbitrary times, you can add these tasks to a queue instead of performing them synchronously. Worker processes then pull tasks from the queue in a controlled manner. As the application grows, you can add queue consumers to scale up back-end task handling. Break up monolithic tasks that may otherwise block the Node.js event loop. For example, if a user request requires CPU-intensive work like audio transcoding, you can delegate this task to other processes, so user-facing processes remain responsive. Provide a reliable communication channel across services. For example, you can queue tasks (jobs) in one process or service and consume them in another. By listening for status events, any process or service can be notified of completion, errors, or other state changes in the job lifecycle. When queue producers or consumers fail, their state is preserved, and task handling can resume automatically when nodes restart.
blocks.zh:
- 平滑处理峰值。例如，如果用户可以在任意时间启动资源密集型任务，则可以将这些任务添加到队列中，而不是同步执行它们。然后，工作进程以受控的方式从队列中提取任务。随着应用程序的增长，您可以添加队列使用者来扩展后端任务处理。
- 拆分可能会阻碍 Node.js 事件循环。例如，如果用户请求需要 CPU-音频转码等密集型工作，您可以将此任务委托给其他流程，以便面向用户的流程保持响应。
- 提供跨服务的可靠沟通渠道。例如，您可以在一个进程或服务中排队任务（作业），并在另一个进程或服务中使用它们。通过监听状态事件，可以通知任何流程或服务作业生命周期中的完成、错误或其他状态更改。当队列生产者或消费者失败时，它们的状态被保留，并且当节点重新启动时，任务处理可以自动恢复。

blocks.md: Nest provides the `@nestjs/bullmq` package for BullMQ integration and the `@nestjs/bull` package for Bull integration. Both packages wrap their respective libraries, which are developed by the same team. Bull is in maintenance mode (the team only fixes bugs), while BullMQ is actively developed and offers a modern TypeScript implementation with a different set of features. If Bull meets your requirements, it remains a reliable, battle-tested choice.

blocks.md: Both BullMQ and Bull use [Redis](https://redis.io/) to persist job data, so you need a running Redis instance. Because they are Redis-backed, your queue architecture can be fully distributed and platform-independent. For example, you can run some queue producers, consumers, and listeners in Nest on one or more nodes, and other producers, consumers, and listeners on other Node.js platforms on other network nodes.

blocks.md: Jobs can have additional options associated with them. Pass an options object as the third argument of the `Queue.add()` method, after the job data. Some of the job options are:

blocks.zh: 作业可以有与之相关联的其他选项。传递 options 对象作为第三个参数 `Queue.add()` 方法，在作业数据之后。一些工作选项包括：

blocks.md:
- `priority`: `number` - Priority value, from 0 to 2,097,151. `0` (the default) means no explicit priority; jobs without a priority are processed before prioritized jobs, and among prioritized jobs, lower numbers are processed first. Using priorities has a slight impact on performance, so use them only when required.
- `delay`: `number` - Time (in milliseconds) to wait until this job can be processed. For accurate delays, workers and producers should have their clocks synchronized.
- `attempts`: `number` - The total number of attempts to try the job until it completes (defaults to 1).
- `backoff`: `number | BackoffOptions` - Backoff setting for automatic retries if the job fails. See [BackoffOptions](https://docs.bullmq.io/api/interfaces/v6.BackoffOptions.html).
- `lifo`: `boolean` - If `true`, adds the job to the right end of the queue instead of the left (default `false`).
- `jobId`: `string` - Overrides the job ID. By default, the job ID is a unique integer. If you use this option, it's up to you to ensure the ID is unique. A job with an ID that already exists is not added.
- `removeOnComplete`: `boolean | number | KeepJobs` - If `true`, removes the job when it successfully completes. A number specifies how many jobs to keep, and a `KeepJobs` object specifies a maximum age and/or count. By default, the job is kept in the completed set.
- `removeOnFail`: `boolean | number | KeepJobs` - If `true`, removes the job when it fails after all attempts. A number or `KeepJobs` object works as for `removeOnComplete`. By default, the job is kept in the failed set.
- `stackTraceLimit`: `number` - Limits the number of stack trace lines recorded for a failed job.

blocks.zh:
- `priority`:`number`-优先级值，从 0 到 2,097,151。`0`（默认）意味着没有明确的优先级；没有优先级的作业在优先级作业之前处理，在优先级作业中，优先级较低的作业优先处理。使用优先级对性能的影响很小，因此仅在需要时使用它们。
- `delay`:`number`-等待时间（以毫秒为单位），直到可以处理此作业。为了准确的延迟，工人和生产者应该同步他们的时钟。
- `attempts`:`number`-尝试作业直到完成的总次数（默认为 1）。
- `backoff`:`number | BackoffOptions`-作业失败时自动重试的回退设置。参见 [BackoffOptions](https://docs.bullmq.io/api/interfaces/v6.BackoffOptions.html)。
- `lifo`:`boolean`-如果 `true`，将作业添加到队列的右端而不是左端（默认值 `false`）。
- `jobId`: `string` - 覆盖作业 ID。默认情况下，作业 ID 是唯一的整数。如果您使用此选项，则由您来确保 ID 是唯一的。不会添加已存在的带有 ID 的作业。
- `removeOnComplete`:`boolean | number | KeepJobs`- 如果 `true`，在作业成功完成时删除作业。一个数字指定要保留多少个作业，以及 `KeepJobs` 对象指定最大年龄和/或计数。默认情况下，作业保留在已完成的集合中。
- `removeOnFail`：`boolean | number | KeepJobs`-如果 `true`，当作业在所有尝试后失败时删除。数字或 `KeepJobs` 对象与 `removeOnComplete` 一样有效。默认情况下，作业保留在失败集合中。
- `stackTraceLimit`:`number`-限制为失败作业记录的堆栈跟踪行数。

blocks.md: Queues fail in ways that HTTP endpoints don't. A job doesn't return a status code to an impatient user. It retries quietly, three times, with backoff, and the only symptom is that something downstream never happened. The two questions that matter are therefore *"is this queue keeping up?"* and *"did that job run at all?"*, and the consumer's own logs can't answer either of them.

The two questions that matter are therefore *"is this queue keeping up?"* and *"did that job run at all?"*, and the consumer's own logs can't answer either of them.
blocks.zh: 队列失败的方式是 HTTP 端点不会。作业不会向不耐烦的用户返回状态代码。它悄悄地重试，三次，有后退，唯一的症状是下游的事情从未发生过。因此，两个重要的问题是*“这个队列保持不变吗？”*和*“那个作业运行过吗？”*，而消费者自己的日志无法回答这两个问题。

blocks.md:
- **Queue wait time is measured separately from execution time.** A job that takes 200 ms to run but sat in the queue for four minutes is a capacity problem, not a slow handler. The two numbers are reported side by side, so you can tell which one you have.
- **Attempts and failure reasons are recorded per run.** You see that a job succeeded on attempt 3 rather than seeing only the success, which is usually the difference between "fine" and "quietly degrading".
- **Silence is alertable.** A *job silence* rule fires when a named job hasn't reported for longer than a tolerance you choose. That's how you find out that the nightly billing consumer stopped running on the night it stops, rather than at the end of the month.
blocks.text: Queue wait time is measured separately from execution time. A job that takes 200 ms to run but sat in the queue for four minutes is a capacity problem, not a slow handler. The two numbers are reported side by side, so you can tell which one you have. Attempts and failure reasons are recorded per run. You see that a job succeeded on attempt 3 rather than seeing only the success, which is usually the difference between "fine" and "quietly degrading". Silence is alertable. A *job silence* rule fires when a named job hasn't reported for longer than a tolerance you choose. That's how you find out that the nightly billing consumer stopped running on the night it stops, rather than at the end of the month.
blocks.zh:
- **队列等待时间与执行时间分开测量。**运行时间为 200 毫秒但在队列中停留四分钟的作业是容量问题，而不是处理程序速度慢。这两个数字是并排报告的，所以你可以分辨出你有哪一个。
- **每次运行都会记录尝试和失败原因。**您会看到作业在尝试 3 时成功，而不是只看到成功，这通常是“良好”和“悄然降级”之间的区别。
- **静默是可警报的。**当指定作业未报告的时间超过您选择的容差时，*作业静默*规则将触发。这就是您如何发现夜间计费消费者在停止运行的当晚停止运行，而不是在月底。

blocks.md: Job handlers can also run in a separate (forked) process (see [Sandboxed processors](https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/workers/sandboxed-processors) in the BullMQ documentation). This has several advantages:
blocks.text: Job handlers can also run in a separate (forked) process (see Sandboxed processors in the BullMQ documentation). This has several advantages:

- The process is sandboxed, so if it crashes, the worker isn't affected.
- You can run blocking code without affecting the queue (jobs don't stall).
- Better utilization of multi-core CPUs.
- Fewer connections to Redis.

- 您可以在不影响队列的情况下运行阻塞代码（作业不会停滞）。
- 更好地利用多核 CPU。
- 到 Redis 的连接较少。

blocks.md: Job options
blocks.text: Job options
blocks.zh: 工作选项

blocks.md: Jobs can have additional options associated with them. Pass an options object after the job data in the `Queue.add()` method. The job options are:
blocks.text: Jobs can have additional options associated with them. Pass an options object after the job data in the Queue.add() method. The job options are:
blocks.zh: 作业可以有与之相关联的其他选项。在作业数据之后传递选项对象 `Queue.add()` 方法。工作选项有：

blocks.md:
- `priority`: `number` - Optional priority value. Ranges from 1 (highest priority) to MAX_INT (lowest priority). Using priorities has a slight impact on performance, so use them with caution.
- `delay`: `number` - Time (in milliseconds) to wait until this job can be processed. For accurate delays, both server and clients should have their clocks synchronized.
- `attempts`: `number` - The total number of attempts to try the job until it completes.
- `repeat`: `RepeatOpts` - Repeats the job according to a cron specification. See [RepeatOpts](https://github.com/OptimalBits/bull/blob/master/REFERENCE.md#queueadd).
- `backoff`: `number | BackoffOpts` - Backoff setting for automatic retries if the job fails. See [BackoffOpts](https://github.com/OptimalBits/bull/blob/master/REFERENCE.md#queueadd).
- `lifo`: `boolean` - If `true`, adds the job to the right end of the queue instead of the left (default `false`).
- `timeout`: `number` - The number of milliseconds after which the job fails with a timeout error.
- `jobId`: `number | string` - Overrides the job ID. By default, the job ID is a unique integer. If you use this option, it's up to you to ensure the ID is unique. A job with an ID that already exists is not added.
- `removeOnComplete`: `boolean | number` - If `true`, removes the job when it successfully completes. A number specifies how many jobs to keep. By default, the job is kept in the completed set.
- `removeOnFail`: `boolean | number` - If `true`, removes the job when it fails after all attempts. A number specifies how many jobs to keep. By default, the job is kept in the failed set.
- `stackTraceLimit`: `number` - Limits the number of stack trace lines recorded for a failed job.

blocks.zh:
- `priority`:`number`-可选的优先级值。范围从 1（最高优先级）到 MAX_INT（最低优先级）。使用优先级对性能有轻微影响，因此请谨慎使用。
- `delay`:`number`-等待时间（以毫秒为单位），直到可以处理此作业。为了获得准确的延迟，服务器和客户端都应该同步它们的时钟。
- `attempts`:`number`-尝试作业直至完成的总次数。
- `repeat`:`RepeatOpts`-根据 cron 规范重复作业。参见 [RepeatOpts](https://github.com/OptimalBits/bull/blob/master/REFERENCE.md#queueadd)。
- `backoff`:`number | BackoffOpts`-作业失败时自动重试的回退设置。参见 [BackoffOpts](https://github.com/OptimalBits/bull/blob/master/REFERENCE.md#queueadd)。
- `lifo`:`boolean`-如果 `true`，将作业添加到队列的右端而不是左端（默认值 `false`）。
- `timeout`:`number`-作业失败并出现超时错误的毫秒数。
- `jobId`: `number | string` - 覆盖作业 ID。默认情况下，作业 ID 是唯一的整数。如果您使用此选项，则由您来确保 ID 是唯一的。不会添加已存在的带有 ID 的作业。
- `removeOnComplete`:`boolean | number`- 如果 `true`，在作业成功完成时删除作业。一个数字指定要保留多少工作。默认情况下，作业保留在已完成的集合中。
- `removeOnFail`:`boolean | number`- 如果 `true`，在所有尝试后都失败时删除作业。一个数字指定要保留多少工作。默认情况下，作业保留在失败集合中。
- `stackTraceLimit`:`number`-限制为失败作业记录的堆栈跟踪行数。

blocks.md: Because Bull operates in a distributed (multi-node) environment, it defines the concept of event locality. Events may be triggered either entirely within a single process, or on shared queues from different processes. A **local** event is produced when an action or state change is triggered on a queue in the local process. In other words, when your event producers and consumers are local to a single process, all events happening on queues are local.

Events may be triggered either entirely within a single process, or on shared queues from different processes. A local event is produced when an action or state change is triggered on a queue in the local process. In other words, when your event producers and consumers are local to a single process, all events happening on queues are local.
blocks.zh: 因为 Bull 在分布式（多节点）环境中运行，所以它定义了事件局部性的概念。事件可以完全在单个进程内触发，也可以在来自不同进程的共享队列上触发。当在本地进程中的队列上触发操作或状态更改时，会产生**local**事件。换句话说，当您的事件生产者和消费者是单个进程的本地用户时，队列上发生的所有事件都是本地用户。

blocks.md: When a queue is shared across multiple processes, **global** events come into play. For a listener in one process to receive an event notification triggered by another process, it must register for a global event.

Local event listeners Global event listeners Handler method signature / When fired
@OnQueueError()@OnGlobalQueueError()handler(error: Error) - An error occurred. error contains the triggering error.
@OnQueueWaiting()@OnGlobalQueueWaiting()handler(jobId: number | string) - A job is waiting to be processed as soon as a worker is idle. jobId contains the ID of the job that has entered this state.
@OnQueueActive()@OnGlobalQueueActive()handler(job: Job) - Job job has started.
@OnQueueStalled()@OnGlobalQueueStalled()handler(job: Job) - Job job has been marked as stalled. This is useful for debugging job workers that crash or pause the event loop.
@OnQueueProgress()@OnGlobalQueueProgress()handler(job: Job, progress: number) - Job job's progress was updated to value progress.
@OnQueueCompleted()@OnGlobalQueueCompleted()handler(job: Job, result: any) - Job job successfully completed with a result result.
@OnQueueFailed()@OnGlobalQueueFailed()handler(job: Job, err: Error) - Job job failed with reason err.
@OnQueuePaused()@OnGlobalQueuePaused()handler() - The queue has been paused.
@OnQueueResumed()@OnGlobalQueueResumed()handler() - The queue has been resumed.
@OnQueueCleaned()@OnGlobalQueueCleaned()handler(jobs: Job[], type: string) - Old jobs have been cleaned from the queue. jobs is an array of cleaned jobs, and type is the type of jobs cleaned.
@OnQueueDrained()@OnGlobalQueueDrained()handler() - Emitted whenever the queue has processed all the waiting jobs (even if some delayed jobs are not yet processed).
@OnQueueRemoved()@OnGlobalQueueRemoved()handler(job: Job) - Job job was successfully removed.

blocks.md: Separate processes
blocks.text: Separate processes

blocks.md: Job handlers can also run in a separate (forked) process (see [Separate processes](https://github.com/OptimalBits/bull#separate-processes) in the Bull documentation). This has several advantages:
blocks.text: Job handlers can also run in a separate (forked) process (see Separate processes in the Bull documentation). This has several advantages:
blocks.zh: 作业处理程序也可以在单独的（分叉的）进程中运行（请参见 [Separate processes](https://github.com/OptimalBits/bull#separate-processes) 在公牛文档中）。这有几个优点：

blocks.md:
- The process is sandboxed, so if it crashes, the worker isn't affected.
- You can run blocking code without affecting the queue (jobs don't stall).
- Better utilization of multi-core CPUs.
- Fewer connections to Redis.
blocks.text: The process is sandboxed, so if it crashes, the worker isn't affected. You can run blocking code without affecting the queue (jobs don't stall). Better utilization of multi-core CPUs. Fewer connections to Redis.
blocks.zh:

chapters.title: HTTP client
chapters.summary: Most applications call other services over HTTP.

blocks.md: Most applications call other services over HTTP. The `@nestjs/http-client` package provides a client for this, built on the `fetch` API that ships with Node.js. It adds what `fetch` leaves out: base URLs, default headers, JSON bodies, path and query parameters, typed responses, timeouts, retries, interceptors, and named clients. You configure it as a Nest module and inject it like any other provider.
blocks.text: Most applications call other services over HTTP. The @nestjs/http-client package provides a client for this, built on the fetch API that ships with Node.js. It adds what fetch leaves out: base URLs, default headers, JSON bodies, path and query parameters, typed responses, timeouts, retries, interceptors, and named clients. You configure it as a Nest module and inject it like any other provider.
blocks.zh: 大多数应用程序调用其他服务 HTTP.这 `@nestjs/http-client` 包为此提供了一个客户端，建立在 `fetch` API 与 Node.js.它增加了什么 `fetch` 省略：基本 URL、默认标题， JSON 主体、路径和查询参数、类型化响应、超时、重试、拦截器和命名客户端。您将其配置为 Nest 模块并像任何其他提供者一样注入它。

blocks.md: The package has no dependencies besides `@nestjs/common` and `@nestjs/core`. Every method returns a Promise, so you `await` requests and handle failures with `try`/`catch`. If you prefer Observables, see [Working with RxJS](/application/http-client#working-with-rxjs).
blocks.text: The package has no dependencies besides @nestjs/common and @nestjs/core. Every method returns a Promise, so you await requests and handle failures with try/catch. If you prefer Observables, see Working with RxJS.
blocks.zh: 除了 `@nestjs/common` 和 `@nestjs/core` 之外，该包没有依赖项。每个方法都返回一个承诺，因此您 `await` 请求并使用 `try`/`catch` 处理失败。如果您更喜欢可观测值，请参见 [Working with RxJS](/application/http-client#working-with-rxjs)。

blocks.text: Making requests

blocks.md: A client has a method for each HTTP verb: `get()`, `post()`, `put()`, `patch()`, `delete()`, `head()`, and `options()`. Each one takes a URL and an optional options object, and resolves to an `HttpResponse`. The `request()` method takes the verb as the `method` option.

blocks.zh: 客户端对每个 HTTP 动词： `get()`, `post()`, `put()`, `patch()`, `delete()`, `head()`，和 `options()`.每个人都需要一个 URL 和可选的 options 对象，并解析为 `HttpResponse`.这 `request()` 方法将动词作为 `method` 选择。

blocks.md: The options mirror what a Nest controller reads from a request:
blocks.text: The options mirror what a Nest controller reads from a request:
blocks.zh: 选项反映了什么 Nest 控制器从请求中读取：

blocks.md:
- `params` fills the `:name` segments of the path, URI-encoded. A segment without a value throws, even when `params` is omitted, and so does a key that matches no segment, or a value that would move the request to another endpoint (an empty string, `.`, or `..`).
- `query` is an object or a `URLSearchParams` instance, appended to any query already in the URL. Arrays repeat the key (`topic=nest&topic=typescript`), `Date` values become ISO strings, and `null` and `undefined` values are skipped. The first request above goes to `https://api.github.com/orgs/nestjs/repos?type=public&sort=updated&topic=nest&topic=typescript`.
- `json` is serialized with `JSON.stringify()`, and sets the `content-type: application/json` header unless you set one.
- `body` is passed to `fetch` as is: a string, `Buffer`, `FormData`, `URLSearchParams`, `Blob`, a web or Node.js stream, or an async iterable. Pass either `json` or `body`, not both. A `GET` or `HEAD` request with a body throws before anything is sent.
- `headers` is merged over the client's headers. A `null` value removes a header.
- `timeout`, `retry`, `signal`, `throwOnHttpError`, `redirect`, and `dispatcher` override the client's settings for one request, and are covered below.
- `context` is a free-form object that [interceptors](/application/http-client#interceptors) can read.

- `query` 是一个对象还是一个 `URLSearchParams` 实例，附加到已经在 URL.数组重复键（`topic=nest&topic=typescript`), `Date` 价值观变得 ISO 字符串，以及 `null` 和 `undefined` 值被跳过。上面的第一个请求转到 `https://api.github.com/orgs/nestjs/repos?type=public&sort=updated&topic=nest&topic=typescript`.

blocks.md: The type argument, such as `Repo[]`, describes `data`. Nothing checks it at runtime, so validate responses from APIs you don't control. The `responseType` option controls how the body is read:
blocks.text: The type argument, such as Repo[], describes data. Nothing checks it at runtime, so validate responses from APIs you don't control. The responseType option controls how the body is read:

A `304` response throws by default, like any non-2xx; with `throwOnHttpError: false`, its `data` is `undefined`. |

| `'text'` | A string. |
| `'arrayBuffer'` | An `ArrayBuffer`. |
| `'stream'` | A Node.js `Readable`. See [Streaming responses](/application/http-client#streaming-responses). |

blocks.md: Timeouts and cancellation
blocks.text: Timeouts and cancellation
blocks.zh: 超时和取消

blocks.md: `fetch` has no timeout of its own, apart from the 5-minute limits of undici, the HTTP client inside Node.js. Set a `timeout` on each client, either in milliseconds or as a duration string such as `'500ms'`, `'5s'`, or `'2m'`. An invalid value fails at startup, with an error that names the option. `0` means no timeout, which is the default.
blocks.text: fetch has no timeout of its own, apart from the 5-minute limits of undici, the HTTP client inside Node.js. Set a timeout on each client, either in milliseconds or as a duration string such as '500ms', '5s', or '2m'. An invalid value fails at startup, with an error that names the option. 0 means no timeout, which is the default.
blocks.zh: `fetch` 没有自己的超时，除了 Node.js 内的 HTTP 客户端 undici 的 5 分钟限制。在每个客户端上设置一个 `timeout`，单位可以是毫秒，也可以是持续时间字符串，如 `'500ms'`、`'5s'` 或 `'2m'`。一个无效的值在启动时失败，会出现命名选项的错误。`0` 表示没有超时，这是默认值。

blocks.md: The timeout applies to **each attempt**, not to the whole call. It covers the attempt's interceptors and reading the response body. For `responseType: 'stream'` and `'response'`, it stops once the headers arrive, so a long download isn't cut off. When it elapses, the attempt fails with an `HttpTimeoutError`, and the request is retried like after any other [transient failure](/application/http-client#retries).
blocks.text: The timeout applies to each attempt, not to the whole call. It covers the attempt's interceptors and reading the response body. For responseType: 'stream' and 'response', it stops once the headers arrive, so a long download isn't cut off. When it elapses, the attempt fails with an HttpTimeoutError, and the request is retried like after any other transient failure.
blocks.zh: 超时适用于**每次尝试**，而不是整个呼叫。它涵盖了企图的拦截器和读取响应体。为了 `responseType: 'stream'` 和 `'response'`，一旦标头到达，它就会停止，因此长时间的下载不会中断。当它过去时，尝试会失败 `HttpTimeoutError`，并像在任何其他请求之后一样重试该请求 [瞬态失效](/application/http-client#retries).

blocks.md: To cancel a request, pass an `AbortSignal` as the `signal` option. It is combined with the timeout. A cancelled request rejects with the signal's `reason`, as `fetch` does, and is never retried, even while it waits between two attempts.
blocks.text: To cancel a request, pass an AbortSignal as the signal option. It is combined with the timeout. A cancelled request rejects with the signal's reason, as fetch does, and is never retried, even while it waits between two attempts.
blocks.zh: 若要取消请求，请传递 `AbortSignal` 作为 `signal` 选择。它与超时相结合。取消的请求被拒绝，信号为 `reason`,作为 `fetch` 即使在两次尝试之间等待，也不会重试。

blocks.md: The deadline rejects with a `DOMException` named `TimeoutError`, which `toHttpException()` maps to `504 Gateway Timeout`, like an `HttpTimeoutError`. To combine it with another signal, use `AbortSignal.any([signal, AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)])`.
