Pass the matching provider to prisma init (e.g., --datasource-provider postgresql), or change the provider field of the datasource block, and set DATABASE_URL in .env. See the connection URL reference for the required format. PostgreSQL groovy datasource db { provider = "postgresql" } bash DATABASE_URL="postgresql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE?schema=SCHEMA" Replace the uppercase placeholders with your database credentials. If you're unsure what to provide for the SCHEMA placeholder, it's most likely the default value public. If you don't have a PostgreSQL server yet, run npx prisma dev to start a local Prisma Postgres database in your terminal. MySQL groovy datasource db { provider = "mysql" } bash DATABASE_URL="mysql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE" Replace the uppercase placeholders with your database credentials. Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL Server groovy datasource db { provider = "sqlserver" } bash DATABASE_URL="sqlserver://HOST:PORT;database=DATABASE;user=USER;password=PASSWORD;encrypt=true" Replace the uppercase placeholders with your database credentials. If you're unsure what to provide for the encrypt option, it's most likely the default value true.
blocks.zh:
使用 PostgreSQL、MySQL 和 SQL 服务器，连接 URL 指向_数据库服务器_。将匹配的提供程序传递给 `prisma init` (e.g., `--datasource-provider postgresql`），或更改 `provider` 的领域 `datasource` 块，并设置 `DATABASE_URL` 在 `.env`.参见 [联系 URL 参考](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/reference/connection-urls) 对于所需的格式。

**邮政 QL**

古怪的
数据源数据库 {
provider = "postgresql"
}
```

巴什
数据库网址=“postgresql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE?模式=SCHEMA"
```

用数据库凭据替换大写占位符。如果您不确定为 `SCHEMA` 占位符，很可能是默认值 `public`.如果您还没有 PostgreSQL 服务器，请运行 `npx prisma dev` 启动本地 Prisma 终端中的 Postgres 数据库。

**MySQL**

古怪的
数据源数据库 {
provider = "mysql"
}
```

巴什
数据库网址="mysql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE"
```

用数据库凭据替换大写占位符。

**微软 SQL 服务器/Azure SQL 服务器**

古怪的
数据源数据库 {
provider = "sqlserver"
}
```

巴什
数据库网址="sqlserver://HOST:PORT;数据库=DATABASE;用户=USER;密码=PASSWORD;加密=真”
```

用数据库凭据替换大写占位符。如果您不确定为 `encrypt` 选项，很可能是默认值 `true`.

blocks.md: [Prisma Migrate](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-migrate/getting-started) generates SQL migration files from the declarative data model in your Prisma schema. These migration files are fully customizable, so you can configure additional features of the underlying database or include additional commands (e.g., for seeding).

blocks.zh: [Prisma Migrate](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-migrate/getting-started) 生成 SQL 从声明性数据模型迁移文件 Prisma 模式。这些迁移文件是完全可定制的，因此您可以配置底层数据库的附加功能或包含附加命令（例如，用于播种）。

blocks.md: This chapter uses two models. Add them to your `schema.prisma` file:
blocks.text: This chapter uses two models. Add them to your schema.prisma file:
blocks.zh: 本章使用了两个模型。将它们添加到您的 `schema.prisma` 文件：

blocks.code:
model User {
  id    Int     @default(autoincrement()) @id
  email String  @unique
  name  String?
  posts Post[]
}

model Post {
  id        Int      @default(autoincrement()) @id
  title     String
  content   String?
  published Boolean? @default(false)
  author    User?    @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])
  authorId  Int?
}

blocks.md: Generate Prisma Client
blocks.text: Generate Prisma Client
blocks.zh: 产生 Prisma 客户

blocks.md: Prisma Client is a type-safe database client that's _generated_ from your Prisma schema. This approach lets Prisma Client expose [CRUD](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/queries/crud) operations that are _tailored_ specifically to your models. Generate the client and its types with the `generate` command:
blocks.text: Prisma Client is a type-safe database client that's _generated_ from your Prisma schema. This approach lets Prisma Client expose CRUD operations that are _tailored_ specifically to your models. Generate the client and its types with the generate command:
blocks.zh: Prisma 客户端是一个类型安全的数据库客户端，它从您的 Prisma 模式。这种方法让 Prisma 客户端暴露 [CRUD](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/queries/crud) 专门为您的模型量身定制的操作。使用 `generate` 命令：

blocks.code: $ npx prisma generate

blocks.md: `prisma migrate dev` doesn't run this command for you. Whenever you change your schema, rerun `prisma generate` to keep the client and its types in sync.
blocks.text: prisma migrate dev doesn't run this command for you. Whenever you change your schema, rerun prisma generate to keep the client and its types in sync.
blocks.zh: `prisma migrate dev` 不为您运行此命令。每当您更改架构时，请重新运行 `prisma generate` 使客户端及其类型保持同步。

blocks.md: The generated `client.ts` file is the entry point of the client. It exports the `PrismaClient` class, a type for each model (e.g., `User` and `Post`), and the `Prisma` namespace, which contains the input types for queries (e.g., `Prisma.UserCreateInput`). Like any other relative import in an ESM project, import it with a `.js` extension (`./generated/prisma/client.js`).

Like any other relative import in an ESM project, import it with a .js extension (./generated/prisma/client.js).

blocks.md: Connection lifecycle
blocks.text: Connection lifecycle
blocks.zh: 连接生命周期

blocks.md: Prisma Client connects lazily, when it sends the first query. Calling `$connect()` in the `onModuleInit()` hook connects during application bootstrap instead, so a misconfigured connection fails at startup rather than on the first request.
blocks.text: Prisma Client connects lazily, when it sends the first query. Calling $connect() in the onModuleInit() hook connects during application bootstrap instead, so a misconfigured connection fails at startup rather than on the first request.
blocks.zh: Prisma 当客户端发送第一个查询时，它会延迟连接。呼叫 `$connect()` 在 `onModuleInit()` 相反，钩子连接是在应用程序引导期间进行的，因此配置错误的连接会在启动时失败，而不是在第一次请求时失败。

blocks.md: Calling `$disconnect()` in the `onModuleDestroy()` hook closes the connection when the application shuts down. It also disposes of the driver adapter, which closes the underlying driver connection (for example, it ends the connection pool that `PrismaPg` creates). Nest calls `onModuleDestroy()` when you call `app.close()`. To also call it when the process receives a termination signal, such as `SIGTERM`, enable shutdown hooks in your `main.ts` file:
blocks.text: Calling $disconnect() in the onModuleDestroy() hook closes the connection when the application shuts down. It also disposes of the driver adapter, which closes the underlying driver connection (for example, it ends the connection pool that PrismaPg creates). Nest calls onModuleDestroy() when you call app.close(). To also call it when the process receives a termination signal, such as SIGTERM, enable shutdown hooks in your main.ts file:
blocks.zh: 在 `onModuleDestroy()` 挂钩中调用 `$disconnect()` 会在应用程序关闭时关闭连接。它还处理驱动程序适配器，该适配器关闭底层驱动程序连接（例如，它结束 `PrismaPg` 创建的连接池）。当您调用 `app.close()` 时，Nest 调用 `onModuleDestroy()`。要在进程接收到终止信号（例如 `SIGTERM`）时调用它，请在 `main.ts` 文件中启用关机挂钩：

blocks.md: See [Application shutdown](/fundamentals/lifecycle-events#application-shutdown) to learn more about shutdown hooks.
blocks.text: See Application shutdown to learn more about shutdown hooks.
blocks.zh: 看 [Application shutdown](/fundamentals/lifecycle-events#application-shutdown) 了解有关关闭挂钩的更多信息。

blocks.md: Prisma ORM 7 doesn't support the `beforeExit` event (`$on('beforeExit', ...)`) that older Prisma integrations used to close the application. Use the Nest lifecycle hooks shown above instead.

blocks.md: Transactions
blocks.text: Transactions
blocks.zh: 交易

blocks.md: Prisma Client offers several ways to run queries in a transaction (see [Transactions and batch queries](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/queries/transactions)):
blocks.text: Prisma Client offers several ways to run queries in a transaction (see Transactions and batch queries):
blocks.zh: Prisma 客户端提供了几种在事务中运行查询的方法（参见 [Transactions and batch queries](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/queries/transactions)）：

blocks.md:
- **Nested writes**, which create or update a record together with related records in a single query, run in a transaction automatically.
- **Sequential operations**: pass an array of queries to `$transaction()`. Prisma runs them in order, in a single transaction, and resolves to an array with their results.
- **Interactive transactions**: pass an async function to `$transaction()`. Prisma commits the transaction when the function resolves and rolls it back when it throws.
blocks.text: Nested writes, which create or update a record together with related records in a single query, run in a transaction automatically. Interactive transactions: pass an async function to $transaction(). Prisma commits the transaction when the function resolves and rolls it back when it throws.
blocks.zh:
- **嵌套写入**在单个查询中创建或更新记录以及相关记录，在事务中自动运行。
- **顺序操作**：将查询数组传递给 `$transaction()`。Prisma 在一个事务中按顺序运行它们，并将它们的结果解析为一个数组。
- **交互式事务**：将异步函数传递给 `$transaction()`。Prisma 在函数解析时提交事务，并在抛出时回滚事务。

chapters.title: MikroORM
chapters.summary: MikroORM is a TypeScript ORM for Node.js based on the Data Mapper, Unit of Work, and Identity Map patterns.

blocks.md: [MikroORM](https://mikro-orm.io) is a TypeScript ORM for Node.js based on the Data Mapper, Unit of Work, and Identity Map patterns. It supports MongoDB, MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Microsoft SQL Server, and Oracle. The `@mikro-orm/nestjs` package integrates it with Nest: it registers the ORM and its `EntityManager` as providers, provides repository injection, creates a request context for every HTTP request, and closes the database connection when the application shuts down.
blocks.text: MikroORM is a TypeScript ORM for Node.js based on the Data Mapper, Unit of Work, and Identity Map patterns. It supports MongoDB, MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Microsoft SQL Server, and Oracle. The @mikro-orm/nestjs package integrates it with Nest: it registers the ORM and its EntityManager as providers, provides repository injection, creates a request context for every HTTP request, and closes the database connection when the application shuts down.
blocks.zh: [MikroORM](https://mikro-orm.io) 是一个 TypeScriptORM 为了 Node.js 基于数据映射器、工作单元和身份映射模式。它支持 MongoDBMySQL、MariaDB、PostgreSQL、SQLite、微软 SQL 服务器和甲骨文。这个 `@mikro-orm/nestjs` 包将其与 Nest：它注册 ORM 及其 `EntityManager` 作为提供程序，提供存储库注入，为每个存储库创建请求上下文 HTTP 请求，并在应用程序关闭时关闭数据库连接。

blocks.md: Load entities automatically
blocks.text: Load entities automatically
blocks.zh: 自动加载实体

blocks.md: Manually adding entities to the `entities` array of the configuration can be tedious. In addition, referencing entities from the root module breaks application domain boundaries and leaks implementation details to other parts of the application. Glob paths solve this issue, but they don't work when you bundle your application (e.g., in a [monorepo](/cli/monorepo)): MikroORM looks up the matching files at runtime, and a bundle doesn't contain them as separate files.

Glob paths solve this issue, but they don't work when you bundle your application (e.g., in a monorepo): MikroORM looks up the matching files at runtime, and a bundle doesn't contain them as separate files.
blocks.zh: 手动将实体添加到 `entities` 配置的数组可能会很乏味。此外，从根模块引用实体会打破应用程序域边界，并将实现细节泄露给应用程序的其他部分。全局路径解决了这个问题，但是当您捆绑应用程序时，它们不起作用（例如，在 [单存储库](/cli/monorepo))：MikroORM 在运行时查找匹配的文件，并且包中不包含它们作为单独的文件。

blocks.md: Request context
blocks.text: Request context
blocks.zh: 请求语境

blocks.md: MikroORM keeps loaded entities in an [identity map](https://mikro-orm.io/docs/identity-map), which must not be shared between concurrent requests. Each request needs its own fork of the `EntityManager`, with a clean identity map. The `MikroOrmModule` handles this for you: it registers a middleware for all routes that runs each HTTP request inside a `RequestContext`. Within that context, the global `EntityManager` that you inject (and every repository that depends on it) transparently delegates to the request's fork.
blocks.text: MikroORM keeps loaded entities in an identity map, which must not be shared between concurrent requests. Each request needs its own fork of the EntityManager, with a clean identity map. The MikroOrmModule handles this for you: it registers a middleware for all routes that runs each HTTP request inside a RequestContext. Within that context, the global EntityManager that you inject (and every repository that depends on it) transparently delegates to the request's fork.
blocks.zh: MikroORM 将加载的实体保留在 [身份映射](https://mikro-orm.io/docs/identity-map)，不得在并发请求之间共享。每个请求都需要自己的分叉 `EntityManager` 有一张干净的身份图。这个 `MikroOrmModule` 为您处理这个问题：它为运行每个路由的所有路由注册一个中间件 HTTP 请求内部 `RequestContext` 在这种情况下，全球 `EntityManager` 您注入的（以及依赖于它的每个存储库）透明地委托给请求的 fork。

blocks.md: Outside of a request context, MikroORM refuses to use the global `EntityManager` for operations that depend on the identity map, such as `find()` or `flush()`, and throws a `ValidationError`. The [next section](/data/mikroorm#request-scoped-handlers-in-queues) shows how to create a context for code that doesn't run as part of an HTTP request.
blocks.text: Outside of a request context, MikroORM refuses to use the global EntityManager for operations that depend on the identity map, such as find() or flush(), and throws a ValidationError. The next section shows how to create a context for code that doesn't run as part of an HTTP request.
blocks.zh: 在请求上下文之外，MikroORM 拒绝使用全局 `EntityManager` 对于依赖于标识映射的操作，例如 `find()` 或者 `flush()`，并抛出一个 `ValidationError`.这 [下一节](/data/mikroorm#request-scoped-handlers-in-queues) 演示如何为不作为代码的一部分运行的代码创建上下文 HTTP 请求。

blocks.md: Transactions
blocks.text: Transactions
blocks.zh: 交易

blocks.md: MikroORM queues all write operations until you call `em.flush()`, which then wraps them in a single transaction. To control the transaction boundaries yourself, for example, to flush several times or to combine the changes with other queries, use the `em.transactional()` method:

blocks.zh: MikroORM 将所有写操作排队，直到您调用 `em.flush()`，然后将它们包装在一个事务中。要自行控制事务边界，例如，要刷新多次或将更改与其他查询合并，请使用 `em.transactional()` 方法：

blocks.md: The callback receives a forked `EntityManager` that runs inside the transaction. When the callback completes, MikroORM flushes the fork and commits the transaction. If the callback throws, MikroORM rolls the transaction back and rethrows the error.
blocks.text: The callback receives a forked EntityManager that runs inside the transaction. When the callback completes, MikroORM flushes the fork and commits the transaction. If the callback throws, MikroORM rolls the transaction back and rethrows the error.
blocks.zh: 回调收到分叉 `EntityManager` 这在交易中运行。当回调完成时，MikroORM 刷新分叉并提交事务。如果回调引发，MikroORM 会回滚事务并重新引发错误。

blocks.md: Alternatively, use the `@Transactional()` decorator, which wraps the decorated `async` method in `em.transactional()`:

blocks.zh: 或者，使用 `@Transactional()` 装饰器，它将装饰的 `async` 方法包装在 `em.transactional()` 中：

blocks.md: Like `@CreateRequestContext()`, the decorator finds the `EntityManager` through the `em` or `orm` property of the class, and falls back to the current context if the class has neither. When called inside another transaction, `em.transactional()` starts a nested transaction (a savepoint), while `@Transactional()` joins the existing transaction by default. See the [MikroORM transactions documentation](https://mikro-orm.io/docs/transactions) for propagation options, isolation levels, and locking.

See the MikroORM transactions documentation for propagation options, isolation levels, and locking.

blocks.md: Serialization
blocks.text: Serialization
blocks.zh: 序列化

blocks.md: MikroORM entities have a `toJSON()` method that applies MikroORM's [serialization rules](https://mikro-orm.io/docs/serializing): it omits hidden properties, applies custom property serializers, and serializes populated relations as nested objects and unpopulated relations as their primary keys. When a route handler returns an entity, Nest converts it to JSON, so these rules apply automatically.
blocks.text: MikroORM entities have a toJSON() method that applies MikroORM's serialization rules: it omits hidden properties, applies custom property serializers, and serializes populated relations as nested objects and unpopulated relations as their primary keys. When a route handler returns an entity, Nest converts it to JSON, so these rules apply automatically.
blocks.zh: MikroORM 实体具有 `toJSON()` 应用 MikroORM 的方法 [序列化规则](https://mikro-orm.io/docs/serializing)：它省略隐藏属性，应用自定义属性序列化程序，并将填充关系序列化为嵌套对象，将未填充关系序列化为其主键。当路由处理程序返回实体时，Nest 将其转换为 JSON，因此这些规则自动应用。

blocks.title: Warning
blocks.md: Don't use [Nest's built-in serializer](/application/serialization) (the `ClassSerializerInterceptor`) with MikroORM entities. It relies on `class-transformer`, which doesn't understand the wrappers that MikroORM uses for relations: it serializes the internal structure of a `Reference`, and traversing a `Collection` leads to infinite recursion (a "Maximum call stack size exceeded" error).

blocks.md: Testing
blocks.text: Testing
blocks.zh: 检测

blocks.md: When unit testing an application, you usually want to avoid a database connection, which keeps test suites independent and fast. However, your classes might depend on repositories and the `EntityManager`. To resolve these classes, provide mock implementations using [custom providers](/fundamentals/custom-providers).

blocks.md: Relations
blocks.text: Relations
blocks.zh: 关系

blocks.md: Relations are associations established between two or more tables. Relations are based on common fields from each table, often involving primary and foreign keys.
blocks.text: Relations are associations established between two or more tables. Relations are based on common fields from each table, often involving primary and foreign keys.
blocks.zh: 关系是两个或多个表之间建立的关联。关系基于每个表中的公共字段，通常涉及主键和外键。

blocks.md: There are three types of relations:
blocks.text: There are three types of relations:
blocks.zh: 有三种类型的关系：

blocks.md:
One-to-one Every row in the primary table has one and only one associated row in the foreign table
One-to-many / Many-to-one Every row in the primary table has one or more related rows in the foreign table
Many-to-many Every row in the primary table has many related rows in the foreign table, and every record in the foreign table has many related rows in the primary table
To define relations in models, use the corresponding **decorators**. For example, to define that each `User` can have multiple photos, use the `@HasMany()` decorator.
blocks.text: To define relations in models, use the corresponding decorators. For example, to define that each User can have multiple photos, use the @HasMany() decorator.

blocks.md: Testing
blocks.text: Testing
blocks.zh: 检测

blocks.md: When it comes to unit testing an application, we usually want to avoid making a database connection, keeping our test suites independent and their execution process as fast as possible. But our classes might depend on models that are pulled from the connection instance. How do we handle that? The solution is to create mock models. In order to achieve that, we set up [custom providers](/fundamentals/custom-providers). Each registered model is automatically represented by a `<ModelName>Model` token, where `ModelName` is the name of your model class.
blocks.text: When it comes to unit testing an application, we usually want to avoid making a database connection, keeping our test suites independent and their execution process as fast as possible. But our classes might depend on models that are pulled from the connection instance. How do we handle that? The solution is to create mock models. In order to achieve that, we set up custom providers. Each registered model is automatically represented by a Model token, where ModelName is the name of your model class.
blocks.zh: 当涉及到对应用程序进行单元测试时，我们通常希望避免建立数据库连接，保持我们的测试套件的独立性，并且它们的执行过程尽可能快。但是我们的类可能依赖于从连接实例中提取的模型。我们如何处理？解决方案是创建模拟模型。为了实现这一点，我们设置了 [定制提供者](/fundamentals/custom-providers)。每个注册的模型都自动由 `<ModelName>Model` 令牌表示，其中 `ModelName` 是模型类的名称。

blocks.zh: 这个 `@nestjs/sequelize` 包暴露了 `getModelToken()` 函数，该函数根据给定的模型返回准备好的令牌。

chapters.title: Caching
chapters.summary: Caching is a straightforward and effective technique for improving your application's performance.

blocks.md: Caching is a straightforward and effective **technique** for improving your application's performance. A cache acts as a temporary storage layer that provides quick access to frequently used data, so you don't have to fetch or compute the same information repeatedly. The result is faster response times and better overall efficiency.
blocks.text: Caching is a straightforward and effective technique for improving your application's performance. A cache acts as a temporary storage layer that provides quick access to frequently used data, so you don't have to fetch or compute the same information repeatedly. The result is faster response times and better overall efficiency.
blocks.zh: 缓存是提高应用程序性能的一种简单有效的**技术**。缓存充当临时存储层，提供对常用数据的快速访问，因此您不必重复获取或计算相同的信息。其结果是更快的响应时间和更好的整体效率。

blocks.code: $ npm install @nestjs/cache-manager cache-manager

Because `cache-manager` uses [Keyv](https://keyv.org/docs/) under the hood, you can switch to a different storage solution, such as Redis, by installing the appropriate package. See [Using alternative Cache stores](/data/caching#using-alternative-cache-stores) below.

blocks.md: Use the `get()` method of the `Cache` instance (from the `cache-manager` package) to retrieve items from the cache. If the item doesn't exist in the cache, `get()` returns `undefined` (`cache-manager` v6 returned `null` instead). Treat both as a cache miss when migrating.

blocks.zh: 使用 `get()` 方法 `Cache` 实例（来自 `cache-manager` 包）从缓存中检索项目。如果该项不存在于缓存中，`get()` 回报 `undefined`(`cache-manager`v6 返回 `null` 相反）。迁移时，将两者都视为缓存未命中。

blocks.code: const value = await this.cacheManager.get('key');

blocks.md: To add an item to the cache, use the `set()` method:
blocks.text: To add an item to the cache, use the set() method:
blocks.zh: 若要将项目添加到缓存，请使用 `set()` 方法：

blocks.code: await this.cacheManager.set('key', 'value');

blocks.title: Note
blocks.md: The default in-memory store keeps a reference to the value instead of a copy: `get()` returns the same object that was passed to `set()`, so changing that object afterwards also changes the cached entry. Treat cached values as read-only, or copy a value before changing it. The Keyv stores in [Using alternative Cache stores](/data/caching#using-alternative-cache-stores) serialize values to JSON instead, so class instances come back as plain objects and `Date` objects come back as strings.

Treat cached values as read-only, or copy a value before changing it. The Keyv stores in Using alternative Cache stores serialize values to JSON instead, so class instances come back as plain objects and Date objects come back as strings.
blocks.zh: 默认的内存存储保留对该值的引用，而不是副本：`get()` 返回传递到的相同对象 `set()`，因此之后更改该对象也会更改缓存条目。将缓存值视为只读值，或在更改值之前复制该值。Keyv 存储在 [Using alternative Cache stores](/data/caching#using-alternative-cache-stores) 将值序列化为 JSON 相反，类实例作为普通对象返回 `Date` 对象以字符串的形式返回。

blocks.md: When the `CacheInterceptor` is bound globally, cache entries are stored under a key that is generated automatically from the request URL. You can override certain cache settings (`@CacheKey()` and `@CacheTTL()`) on a per-method basis to customize the caching strategy for individual controller methods. This is most relevant when using [different cache stores](/data/caching#using-alternative-cache-stores).

You can override certain cache settings (@CacheKey() and @CacheTTL()) on a per-method basis to customize the caching strategy for individual controller methods. This is most relevant when using different cache stores.
blocks.zh: 当 `CacheInterceptor` 被全局绑定时，缓存条目存储在从请求 URL 自动生成的密钥下。您可以在每个方法的基础上覆盖某些缓存设置（`@CacheKey()` 和 `@CacheTTL()`），以自定义各个控制器方法的缓存策略。这在使用 [不同的缓存存储](/data/caching#using-alternative-cache-stores) 时最为相关。

blocks.md: You can also apply the `@CacheTTL()` decorator to a controller to set the TTL for all of its routes. When both controller-level and method-level TTL settings are defined, the method-level setting takes priority.

chapters.title: Authentication
chapters.summary: @nestjs/authentication signs users in and tells the rest of your application who they are.

blocks.md: `@nestjs/authentication` signs users in and tells the rest of your application who they are. It registers a global guard, gives you decorators and an injectable context to read the current user, and ships the parts every sign-in flow needs: server-side sessions, password hashing, email verification and password reset links, TOTP two-factor authentication, magic links, OpenID Connect, access and refresh tokens, and API keys. All of them are built on Node.js built-ins, and they keep their state in your database through a store you write against documented interfaces, with the package's tests to check it. You write what only your application knows: how to load a user, which routes are public, and the endpoints of your sign-in flows.
blocks.text: @nestjs/authentication signs users in and tells the rest of your application who they are. It registers a global guard, gives you decorators and an injectable context to read the current user, and ships the parts every sign-in flow needs: server-side sessions, password hashing, email verification and password reset links, TOTP two-factor authentication, magic links, OpenID Connect, access and refresh tokens, and API keys. All of them are built on Node.js built-ins, and they keep their state in your database through a store you write against documented interfaces, with the package's tests to check it. You write what only your application knows: how to load a user, which routes are public, and the endpoints of your sign-in flows.
blocks.zh: `@nestjs/authentication` 登录用户并告诉应用程序的其余部分他们是谁。它注册了一个全局守卫，为您提供了装饰器和一个可注入的上下文来读取当前用户，并发送了每个登录流程所需的部分：服务器端会话、密码散列、电子邮件验证和密码重置链接，TOTP 双因素身份验证、magic links、OpenID Connect、访问和刷新令牌以及 API 钥匙。所有这些都建立在 Node.js 内置的，它们通过您根据文档接口编写的存储将它们的状态保存在您的数据库中，并通过包的测试来检查它。您编写只有您的应用程序知道的内容：如何加载用户，哪些路由是公共的，以及登录流的端点。

blocks.md: In this tutorial, you'll add sign-in to the API of an online store for cat food and supplies. By the end, it will:
blocks.text: In this tutorial, you'll add sign-in to the API of an online store for cat food and supplies. By the end, it will:
blocks.zh: 在本教程中，您将向 API 猫粮和用品的网上商店。最后，它将：

blocks.md:
- Sign customers in with a password, with Google, or with a link sent by email, and keep the web app signed in with a session cookie.
- Confirm customers' email addresses, and let them reset a forgotten password.
- Give the mobile app short-lived bearer tokens and rotating refresh tokens.
- Offer two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, and require it to change an account's email address.
- Let customers see where they are signed in, and sign out everywhere.
- Limit how fast anyone can guess passwords.
- Keep its sessions, tokens and pending links in PostgreSQL, through Drizzle (or TypeORM).
- Let partners' systems and customers' scripts call the API with keys that customers create and revoke.

blocks.zh:
- 使用密码、Google 或通过电子邮件发送的链接登录客户，并使用会话 cookie 保持 web 应用程序登录。
- 确认客户的电子邮件地址，并让他们重置忘记的密码。
- 给移动应用短期承载令牌和旋转刷新令牌。
- 使用 authenticator 应用程序提供双因素身份验证，并要求它更改帐户的电子邮件地址。
- 让客户看到他们在哪里登录，并在任何地方注销。
- 限制任何人猜测密码的速度。
- 在 PostgreSQL 中保留其会话、令牌和挂起的链接，通过 Drizzle （或 TypeORM).
- 让合作伙伴的系统和客户的脚本调用 API 使用客户创建和撤销的密钥。

blocks.md: Next comes a **credential provider**. A provider looks at an incoming request and returns the user the request proves, or `null` when the request carries no credentials it understands. `SessionCookieProvider` reads the session cookie, loads the session, and passes it to your `validate()` method, which loads the user:

blocks.md: Providers are ordinary `@Injectable()` classes, so they inject whatever they need, and they register themselves: the constructor hands `this` to `AuthenticationRegistry`, the package's list of providers, which the guard consults. The base class receives `SessionService` through property injection, which is why the constructor lists only `UsersRepository` and the registry. Because `validate()` runs on every authenticated request, a deleted user loses access right away, not when the session expires. When the users live in the same database as the sessions, the store can read the user in the same query and hand it to `validate()` as `session.extra`, so a request costs one read instead of two; [Keep sessions and tokens in your database](/security/authentication#keep-sessions-and-tokens-in-your-database) shows how.

blocks.md: `forRoot()` takes values only: lifetimes, secrets, client ids, the pages your emails link to. No class goes in the options. The credential providers, the handlers that later sections add and the [database store](/security/authentication#keep-sessions-and-tokens-in-your-database) are providers of your own modules, and each registers itself from its constructor, so it lives next to whatever it injects, and the module's options stay plain data. Lifetimes are milliseconds, or strings such as `'15m'` and `'14d'`, up to 100 years. `@nestjs/jwt` counts seconds instead, so a numeric lifetime under a minute logs a warning at startup: `3600` is 3.6 seconds here, not an hour.

blocks.md: `PasswordHasher` hashes passwords with scrypt (`crypto.scrypt`, on the libuv threadpool, so it doesn't block the event loop), using OWASP's recommended parameters by default. A service wraps the two things the controller needs:
blocks.text: PasswordHasher hashes passwords with scrypt (crypto.scrypt, on the libuv threadpool, so it doesn't block the event loop), using OWASP's recommended parameters by default. A service wraps the two things the controller needs:
blocks.zh: `PasswordHasher` 使用 scrypt 散列密码（`crypto.scrypt`，在 libuv 线程池上，因此它不会阻塞事件循环），使用 OWASP 默认情况下推荐的参数。服务包装了控制器需要的两件事：

blocks.md:
- `verify()` with no stored hash checks the password against a dummy hash. An unknown email and a wrong password take the same time and produce the same answer, so neither reveals which emails have accounts.
- Passwords are hashed with scrypt from `node:crypto`, at the parameters OWASP recommends (N=2^17, r=8, p=1: about 128 MiB of memory per hash), on the libuv thread pool. That's a memory-hard function, which bcrypt isn't, and it needs no native dependency. Every hash records the parameters it was made with (`$scrypt$ln=17,r=8,p=1$...`). When you raise the cost with the `password` option, `needsRehash()` tells you which stored hashes to upgrade, and the only moment you can do that is while the user signs in. Until then, `verify()` tops up the check of an older, cheaper hash to the work of the new parameters, so it still takes as long as an unknown email. Lowering the cost can't be hidden that way: a hash made with the costlier parameters takes longer to check until it's upgraded. The cost has a ceiling of 1 GiB of memory and 16 times the default work per hash, so with `r` at 8, `logN` stops at 20. Parameters beyond it fail at startup, and a stored hash made with them never verifies.
- `register()` leaves the address unverified. Typing an email into a sign-up form doesn't prove you own it.

blocks.zh:
- `verify()` 在没有存储哈希的情况下，根据虚拟哈希检查密码。一个未知的电子邮件和一个错误的密码需要相同的时间并产生相同的答案，因此都不会透露哪些电子邮件有帐户。
- 在 libuv 线程池上，使用 `node:crypto` 中的 scrypt 散列密码，参数为 OWASP 推荐（N=2^17，r=8，p=1：每个散列大约 128 MiB 内存）。这是一个内存硬函数，而 bcrypt 不是，它不需要本机依赖关系。每个散列记录了它所使用的参数（`$scrypt$ln=17,r=8,p=1$...`）。当您使用 `password` 选项提高成本时，`needsRehash()` 会告诉您要升级哪些存储的哈希值，您唯一可以这样做的时刻是在用户登录时。在此之前，`verify()` 会将旧的、更便宜的散列检查添加到新参数的工作中，因此它仍然需要像未知电子邮件一样长的时间。降低成本不能这样隐藏：用更昂贵的参数制作的散列需要更长的时间来检查，直到它被升级。成本上限为 1 GiB 内存，是每个散列默认工作量的 16 倍，因此 `r` 在 8 时，`logN` 在 20 时停止。超出它的参数在启动时失败，用它们制作的存储哈希永远不会验证。
- `register()` 使地址未经验证。在注册表格中键入电子邮件并不能证明您拥有它。

It creates the session and sets the session cookie on the response itself, on Express and Fastify alike, so the controller needs neither @Req() nor @Res():
blocks.zh: 类上的 `@Public()` 跳过两条路由的身份验证。`SignInService.signIn()` 是第一个因素变成会话的地方：这一步在密码之后调用它，Google 和 magic-link 步骤也会经过它。它创建会话并在响应本身上设置会话 cookie，在 Express 和 Fastify 上都是如此，因此控制器既不需要 `@Req()` 也不需要 `@Res()`：

blocks.md:
- The cookie, `__Host-sid`, holds a random 256-bit token and is `HttpOnly`, `Secure` and `SameSite=Lax`. The `__Host-` prefix tells browsers to accept it only from this host, so a page on another subdomain can't plant a session cookie of its own. Only the token's SHA-256 hash is stored, so a leaked session store can't be replayed as cookies.
- It deletes the session this browser had before, which defends against session fixation.
- It refuses, with a 403, a sign-in posted from another website's page. Otherwise that page could sign the customer's browser in to an account of the attacker's choosing (login CSRF).
- `method` is recorded in the audit trail, which the section on [managing sessions](/security/authentication#let-customers-manage-their-sessions) mentions.
- `mfaRequired` stays `false` until you [add a second factor](/security/authentication#add-two-factor-authentication).

- 饼干， `__Host-sid`，保存一个随机 256 位令牌，并且是 `HttpOnly`, `Secure` 和 `SameSite=Lax`.这 `__Host-` 前缀告诉浏览器只从这个主机接受它，所以另一个子域上的页面不能植入自己的会话 cookie。只有令牌的 SHA-256 哈希被存储，因此泄露的会话存储不能作为 cookies 重播。
- 它会删除此浏览器之前拥有的会话，从而防止会话固定。
- 它以 403 拒绝了另一个网站页面上发布的登录。否则，该页面可能会将客户的浏览器登录到攻击者选择的帐户（登录 CSRF）。
- `method` 记录在审计跟踪中，[管理会话](/security/authentication#let-customers-manage-their-sessions) 提及。
- `mfaRequired` 停留 `false`，直到您 [添加第二个因素](/security/authentication#add-two-factor-authentication)。

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: Chrome, Firefox and curl treat `http://localhost` as a secure origin and accept `Secure` and `__Host-` cookies from it, so you don't need HTTPS during development. On another host over plain HTTP, such as a LAN address, set `cookie.secure` to `false` in the `session` options there; the cookie is then named `sid`.
blocks.text: Chrome, Firefox and curl treat http://localhost as a secure origin and accept Secure and __Host- cookies from it, so you don't need HTTPS during development. On another host over plain HTTP, such as a LAN address, set cookie.secure to false in the session options there; the cookie is then named sid.
blocks.zh: Chrome、Firefox 和 curl treat `http://localhost` 作为安全来源并接受 `Secure` 和 `__Host-` 它的饼干，所以你不需要 HTTPS 开发过程中。在另一台主机上 HTTP，如 a LAN 地址，设置 `cookie.secure` 二 `false` 在 `session` 那里的选项然后将 cookie 命名为 `sid`.

blocks.md: The session cookie is also protected against cross-site request forgery. Besides `SameSite=Lax`, the module ignores the cookie on `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` requests, and on WebSocket handshakes, that come from another origin, judged by the `Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Origin` and `Host` headers, so those requests are anonymous. Clients that send neither `Sec-Fetch-Site` nor `Origin`, such as curl and your mobile app, are unaffected. If your web app runs on another origin than the API, list it in `session.trustedOrigins`.
blocks.text: The session cookie is also protected against cross-site request forgery. Besides SameSite=Lax, the module ignores the cookie on POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE requests, and on WebSocket handshakes, that come from another origin, judged by the Sec-Fetch-Site, Origin and Host headers, so those requests are anonymous. Clients that send neither Sec-Fetch-Site nor Origin, such as curl and your mobile app, are unaffected. If your web app runs on another origin than the API, list it in session.trustedOrigins.
blocks.zh: 会话 cookie 还受到保护，防止跨站点请求伪造。除了 `SameSite=Lax`，模块忽略 cookie `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` 和 `DELETE` 请求和 WebSocket 握手来自另一个来源，由 `Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Origin` 和 `Host` 头，所以这些请求是匿名的。既不发送 `Sec-Fetch-Site` 也不 `Origin`，如 curl 和您的移动应用程序，不受影响。如果您的 web 应用程序运行在除 API，列在 `session.trustedOrigins`.

blocks.md: On Nest 12.1 or later, also call `app.enableCsrfProtection()` in `main.ts`. It makes the same decision for every route, with a 403, including the public ones that have no session to protect yet. Pass it the same `trustedOrigins` as the `session` options.

blocks.md:
- `EmailVerificationService.send()` stores the SHA-256 hash of a random 256-bit token, with the customer's id and the address, and passes the link to your handler. The token itself only exists in the email.
- A link works once, for 24 hours (`emailVerification.ttl`), and only for the address it was sent to. `verify()` returns `null` for an unknown, used or expired token, and for an address that has changed since, and the route answers 400.

- `EmailVerificationService.send()` 存储 SHA-256 随机 256 位令牌的散列，包含客户的 id 和地址，并将链接传递给处理程序。令牌本身只存在于电子邮件中。
- 链接工作一次，持续 24 小时（`emailVerification.ttl`），并且仅限于它被发送到的地址。`verify()` 回报 `null` 对于未知的、使用过的或过期的令牌，以及对于从那时起已经改变的地址，并且路由响应 400。

blocks.md: `findUser()` returns the account's id, its stored address and its stored password hash, `null` for an account without a password. The link goes to that stored address, never to the one typed into the form: a lookup that ignores accents or dots, as MySQL's default collation does, would otherwise mail one customer's link to whoever typed a lookalike address. A link works only while the address and the hash are unchanged, so a password change, by any route, invalidates the links sent before it. Leaving the address or the hash out is an error, which the package logs instead of sending the link.

blocks.md:
- `request()` returns before it looks the address up. Finding the account, storing the token and sending the email happen after the response, so a request for an address nobody registered gets the same 202, in the same time, as a customer's: the route can't tell anyone who has an account. That's why `forgot` doesn't `await` anything. A failure after the response, such as a mail server that is down, is logged.
- A link works once, for an hour (`passwordReset.ttl`), and only while the account still has the address and the password it had when the link was sent.
- `reset()` stores the new password's hash, invalidates the customer's other reset links, and ends every session of the account, and every refresh token once the application [issues them](/security/authentication#issue-tokens-to-the-mobile-app), so whoever knew the old password is signed out everywhere. [API keys](/security/authentication#issue-api-keys-to-partners) live in your own table and stay valid: to cut them off too, revoke them on the `password-reset` event. A password that `PasswordHasher` refuses, empty or over 4 KiB, gets `null` without spending the link, so the customer can try again. With `signIn: true`, it then signs the customer in on this browser through `SignInService`, so a customer with [two-factor authentication](/security/authentication#add-two-factor-authentication) still has to enter a code.
- The link proves the address too, so `reset()` marks it verified, through your `markVerified()`. That also rescues an account that someone else signed up for with the customer's address: the reset replaces the stranger's password and signs them out.

blocks.zh:
- `request()` 在它查找地址之前返回。查找帐户、存储令牌和发送电子邮件发生在响应之后，因此对无人注册的地址的请求会同时获得与客户相同的 202：路由不能告诉任何人谁有帐户。这就是为什么 `forgot` 没有 `await` 任何事情。响应后的故障（如邮件服务器关闭）将被记录。
- 链接工作一次，持续一小时（`passwordReset.ttl`)，并且仅当帐户仍然拥有发送链接时的地址和密码时。
- `reset()` 存储新密码的哈希值，使客户的其他重置链接失效，并在应用程序 [发行它们](/security/authentication#issue-tokens-to-the-mobile-app) 所以任何知道旧密码的人都会被注销。[API 钥匙](/security/authentication#issue-api-keys-to-partners) 住在你自己的表格中并保持有效：要切断它们，请在 `password-reset` 事件。密码 `PasswordHasher` 拒绝，为空或超过 4 KiB，获取 `null` 无需花费链接，因此客户可以再次尝试。和 `signIn: true` 然后，它通过以下方式在此浏览器上登录客户 `SignInService`，所以一个客户 [双因素认证](/security/authentication#add-two-factor-authentication) 仍然需要输入一个代码。
- 该链接也证明了地址，因此 `reset()` 通过您的 `markVerified()` 标记为已验证。这还可以挽救其他人使用客户地址注册的帐户：重置会替换陌生人的密码并注销他们。

blocks.md: Optional: tell the package your user type once, and its types follow. Augment the `AuthenticationTypes` interface of `@nestjs/authentication` in a `declare module` block, with `user: User` (the tutorial keeps it in `src/auth/auth-types.ts`). From then on `@CurrentUser('key')` accepts only keys of `User` and is typed to return that property, and `AuthenticationContext.user` and `.session` are typed too. A `sessionExtra` key types `SessionRecord.extra`, what a session store reads along with each session (exported as `SessionExtra`, `unknown` without the key). It doesn't type the parameter itself: a parameter decorator has no say over the annotation, so `user: User` stays on the parameter. And it is one user type for the whole application, so an application with two kinds of principal keeps the annotations instead. The same interface takes `refreshTokens: false` for an application that [turns refresh tokens off](/security/authentication#issue-tokens-to-the-mobile-app).

blocks.md: `AuthenticationContext` is a singleton. It reads the current request's user from an `AsyncLocalStorage` that the module opens around each handler, so it's correct in anything the handler calls or awaits, however many requests run at the same time. `requireUser()` returns the user, or throws an `AuthenticationError`, which the module answers with a 401 on any transport. Outside a request, in a queue consumer or a cron job, `AuthenticationContext` is empty, and its `run()` method runs a function as a given user. It's also empty in middleware, guards and exception filters, which run outside the handler.

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: HS256 with a shared secret suits an API that both issues and verifies its tokens. If other services verify them too, make the `accessToken` key an ES256 private key: `JwtAuth` then verifies with its public half, and so can they. To accept tokens from another issuer instead, pass `super()` its `jwks` URL, which must be https (plain http only on localhost), or its public `key`, with `issuer` and `audience`: both are required, because an identity provider signs every client's tokens with the same keys. For tokens without an audience, pass `audience: false` and check the claim that names your client in `validate()`. Add `clockTolerance: '30s'` for another issuer's clock. Keys are PEM text or a `KeyObject`; import a JWK with `createPublicKey()` from `node:crypto`, passing the JWK as `key` and `'jwk'` as `format`. An empty `key` or `jwks`, such as an unset environment variable, fails at startup instead of falling back to the `accessToken` options. A service that only verifies tokens can leave `accessToken` out entirely and give `super()` what it verifies with: the shared `key`, or the `jwks` with `issuer` and `audience`.

blocks.md: For each request, the guard asks the providers in ascending `order`, and the first one that returns a user wins. `SessionAuth` registered with the default order, `0`, and `JwtAuth` asked for `1`, so a request with a session cookie is signed in by `SessionAuth`, and a request with a bearer token, which has no cookie, gets `null` from `SessionAuth` and is handled by `JwtAuth`. The order is given at registration rather than left to the order in which Nest constructs the providers: that one follows the module graph, and changes when a provider moves to another module or an import is added. Two providers asking for the same order fail at startup, naming both. A request with neither gets a 401 with `missing_credentials` as its `errorCode`; its `WWW-Authenticate` header lists what the providers accept: `Bearer realm="store"`. A token that fails verification gets a 401 that says why, as RFC 6750 describes, for example `error="invalid_token", error_description="token expired"`. That tells the mobile app to refresh.

blocks.md: `TokenService.issue()` signs an access token with the `accessToken` options, starts a refresh token, and returns both, with `expiresIn`, the access token's lifetime in seconds. Refresh tokens are opaque, and stored as hashes. Each one works once: `refresh()` spends it and returns its successor, with a new access token. The successors of one sign-in form a family. If a spent token comes back, two parties hold it, a thief and the app, so the service revokes the whole family and both have to sign in again. A refresh token that is unknown, expired or reused throws `RefreshTokenError`, an `AuthenticationError`, which the module answers with a 401, so `refresh` needs no error handling of its own.

blocks.md: The `amr` claim records how the user signed in, and [two-factor authentication](/security/authentication#add-two-factor-authentication) relies on it. `issue()` stores the `claims` with the refresh-token family, and `refresh()` puts them into every access token it mints, so refreshed tokens describe the same sign-in. Keep facts that can change, such as roles, out of `claims`: they would stay in the tokens for as long as the family lives. `validate()` loads the current user on every request instead.

blocks.md: The MFA endpoints enroll an authenticator, confirm it, and complete a sign-in:
blocks.text: The MFA endpoints enroll an authenticator, confirm it, and complete a sign-in:
blocks.zh: 这个 MFA 端点注册身份验证器、确认身份验证器并完成登录：

blocks.md:
- `enroll()` stores a new, unconfirmed secret, and returns it with an `otpauth://` URI that the web app shows as a QR code. Once an authenticator is confirmed, `enroll()` refuses to overwrite it and throws `MfaAlreadyEnrolledError`, which the module answers with a 409, `Authenticator already enrolled`. Overwriting it would switch two-factor authentication off until the new one was confirmed.
- `replace` handles a new phone. `enroll()` with `replace: true` stages a second secret, and the current authenticator keeps working until `confirm()` receives a code from the new one. `@Authenticate()` with `mfa: true` makes the route require a verified second factor, so a stolen password alone can't swap in someone else's authenticator.
- `SignInService.confirmMfa()` activates the authenticator once it produces a valid code, so a mistyped secret can't lock anyone out. That code also proves this browser has the authenticator, so the session becomes verified, under a new cookie: the customer can use the routes that require a second factor right away, without signing in again. A confirmation sent with a bearer token, which has no session, only activates the authenticator. The ten recovery codes the route returns are shown only this once, and stored under a slow hash salted with the customer's id, so a copy of the database doesn't reveal them.
- Once an authenticator is confirmed, `SignInService.signIn()` creates **pending** sessions for that user. A pending session isn't signed in anywhere: routes that need a user answer with a 401 and `"errorCode": "mfa_required"`, which tells the web app to ask for a code. That's why `verify` is `@Public()`. `completeMfa()` reads the session from this browser's cookie, checks a code or a recovery code, and rotates the session to a new id with `mfa: 'verified'`, setting the new cookie. A pending session expires after 10 minutes (`mfa.pendingTtl`), not after the 14 days of `session.absoluteTtl`: a pending cookie is half a credential. Verifying the code gives the session its full lifetime.
- `completeMfa()` only acts on the session cookie. A request with a bearer token and no cookie gets a 401.
- Codes are accepted 30 seconds either side of now, and each code works once. After 5 wrong codes in 15 minutes, the account refuses every code, right ones included, until the window passes. Each attempt is counted before it's checked, so sending guesses in parallel doesn't get around the limit.

- `enroll()` 存储一个新的、未经确认的秘密，并以 `otpauth://` URI web 应用程序显示为 QR 代码。一旦验证器被确认， `enroll()` 拒绝覆盖它并抛出 `MfaAlreadyEnrolledError` 模块用 409 回答， `Authenticator already enrolled`.覆盖它将关闭双因素身份验证，直到确认新的身份验证。
- `replace` 处理一部新手机。`enroll()` 和 `replace: true` 阶段第二个秘密，当前身份验证器继续工作，直到 `confirm()` 从新代码接收代码。`@Authenticate()` 和 `mfa: true` 使得路由需要经过验证的第二个因素，因此单独被盗密码不能替换其他人的身份验证器。
- `SignInService.confirmMfa()` 一旦身份验证器生成有效代码，就会激活它，因此输入错误的秘密不能将任何人锁定在外。该代码还证明该浏览器具有身份验证器，因此会话在新的 cookie 下得到验证：客户可以立即使用需要第二个因素的路由，而无需再次登录。使用没有会话的承载令牌发送的确认仅激活身份验证器。路由返回的 10 个恢复代码只显示一次，并存储在带有客户 id 的缓慢散列下，因此数据库的副本不会显示它们。
- 一旦验证器被确认， `SignInService.signIn()` 为该用户创建**挂起**会话。挂起的会话没有在任何地方签名：需要用户使用 401 和 `"errorCode": "mfa_required"`，它告诉 web 应用程序请求代码。这就是为什么 `verify` 是 `@Public()`. `completeMfa()` 从此浏览器的 cookie 中读取会话，检查代码或恢复代码，并将会话旋转到新的 id `mfa: 'verified'`，设置新的 cookie。挂起的会话将在 10 分钟后过期（`mfa.pendingTtl`），而不是在 14 天后 `session.absoluteTtl`：挂起的 cookie 是半个凭据。验证代码赋予会话完整的生命周期。
- `completeMfa()` 仅作用于会话 cookie。具有承载令牌但没有 cookie 的请求得到 401。
- 现在两边都接受代码 30 秒，每个代码工作一次。在 15 分钟内出现 5 个错误代码后，帐户会拒绝每个代码，包括正确的代码，直到窗口通过。每次尝试在被检查之前都会被计算在内，所以并行发送猜测不会绕过限制。

blocks.md: `MfaService.disable()` removes the customer's authenticator and their recovery codes, and emits `mfa-disabled`. Add a route to `MfaController`, with `SessionService` and `TokenService` injected into its constructor:
blocks.text: MfaService.disable() removes the customer's authenticator and their recovery codes, and emits mfa-disabled. Add a route to MfaController, with SessionService and TokenService injected into its constructor:
blocks.zh: `MfaService.disable()` 删除客户的身份验证器及其恢复代码，并发出 `mfa-disabled`。将路由添加到 `MfaController`，并将 `SessionService` 和 `TokenService` 注入到其构造函数中：

blocks.md:
- `@Authenticate()` with `mfa: true` is the minimum: without it, a stolen password alone could turn the second factor off. An API key never passes it. It doesn't prove the customer is at the keyboard now, though: a session stays verified for its whole lifetime. So the route asks for a code as well. `verifyTotp()` resolves `false` for a wrong code, counts toward the same lockout as signing in, and each code works once.
- `disable()` deletes every recovery code along with the authenticator, and drops a replacement staged by `replace` that was never confirmed. Enrolling again starts from scratch, with a new batch of recovery codes.
- `disable()` leaves sessions and tokens alone. The customer's other verified sessions would keep passing `mfa: true` routes, and so would their refresh-token families, whose `amr` keeps `mfa` on every refresh. The route ends them, keeping this browser's session. Access tokens already issued stay valid until they expire. Sent with a bearer token, the request has no session id to keep: every session ends, and `TokenService.revokeAll()` signs that client out too.
- A session still waiting for its second factor can't complete it, since there's no authenticator left to check a code against. `revokeAll()` ends it with the others.
- A customer whose enrollment was never confirmed has no verified session, so this route refuses them. To cancel such an enrollment, call `disable()` from a route without it while `isEnrolled()` is `false`, or call `enroll()` again.

blocks.zh:
- `@Authenticate()` 和 `mfa: true` 是最低限度：没有它，一个被盗的密码就可以关闭第二个因素。安 API 钥匙从不通过。不过，这并不能证明客户现在就在键盘前：一个会话在其整个生命周期内都会受到验证。所以路线也需要一个代码。`verifyTotp()` 决议 `false` 对于错误的代码，计入与登录相同的锁定，每个代码工作一次。
- `disable()` 删除每个恢复代码连同身份验证器，并删除由 `replace` 这从未得到证实。再次注册从头开始，使用新的一批恢复代码。
- `disable()` 不考虑会话和令牌。客户的其他已验证会话将继续通过 `mfa: true` 路线，以及他们的刷新令牌家族，其 `amr` 保持 `mfa` 每次刷新。路由结束它们，保留这个浏览器的会话。已发行的访问令牌在过期前一直有效。与承载令牌一起发送，请求没有要保留的会话 id：每个会话结束，并且 `TokenService.revokeAll()` 把那个客户也签了出去。
- 仍在等待第二个因素的会话无法完成它，因为没有身份验证器可以检查代码。`revokeAll()` 和其他人一起结束。
- 从未确认注册的客户没有经过验证的会话，因此此路由拒绝他们。要取消此类注册，请致电 `disable()` 从没有它的路线 `isEnrolled()` 是 `false`，或致电 `enroll()` 再一次。

blocks.md:
- **Google must have verified it** (`profile.emailVerified`). Otherwise, anyone could create a Google account with a customer's address and take over their account at the store. Returning `null` refuses the sign-in with a 403.
- **The store account must have verified it too** (`existing.emailVerified`). Otherwise, someone could sign up first with a customer's address and a password of their choosing, and keep access once the customer signs in with Google. This is called account pre-hijacking. An account created with a password is unverified until its owner opens the [verification link](/security/authentication#verify-email-addresses), or [resets the password](/security/authentication#reset-forgotten-passwords). Until then, it gets a 403 that asks the customer to sign in with their password and connect Google from their account.

- **谷歌必须验证过**（`profile.emailVerified`）。否则，任何人都可以用顾客的地址创建一个谷歌账户，并在商店接管他们的账户。返回 `null` 拒绝使用 403 登录。
- **商店账户也必须验证过**（`existing.emailVerified`）。否则，有人可以先用客户的地址和他们选择的密码注册，并在客户登录谷歌后保留访问权限。这叫做账户预劫持。使用密码创建的帐户在其所有者打开 [验证链接](/security/authentication#verify-email-addresses) 或 [重置密码](/security/authentication#reset-forgotten-passwords) 之前未经验证。在那之前，它会收到一个 403，要求客户用他们的密码登录，并从他们的帐户连接谷歌。

blocks.md: Connecting Google to an account the customer is signed in to needs no email match at all. The package calls it a link flow: the web app's "Connect Google" button points to `GET /auth/oidc/google/login?link=true`. The package only starts it for a fully signed-in session, and not from another site's page, which gets a 403: a link attaches whatever Google account is signed in on this browser. On the callback it checks that the same session is still live, then calls `resolveUser()` with `linkTo`, the signed-in user. The resolver links the Google account to them, unless it already belongs to another customer. The session stays as it is, and the browser is redirected to `redirectTo`.

On the callback it checks that the same session is still live, then calls resolveUser() with linkTo, the signed-in user. The resolver links the Google account to them, unless it already belongs to another customer. The session stays as it is, and the browser is redirected to redirectTo.
blocks.zh: 将谷歌连接到客户登录的帐户根本不需要电子邮件匹配。该软件包称之为链接流：web 应用程序的“连接谷歌”按钮指向 `GET /auth/oidc/google/login?link=true`。该软件包只在完全登录的会话中启动，而不是从另一个网站的页面启动，这个页面会得到一个 403：一个链接附加在这个浏览器上登录的任何谷歌帐户。在回调时，它会检查同一会话是否仍然有效，然后使用登录用户 `linkTo` 调用 `resolveUser()`。解析器将 Google 帐户链接到他们，除非它已经属于另一个客户。会话保持原样，浏览器被重定向到 `redirectTo`。

blocks.md: The routes are yours, so they sit with your other routes, under your prefixes, versions and throttling. `OidcService.start()` builds the redirect to Google and `finish()` handles the callback; a controller exposes the two:
blocks.text: The routes are yours, so they sit with your other routes, under your prefixes, versions and throttling. OidcService.start() builds the redirect to Google and finish() handles the callback; a controller exposes the two:
blocks.zh: 路由是你的，所以它们和你的其他路由在你的前缀、版本和节流下。`OidcService.start()` 构建重定向到 Google 和 `finish()` 处理回调；控制器公开这两个：

blocks.md:
- `GET /auth/oidc/google/login?redirectTo=/orders` redirects the browser to Google. The web app's "Sign in with Google" button is a plain link to it. `start()` uses the authorization code flow with PKCE, a `state` and a `nonce`. The login transaction is stored server-side under `state`, and the browser gets a secret whose SHA-256 hash is the `state`, in an `HttpOnly` cookie named `__Host-oidc_tx`, for 10 minutes.
- `GET /auth/oidc/google/callback` is where Google sends the browser back. `finish()` checks that the `state` in the query is the hash of the secret in the browser's cookie (so nobody can finish a login they didn't start in this browser, even with a callback URL read from a log or a browser's history), exchanges the code, verifies the ID token's signature against Google's published keys, and checks its issuer, audience, expiry and nonce. If Google can't be reached, or answers with an endpoint that isn't https, the answer is a 502, not a 401. It then calls `resolveUser()`, signs the user in through `SignInService` (so a customer with an authenticator gets a pending session), and returns the redirect to `redirectTo`, or to `/`. Only relative paths are accepted as `redirectTo`, so the login can't be turned into an open redirect.
- Both read the request and set their cookies through Nest's HTTP adapter, and return what `@Redirect()` expects, so the controller works on Express and Fastify alike, without `@Req()` or `@Res()`.

The login transaction is stored server-side under state, and the browser gets a secret whose SHA-256 hash is the state, in an HttpOnly cookie named __Host-oidc_tx, for 10 minutes. GET /auth/oidc/google/callback is where Google sends the browser back. finish() checks that the state in the query is the hash of the secret in the browser's cookie (so nobody can finish a login they didn't start in this browser, even with a callback URL read from a log or a browser's history), exchanges the code, verifies the ID token's signature against Google's published keys, and checks its issuer, audience, expiry and nonce. If Google can't be reached, or answers with an endpoint that isn't https, the answer is a 502, not a 401. It then calls resolveUser(), signs the user in through SignInService (so a customer with an authenticator gets a pending session), and returns the redirect to redirectTo, or to /. Only relative paths are accepted as redirectTo, so the login can't be turned into an open redirect. Both read the request and set their cookies through Nest's HTTP adapter, and return what @Redirect() expects, so the controller works on Express and Fastify alike, without @Req() or @Res().
blocks.zh:
- `GET /auth/oidc/google/login?redirectTo=/orders` 将浏览器重定向到谷歌。网络应用的“用谷歌登录”按钮是一个简单的链接。 `start()` 将授权代码流与 PKCE, a `state` 和一个 `nonce`.登录事务存储在服务器端 `state`，浏览器得到一个秘密 SHA-256 哈希是 `state`,在安 `HttpOnly` cookie 命名 `__Host-oidc_tx`，10 分钟。
- `GET /auth/oidc/google/callback` 是谷歌把浏览器送回去的地方。 `finish()` 检查 `state` 在查询中是浏览器 cookie 中的秘密的散列（所以没有人可以完成他们没有在这个浏览器中开始的登录，即使是回调 URL 从日志或浏览器历史记录中读取），交换代码，验证 ID 令牌的签名对照谷歌发布的密钥，并检查其发行者、受众、到期和随机。如果无法联系到 Google，或者用不是 https 的端点回答，答案是 502，而不是 401。然后它调用 `resolveUser()`，通过 `SignInService` （因此具有身份验证器的客户会得到一个挂起的会话），并将重定向返回到 `redirectTo`,或两个 `/`.仅接受相对路径作为 `redirectTo`，因此登录不能变成打开重定向。
- 两者都读取请求并设置他们的 cookies Nest's HTTP 适配器，并返回什么 `@Redirect()` 期望，因此控制器在 Express 和 Fastify 相似，没有 `@Req()` 或者 `@Res()`.

blocks.md: An application served under several domains, such as one domain per customer, can't name a single callback URL: a login started on one domain must come back to that domain. Pass a function of the request as `callbackUrl` instead. `start()` calls it on the login, and `finish()` calls it again on the callback, so it must return the same URL for both. Compare the host with your own list of domains rather than trusting the header, and register every URL it can return with each provider:

Pass a function of the request as callbackUrl instead. start() calls it on the login, and finish() calls it again on the callback, so it must return the same URL for both. Compare the host with your own list of domains rather than trusting the header, and register every URL it can return with each provider:
blocks.zh: 服务于多个域（例如每个客户一个域）的应用程序不能命名单个回调 URL: 在一个域上启动的登录必须返回到该域。将请求的函数作为 `callbackUrl` 反而。`start()` 在登录时调用它，并且 `finish()` 在回调时再次调用它，因此它必须返回相同的 URL 两者都有。将主机与您自己的域列表进行比较，而不是信任标头，并注册每个 URL 它可以返回每个提供者：

blocks.md: The function can also be `async`, to look the domains up in your database. Whatever it throws is the login's answer, like the 404 above for a domain the application doesn't serve, and a URL that isn't absolute fails the login with an error that names the function. The `__Host-oidc_tx` cookie belongs to the domain that set it, so a login finishes on the domain where it started. If the function ever returned another URL on the callback, the provider would refuse the code, and the callback would get a 401. Behind a proxy that rewrites the host, read the header it forwards instead, such as `X-Forwarded-Host`, and only from a proxy you trust.

Whatever it throws is the login's answer, like the 404 above for a domain the application doesn't serve, and a URL that isn't absolute fails the login with an error that names the function. The __Host-oidc_tx cookie belongs to the domain that set it, so a login finishes on the domain where it started. If the function ever returned another URL on the callback, the provider would refuse the code, and the callback would get a 401. Behind a proxy that rewrites the host, read the header it forwards instead, such as X-Forwarded-Host, and only from a proxy you trust.
blocks.zh: 函数也可以是 `async`，在数据库中查找域。无论它抛出什么都是登录的答案，就像上面针对应用程序不服务的域的 404 一样，以及一个 URL 这不是绝对的，登录失败，并出现命名函数的错误。这个 `__Host-oidc_tx`cookie 属于设置它的域，因此登录在它开始的域上结束。如果函数曾经返回另一个 URL 在回调时，提供程序将拒绝代码，回调将得到 401。在重写主机的代理后面，读取它转发的头，例如 `X-Forwarded-Host` 而且只能通过你信任的代理人。

blocks.md: A magic link signs a customer in from their inbox, without a password. The package creates and checks the links; delivering them is up to you, through a `MagicLinkHandler`. The store emails them like the verification links, with a template and a mail class of their own:
blocks.text: A magic link signs a customer in from their inbox, without a password. The package creates and checks the links; delivering them is up to you, through a MagicLinkHandler. The store emails them like the verification links, with a template and a mail class of their own:
blocks.zh: 一个神奇的链接从客户的收件箱登录，没有密码。包创建并检查链接；交付它们取决于您，通过 `MagicLinkHandler`。商店会像验证链接一样通过电子邮件发送它们，并使用自己的模板和邮件类：

blocks.code:
Sign in to the store

The link works once, for 15 minutes. If you didn't ask for it, ignore this email.

blocks.md: Enable magic links: the handler in `AuthModule`, and the URL the links point to in the options:
blocks.text: Enable magic links: the handler in AuthModule, and the URL the links point to in the options:
blocks.zh: 启用魔法链接：中的处理程序 `AuthModule`，以及 URL 链接指向选项：

blocks.md: `MagicLinkService.create()` makes a random 256-bit token, valid for 15 minutes and usable once, and passes the link to your handler. It stores the SHA-256 hash of the token combined with a secret that only this browser's transaction cookie holds (see below), so a link read from a log, or forwarded, finds nothing, even with a forged cookie. With `bindToBrowser: false`, it stores the hash of the token alone. The token is added to the URL as a `token` query parameter, and your code never sees it otherwise.
blocks.text: MagicLinkService.create() makes a random 256-bit token, valid for 15 minutes and usable once, and passes the link to your handler. It stores the SHA-256 hash of the token combined with a secret that only this browser's transaction cookie holds (see below), so a link read from a log, or forwarded, finds nothing, even with a forged cookie. With bindToBrowser: false, it stores the hash of the token alone. The token is added to the URL as a token query parameter, and your code never sees it otherwise.
blocks.zh: `MagicLinkService.create()` 创建一个随机的 256 位令牌，有效期为 15 分钟，可使用一次，并将链接传递给处理程序。它存储 SHA 令牌的-256 哈希值与只有此浏览器的事务 cookie 持有的秘密相结合（见下文），因此从日志读取或转发的链接不会找到任何内容，即使使用伪造的 cookie。和 `bindToBrowser: false`，它只存储令牌的散列。令牌被添加到 URL 作为一个 `token` 查询参数，否则您的代码永远不会看到它。

blocks.md: Point the link at a page of your web app, not at the API. The page reads the token from its URL and POSTs it back. Email scanners and link previews follow links in emails with GET requests, and would use up the token before the customer clicks. The page must be on the same site as the API: requesting a link sets a cookie that the browser sends back with the token.

Email scanners and link previews follow links in emails with GET requests, and would use up the token before the customer clicks. The page must be on the same site as the API: requesting a link sets a cookie that the browser sends back with the token.
blocks.zh: 将链接指向 web 应用程序的页面，而不是 API.页面从其 URL 然后把它贴回去。电子邮件扫描器和链接预览跟踪电子邮件中的链接 GET 请求，并且会在客户点击之前用完令牌。页面必须与 API：请求链接会设置一个 cookie，浏览器会将该 cookie 连同令牌一起发送回来。

blocks.md:
- The request route answers 202 whether or not the address has an account, and the account is only created once the link is used. A request posted from another site's page gets a 403, as a sign-in does: that page could otherwise set this browser's transaction cookie for a link to its author's address, then get the customer to open it (login CSRF).
- `consume()` burns the token, calls `resolveUser()`, and signs the user in through `SignInService`, which sets the cookie, so two-factor authentication still applies. `resolveUser()` returns the account with its stored `email`, and the link signs the account in only if that is the address the link was sent to, compared trimmed, lowercased and in Unicode NFC. A lookup that ignores accents or dots, as MySQL's default collation does, can't hand one mailbox another customer's account: `consume()` returns `null` instead.
- A link works only in the browser that asked for it. `create()` sets a transaction cookie, `__Host-magic_link_tx`, and `consume()` refuses the token without it, before looking anything up: it throws a `MagicLinkError`, and the module answers it with a 401 whose `error` is `not_this_browser` and whose message tells the customer to open the latest link in the browser they requested it from, or to request a new one here. Otherwise anyone could request a link for their own address and get a customer to open it, which would sign the customer's browser in to the attacker's account (login CSRF). The refused link stays valid in the browser that requested it, and the answer reveals nothing about the token, since a made-up one gets it too. The cookie keeps the last five links the browser requested, so a customer who clicks "Resend" and then opens the first email is still signed in; a link older than those five gets the same 401. So a customer who asks for a link on the laptop and opens the email on the phone is told to open it on the laptop, or to ask for a new link on the phone, which then works there; an application that would rather let the link itself work on the phone sets `bindToBrowser: false` in the `magicLink` options. Unknown, used and expired links, and addresses the handler refuses, get the controller's one generic answer: `consume()` returns `null` for all of them, and only the `magic-link-refused` event says which it was.
- Using the link proves the address, so accounts created by a link are verified. An account created with a password is different while its address is unverified: the link proves who owns the address now, not who chose the password, so the handler refuses it with a 403 rather than handing a pre-hijacked account to its owner. Once the owner has used the [verification link](/security/authentication#verify-email-addresses), or [reset the password](/security/authentication#reset-forgotten-passwords), magic links work for that account too.
- `redirectTo` survives the round trip only if it's a relative path, such as `/orders`.

blocks.zh:
- 请求路由回答 202 地址是否具有帐户，并且仅在使用链路时创建帐户。从另一个站点的页面发布的请求会得到 403，就像登录一样：否则，该页面可以将此浏览器的事务 cookie 设置为指向其作者地址的链接，然后让客户打开它（登录 CSRF).
- `consume()` 烧录令牌，调用 `resolveUser()`，并通过设置 cookie 的 `SignInService` 登录用户，因此双因素身份验证仍然适用。`resolveUser()` 返回帐户及其存储的 `email`，并且只有当链接发送到的地址是该地址时，链接才会在帐户上签名，比较修剪、小写和 UnicodeNFC。像 MySQL 的默认排序一样，忽略重音符号或点的查找不能将一个邮箱交给另一个客户的帐户：`consume()` 返回 `null`。
- 链接仅在请求链接的浏览器中有效。 `create()` 设置事务 cookie， `__Host-magic_link_tx`，和 `consume()` 在查找任何内容之前，拒绝没有它的令牌：它抛出一个 `MagicLinkError`，模块用 401 回答它 `error` 是 `not_this_browser` 其消息告诉客户在他们请求的浏览器中打开最新的链接，或者在这里请求一个新的链接。否则，任何人都可以请求自己地址的链接，并让客户打开它，这将使客户的浏览器登录到攻击者的帐户（登录 CSRF).被拒绝的链接在请求它的浏览器中保持有效，答案不会透露任何关于令牌的信息，因为一个虚构的链接也会得到它。cookie 保留浏览器请求的最后五个链接，因此单击“重新发送”然后打开第一封电子邮件的客户仍然登录；比这五个更老的链接得到相同的 401。因此，一个在笔记本电脑上请求链接并在手机上打开电子邮件的客户被告知在笔记本电脑上打开它，或者在手机上请求一个新的链接，然后在那里工作；一个宁愿让链接本身在手机上工作的应用程序 `bindToBrowser: false` 在 `magicLink` 选项。未知、已使用和过期的链接，并解决处理程序拒绝的问题，获取控制器的一个通用答案： `consume()` 回报 `null` 对他们所有人来说，只有那些 `magic-link-refused` 事件说明是哪一个。
- 使用链接可以证明地址，因此通过链接创建的帐户会得到验证。使用密码创建的帐户在其地址未经验证时是不同的：该链接证明了谁现在拥有该地址，而不是谁选择了该密码，因此处理程序使用 403 拒绝它，而不是将预先被劫持的帐户交给其所有者。一旦所有者使用 [验证链接](/security/authentication#verify-email-addresses), 或 [重置密码](/security/authentication#reset-forgotten-passwords) 魔法链接也适用于该帐户。
- 只有当 `/orders` 是相对路径时，`redirectTo` 才能在往返中存活。

blocks.md:
- Session ids are SHA-256 hashes of the cookie tokens. Showing them to their owner is safe, since a cookie can't be derived from one. `revoke()` takes the user as well as the id, and only ends a session that belongs to them, so an id from the URL can't end another customer's session.
- `sign-out` is `@Public()`, like `verify` in [two-factor authentication](/security/authentication#add-two-factor-authentication), so a customer who never finishes the second factor can still sign out. `signOut()` ends the session in this browser's cookie and clears the cookie. It returns `false` when there was no session, and the route answers 401: a bearer token here signs nothing out.
- `signOutEverywhere()` ends every session and, when the application issues them, every refresh token of the user, and clears this browser's cookie. Access tokens that were already issued stay valid until they expire, which is why they only last 15 minutes.

Access tokens that were already issued stay valid until they expire, which is why they only last 15 minutes.
blocks.zh:
- 会话 ID 是 SHA-256 个 cookie 令牌的散列。把它们展示给它们的主人是安全的，因为饼干不能从饼干中衍生出来。`revoke()` 获取用户和 id，并且只结束属于他们的会话，因此来自 URL 无法结束其他客户的会话。
- `sign-out` 是 `@Public()`,喜欢 `verify` 在 [双因素认证](/security/authentication#add-two-factor-authentication)，所以一个从来没有完成第二个因素的客户仍然可以退出。`signOut()` 结束此浏览器 cookie 中的会话并清除 cookie。它返回 `false` 当没有会话时，路由回答 401：这里的承载令牌没有显示任何内容。
- `signOutEverywhere()` 结束每个会话，当应用程序发布它们时，结束用户的每个刷新令牌，并清除此浏览器的 cookie。已经发放的访问令牌在过期前一直有效，这就是为什么它们只能持续 15 分钟。

blocks.md: The guard is registered in the root module, so it runs before the authentication guard. Global guards run in module order, and the root module comes first. That means guessed bearer tokens count against the limit too, rather than only being rejected with a 401.

blocks.md: `Throttle` and `minutes` are imported from `@nestjs/throttler`. The limits on the routes that send email also keep anyone from flooding a customer's inbox from one address. The two-factor codes don't need a throttle of their own: the package locks an account's codes after 5 failures, from any IP address, route or transport. Neither does `POST /auth/password/reset`: a guessed token costs one lookup, and there are 2^256 of them.

It describes what it stores as six interfaces, `SessionStore`, `RefreshTokenStore`, `MfaStore`, `MagicLinkStore`, `OidcStateStore` and `EmailTokenStore`, and your application implements them with the database access it already has, then registers the implementation.

blocks.md: Start with the tables. They're ordinary Drizzle tables in the application's schema, next to your own:
blocks.text: Start with the tables. They're ordinary Drizzle tables in the application's schema, next to your own:

blocks.md:
- Sessions, tokens and links are stored as SHA-256 hashes of the values in the cookies and emails, TOTP secrets arrive encrypted with your key (see [two-factor authentication](/security/authentication#add-two-factor-authentication)), and recovery codes arrive hashed with scrypt. Nothing in these tables can be replayed.
- `revoked` is on each refresh token rather than in a table of families: a family counts as revoked when any of its tokens is. That covers a token saved after the revocation, by a refresh that lost a race.

Nothing in these tables can be replayed. revoked is on each refresh token rather than in a table of families: a family counts as revoked when any of its tokens is. That covers a token saved after the revocation, by a refresh that lost a race.
blocks.zh:
- 会话、令牌和链接存储为 SHA-Cookie 和电子邮件中的值的 256 个散列，TOTP 机密将与您的密钥一起加密到达（请参阅 [双因素认证](/security/authentication#add-two-factor-authentication)），恢复代码到达时使用 scrypt 散列。这些表格中的任何内容都不能重放。
- `revoked` 在每个刷新令牌上，而不是在族表中：当一个族的任何令牌被撤销时，它被算作被撤销。这涵盖了在撤销后通过输掉比赛的刷新保存的令牌。

blocks.md:
- **One provider or several.** `registerSource()` takes the interfaces by name, so one class can implement all six, as here, or several classes can split them: a `RedisSessionStore` that registers `sessions`, and this class registering the other five. A second store for the same name fails at startup, naming both classes.
- **Some methods must be one statement.** Whatever decides that something works only once is a single conditional statement, never a read followed by a write. `touchSession()` updates only a session that still exists, so a request racing a sign-out can't bring the session back. `deleteSession()` resolves whether it deleted the row, so of two rotations of one session, or a rotation and a sign-out, exactly one wins. `markRefreshTokenUsed()`, `claimTotpStep()` and `consumeRecoveryCode()` count the rows they changed, and the three `consume` methods are a `DELETE … RETURNING`. `saveTotp()` keeps the larger time step with `greatest()`, the one place the store writes SQL by hand. `recordMfaFailure()` inserts first and counts second, outside a transaction, so a burst of parallel guesses can't all see a low count. Each method of the store interfaces gives its rule, and the race it prevents, in its doc comment.
- **Recording activity is best-effort.** If `touchSession()` fails (a lock timeout, a read-only replica), the request and sign-outs still succeed. The session is kept, `lastActiveAt` doesn't move, and the session goes idle at its previous deadline unless a later request records activity. Every failure emits a `session-touch-failed` event; the log gets one warning when failures start, nothing while they continue, and one line with their count on the next successful touch.
- **The tables stay bounded.** Anyone can ask for a magic link or a reset link, so each save deletes what has expired and, past 100,000 pending rows in a table, what expires first. Expired sessions and refresh-token families go as new ones are written.
- **Password reset and email verification keep working unchanged.** Their links are rows in `email_tokens` now, and their mailers still send them through `@nestjs/mail`.
- **Production refuses memory.** With `NODE_ENV` set to `production`, the module won't start while a store that a configured feature uses isn't registered, and names the interfaces to implement. Each feature needs only the stores it uses: `MfaStore` only with `mfa`, and `RefreshTokenStore` only with `accessToken` while refresh tokens are on. [The store contract](/security/authentication#the-store-contract) lists them. A store that none of your configured features uses fails at its first read instead. `allowInMemoryStorage: true` in the module options runs in memory anyway, but then every restart or deploy signs everyone out and forgets enrolled authenticators, and instances don't share any of it.

blocks.zh:
- **一个或多个提供者。**`registerSource()` 按名称获取接口，因此一个类可以实现所有六个接口，如这里所示，或者几个类可以拆分它们：a`RedisSessionStore` 注册 `sessions`，这个班注册了其他五个。同名的第二个存储在启动时失败，命名两个类。
- **有些方法必须是一个语句。**任何决定某个东西只起作用一次的东西都是一个单一的条件语句，而不是读取后写入。`touchSession()` 仅更新仍然存在的会话，因此请求注销无法恢复会话。`deleteSession()` 解决它是否删除了行，因此在一个会话的两次旋转中，或者一次旋转和一次注销中，正好有一个获胜。`markRefreshTokenUsed()`、`claimTotpStep()` 和 `consumeRecoveryCode()` 计算它们更改的行，三个 `consume` 方法是 `DELETE … RETURNING`。`saveTotp()` 与 `greatest()` 保持较大的时间步长，商店手写 SQL 的一个地方。`recordMfaFailure()` 首先插入，然后计数，在事务之外，所以一连串的平行猜测不可能都看到低计数。存储接口的每种方法都在它的 doc 注释中给出了它的规则和它阻止的竞争。
- **尽力记录活动。**如果 `touchSession()` 失败（锁超时，只读副本），请求和注销仍然成功。会话被保留，`lastActiveAt` 不会移动，并且会话在其上一个截止日期空闲，除非稍后的请求记录了活动。每次故障都会发出 `session-touch-failed` 事件；当失败开始时，日志会收到一个警告，当失败继续时什么也没有，还有一行记录下一次成功触摸的计数。
- **表保持有界。**任何人都可以请求魔法链接或重置链接，因此每次保存都会删除已过期的内容，并且当表中超过 100,000 行待处理时，会删除最先过期的内容。过期的会话和刷新令牌族会随着新会话的写入而消失。
- **密码重置和电子邮件验证保持不变。**他们的链接现在是 `email_tokens` 中的行，他们的邮件发送者仍然通过 `@nestjs/mail` 发送。
- **生产拒绝记忆。**`NODE_ENV` 设置为 `production`，当配置的功能使用的存储未注册时，模块不会启动，并命名要实现的接口。每个功能只需要它使用的存储：`MfaStore` 仅与 `mfa`，和 `RefreshTokenStore` 仅与 `accessToken` 当刷新令牌打开时。[The store contract](/security/authentication#the-store-contract) 列出它们。您配置的功能都不使用的存储会在第一次读取时失败。`allowInMemoryStorage: true` 在模块中，选项无论如何都在内存中运行，但是每次重新启动或部署都会注销所有人，并忘记注册的身份验证器，并且实例不会共享任何身份验证器。

blocks.md:
- **Conditional updates and deletes** put the condition in the criteria of `update()` and `delete()`, with `LessThan()`, `IsNull()` and `Or()`, and read `affected`. Never `save()`: it would write back a session that a sign-out just deleted.
- **`saveTotp()`** keeps the larger time step with `GREATEST()` over the conflicting row, which the upsert API can't express, so it is the one statement written as SQL, through `manager.query()`.
- **The `consume` methods** are the delete query builder with `returning('*')`. It returns raw rows under the database's column names, so `deleteReturning()` maps them back to entity properties through the entity metadata.
- **`recordMfaFailure()`** is two statements on `dataSource.manager`, each committed on its own, and `saveRecoveryCodes()` is the one method inside `dataSource.transaction()`.
- **Use it** in place of the Drizzle store: `TypeOrmModule.forRoot(dataSourceOptions)` in `AppModule` instead of `DrizzleModule`, and `TypeOrmAuthenticationStore` in the providers of `AuthModule` instead of `DrizzleAuthenticationStore`. It injects the `DataSource` that `TypeOrmModule` provides.

blocks.zh:
- **条件更新和删除**将条件置于 `update()` 和 `delete()`，与 `LessThan()`, `IsNull()` 和 `Or()`，并阅读 `affected`.从不 `save()`：它将写回注销刚刚删除的会话。
- **`saveTotp()`**在冲突行上与 `GREATEST()` 保持较大的时间步长，upsertAPI 无法表达，因此它是写成 SQL 的唯一语句，直到 `manager.query()`。
- **`consume` 方法**是带有 `returning('*')` 的删除查询生成器。它返回数据库列名下的原始行，因此 `deleteReturning()` 通过实体元数据将它们映射回实体属性。
- **`recordMfaFailure()`**是 `dataSource.manager` 上的两个语句，每个语句都单独提交，`saveRecoveryCodes()` 是 `dataSource.transaction()` 中的一个方法。
- **用它**代替 Drizzle 商店： `TypeOrmModule.forRoot(dataSourceOptions)` 在 `AppModule` 而不是 `DrizzleModule`，和 `TypeOrmAuthenticationStore` 在提供者中 `AuthModule` 而不是 `DrizzleAuthenticationStore`.它注入 `DataSource` 那个 `TypeOrmModule` 提供。

blocks.md: Cat shelters and pet shops restock in bulk from their own inventory systems, and some customers reorder with a script. A script can't fill in a sign-in form, and a refresh token that changes with every use is a poor fit for a nightly job. Give them API keys instead: long-lived secrets that a customer creates in the web app and revokes when they're no longer needed. The script sends its key as a bearer token, and acts as the customer who created it.

blocks.md: The third credential provider extends `ApiKeyProvider`, and does one thing: it finds a key by its id.
blocks.text: The third credential provider extends ApiKeyProvider, and does one thing: it finds a key by its id.
blocks.zh: 第三凭证提供者扩展 `ApiKeyProvider`，并做一件事：它通过它的 id 找到一个密钥。

blocks.md: A key reads `cat_<id>_<secret>`: the prefix, a public id of 16 hex characters, and a secret of 256 random bits. `findKey()` looks up the id, and the provider does the rest. It compares the SHA-256 of the whole key with the stored `hash`, in constant time and with the same work for an id that doesn't exist, and refuses the key from `expiresAt` on. A slow hash such as the passwords' scrypt would add nothing here, since nobody guesses 256 random bits, and it would slow down every request. A wrong, expired or revoked key gets a 401 with `error="invalid_token"`, like a bad access token.

A slow hash such as the passwords' scrypt would add nothing here, since nobody guesses 256 random bits, and it would slow down every request. A wrong, expired or revoked key gets a 401 with error="invalid_token", like a bad access token.
blocks.zh: 密钥读取 `cat_<id>_<secret>`：前缀、16 个十六进制字符的公共 id 和 256 个随机位的秘密。`findKey()` 查找 id，提供程序完成剩下的工作。它比较 SHA-256 整个密钥与存储 `hash`，在恒定时间内，对不存在的 id 进行相同的工作，并拒绝从 `expiresAt` 在。像密码脚本这样的缓慢散列在这里不会添加任何东西，因为没有人猜测 256 位随机位，它会减慢每个请求的速度。错误、过期或被撤销的密钥将获得 401`error="invalid_token"` 就像一个坏的访问令牌。

blocks.md: `JwtAuth` reads the same `Authorization` header. A JWT always contains two dots and a key contains none, so `JwtAuth` leaves keys to `ApiKeyAuth`, whichever of the two runs first. A request without credentials still gets a single challenge, `Bearer realm="store"`, since both providers use the same realm.
blocks.text: JwtAuth reads the same Authorization header. A JWT always contains two dots and a key contains none, so JwtAuth leaves keys to ApiKeyAuth, whichever of the two runs first. A request without credentials still gets a single challenge, Bearer realm="store", since both providers use the same realm.
blocks.zh: `JwtAuth` 读起来一样 `Authorization` 头球。一个 JWT 总是包含两个点，而一个键不包含任何点，因此 `JwtAuth` 将钥匙留给 `ApiKeyAuth`，两者中的哪一个先运行。没有凭据的请求仍然会受到单一质询，`Bearer realm="store"`，因为两个提供程序使用相同的领域。

blocks.text: Now the endpoints that create, list and revoke keys:
