An exception your code throws on purpose, such as a NotFoundException or a failed validation, still shows up in the Errors view, since it is still a failed request, but it doesn't count as a new defect for alerting. Only unhandled failures do: an error whose request answered with a 5xx, or one that failed on an entry point with no HTTP status at all, such as an RPC handler or a gateway message.
blocks.zh: 不是每个错误都是 bug。代码故意抛出的异常，例如 `NotFoundException` 或者一个失败的验证，仍然显示在**错误**视图中，因为它仍然是一个失败的请求，但它不算作警报的新缺陷。只有未处理的故障才会发生：请求回答为 5xx 的错误，或者在入口点上失败，回答为 noHTTP 任何状态，例如 RPC 处理程序或网关消息。

blocks.md: Source context
blocks.text: Source context
blocks.zh: 源上下文

blocks.md: A stack trace from production usually points at compiled output you don't have checked out. With `sourceContext` enabled (the default), the SDK reads the source lines around each in-app frame of a captured error and sends them with it, so the dashboard shows the failing code next to the stack trace:
blocks.text: A stack trace from production usually points at compiled output you don't have checked out. With sourceContext enabled (the default), the SDK reads the source lines around each in-app frame of a captured error and sends them with it, so the dashboard shows the failing code next to the stack trace:
blocks.zh: 生产中的堆栈跟踪通常指向您尚未检出的编译输出。和 `sourceContext` 启用（默认值），SDK 读取捕获的错误的每个应用内帧周围的源代码行，并将其与之一起发送，以便仪表板在堆栈跟踪旁边显示失败代码：

blocks.md: To see your TypeScript rather than the compiled JavaScript, run Node with source map support (`--enable-source-maps`, or `process.setSourceMapsEnabled(true)`), or set `sourceContext.sourceMaps: true` to have the SDK resolve compiled frames itself. Frames inside `node_modules` and Node internals are never read. See [Error source context](/observability/sdk#error-source-context) for every option.
blocks.text: To see your TypeScript rather than the compiled JavaScript, run Node with source map support (--enable-source-maps, or process.setSourceMapsEnabled(true)), or set sourceContext.sourceMaps: true to have the SDK resolve compiled frames itself. Frames inside node_modules and Node internals are never read. See Error source context for every option.
blocks.zh: 看看你的 TypeScript 而不是编译的 JavaScript,运行 Node 具有源映射支持（`--enable-source-maps`, 或 `process.setSourceMapsEnabled(true)`），或设置 `sourceContext.sourceMaps: true` 拥有 SDK 解析编译的帧本身。内部框架 `node_modules` 和 Node 内部文件从不被阅读。看 [Error source context](/observability/sdk#error-source-context) 对于每个选项。

blocks.title: Warning
blocks.md: Source context ships a few lines of your application's source code to your dashboard, stored alongside the error. Set `sourceContext: false` if shipping any source is not acceptable for your codebase.
blocks.text: Source context ships a few lines of your application's source code to your dashboard, stored alongside the error. Set sourceContext: false if shipping any source is not acceptable for your codebase.
blocks.zh: 源代码上下文将应用程序的几行源代码发送到您的仪表板，存储在错误旁边。设置 `sourceContext: false` 如果您的代码库不能接受发送任何源代码。

blocks.md: Handled errors
blocks.text: Handled errors
blocks.zh: 处理错误

blocks.md: An error you catch and recover from never propagates, so it is never captured automatically. When you still want it visible, report it with `captureError()` on `TracerService`:
blocks.text: An error you catch and recover from never propagates, so it is never captured automatically. When you still want it visible, report it with captureError() on TracerService:
blocks.zh: 您捕获并从中恢复的错误永远不会传播，因此它永远不会自动捕获。如果您仍然希望它可见，请在 `TracerService` 上使用 `captureError()` 报告它：

blocks.md: The error is attached to the current trace with the optional tags recorded alongside it, and gets the same source context as any other captured error. See [Capturing handled errors](/observability/manual-instrumentation#capturing-handled-errors).
blocks.text: The error is attached to the current trace with the optional tags recorded alongside it, and gets the same source context as any other captured error. See Capturing handled errors.
blocks.zh: 该错误附加到当前跟踪，并在其旁边记录可选标记，并获得与任何其他捕获的错误相同的源上下文。参见 [Capturing handled errors](/observability/manual-instrumentation#capturing-handled-errors)。

blocks.md: Grouping errors into defects
blocks.text: Grouping errors into defects
blocks.zh: 将错误分组为缺陷

blocks.md: A spike of 3,140 `TypeError`s is one bug, not 3,140. The **Group into defects** switch on the Errors page collapses occurrences with the same exception class and the same normalized stack shape into one **error group**, fingerprinted server-side, regardless of how the message was worded, which line numbers moved, or which deploy produced it.
blocks.text: A spike of 3,140 TypeErrors is one bug, not 3,140. The Group into defects switch on the Errors page collapses occurrences with the same exception class and the same normalized stack shape into one error group, fingerprinted server-side, regardless of how the message was worded, which line numbers moved, or which deploy produced it.
blocks.zh: 峰值 3,140`TypeError`s 是一个 bug，不是 3140。错误页面上的**分组为缺陷**开关会将具有相同异常类和相同规范化堆栈形状的事件折叠成一个**错误组**，即服务器端的指纹识别，无论消息的措辞如何、移动了哪些行号，或者哪个部署生成了它。

blocks.md: A group carries what triage needs, rather than the details of a single occurrence:
blocks.text: A group carries what triage needs, rather than the details of a single occurrence:
blocks.zh: 一个组携带的是分类需求，而不是单个事件的详细信息：

blocks.md:
| Field                    | What it tells you                                                    |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Class and sample message | What the defect is, taken from its first occurrence                  |
| Status                   | Open, Resolved, or Ignored                                           |
| First and last seen      | Whether it's new, ongoing, or has gone away                          |
| Introduced in            | The release the first occurrence ran on, when it reported one        |
| Occurrences              | How often it fired in the selected window, not all time              |
| Issue                    | The [issue](/observability/dashboard#issues) it was promoted to, if any |
blocks.zh:
| 领域 | 它告诉你什么 |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 类和示例消息 | 缺陷是什么，从它第一次出现开始 |
| 状况 | 打开、解决或忽略 |
| 第一次和最后一次见到 | 无论是新的、正在进行的还是已经消失的 |
| 介绍于 | 第一次发生时运行的版本，当它报告一个 |
| 事件 | 它在选定的窗口中触发的频率，而不是一直触发 |
| 发布 | 这个 [发布](/observability/dashboard#issues) 它被提升到，如果有的话 |

blocks.md: **Introduced in** comes from the `serviceVersion` your application reports (a semantic version or a commit hash, passed to [`forRoot()`](/observability/sdk)). Without it, a group can't tell which deploy it arrived with.
blocks.text: Introduced in comes from the serviceVersion your application reports (a semantic version or a commit hash, passed to forRoot()). Without it, a group can't tell which deploy it arrived with.
blocks.zh: **Introduced in**来自应用程序报告的 `serviceVersion`（语义版本或提交散列，传递给 [`forRoot()`](/observability/sdk)）。没有它，一个团队就无法知道它是随哪个部署一起到达的。

blocks.md: The two closed states are deliberately asymmetric. **Resolved** is a claim about the code, so a resolved group reopens as soon as the error recurs; a fix that didn't hold surfaces instead of staying quietly green. **Ignored** is a decision about noise, and stays ignored.
blocks.text: The two closed states are deliberately asymmetric. Resolved is a claim about the code, so a resolved group reopens as soon as the error recurs; a fix that didn't hold surfaces instead of staying quietly green. Ignored is a decision about noise, and stays ignored.
blocks.zh: 这两个封闭状态是故意不对称的。**已解决**是关于代码的声明，因此一旦错误再次出现，已解决的组就会重新打开；一个不能保持表面的修复，而是保持安静的绿色。**忽略**是一个关于噪声的决定，并且保持忽略。

blocks.md: Getting notified
blocks.text: Getting notified
blocks.zh: 收到通知

blocks.md: Every plan, Free included, gets a built-in **new-error email** with no rule to set up: one email per project listing the errors it has never seen before, at most six a day. Each member can switch it off for themselves under **Settings → New error emails**.
blocks.text: Every plan, Free included, gets a built-in new-error email with no rule to set up: one email per project listing the errors it has never seen before, at most six a day. Each member can switch it off for themselves under Settings → New error emails.
blocks.zh: 每个计划，包括免费的，都有一个内置的**新错误电子邮件**，没有规则设置：每个项目一封电子邮件，列出它从未见过的错误，每天最多六封。每个成员都可以在**设置→新建错误电子邮件**下自行关闭。

blocks.md: On paid plans, [alert rules](/observability/dashboard#alerts) go further:
blocks.text: On paid plans, alert rules go further:
blocks.zh: 在付费计划中，[警报规则](/observability/dashboard#alerts) 继续：

blocks.md:
- A **new error groups** rule fires when a defect appears for the first time, for one application or the whole project. It notifies through email, Slack, a webhook, or an in-app notification, or by opening an issue.
- An **error rate** rule watches the share of failed requests for an application, or for one route and method, against a fixed threshold or against its own recent baseline with anomaly detection.
- A **job failure rate** rule does the same for queue consumers and cron runs.
blocks.text: A new error groups rule fires when a defect appears for the first time, for one application or the whole project. It notifies through email, Slack, a webhook, or an in-app notification, or by opening an issue. An error rate rule watches the share of failed requests for an application, or for one route and method, against a fixed threshold or against its own recent baseline with anomaly detection. A job failure rate rule does the same for queue consumers and cron runs.
blocks.zh:
- 当一个应用程序或整个项目首次出现缺陷时，**新错误组**规则将触发。它通过电子邮件、Slack、webhook 或应用内通知，或者通过打开问题进行通知。
- **错误率**规则根据固定阈值或根据其自身最近的异常检测基线监控应用程序或一个路由和方法的失败请求份额。
- **作业失败率**规则对队列使用者和 cron 运行也有同样的作用。

blocks.md: On the higher tiers, an availability [SLO](/observability/dashboard#slos) (the share of requests that finished without an unhandled error) turns the same errors into an error budget with burn-rate alerts.
blocks.text: On the higher tiers, an availability SLO (the share of requests that finished without an unhandled error) turns the same errors into an error budget with burn-rate alerts.
blocks.zh: 在更高层次上，可用性 [SLO](/observability/dashboard#slos)（没有未处理错误完成的请求份额）将相同的错误转换为带有燃烧率警报的错误预算。

blocks.md: From an error to a fix
blocks.text: From an error to a fix
blocks.zh: 从错误到修复

blocks.md: Because each error already carries its stack trace, source lines, trace, and logs, **Copy agent prompt** on its page packages all of it into a self-contained prompt for a coding agent such as Claude Code, Cursor, or any other tool that has your repository open. An agent connected to the [MCP server](/observability/mcp-server) can go further on its own: list error groups with their introducing release, pull recent occurrences with their trace ids, tell whether an error is growing or decaying, and see which users it affected.
blocks.text: Because each error already carries its stack trace, source lines, trace, and logs, Copy agent prompt on its page packages all of it into a self-contained prompt for a coding agent such as Claude Code, Cursor, or any other tool that has your repository open. An agent connected to the MCP server can go further on its own: list error groups with their introducing release, pull recent occurrences with their trace ids, tell whether an error is growing or decaying, and see which users it affected.
blocks.zh: 因为每个错误已经携带了它的堆栈跟踪、源代码行、跟踪和日志，所以其页面上的**复制代理提示**将所有这些打包成一个独立的提示，用于编码代理，如 Claude Code、Cursor 或任何其他打开存储库的工具。连接到 [MCP 服务器](/observability/mcp-server) 可以自行更进一步：列出错误组及其引入版本，用它们的跟踪 id 提取最近发生的事件，判断错误是在增长还是在衰减，并查看它影响了哪些用户。

blocks.md: To track the work, promote an error group into an [issue](/observability/dashboard#issues) in one click; promoting a group that already has an open issue links to it instead of opening a second one. When you mark the issue resolved (optionally naming the release the fix shipped in), the dashboard watches the affected operation against its pre-incident baseline, and either closes the issue once the fix has held or reopens it with the reading that broke it.
blocks.text: To track the work, promote an error group into an issue in one click; promoting a group that already has an open issue links to it instead of opening a second one. When you mark the issue resolved (optionally naming the release the fix shipped in), the dashboard watches the affected operation against its pre-incident baseline, and either closes the issue once the fix has held or reopens it with the reading that broke it.
blocks.zh: 若要跟踪工作，请将错误组提升为 [发布](/observability/dashboard#issues) 只需点击一下；推广一个已经有一个公开问题的组会链接到它，而不是打开第二个。当您标记问题已解决（可选地将修复程序发送到的版本命名为版本）时，仪表板会根据事件前的基线监视受影响的操作，并在修复程序保持不变后关闭问题，或者使用破坏问题的读数重新打开问题。

blocks.md: After a deploy, the **Releases** view compares each `serviceVersion` against the one before it, error rate included, so a regression shows up as a difference between two versions rather than as a bump somewhere in a week-long chart.
blocks.text: After a deploy, the Releases view compares each serviceVersion against the one before it, error rate included, so a regression shows up as a difference between two versions rather than as a bump somewhere in a week-long chart.
blocks.zh: 部署后，**版本**视图会比较每个版本 `serviceVersion` 与之前的版本相比，包括错误率，因此回归显示为两个版本之间的差异，而不是一周图表中某个地方的凸起。

chapters.title: Dashboard
chapters.summary: Once an application is instrumented and sending data, its project dashboard fills in automatically, with no queries to write and no dashboards to build.

blocks.md: Once an application is instrumented and sending data, its project dashboard fills in automatically, with no queries to write and no dashboards to build. This chapter covers what each view shows, how the views relate to each other, and how the features built on top of the telemetry (alerts, SLOs, issues, and the agent handoff) fit together. For the full reference, see the [NestJS Observe documentation](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/documentation 'NestJS Observe documentation').
blocks.text: Once an application is instrumented and sending data, its project dashboard fills in automatically, with no queries to write and no dashboards to build. This chapter covers what each view shows, how the views relate to each other, and how the features built on top of the telemetry (alerts, SLOs, issues, and the agent handoff) fit together. For the full reference, see the NestJS Observe documentation.
blocks.zh: 一旦应用程序被检测并发送数据，它的项目仪表板就会自动填充，无需编写查询，也无需构建仪表板。本章介绍了每个视图显示的内容、视图如何相互关联，以及建立在遥测之上的功能（警报、SLO、问题和代理切换）如何组合在一起。有关完整参考，请参见 [NestJS Observe documentation](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/documentation)。

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: Every view described below can be clicked through in the [live demo](https://www.observe-demo.nestjs.com/dashboard 'NestJS Observe live demo'), which runs the dashboard over a generated dataset from a busy service: realistic request volumes, traces with waterfalls, errors, jobs, and alerts. It needs no account and runs entirely in your browser.
blocks.text: Every view described below can be clicked through in the live demo, which runs the dashboard over a generated dataset from a busy service: realistic request volumes, traces with waterfalls, errors, jobs, and alerts. It needs no account and runs entirely in your browser.
blocks.zh: 下面描述的每个视图都可以在 [现场演示](https://www.observe-demo.nestjs.com/dashboard)，它在繁忙服务生成的数据集上运行仪表板：真实的请求卷、带有瀑布的跟踪、错误、作业和警报。它不需要帐户，完全在你的浏览器中运行。

blocks.md: How the views nest
blocks.text: How the views nest
blocks.zh: 视图如何嵌套

blocks.md: Almost every telemetry view belongs to one of three levels, and you move between them by clicking through:
blocks.text: Almost every telemetry view belongs to one of three levels, and you move between them by clicking through:
blocks.zh: 几乎每个遥测视图都属于三个级别之一，您可以通过单击来在它们之间移动：

blocks.md:
1. **Analytics** - the list view. Every route, job, span, or metric your applications reported in the selected window, aggregated: throughput, latency, failure rate. This is where you notice something.
2. **Operation** - one route (`GET /orders/:id`), one job name, one span name. The same numbers over time, plus the list of individual executions behind them. This is where you confirm the shape of a problem: constant or spiky, everywhere or one release.
3. **Execution** - a single request, a single job run, a single span invocation. Its exact duration, status, user, tags, the error it raised, the waterfall of everything it did, and the logs it wrote. This is where you diagnose.
blocks.text: Analytics - the list view. Every route, job, span, or metric your applications reported in the selected window, aggregated: throughput, latency, failure rate. This is where you notice something. Operation - one route (GET /orders/:id), one job name, one span name. The same numbers over time, plus the list of individual executions behind them. This is where you confirm the shape of a problem: constant or spiky, everywhere or one release. Execution - a single request, a single job run, a single span invocation. Its exact duration, status, user, tags, the error it raised, the waterfall of everything it did, and the logs it wrote. This is where you diagnose.
blocks.zh:
1. **分析**-列表视图。应用程序在选定窗口中报告的每个路由、作业、跨度或指标，汇总：吞吐量、延迟、故障率。这是你注意到一些事情的地方。
2. **操作** - 一条路线（`GET /orders/:id`），一个作业名称，一个跨度名称。随着时间的推移，相同的数字，加上它们背后的个人处决列表。这是确认问题形状的地方：持续或尖峰，无处不在或一个释放。
3. **执行**-单个请求、单个作业运行、单个跨度调用。它的确切持续时间、状态、用户、标签、它引发的错误、它所做的一切的瀑布，以及它写的日志。这是你诊断的地方。

blocks.md: Aggregates tell you _that_ something is wrong and how much it matters; a single execution tells you _why_. Every view shares one control bar (a time range and an optional application filter), and everything on the page follows it.
blocks.text: Aggregates tell you _that_ something is wrong and how much it matters; a single execution tells you _why_. Every view shares one control bar (a time range and an optional application filter), and everything on the page follows it.
blocks.zh: 聚合告诉你，事情出了问题，这有多重要；一次执行就能告诉你为什么。每个视图共享一个控制栏（时间范围和可选的应用程序过滤器），页面上的所有内容都遵循它。

blocks.md: Telemetry views
blocks.text: Telemetry views
blocks.zh: 遥测视图

blocks.md:
| View        | What it shows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Requests** | Every HTTP, GraphQL, gRPC, microservice and WebSocket gateway request, broken down by operation. A request detail page compares the call against the route's own baseline ("slower than 95% of calls") and, when the process was struggling, states by how much host pressure slowed this operation.                                          |
| **Services** | Time spent per NestJS **class and method**, split into own time (with everything awaited subtracted out) and total time. Only instrumented classes appear, so a short list means low coverage, not low traffic.                                                                                               |
| **Errors**   | Every unhandled error, grouped by operation, with the failure leading the page: class, message, stack trace, and source code. The **Group into defects** switch collapses occurrences with the same class and stack shape into one fingerprinted group with first/last seen and the release that introduced it. See [Error monitoring](/observability/error-monitoring). |
| **Jobs**     | Background work - queue consumers, cron runs - with queue wait time, attempt number, and failure reason alongside duration and failure rate.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Spans**    | Analytics over span names across every route that calls them - "how slow is `OrdersService.recalculate` everywhere", rather than "how slow is this one endpoint".                                                                                                                                             |
| **Traces**   | The waterfall for a trace id, across every service that shares it - see [Distributed tracing](/observability/distributed-tracing).                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Users**    | Per-user activity when `getUserId` is configured: failure rate per user, calls grouped into the actions they performed, a replay of each action, and the paths between them. A **Group by customer** switch rolls identities up by email domain.                                                                 |
| **Custom**   | Counters, gauges, and summaries reported through [`TracerService`](/observability/manual-instrumentation#custom-metrics), grouped by metric name and labels.                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Releases** | Each `serviceVersion` compared against the one before it - error rate, latency, and throughput side by side.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Logs**     | Everything your services logged (with `forwardLogs` on), correlated to the traces they ran in. On an execution page, each line is placed on the trace's clock next to the span that was in flight.                                                                                                               |
| **Profiler** | CPU, memory, event loop delay and utilization, and garbage collection per application, with per-instance comparison when an application runs on more than one node. Click a spike on the Memory or Event loop delay chart to see which operations ran at that moment, ranked by deviation from their baseline.   |
blocks.zh:
| 视图 | 它显示了什么 |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **请求** | 每一 HTTP,GraphQL,gRPC，微服务和 WebSocket 网关请求，按操作细分。请求详细信息页面将呼叫与路由自己的基线（“比 95%的呼叫慢”）进行比较，当进程陷入困境时，它会说明主机压力减慢了此操作的程度。 |
| **服务** | 每次花费的时间 NestJS**类和方法**，分为自己的时间（减去所有等待的内容）和总时间。只有工具类出现，因此短列表意味着低覆盖率，而不是低流量。 |
| **错误** | 每个未处理错误，按操作分组，失败位于页面前面：类、消息、堆栈跟踪和源代码。**分组为缺陷**开关将具有相同类别和堆栈形状的事件折叠为一个指纹组，其中包含首次/最后出现的指纹组以及引入它的版本。参见 [Error monitoring](/observability/error-monitoring)。 |
| **职位** | 后台工作-队列使用者，cron 运行-队列等待时间，尝试次数，失败原因以及持续时间和故障率。 |
| **跨度** | 对调用它们的每条路由上的跨度名称进行分析——“有多慢 `OrdersService.recalculate` 无处不在”，而不是“这一个端点有多慢”。 |
| **痕迹** | 跟踪 id 的瀑布，跨越共享它的每个服务-请参阅 [Distributed tracing](/observability/distributed-tracing). |
| **用户** | 每用户活动时 `getUserId` 配置为：每个用户的故障率、按他们执行的操作分组的调用、每个操作的重播以及它们之间的路径。**按客户分组**开关按电子邮件域列出身份。 |
| **定制** | 通过以下方式报告的计数器、仪表和汇总 [`TracerService`](/observability/manual-instrumentation#custom-metrics)，按度量名称和标签分组。 |
| **发布** | 每个 `serviceVersion` 与之前的版本相比——错误率、延迟和吞吐量并列。 |
| **日志** | 您的服务记录的所有内容（使用 `forwardLogs` 上），与他们遇到的痕迹相关。在执行页面上，每条线都放在轨迹的时钟上，紧挨着飞行中的跨度。 |
| **侧写** | CPU、内存、事件循环延迟和利用率以及每个应用程序的垃圾收集，当应用程序在多个节点上运行时，每个实例都会进行比较。单击内存或事件循环延迟图表上的尖峰，以查看当时运行的操作，并按与基线的偏差排序。 |

blocks.md: In a trace's waterfall, a database query or an outbound HTTP request is a row of its own under the method that made it: an icon, the operation (`SELECT orders`, `POST api.stripe.com`), and the statement or URL beside it, visible without hovering. The row's caret opens the full statement laid out by clause, with its placeholders highlighted and a copy button. Values never appear, because the agent removes them before anything is sent. The spans table beneath lists only your application's methods; the agent's query spans are left out and their time counts as the calling method's own, so the table still answers "which of my methods took the time". The **Services** page follows the same rule: drivers (`pg`, `mysql2`, `mongodb`, `http`) are not listed as classes, and a query's wait counts as the own time of the method that ran it.

blocks.md: A project's **Activity → Map** page shows how its applications, queues, and databases talk to each other. Applications and queues run left to right in call order, and the databases and external services each one depends on hang beneath it. A line's thickness and the speed of the traffic along it show volume. Soft red marks an error rate above 1%, full red above 5%, and teal means healthy. Hover over any node to isolate what it touches, and click it for its numbers: for a database, the statements the time went to; for an application, what it calls and what calls it, with a link to its requests.

blocks.md: The map needs no configuration and collects nothing new. Databases and external hosts come from the agent's [query and outbound-HTTP spans](/observability/sdk#database-queries-and-outbound-http), queues from the jobs an application works, and the dashed lines between applications from executions that share a [trace id](/observability/distributed-tracing). Each application gets one database node per driver, so two services on Postgres usually show as two databases, since nothing on the wire says they share one. An external host, by contrast, is a single node shared by every caller, up to the eight busiest per application.

blocks.zh: 地图不需要配置，也不收集任何新的东西。数据库和外部主机来自代理的 [查询和出站-HTTP 跨度](/observability/sdk#database-queries-and-outbound-http)，队列来自应用程序工作的作业，应用程序之间的虚线来自共享 [痕迹 id](/observability/distributed-tracing) 的执行。每个应用程序每个驱动程序都有一个数据库节点，因此 Postgres 上的两个服务通常显示为两个数据库，因为 wire 上没有任何内容表明它们共享一个数据库。相比之下，外部主机是每个呼叫者共享的单个节点，每个应用程序最多有八个最繁忙的节点。

blocks.md: Alerts
blocks.text: Alerts
blocks.zh: 警报

blocks.md: Alerts notify you when your telemetry crosses a threshold you care about, so you don't find out from a customer. A rule watches one metric from one of these families:
blocks.text: Alerts notify you when your telemetry crosses a threshold you care about, so you don't find out from a customer. A rule watches one metric from one of these families:
blocks.zh: 当您的遥测超过您关心的阈值时，警报会通知您，因此您不会从客户那里发现。规则监视以下族中的一个指标：

blocks.md:
| Family  | Metrics                                         | Scoped to                                           |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Request | Error rate, p95 latency, avg latency, throughput | An application, and optionally one route + method   |
| Job     | Job failure rate, job throughput, p95 queue wait | An application, and optionally one job name + queue |
| Absence | Telemetry silence, job silence                  | An application, or one job name + queue             |
| Logs    | Matching log lines                              | A pattern, and optionally levels + logger context   |
| Errors  | New error groups                                | An application, or the whole project                |
| Runtime | Event loop delay, CPU usage, memory usage       | An application (sampled per process)                |
| Custom  | Any custom metric your application reports      | A metric name, and optionally one label             |
| SLO     | SLO burn rate                                   | The SLO itself                                      |
blocks.zh:
| 家庭 | 度量 | 范围 |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| 请求 | 错误率、p95 延迟、平均延迟、吞吐量 | 一个应用程序，以及可选的一个路由+方法 |
| 工作 | 作业失败率、作业吞吐量、p95 队列等待 | 一个应用程序，以及可选的一个作业名称+队列 |
| 缺乏 | 遥测静音，作业静音 | 一个应用程序，或一个作业名称+队列 |
| 日志 | 匹配日志线 | 模式，以及可选的级别+记录器上下文 |
| 错误 | 新错误组 | 应用程序或整个项目 |
| 运行时 | 事件循环延迟，CPU 使用、内存使用 | 应用程序（每个过程采样） |
| 习惯 | 应用程序报告的任何自定义指标 | 度量名称，以及可选的一个标签 |
| SLO | SLO 燃烧速率 | 这个 SLO 本身 |

blocks.md: Every rule runs in one of two modes: a **fixed threshold** ("error rate above 5%"), or **anomaly detection**, which fires when the metric deviates from its own recent baseline by more than a sensitivity you set. Anomaly mode is often the better choice for runtime metrics: a fixed CPU threshold that's right for one service is wrong for the next, but "unlike its own recent baseline" applies to both.
blocks.text: Every rule runs in one of two modes: a fixed threshold ("error rate above 5%"), or anomaly detection, which fires when the metric deviates from its own recent baseline by more than a sensitivity you set. Anomaly mode is often the better choice for runtime metrics: a fixed CPU threshold that's right for one service is wrong for the next, but "unlike its own recent baseline" applies to both.
blocks.zh: 每条规则都以两种模式之一运行：**固定阈值**（“错误率高于 5%”），或**异常检测**，当指标偏离其最近的基线超过您设置的灵敏度时，异常检测将触发。异常模式通常是运行时度量的更好选择：一个固定的 CPU 对一项服务正确的阈值对另一项服务是错误的，但“与其最近的基线不同”适用于两项服务。

blocks.md: Two families depend directly on SDK instrumentation:
blocks.text: Two families depend directly on SDK instrumentation:
blocks.zh: 两个家庭直接依赖 SDK 仪器：

blocks.md:
- **Absence detection.** A **Telemetry silence** rule watches the runtime heartbeat the SDK's `runtimeMetrics` sampler emits even when the application is otherwise idle, and fires once it has been silent longer than a tolerance you set (2 minutes to 7 days). A **Job silence** rule does the same for one named job, e.g., a cron that didn't run. The same mechanism gives you both lightweight uptime monitoring without an external probe and cron monitoring. A scope that has never reported anything doesn't fire: "not yet integrated" isn't "down".
- **Log-pattern alerts** count log lines containing a substring within the window ("alert me when `payment declined` appears more than 10 times in 15 minutes"), and require `forwardLogs` to be on.
blocks.text: Absence detection. A Telemetry silence rule watches the runtime heartbeat the SDK's runtimeMetrics sampler emits even when the application is otherwise idle, and fires once it has been silent longer than a tolerance you set (2 minutes to 7 days). A Job silence rule does the same for one named job, e.g., a cron that didn't run. The same mechanism gives you both lightweight uptime monitoring without an external probe and cron monitoring. A scope that has never reported anything doesn't fire: "not yet integrated" isn't "down". Log-pattern alerts count log lines containing a substring within the window ("alert me when payment declined appears more than 10 times in 15 minutes"), and require forwardLogs to be on.
blocks.zh:
- **缺席检测。**遥测静音**规则监视运行时心跳 SDK 的 `runtimeMetrics` 即使应用程序处于空闲状态，采样器也会发射，一旦沉默的时间超过您设置的公差（2 分钟到 7 天），采样器就会发射。**作业静默**规则对一个命名的作业执行同样的操作，例如，一个没有运行的 cron。相同的机制为您提供了无需外部探针的轻量级正常运行时间监控和 cron 监控。一个从未报告过任何事情的范围不会开火：“尚未集成”不是“关闭”。
- **日志模式警报**计数窗口中包含子字符串的日志行（“当 `payment declined`15 分钟内出现 10 次以上”），并要求 `forwardLogs` 继续。

blocks.md: A rule can notify through **email**, **Slack** (incoming webhook), a generic **webhook**, an **in-app** notification, or by **creating an issue** pre-filled with the rule's severity and scope. Rules can carry a recurring mute schedule for quiet hours, and every state transition (OK → Firing → Resolved) is recorded with per-channel delivery status.
blocks.text: A rule can notify through email, Slack (incoming webhook), a generic webhook, an in-app notification, or by creating an issue pre-filled with the rule's severity and scope. Rules can carry a recurring mute schedule for quiet hours, and every state transition (OK → Firing → Resolved) is recorded with per-channel delivery status.
blocks.zh: 规则可以通过**电子邮件**、**Slack**（传入 webhook）、通用**webhook**、**应用内**通知，或者通过**创建预先填充规则严重性和范围的问题**进行通知。规则可以携带安静时间的重复静音计划，并且每个状态转换（OK→ 发射 → 解决）以每通道传递状态记录。

blocks.md: **New errors.** A *new error groups* rule fires when an error Observe has never seen before appears. It counts unhandled failures only: a group whose first occurrence answered with a 5xx, or failed on an entry point with no HTTP status (an RPC handler, a gateway message). An error your code threw on purpose, such as a `NotFoundException` or a failed validation, still appears in the Errors view but doesn't count as a new bug. Every plan, Free included, also gets a built-in **new-error email** without creating a rule: one email per project listing the new errors, at most six a day. Each person can switch it off under **Settings → New error emails**.
blocks.text: New errors. A *new error groups* rule fires when an error Observe has never seen before appears. It counts unhandled failures only: a group whose first occurrence answered with a 5xx, or failed on an entry point with no HTTP status (an RPC handler, a gateway message). An error your code threw on purpose, such as a NotFoundException or a failed validation, still appears in the Errors view but doesn't count as a new bug. Every plan, Free included, also gets a built-in new-error email without creating a rule: one email per project listing the new errors, at most six a day. Each person can switch it off under Settings → New error emails.
blocks.zh: **新错误。**当出现从未见过的错误观察者时，会触发*新错误组*规则。它只计算未处理的失败：第一次出现的组回答为 5xx，或者在入口点上失败，回答为 noHTTP 状态（安 RPC 处理程序，网关消息）。代码故意抛出的错误，例如 `NotFoundException` 或者失败的验证，仍然出现在错误视图中，但不算作新的错误。每个计划，包括免费的，也会得到一个内置的**新错误电子邮件**，而无需创建规则：每个项目一封列出新错误的电子邮件，每天最多六封。每个人都可以在**设置→新建错误邮件**下关闭它。

blocks.md: SLOs
blocks.text: SLOs
blocks.zh: 斯洛斯

blocks.md: SLOs turn "error rate above 5%" into "we promised 99.9% and we're spending the budget too fast". They're objectives over telemetry you already collect, so no new instrumentation is required. An SLO is built from three layered concepts:
blocks.text: SLOs turn "error rate above 5%" into "we promised 99.9% and we're spending the budget too fast". They're objectives over telemetry you already collect, so no new instrumentation is required. An SLO is built from three layered concepts:
blocks.zh: SLO 将“错误率超过 5%”变成了“我们承诺 99.9%，但我们花费预算太快了”。它们是您已经收集的遥测目标，因此不需要新的仪器。安 SLO 由三个分层概念构建：

blocks.md:
- **SLI (service level indicator)**: a ratio of good events to total events over a window, measuring availability (requests without an unhandled error), latency (requests under a threshold you set), or job success.
- **Objective**: the SLI plus a target percentage (90-99.999%) over a rolling compliance window of 7, 14, 28, or 30 days.
- **Error budget**: how much room you have to miss the target (`1 − target`), and **burn rate**, how fast that budget is being spent. A burn rate of 1.0 spends it exactly on schedule; 14.4 means a 28-day budget would be gone in about two days.
blocks.text: SLI (service level indicator): a ratio of good events to total events over a window, measuring availability (requests without an unhandled error), latency (requests under a threshold you set), or job success. Objective: the SLI plus a target percentage (90-99.999%) over a rolling compliance window of 7, 14, 28, or 30 days. Error budget: how much room you have to miss the target (1 − target), and burn rate, how fast that budget is being spent. A burn rate of 1.0 spends it exactly on schedule; 14.4 means a 28-day budget would be gone in about two days.
blocks.zh:
- **SLI（服务级别指示器）**：一个窗口内良好事件与总事件的比率，衡量可用性（没有未处理错误的请求）、延迟（低于您设置的阈值的请求）或作业成功。
- **目标**：SLI 加上 7、14、28 或 30 天的滚动合规窗口内的目标百分比（90-99.999%）。
- **错误预算**：错过目标的空间有多少（`1 − target`），以及**燃烧率**，即预算花费的速度。1.0 的燃烧率准时消耗；14.4 意味着 28 天的预算将在大约两天内耗尽。

blocks.md: A burn-rate alert is a regular alert rule pointed at an SLO instead of a raw metric. Typical starting points are a fast-burn rule (1 hour window, 14.4×), a slow-burn rule (6 hours, 6×), and a trickle rule (3 days, 1×). A compliance window can't exceed how long your plan retains telemetry.
blocks.text: A burn-rate alert is a regular alert rule pointed at an SLO instead of a raw metric. Typical starting points are a fast-burn rule (1 hour window, 14.4×), a slow-burn rule (6 hours, 6×), and a trickle rule (3 days, 1×). A compliance window can't exceed how long your plan retains telemetry.
blocks.zh: 燃烧率警报是一个常规警报规则，指向 SLO 而不是原始指标。典型的起点是快速燃烧规则（1 小时窗口，14.4×）、缓慢燃烧规则（6 小时，6×）和涓流规则（3 天，1×）。合规窗口不能超过您的计划保留遥测的时间。

blocks.md: Issues
blocks.text: Issues
blocks.zh: 问题

blocks.md: Issues are lightweight, project-scoped tracking for the work that comes out of your telemetry, such as a recurring error worth fixing or a latency regression to investigate. Create them by hand from any execution page, promote an error group into one, or let a firing alert open one automatically. An issue links to the request, error, job, or trace it came from, so anyone opening it later has the telemetry in context, not only a description of it.
blocks.text: Issues are lightweight, project-scoped tracking for the work that comes out of your telemetry, such as a recurring error worth fixing or a latency regression to investigate. Create them by hand from any execution page, promote an error group into one, or let a firing alert open one automatically. An issue links to the request, error, job, or trace it came from, so anyone opening it later has the telemetry in context, not only a description of it.
blocks.zh: 问题是对遥测工作的轻量级、项目范围内的跟踪，例如值得修复的重复错误或需要调查的延迟回归。从任何执行页面手动创建它们，将错误组提升为一个错误组，或者让触发警报自动打开一个错误组。问题与请求、错误、作业或它来自的跟踪相关联，因此以后打开它的任何人都有遥测上下文，而不仅仅是对它的描述。

blocks.md: When you mark an issue resolved and it names something measurable (an operation, an alert rule's scope), the dashboard watches that operation's telemetry against its pre-incident baseline and tells you whether the fix held. It moves the issue to **Verifying**, then either closes it on its own or moves it back to **Open** with the reading that broke it. If you name the release the fix shipped in (your `serviceVersion`), verification waits until that release shows up in telemetry.

It moves the issue to Verifying, then either closes it on its own or moves it back to Open with the reading that broke it. If you name the release the fix shipped in (your serviceVersion), verification waits until that release shows up in telemetry.
blocks.zh: 当您标记一个问题已解决，并且它命名了一些可测量的内容（操作、警报规则的范围）时，仪表板会根据事件发生前的基线监视该操作的遥测，并告诉您修复是否有效。它会将问题移到**验证**，然后要么自动关闭它，要么将它移回**打开**，读数会破坏它。如果您命名发行的修复程序（您的 `serviceVersion`），验证等待，直到该版本出现在遥测中。

blocks.text: A worked path through the dashboard

blocks.md: The views are designed to be used in order. A typical investigation:
blocks.text: The views are designed to be used in order. A typical investigation:
blocks.zh: 视图被设计成按顺序使用。一个典型的调查：

blocks.md:
1. An alert fires, or the **Requests** chart shows p95 climbing.
2. Sort the route list by duration or failure rate to find which operation moved.
3. Open the operation. Is it constant or spiky? Did it start at a deploy? Check **Releases**.
4. Open a single execution from the tail of the distribution, e.g., one the baseline card calls _slower than 95% of calls_.
5. Read the **waterfall**: which span holds the self time?
6. If it failed, read the **error card** - stack trace and the source lines around the throw.
7. Check the **logs** for that trace, hovering lines to line them up with the spans.
8. **Copy the agent prompt** and hand the whole thing to a coding agent, or open an **issue** linked to the execution so whoever picks it up starts where you stopped.

Check the logs for that trace, hovering lines to line them up with the spans. Copy the agent prompt and hand the whole thing to a coding agent, or open an issue linked to the execution so whoever picks it up starts where you stopped.
blocks.zh:
1. 警报触发，或者**请求**图表显示 p95 攀升。
2. 按持续时间或故障率对路由列表进行排序，以查找哪个操作移动了。
3. 打开操作。是恒定的还是尖锐的？是从部署开始的吗？检查**版本**。
4. 从分布的尾部打开单个执行，例如基线卡调用速度低于 95%的调用速度。
5. 阅读**瀑布**：哪个跨度持有自我时间？
6. 如果失败，读取**错误卡**-堆栈跟踪和抛出周围的源代码线。
7. 检查**日志**中的跟踪，悬停线条使它们与跨度对齐。
8. **复制代理提示**并将整个事情交给编码代理，或者打开一个与执行相关的**问题**，这样无论谁拿起它，都会从你停止的地方开始。

chapters.title: MCP server
chapters.summary: NestJS Observe exposes an MCP server, so an MCP-compatible client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, or an agent you wrote yourself) can query your projects directly instead of you copying dashboard data into a prompt.

blocks.md: NestJS Observe exposes an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server, so an MCP-compatible client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, or an agent you wrote yourself) can query your projects directly instead of you copying dashboard data into a prompt. Regressions, slow operations, error groups, traces, jobs, and alerts are available: the same data the dashboard shows, scoped to exactly what you can see.

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: MCP is one of two ways to get telemetry to an agent. The **Copy agent prompt** button (see [Dashboard](/observability/dashboard#handing-a-failure-to-a-coding-agent)) packages one page as text for a single paste. MCP is for an agent that needs to keep asking questions (follow a trace, check whether the error is still firing) without you relaying each answer.

MCP is for an agent that needs to keep asking questions (follow a trace, check whether the error is still firing) without you relaying each answer.
blocks.zh: MCP 是向代理获取遥测信息的两种方法之一。**复制代理提示**按钮（参见 [Dashboard](/observability/dashboard#handing-a-failure-to-a-coding-agent)) 将一个页面打包为单个粘贴的文本。MCP 适用于需要不断提问的代理（跟踪，检查错误是否仍在触发），而无需您转发每个答案。

blocks.md: The endpoint speaks Streamable HTTP at `POST https://<api-host>/mcp`. It's stateless: there's no session to open, nothing to keep alive, and no setup beyond the request itself. The exact host is shown next to your tokens in the dashboard.
blocks.text: The endpoint speaks Streamable HTTP at POST https:// /mcp. It's stateless: there's no session to open, nothing to keep alive, and no setup beyond the request itself. The exact host is shown next to your tokens in the dashboard.
blocks.zh: 端点在 `POST https://<api-host>/mcp` 处调用可流式 HTTP。它是无状态的：没有要打开的会话，没有要保持的东西，除了请求本身之外没有设置。确切的主机显示在仪表板中您的令牌旁边。

blocks.md: Getting a token
blocks.text: Getting a token
blocks.zh: 获取令牌

blocks.md: Personal MCP tokens are minted in the dashboard under **MCP tokens**.
blocks.text: Personal MCP tokens are minted in the dashboard under MCP tokens.
blocks.zh: 个人的 MCP 令牌在仪表板中铸造**下的代币 MCP 代币**。

blocks.md:
- Click **Create token**, give it a name, and optionally set an expiry. A token with no expiry never expires, because MCP clients have no refresh flow.
- The secret (`omcp_...`) is shown **once**, in the response to creating it. Copy it immediately; only its hash is stored, so it cannot be retrieved again. If you lose it, revoke the token and mint another.
- Tokens act **as the user who created them**, with their exact project permissions. There is nothing to scope: if you can see it in the dashboard, the token can read it over MCP, and if you can't, neither can the token.

The secret (omcp_...) is shown once, in the response to creating it. Copy it immediately; only its hash is stored, so it cannot be retrieved again. If you lose it, revoke the token and mint another. Tokens act as the user who created them, with their exact project permissions. There is nothing to scope: if you can see it in the dashboard, the token can read it over MCP, and if you can't, neither can the token.
blocks.zh:
- 单击**创建令牌**，给它命名，并可选地设置到期日。没有过期的令牌永远不会过期，因为 MCP 客户端没有刷新流。
- 秘密（`omcp_...`) 在创建它的响应中显示**一次**。立即复制；只存储它的散列，因此不能再次检索它。如果您丢失了它，请撤销代币并铸造另一个。
- 令牌充当**创建它们的用户**，拥有它们确切的项目权限。没有作用域：如果您可以在仪表板中看到它，令牌可以读取它 MCP 如果你不能，令牌也不能。

blocks.md: Revoking a token from the same page cuts it off immediately. Token management itself is deliberately dashboard-only: an MCP token cannot mint or revoke MCP tokens, so a leaked credential can't extend its own life.

blocks.md: An example investigation
blocks.text: An example investigation

blocks.md: The tools are shaped around investigations rather than endpoints, so each answer carries the key the next question needs. Suppose a deploy went out and something seems wrong:
blocks.text: The tools are shaped around investigations rather than endpoints, so each answer carries the key the next question needs. Suppose a deploy went out and something seems wrong:
blocks.zh: 这些工具是围绕调查而不是终点设计的，因此每个答案都包含了下一个问题所需的关键。假设部署出来了，似乎出了问题：

blocks.md:
1. **"What regressed after the last deploy?"** - `find_regressions` compares error rate and latency either side of each release boundary (your `serviceVersion` values) and names the release that made things worse, along with the operations it degraded.
2. **"Show me that operation."** - `get_operation_details` returns the route's latency and error summary plus recent individual requests, each with a `traceId`.
3. **"What did that request actually do?"** - `get_trace` resolves the trace id into the waterfall: every execution under it, across services, with span trees.
4. **"What did the code say while it happened?"** - `get_trace_logs` returns every log line emitted under the same trace id, in order.

"Show me that operation." - get_operation_details returns the route's latency and error summary plus recent individual requests, each with a traceId. "What did that request actually do?" - get_trace resolves the trace id into the waterfall: every execution under it, across services, with span trees. "What did the code say while it happened?" - get_trace_logs returns every log line emitted under the same trace id, in order.
blocks.zh:
1. **“上次部署后出现了什么倒退？”** -`find_regressions` 比较每个发布边界两侧的错误率和延迟（您的 `serviceVersion` 值）并命名使事情变得更糟的版本，以及它降级的操作。
2. **“向我展示该操作。”** - `get_operation_details` 返回路由的延迟和错误摘要以及最近的单个请求，每个请求都带有 `traceId`。
3. “那个请求到底做了什么？”`get_trace` 将跟踪 id 解析为瀑布：它下面的每个执行，跨服务，使用生成树。
4. **“事情发生时代码是怎么说的？”** -`get_trace_logs` 按顺序返回在相同跟踪 id 下发出的每条日志行。

blocks.md: Errors and background jobs follow the same shape: `list_error_groups` → `get_error_details` → `get_trace`, and `list_jobs` → `get_job_details` → `get_trace`. In every case, start with `list_projects`, since almost every diagnostic tool takes a `projectId`.

blocks.md: Available tools
blocks.text: Available tools
blocks.zh: 可用工具

blocks.md: Almost every tool is read-only; the ones that write are listed under [Setting up a service](/observability/mcp-server#setting-up-a-service). Most diagnostic tools share a scope: a required `projectId`, an optional `applicationId` to narrow to one service, and an optional `timeInterval` look-back window (`1h`, `3h`, `12h`, `1d`, `3d`, `7d`, `30d`), defaulting to `1d`.

Most diagnostic tools share a scope: a required projectId, an optional applicationId to narrow to one service, and an optional timeInterval look-back window (1h, 3h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 7d, 30d), defaulting to 1d.
blocks.zh: 几乎每个工具都是只读的；写的人列在下面 [Setting up a service](/observability/mcp-server#setting-up-a-service) 大多数诊断工具都有一个范围：一个必需的 `projectId`，可选 `applicationId` 缩小到一项服务，以及一项可选服务 `timeInterval` 后视窗（`1h`, `3h`, `12h`, `1d`, `3d`, `7d`, `30d`），默认为 `1d`.

blocks.md:
| Tool                     | What it answers                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list_projects`          | Every project you're a member of, with team and application counts. Start here to resolve project ids.                                            |
| `get_project`            | One project by id, including your access level and subscription state.                                                                            |
| `search`                 | Full-text search over your projects, applications, alert rules, SLOs, and issues.                                                                 |
| `find_regressions`       | Releases that made things worse: error rate and latency before vs. after each release boundary, with the specific operations each one degraded.    |
| `list_slow_operations`   | The slowest HTTP operations in the window, ranked by p95, with volume alongside, so effort goes to what's slow _and_ hot.                          |
| `get_operation_details`  | One route: latency and error summary plus recent individual requests, each with duration, status, and `traceId`.                                  |
| `get_trace`              | A `traceId` resolved to every execution that ran under it - across services, requests, and jobs - each with its span tree.                        |
| `get_trace_logs`         | Every log line emitted under a `traceId`, in order.                                                                                               |
| `list_error_groups`      | Errors grouped by fingerprint, ranked by occurrence count, with class, sample message and stack trace, first/last seen, and the introducing release. |
| `get_error_details`      | Recent occurrences of one error class: per-occurrence message, status, user, and `traceId`, plus a summary.                                       |
| `get_error_trend`        | Whether errors are growing or decaying over the window, already classified as a direction.                                                        |
| `get_affected_users`     | The blast radius of one error class: which end users hit it and how often.                                                                        |
| `list_jobs`              | Background job performance in the window, per job name and queue: volume, duration, and failure counts.                                           |
| `get_job_details`        | One job name on one queue: duration and wait-time summaries plus recent individual executions, each with status and `traceId`.                    |
| `list_issues`, `get_issue` | Issues across your projects, and one issue with its comments and activity.                                                                      |
| `list_slos`              | A project's SLOs with current status and error-budget burn.                                                                                       |
| `list_alert_rules`, `list_alert_events` | Alert rules across every project you can see, and their firing history.                                                            |
blocks.zh:
| 工具 | 它回答什么 |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list_projects` | 您参与的每个项目，包括团队和应用程序。从这里开始解析项目 id。 |
| `get_project` | 每个 id 一个项目，包括您的访问级别和订阅状态。 |
| `search` | 对您的项目、应用程序、警报规则、SLO 和问题进行全文搜索。 |
| `find_regressions` | 让事情变得更糟的版本：每个版本边界之前和之后的错误率和延迟，每个版本的具体操作都降级了。 |
| `list_slow_operations` | 最慢的 HTTP 窗口中的操作，按 p95 排序，旁边还有音量，因此要把精力放在慢速和热的部分。 |
| `get_operation_details` | 一条路径：延迟和错误摘要加上最近的单个请求，每个请求都有持续时间、状态和 `traceId`. |
| `get_trace` | 一个 `traceId` 解决了在它下面运行的每个执行——跨服务、请求和作业——每个执行都有自己的生成树。 |
| `get_trace_logs` | 在 a 下发出的每条日志行 `traceId`，按顺序。 |
| `list_error_groups` | 按指纹分组的错误，按出现次数排序，带有类、示例消息和堆栈跟踪，第一次/最后一次出现，以及介绍版本。 |
| `get_error_details` | 最近出现的一个错误类：每次出现的消息、状态、用户和 `traceId`，外加摘要。 |
| `get_error_trend` | 误差是在窗口上增长还是衰减，已经被归类为一个方向。 |
| `get_affected_users` | 一个错误类的爆炸半径：哪些最终用户击中它以及多久击中一次。 |

chapters.title: OpenTelemetry
chapters.summary: OpenTelemetry is the vendor-neutral standard for traces, metrics, and logs.

blocks.md: [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/ 'OpenTelemetry') is the vendor-neutral standard for traces, metrics, and logs. You instrument an application once, send the data to any compatible backend - Jaeger, Grafana Tempo, or one of the many vendors that accept the OpenTelemetry protocol (OTLP) - and change backends later without touching application code.
blocks.text: OpenTelemetry is the vendor-neutral standard for traces, metrics, and logs. You instrument an application once, send the data to any compatible backend - Jaeger, Grafana Tempo, or one of the many vendors that accept the OpenTelemetry protocol (OTLP) - and change backends later without touching application code.
blocks.zh: [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) 是跟踪、度量和日志的供应商中立标准。您对应用程序进行一次仪器测试，然后将数据发送到任何兼容的后端 - Jaeger、Grafana Tempo 或接受 OpenTelemetry 协议的众多供应商之一（OTLP）-以后无需接触应用程序代码即可更改后端。

blocks.md: For a NestJS backend, we recommend [NestJS Observe](/observability/overview) instead. This page explains why, and when OpenTelemetry is still the better choice. If OpenTelemetry is what you need, the [setup](#zero-code-setup) follows below.
blocks.text: For a NestJS backend, we recommend NestJS Observe instead. This page explains why, and when OpenTelemetry is still the better choice. If OpenTelemetry is what you need, the setup follows below.
blocks.zh: 对于一个 NestJS 后端，我们推荐 [NestJS Observe](/observability/overview) 反而。本页解释了为什么，以及何时 OpenTelemetry 仍然是更好的选择。如果您需要 OpenTelemetry，[设置](#zero-code-setup) 如下。

blocks.md: Why we recommend NestJS Observe
blocks.text: Why we recommend NestJS Observe
blocks.zh: 为什么我们推荐 NestJS 观察

blocks.md: OpenTelemetry instruments a Node.js application from the outside: it patches the HTTP server, the router, and the database driver as they load. It has no way to see the structure Nest builds in between, so a trace reads in the vocabulary of libraries. A slow `POST /orders` in an OpenTelemetry backend looks roughly like this on NestJS 11 (on NestJS 12, the two Nest spans are missing too):
blocks.text: OpenTelemetry instruments a Node.js application from the outside: it patches the HTTP server, the router, and the database driver as they load. It has no way to see the structure Nest builds in between, so a trace reads in the vocabulary of libraries. A slow POST /orders in an OpenTelemetry backend looks roughly like this on NestJS 11 (on NestJS 12, the two Nest spans are missing too):
blocks.zh: 开放式遥测仪器 aNode.js 从外部应用：它修补 HTTP 服务器、路由器和数据库驱动程序加载时。它没有办法看到结构 Nest 介于两者之间，因此跟踪可以读入库的词汇表。缓慢的 `POST /orders` 在 OpenTelemetry 后端中看起来大致是这样的 NestJS11（上 NestJS12、两个 Nest 跨度也丢失了）：

blocks.code:
POST /orders                          1,812 ms
  OrdersController.create             1,806 ms
    create                            1,806 ms
      pg.query SELECT customers          11 ms
      POST api.stripe.com             1,747 ms

blocks.md: NestJS Observe instruments the framework from the inside. Nest hands it every provider it creates, through the `instrument` option of `NestFactory.create()`, so every method call on a controller, service, repository, guard, interceptor, or pipe becomes a span named the way you named it. The same request in Observe:
blocks.text: NestJS Observe instruments the framework from the inside. Nest hands it every provider it creates, through the instrument option of NestFactory.create(), so every method call on a controller, service, repository, guard, interceptor, or pipe becomes a span named the way you named it. The same request in Observe:
blocks.zh: NestJS 从内部观察仪器框架。Nest 将它交给它创建的每个提供程序，通过 `instrument` 选择 `NestFactory.create()` 因此，控制器、服务、存储库、防护、拦截器或管道上的每个方法调用都会变成一个以您命名的方式命名的跨度。观察中的相同请求：

blocks.code:
POST /orders                          1,812 ms
  AuthGuard.canActivate                   3 ms
  OrdersController.create             1,806 ms   self 1 ms
    OrdersService.create              1,805 ms   self 6 ms
      CustomersService.findById          12 ms
        SELECT customers                 11 ms
      PricingService.quote               38 ms
      PaymentsService.charge          1,749 ms
        POST api.stripe.com           1,747 ms

blocks.md: Nobody wrote a span for `PricingService.quote`, and nobody had to guess in advance that it might matter. Because the tree is complete, Observe can compute the time each method spent on its own (self time) instead of leaving it to guesswork. With OpenTelemetry, getting the same tree means adding a span by hand to every method you care about - code that has to be written, kept up to date, and only ever covers what someone already suspected (see [Adding your own spans](#adding-your-own-spans)).
blocks.text: Nobody wrote a span for PricingService.quote, and nobody had to guess in advance that it might matter. Because the tree is complete, Observe can compute the time each method spent on its own (self time) instead of leaving it to guesswork. With OpenTelemetry, getting the same tree means adding a span by hand to every method you care about - code that has to be written, kept up to date, and only ever covers what someone already suspected (see Adding your own spans).
blocks.zh: 没有人为 `PricingService.quote` 写一个跨度，也没有人事先猜到它可能很重要。因为树是完整的，所以 Observe 可以计算每个方法在自己身上花费的时间（自我时间），而不是让它去猜测。使用 OpenTelemetry，获得相同的树意味着手动为您关心的每个方法添加一个跨度——必须编写、保持最新的代码，并且只涵盖某人已经怀疑的内容（参见 [Adding your own spans](#adding-your-own-spans)）。

blocks.md: The difference continues past the request:
blocks.text: The difference continues past the request:
blocks.zh: 在请求之后，差异仍然存在：

blocks.md:
- **Nothing to run.** An OpenTelemetry pipeline is an SDK, an exporter, usually a collector, and a backend to store, query, and alert on the data. Observe is one command, `npx @nestjs/observe link`, which installs the SDK, wires it into your application, and writes the API key into `.env`. There is no collector and no backend to operate.
- **Nest's building blocks, recorded as what they are.** Queue consumers, `@Cron()` handlers, GraphQL resolvers, microservice handlers, and WebSocket gateways are each recorded as their own kind of operation, and a BullMQ or Bull job shares a trace with the request that enqueued it.
- **Kept in step with the framework.** Observe is built and maintained by the Nest team, alongside Nest itself. OpenTelemetry's Nest instrumentation, by contrast, doesn't support NestJS 12 yet (see [What gets recorded for Nest](#what-gets-recorded-for-nest)).
- **More than traces.** Error monitoring with source context, queue wait times and retries, a per-class breakdown of where time goes, runtime profiling, and releases come with the same SDK, on every plan, free tier included.
blocks.text: Nothing to run. An OpenTelemetry pipeline is an SDK, an exporter, usually a collector, and a backend to store, query, and alert on the data. Observe is one command, npx @nestjs/observe link, which installs the SDK, wires it into your application, and writes the API key into .env. There is no collector and no backend to operate. Nest's building blocks, recorded as what they are. Queue consumers, @Cron() handlers, GraphQL resolvers, microservice handlers, and WebSocket gateways are each recorded as their own kind of operation, and a BullMQ or Bull job shares a trace with the request that enqueued it. Kept in step with the framework. Observe is built and maintained by the Nest team, alongside Nest itself. OpenTelemetry's Nest instrumentation, by contrast, doesn't support NestJS 12 yet (see What gets recorded for Nest). More than traces. Error monitoring with source context, queue wait times and retries, a per-class breakdown of where time goes, runtime profiling, and releases come with the same SDK, on every plan, free tier included.
blocks.zh:
- **无需运行。** OpenTelemetry 管道是一个 SDK、一个导出器（通常是一个收集器）和一个用于存储、查询和提醒数据的后端。观察是一个命令 `npx @nestjs/observe link`，它安装 SDK，将其连接到您的应用程序中，并将 API 键写入 `.env`。没有收集器，也没有后端操作。
- **Nest 的构建块，记录为它们是什么。**队列消费者，`@Cron()` 处理程序，GraphQL 解析器、微服务处理程序和 WebSocket 网关都被记录为它们自己的操作类型，BullMQ 或 Bull 作业与排队它的请求共享一个跟踪。
- **与框架保持同步。** Observe 由 Nest 团队，并肩 Nest 本身。开放式遥测 Nest 相比之下，仪器不支持 NestJS 12 还（见 [What gets recorded for Nest](#what-gets-recorded-for-nest)).
- **不仅仅是跟踪。**错误监控与源上下文、队列等待时间和重试、每个类的时间去向细分、运行时概要分析以及相同的发布 SDK，在每个计划上，包括免费层。

blocks.md: Observe is narrower than OpenTelemetry on purpose, and the trade-offs are real:
blocks.text: Observe is narrower than OpenTelemetry on purpose, and the trade-offs are real:
blocks.zh: Observe 故意比 OpenTelemetry 窄，而且权衡是真实的：

blocks.md:
- It's NestJS on Node.js only. A service written in another language in the same request path doesn't appear in the trace, and services are correlated through the `x-request-id` header (see [Distributed tracing](/observability/distributed-tracing)), not the W3C `traceparent` header that OpenTelemetry propagates.
- It's a hosted service, and it doesn't export or ingest OTLP today. Its traces can't be sent to an OpenTelemetry backend, and spans from an OpenTelemetry SDK don't appear in Observe.
- Its library coverage is narrower. Redis and Kafka client calls, for example, aren't recorded as spans.
blocks.text: It's NestJS on Node.js only. A service written in another language in the same request path doesn't appear in the trace, and services are correlated through the x-request-id header (see Distributed tracing), not the W3C traceparent header that OpenTelemetry propagates. It's a hosted service, and it doesn't export or ingest OTLP today. Its traces can't be sent to an OpenTelemetry backend, and spans from an OpenTelemetry SDK don't appear in Observe. Its library coverage is narrower. Redis and Kafka client calls, for example, aren't recorded as spans.
blocks.zh:
- 是 NestJS 在 Node.js 只有。在同一请求路径中用另一种语言编写的服务不会出现在跟踪中，服务通过 `x-request-id` 标题（参见 [Distributed tracing](/observability/distributed-tracing)），而不是 W3C`traceparent`OpenTelemetry 传播的标题。
- 这是一个托管服务，它不导出或接收 OTLP 当今。它的跟踪不能发送到 OpenTelemetry 后端，而是从 OpenTelemetry 跨越 SDK 不要出现在观察中。
- 它的图书馆覆盖范围较窄。Redis 和 Kafka 例如，客户端呼叫不会记录为跨度。

blocks.md: So choose OpenTelemetry when vendor neutrality, keeping telemetry on your own infrastructure, or one trace across services written in several languages is a hard requirement. For everything else on a NestJS backend - and especially if you have no tracing today because nobody had the week to build a pipeline - start with [NestJS Observe](/observability/overview).
blocks.text: So choose OpenTelemetry when vendor neutrality, keeping telemetry on your own infrastructure, or one trace across services written in several languages is a hard requirement. For everything else on a NestJS backend - and especially if you have no tracing today because nobody had the week to build a pipeline - start with NestJS Observe.
blocks.zh: 因此，当供应商中立、将遥测保留在您自己的基础架构上或跨用多种语言编写的服务的一个跟踪是一个硬性要求时，请选择 OpenTelemetry。对于 NestJS 后端上的其他所有内容——尤其是如果您今天没有跟踪，因为没有人有一周的时间来构建管道——从 [NestJS Observe](/observability/overview) 开始。

blocks.md: The two can be installed in the same application, but both hook the database drivers, so try the combination in a staging environment first. They don't share a trace. For a longer discussion of this trade-off, see [NestJS and OpenTelemetry: why we instrument the framework instead](https://dev.to/nestjs/nestjs-and-opentelemetry-why-we-instrument-the-framework-instead-50i6).

blocks.zh: 两者可以安装在同一个应用程序中，但两者都挂钩数据库驱动程序，因此请先在暂存环境中尝试组合。他们没有共同点。有关这种权衡的更多讨论，请参见 [NestJS and OpenTelemetry: why we instrument the framework instead](https://dev.to/nestjs/nestjs-and-opentelemetry-why-we-instrument-the-framework-instead-50i6)。

blocks.text: Zero-code setup

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: Much of OpenTelemetry's Node.js documentation assumes the compiled application runs as CommonJS. Applications generated by `nest new` on Nest 12 are ES modules, which need an extra loader flag. Both variants are shown below.
blocks.text: Much of OpenTelemetry's Node.js documentation assumes the compiled application runs as CommonJS. Applications generated by nest new on Nest 12 are ES modules, which need an extra loader flag. Both variants are shown below.
blocks.zh: OpenTelemetry 的大部分 Node.js 文档假设编译后的应用程序作为 CommonJS 运行。生成的应用程序 `nest new` 在 Nest12 是 ES 模块，需要一个额外的加载程序标志。两种变体如下所示。

blocks.md: The quickest way to get traces out of a Nest application is OpenTelemetry's zero-code instrumentation. Install the API and the auto-instrumentations bundle:
blocks.text: The quickest way to get traces out of a Nest application is OpenTelemetry's zero-code instrumentation. Install the API and the auto-instrumentations bundle:
blocks.zh: 提取痕迹的最快方法 Nest 应用是 OpenTelemetry 的零代码仪器。安装 API 以及自动仪表包：

blocks.code: $ npm i --save @opentelemetry/api @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node

blocks.md: The instrumentation has to be loaded before Nest and the libraries it patches, so it goes on the `node` command line rather than into `main.ts`. For a CommonJS build:
blocks.text: The instrumentation has to be loaded before Nest and the libraries it patches, so it goes on the node command line rather than into main.ts. For a CommonJS build:
blocks.zh: 仪器必须在 Nest 和它修补的库之前加载，因此它在 `node` 命令行上运行，而不是进入 `main.ts`。对于 CommonJS 构建：

blocks.code:
$ OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=orders-api \
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 \
  node --require @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node/register dist/main.js

blocks.md: For an ES module build, OpenTelemetry's loader hook is required as well:
blocks.text: For an ES module build, OpenTelemetry's loader hook is required as well:
blocks.zh: 对于一个 ES 模块构建，还需要 OpenTelemetry 的加载器挂钩：

blocks.code:
$ OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=orders-api \
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 \
  node --experimental-loader=@opentelemetry/instrumentation/hook.mjs \
  --import @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node/register dist/main.js

blocks.md: If your platform starts the process for you and you can't change the command, put the same flags in the `NODE_OPTIONS` environment variable.
blocks.text: If your platform starts the process for you and you can't change the command, put the same flags in the NODE_OPTIONS environment variable.
blocks.zh: 如果您的平台为您启动了该过程，而您无法更改命令，请将相同的标志放入 `NODE_OPTIONS` 环境变量。

blocks.md: Spans are sent over OTLP to the endpoint you configure. To look at them locally, Jaeger runs in a single container and accepts OTLP on port 4318:
blocks.text: Spans are sent over OTLP to the endpoint you configure. To look at them locally, Jaeger runs in a single container and accepts OTLP on port 4318:
blocks.zh: 跨度被发送 OTLP 到您配置的端点。要在本地查看它们，Jaeger 在一个容器中运行并接受 OTLP 端口 4318：

blocks.code: $ docker run --rm -p 16686:16686 -p 4318:4318 jaegertracing/jaeger

blocks.md: Open `http://localhost:16686`, send a request to your application, and the trace appears under the service name you set.
blocks.text: Open http://localhost:16686, send a request to your application, and the trace appears under the service name you set.
blocks.zh: 打开 `http://localhost:16686`，向您的应用程序发送请求，跟踪将显示在您设置的服务名称下。

blocks.md: Configuring the SDK in code
blocks.text: Configuring the SDK in code
blocks.zh: 配置 SDK 在代码中

blocks.md: To choose the exporter, sampler, or instrumentations yourself, start the SDK from a file of your own instead of the `register` entry point:
blocks.text: To choose the exporter, sampler, or instrumentations yourself, start the SDK from a file of your own instead of the register entry point:
blocks.zh: 要自行选择导出器、采样器或仪器，请启动 SDK 从您自己的文件而不是 `register` 入口点：

blocks.code: $ npm i --save @opentelemetry/api @opentelemetry/sdk-node @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http

blocks.md: `OTLPTraceExporter` reads its endpoint from `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` and defaults to `http://localhost:4318`. Load the file before anything else, the same way as the zero-code entry point:
blocks.text: OTLPTraceExporter reads its endpoint from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and defaults to http://localhost:4318. Load the file before anything else, the same way as the zero-code entry point:
blocks.zh: `OTLPTraceExporter` 从 `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` 读取其端点，并默认为 `http://localhost:4318`。先加载文件，方法与零代码入口点相同：

blocks.code:
# CommonJS
$ node --require ./dist/instrumentation.js dist/main.js

# ES modules
$ node --experimental-loader=@opentelemetry/instrumentation/hook.mjs \
  --import ./dist/instrumentation.js dist/main.js

blocks.md: In a CommonJS build you can instead import the file on the very first line of `main.ts`, before `@nestjs/core` and your `AppModule`. In an ES module build that isn't enough, because the loader hook has to be registered on the command line.
blocks.text: In a CommonJS build you can instead import the file on the very first line of main.ts, before @nestjs/core and your AppModule. In an ES module build that isn't enough, because the loader hook has to be registered on the command line.
blocks.zh: 在 CommonJS 版本中，您可以在 `main.ts` 的第一行导入文件，在 `@nestjs/core` 和 `AppModule` 之前。在 ES 模块构建中，这是不够的，因为加载程序钩子必须在命令行上注册。

blocks.md: The SDK exports spans in batches. To send the last batch when the application stops, call `otelSdk.shutdown()` once Nest has finished shutting down, for example from an `onApplicationShutdown()` hook with [shutdown hooks](/fundamentals/lifecycle-events#application-shutdown) enabled.
blocks.text: The SDK exports spans in batches. To send the last batch when the application stops, call otelSdk.shutdown() once Nest has finished shutting down, for example from an onApplicationShutdown() hook with shutdown hooks enabled.
blocks.zh: 这个 SDK 批量出口跨越。若要在应用程序停止时发送最后一批，请调用 `otelSdk.shutdown()` 一次 Nest 已完成关闭，例如从 `onApplicationShutdown()` 挂钩 [关闭挂钩](/fundamentals/lifecycle-events#application-shutdown) 已启用。

blocks.md: What gets recorded for Nest
blocks.text: What gets recorded for Nest
blocks.zh: 记录什么 Nest

blocks.md: The auto-instrumentations bundle records incoming and outgoing HTTP requests (including `fetch`), Express, and the common database drivers such as `pg`, `mysql2`, `mongodb`, and Mongoose. ORMs built on those drivers, such as TypeORM, MikroORM, and Drizzle, show up through the queries they run.

chapters.title: Resilience
chapters.summary: Sooner or later, every application that calls another system meets one that is slow or down.

blocks.md: Sooner or later, every application that calls another system meets one that is slow or down. Without a plan, a slow dependency ties up your request handlers, your clients wait until their own timeouts fire, and retries from every layer pile even more load onto the service that is already struggling.
blocks.text: Sooner or later, every application that calls another system meets one that is slow or down. Without a plan, a slow dependency ties up your request handlers, your clients wait until their own timeouts fire, and retries from every layer pile even more load onto the service that is already struggling.
blocks.zh: 迟早，每个调用另一个系统的应用程序都会遇到一个变慢或停机的应用程序。如果没有计划，缓慢的依赖会束缚您的请求处理程序，您的客户端会等到他们自己的超时触发，并且每一层的重试都会给已经陷入困境的服务带来更多的负载。

blocks.md: `@nestjs/resilience` gives you the usual tools as decorators: **retry**, **timeout**, **circuit breaker**, **bulkhead** and **fallback**. They apply to your application's **entrypoints**, which are controllers, GraphQL resolvers, microservice message handlers and WebSocket gateways. For code inside services, the same settings are available as policy objects. A single global interceptor applies the decorators, so they behave the same on every transport, and each failure becomes that transport's native error. Over HTTP, for example, a timeout answers `504 Gateway Timeout` and an open breaker answers `503 Service Unavailable` with a `Retry-After` header.
blocks.text: @nestjs/resilience gives you the usual tools as decorators: retry, timeout, circuit breaker, bulkhead and fallback. They apply to your application's entrypoints, which are controllers, GraphQL resolvers, microservice message handlers and WebSocket gateways. For code inside services, the same settings are available as policy objects. A single global interceptor applies the decorators, so they behave the same on every transport, and each failure becomes that transport's native error. Over HTTP, for example, a timeout answers 504 Gateway Timeout and an open breaker answers 503 Service Unavailable with a Retry-After header.
blocks.zh: `@nestjs/resilience` 给你常用的装饰工具：**重试**，**超时**，**断路器**，**隔板**和**回退**。它们应用于应用程序的**入口点**，即控制器，GraphQL 解析器、微服务消息处理程序和 WebSocket 网关。对于服务内部的代码，相同的设置可用作策略对象。单个全局拦截器应用装饰器，因此它们在每个传输上的行为都是相同的，每个失败都成为该传输的本地错误。超过 HTTP，例如，超时响应 `504 Gateway Timeout` 一个打开的断路器回答 `503 Service Unavailable` 用一个 `Retry-After` 头球。

blocks.md: In this tutorial you'll harden the order API of an online store for cat food and supplies. Checkout asks the shipping carrier for quotes, and the carrier's quotes API is slow at the best of times and occasionally down. By the end, a slow carrier costs checkout about three seconds at most. Once the carrier is known to be down, checkout stops waiting for it altogether: customers see flat-rate shipping instead of an error, and a background job stops calling the carrier until it recovers.

blocks.md:
- `defaults` fills in the fields of any stage that a decorator or preset turns on. Defaults never turn a stage on themselves. Here, a retry first waits a random time between 0 and 200 ms (the `delay`), then up to 400 ms, doubling each time up to 2 s (the `maxDelay`). A bare `@Timeout()` means 5 seconds.
- `presets` holds named sets of stages, usually one per dependency. The `carrier` preset gives each attempt 2 seconds, makes at most 2 attempts, and adds a circuit breaker. That breaker is **shared under the name `carrier`** by every route, handler and service that uses the preset. The carrier is one dependency, so it gets one breaker.

blocks.md: When an attempt runs out of time, three things happen:
blocks.text: When an attempt runs out of time, three things happen:

blocks.md:
1. The attempt is rejected with a `ResilienceTimeoutError`.
2. The signal is aborted with that same error. `fetch()` rejects and closes the connection, so nothing keeps waiting for an answer nobody will read. Cancellation is cooperative: code that ignores the signal keeps running in the background, and its result is dropped.
3. Because `GET` is a safe method, the preset's retry makes a second attempt. Only the pipes, inner interceptors and handler run again. Guards and middleware run once per request.

Only the pipes, inner interceptors and handler run again. Guards and middleware run once per request.

1. 尝试以 `ResilienceTimeoutError` 被拒绝。
2. 信号因相同的错误而中止。`fetch()` 拒绝并关闭连接，因此没有什么可以等待没有人会阅读的答案。取消是合作的：忽略信号的代码继续在后台运行，其结果被丢弃。
3. 因为 `GET` 是一种安全的方法，预设的重试进行第二次尝试。只有管道、内部拦截器和处理程序再次运行。防护和中间件每个请求运行一次。

blocks.text: If the second attempt times out as well, the client gets a 504:

blocks.md: The timeout applies **per attempt**, so a carrier that hangs costs this route about 3.2 seconds: two attempts of 1.5 s plus up to 200 ms of backoff. The status is 504 rather than 408 on purpose. A 408 claims that the _client_ was too slow to send its request, and some clients and proxies repeat 408s automatically, even for `POST` requests.

blocks.zh: 超时适用于**每次尝试**，因此挂起的载波在这条路线上花费大约 3.2 秒：两次 1.5 秒的尝试加上长达 200 毫秒的回退。状态是 504 而不是故意的 408。一个 408 声称_client_太慢而无法发送其请求，并且一些客户端和代理自动重复 408，甚至 `POST` 请求。

blocks.md: Client errors are not failures. A request for an unknown order throws `NotFoundException` before the carrier is called. It answers 404, and it is neither retried nor counted by the breaker.
blocks.text: Client errors are not failures. A request for an unknown order throws NotFoundException before the carrier is called. It answers 404, and it is neither retried nor counted by the breaker.
blocks.zh: 客户端错误不是失败。对未知订单的请求抛出 `NotFoundException` 在呼叫承运人之前。它响应 404，断路器既不重试也不计数。

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: Code that can't take the signal as a parameter can inject `ResilienceContext` and read its `signal` and `attempt`. It reads the current attempt from `AsyncLocalStorage`, so it works in any service the handler calls, on every transport. A policy object used inside the attempt inherits its signal too, so the route's timeout also stops that policy's retries.

It reads the current attempt from AsyncLocalStorage, so it works in any service the handler calls, on every transport. A policy object used inside the attempt inherits its signal too, so the route's timeout also stops that policy's retries.

blocks.md: Fail fast with a circuit breaker
blocks.text: Fail fast with a circuit breaker
blocks.zh: 断路器快速失效

blocks.md: The preset's breaker records the outcome of every attempt. The `carrier` breaker opens once it has seen at least `minimumCalls` (10) calls, and at least `failureRateThreshold` (50%) of them failed. By default it looks at the last 20 calls. Every error counts as a failure, timeouts included, except client errors and rejections from other policies. A client error is a 4xx `HttpException`, or any other error with a 4xx `status` or `statusCode` property. That covers `CarrierError`: when the carrier answers `422` to a malformed request, it isn't down, so the breaker ignores the error and the retry doesn't repeat it. A `408` or `429` from the carrier is the exception, because it means the carrier is pushing back, so it counts like a `5xx`. An `HttpException` with one of those statuses is still a client error: the handler threw it to answer its own caller, and that says nothing about the carrier. To change what counts, pass a `recordIf` function in the breaker options.
