blocks.text: Messages and handlers
blocks.zh: 消息和处理程序

blocks.md: A message passed to `outbox.add(tx, message)` ([Save the order and its messages in one transaction](/reliability/outbox#save-the-order-and-its-messages-in-one-transaction)) has these fields:
blocks.text: A message passed to outbox.add(tx, message) (Save the order and its messages in one transaction) has these fields:
blocks.zh: 传递给 `outbox.add(tx, message)`([Save the order and its messages in one transaction](/reliability/outbox#save-the-order-and-its-messages-in-one-transaction)）有以下字段：

blocks.md:
| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `topic` | Yes | What `route` and the handlers match on |
| `payload` | Yes | Serialized to JSON when `add()` runs |
| `key` | No | The ordering key: messages that share it are published one at a time, in commit order |
| `headers` | No | String headers, passed to transports |
| `id` | No | Your own unique id. The default is a UUIDv7; consumers deduplicate by it |
| `delay` or `availableAt` | No | Publish no earlier than this long from now, or than this point in time. Not both |
blocks.zh:
| 领域 | 所需 | 意义 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `topic` | 是的 | 什么 `route` 处理程序匹配 |
| `payload` | 是的 | 序列化到 JSON 何时 `add()` 运行 |
| `key` | 不是 | 排序键：共享它的消息按提交顺序一次发布一条 |
| `headers` | 不是 | 字符串头，传递给传输 |
| `id` | 不是 | 你自己的唯一 id。默认值是 UUIDv7；消费者通过 it 进行重复数据删除 |
| `delay` 或者 `availableAt` | 不是 | 从现在起不得早于这个时间点，也不得早于这个时间点。两者都不是 |

blocks.md:
- `@OnOutboxMessage(topic, options)` takes `consumer` (required: the name of the handler's inbox) and `inbox` (default `true`; `false` runs every delivery). [Handle order.placed in-process](/reliability/outbox#handle-orderplaced-in-process)
- A handler's context has `message`, `consumer`, `attempt`, `signal` and `processInTransaction(tx, work)`.
- `ClientProxyTransport(token, options)` emits the topic with an envelope of `id`, `topic`, `key`, `headers`, `createdAt` and `payload` (`OutboxEnvelope`). Its `toPacket(message, envelope)` option returns your own `pattern` and `data`. [Publish to the analytics microservice](/reliability/outbox#publish-to-the-analytics-microservice)

blocks.md: Services
blocks.text: Services
blocks.zh: 服务

blocks.md:
| Service | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| `Outbox` | `add(tx, messages)`, `notify()` |
| `OutboxRelay` | `stats()`: `pending`, `ready`, `leased`, `deadLetters`, `oldestDueAt`, `lagMs`, `inFlight`. `runOnce()`: `claimed`, `published`, `retried`, `deadLettered`, `released`, `leaseLost`. Also `notify()`, `start()` and `stop()` |
| `OutboxDeadLetters` | `list(query)` (by `topic`, `key`, `limit`, `offset`; newest first), `get(id)`, `requeue(target)`, `purge(target)`. A target is an id, an array of ids, or a filter by `ids`, `topic`, `key`, `failedBefore`, or `all: true`. [Retries and the dead-letter queue](/reliability/outbox#retries-and-the-dead-letter-queue) |
| `OutboxInbox` | `process(consumer, id, work)`, `processInTransaction(tx, consumer, id, work)`, `prune(olderThan)`. Both `process` methods resolve `duplicate`, and `result` when `work` ran |
blocks.zh:
| 服务 | 方法 |
| --- | --- |
| `Outbox` | `add(tx, messages)`,`notify()` |
| `OutboxRelay` | `stats()`:`pending`,`ready`,`leased`,`deadLetters`,`oldestDueAt`,`lagMs`,`inFlight`.`runOnce()`:`claimed`,`published`,`retried`,`deadLettered`,`released`,`leaseLost`.还有 `notify()`、`start()` 和 `stop()` |
| `OutboxDeadLetters` | `list(query)`（按 `topic`、`key`、`limit`、`offset`；以最新为准）、`get(id)`、`requeue(target)`、`purge(target)`。目标是 id、id 数组或由 `ids`、`topic`、`key`、`failedBefore` 或 `all: true` 筛选的过滤器。[Retries and the dead-letter queue](/reliability/outbox#retries-and-the-dead-letter-queue) |
| `OutboxInbox` | `process(consumer, id, work)`,`processInTransaction(tx, consumer, id, work)`,`prune(olderThan)`.当 `work` 运行时，两种 `process` 方法都会解析 `duplicate` 和 `result` |

blocks.md: Events
blocks.text: Events
blocks.zh: 事件

blocks.md: `OutboxEvents.events$` emits each event, and publishes it on its `node:diagnostics_channel` channel. Every payload has `type` and the `message`. [Run several instances](/reliability/outbox#run-several-instances) counts them. Catch errors inside your subscribers: RxJS and `diagnostics_channel` both rethrow a subscriber's error as an uncaught exception.
blocks.text: OutboxEvents.events$ emits each event, and publishes it on its node:diagnostics_channel channel. Every payload has type and the message. Run several instances counts them. Catch errors inside your subscribers: RxJS and diagnostics_channel both rethrow a subscriber's error as an uncaught exception.
blocks.zh: `OutboxEvents.events$` 发出每个事件，并将其发布到其 `node:diagnostics_channel` 渠道。每个有效载荷都有 `type` 和 `message`. [Run several instances](/reliability/outbox#run-several-instances) 数一数。捕捉订阅者内部的错误：RxJS 和 `diagnostics_channel` 两者都将订户的错误作为未捕获的异常重新抛出。

blocks.md:
| Event | Channel | Other fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `published` | `nestjs:outbox:published` | `transport`, `durationMs` | A transport accepted the message |
| `retry-scheduled` | `nestjs:outbox:retry-scheduled` | `transport`, `error`, `attempt`, `delayMs` | A publish failed and will be retried |
| `dead-lettered` | `nestjs:outbox:dead-lettered` | `transport`, `error`, `attempt`, `reason` | The message moved to the dead letters. Alert on it |
| `lease-lost` | `nestjs:outbox:lease-lost` | None | Another relay took the message over mid-publish, so it may be published twice |
blocks.zh:
| 事件 | 渠道 | 其他领域 | 何时 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `published` | `nestjs:outbox:published` | `transport`,`durationMs` | 传输已接受该消息 |
| `retry-scheduled` | `nestjs:outbox:retry-scheduled` | `transport`,`error`,`attempt`,`delayMs` | 发布失败，将重试 |
| `dead-lettered` | `nestjs:outbox:dead-lettered` | `transport`,`error`,`attempt`,`reason` | 信息转移到了死信上。警惕它 |
| `lease-lost` | `nestjs:outbox:lease-lost` | 没有一个 | 另一个中继在发布中途接收消息，因此可能会发布两次 |

blocks.md: A dead letter's `reason` is `exhausted` (the retries ran out) or `rejected` (a `NonRetryableMessageError`, or `retryIf` returned `false`).
blocks.text: A dead letter's reason is exhausted (the retries ran out) or rejected (a NonRetryableMessageError, or retryIf returned false).
blocks.zh: 死信的 `reason` 是 `exhausted`（重试用完）或 `rejected`（一个 `NonRetryableMessageError` 或 `retryIf` 返回 `false`）。

blocks.md: Errors
blocks.text: Errors
blocks.zh: 错误

blocks.md: None of them carries an HTTP status. `OutboxError` is the base class of the four that the package throws.
blocks.text: None of them carries an HTTP status. OutboxError is the base class of the four that the package throws.
blocks.zh: 他们都没有携带 HTTP 状况。`OutboxError` 是包抛出的四个中的基类。

blocks.md:
| Error | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| `OutboxTransactionRequiredError` | `add()` or `processInTransaction()` got no transaction handle, or a store refused a handle that isn't a transaction |
| `OutboxPublishTimeoutError` | A publish outlived `relay.publishTimeout` (`timeoutMs`). Counted as a failed attempt |
| `OutboxNoHandlerError` | No `@OnOutboxMessage()` handler for the topic in this process (`topic`). Retried |
| `OutboxSchemaError` | The store's schema is behind the package's migrations while `migrate` is off, or applying them failed (`cause`): startup and every call fail until it's fixed. With the `schema`, its `version` and the `requiredVersion`. From `@nestjs/outbox/postgres` and `@nestjs/outbox/mysql` |
| `NonRetryableMessageError` | You throw it from a handler or transport to dead-letter the message without retrying |
blocks.zh:
| 错误 | 抚养时间 |
| --- | --- |
| `OutboxTransactionRequiredError` | `add()` 或者 `processInTransaction()` 没有事务句柄，或者商店拒绝了不是事务的句柄 |
| `OutboxPublishTimeoutError` | 发布已过期 `relay.publishTimeout`（`timeoutMs`）。算作失败的尝试 |
| `OutboxNoHandlerError` | 此进程中的主题没有 `@OnOutboxMessage()` 处理程序（`topic`）。重试 |
| `OutboxSchemaError` | 存储的模式是包迁移的后面，而 `migrate` 已关闭，或应用它们失败（`cause`)：启动，每次调用都会失败，直到修复为止。与 `schema`,它的 `version` 和 `requiredVersion`.从 `@nestjs/outbox/postgres` 和 `@nestjs/outbox/mysql` |
| `NonRetryableMessageError` | 您将它从处理程序或传输中丢弃到死信，而无需重试 |

chapters.title: Durable workflows
chapters.summary: Some business processes take days and span several systems.

blocks.md: Some business processes take days and span several systems. In an online store for cat food and supplies, fulfilling an order means:
blocks.text: Some business processes take days and span several systems. In an online store for cat food and supplies, fulfilling an order means:
blocks.zh: 一些业务流程需要几天时间，并且跨越多个系统。在猫粮和用品的在线商店中，履行订单意味着：

blocks.md:
1. Charge the customer's card with the payment provider.
2. Reserve the items in the warehouse.
3. Wait up to 3 days for the carrier's `shipment.delivered` webhook.
4. If it never arrives, or the carrier brings the parcel back, refund the charge and release the stock. Otherwise, wait 7 days and ask the customer for a review.
blocks.text: Charge the customer's card with the payment provider. Reserve the items in the warehouse. Wait up to 3 days for the carrier's shipment.delivered webhook. If it never arrives, or the carrier brings the parcel back, refund the charge and release the stock. Otherwise, wait 7 days and ask the customer for a review.
blocks.zh:
1. 向支付提供者收取客户的卡费用。
2. 储备仓库里的物品。
3. 等待运营商最多 3 天 `shipment.delivered` 网络挂钩。
4. 如果它从未到达，或者承运人把包裹带回来，退还费用并释放库存。否则，等待 7 天，让客户复核。

blocks.md: The process must survive deploys and crashes, charge exactly once, undo its work when it fails, and tell support where every order stands. With `@nestjs/workflows` you write it as one `async` method on an injectable class. Each side effect runs in a journaled **step**. After a restart, the method runs again from the top, and completed steps return their recorded results instead of running twice. Waits and sleeps park the instance in your own database, where any process on any host can pick it up when it's due. There is no workflow server to run.
blocks.text: The process must survive deploys and crashes, charge exactly once, undo its work when it fails, and tell support where every order stands. With @nestjs/workflows you write it as one async method on an injectable class. Each side effect runs in a journaled step. After a restart, the method runs again from the top, and completed steps return their recorded results instead of running twice. Waits and sleeps park the instance in your own database, where any process on any host can pick it up when it's due. There is no workflow server to run.
blocks.zh: 该流程必须经受住部署和崩溃，精确充电一次，失败时撤销其工作，并告诉支持人员每个订单的位置。和 `@nestjs/workflows` 你把它写成一个 `async` 可注入类的方法。每个副作用都在一个记录的**步骤**中运行。重新启动后，该方法从顶部再次运行，完成的步骤返回其记录的结果，而不是运行两次。Waits and sleeps 将实例停放在您自己的数据库中，任何主机上的任何进程都可以在到期时检索它。没有要运行的工作流服务器。

blocks.md: Workflows, queues or sagas?
blocks.text: Workflows, queues or sagas?
blocks.zh: 工作流、队列还是传奇？

blocks.md: Nest already has two tools for work that happens later, and each stays the right choice for its job:
blocks.text: Nest already has two tools for work that happens later, and each stays the right choice for its job:
blocks.zh: Nest 已经有两个工具用于稍后发生的工作，并且每个工具都是其工作的正确选择：

blocks.md:
- **[BullMQ](/application/queues#bullmq-installation)** runs one unit of background work at a time, such as sending an email or transcoding a video, with concurrency limits, rate limits, priorities, and delayed or repeatable jobs. A process with a single delayed action ("cancel the order if it isn't paid within an hour") is a delayed job plus a status column.
- **[CQRS sagas](/recipes/cqrs#sagas)** turn events into commands inside one process. They fit reactions where losing in-flight state on a restart is acceptable. Where it isn't, the same events can start and signal workflows: see [With CQRS](/reliability/workflows#with-cqrs).
- **Workflows** fit a process with several steps that waits hours or days for timers or outside events, must survive restarts and deploys, and must undo its completed steps when it fails or is cancelled. They have concurrency limits, rate limits, priorities and schedules of their own, and a step can still hand heavy work to a BullMQ queue.
blocks.text: BullMQ runs one unit of background work at a time, such as sending an email or transcoding a video, with concurrency limits, rate limits, priorities, and delayed or repeatable jobs. A process with a single delayed action ("cancel the order if it isn't paid within an hour") is a delayed job plus a status column. CQRS sagas turn events into commands inside one process. They fit reactions where losing in-flight state on a restart is acceptable. Where it isn't, the same events can start and signal workflows: see With CQRS. Workflows fit a process with several steps that waits hours or days for timers or outside events, must survive restarts and deploys, and must undo its completed steps when it fails or is cancelled. They have concurrency limits, rate limits, priorities and schedules of their own, and a step can still hand heavy work to a BullMQ queue.
blocks.zh:
- **[BullMQ](/application/queues#bullmq-installation)**一次运行一个单位的后台工作，如发送电子邮件或转码视频，具有并发限制、速率限制、优先级以及延迟或可重复的作业。具有单个延迟操作的流程（“如果在一小时内没有付款，则取消订单”）是一个延迟作业加上一个状态列。
- **[CQRS 传奇](/recipes/cqrs#sagas)**在一个进程中将事件转换为命令。它们适合在重新启动时失去飞行状态是可以接受的反应。如果不是，相同的事件可以启动工作流并发出信号：参见 [With CQRS](/reliability/workflows#with-cqrs)。
- **Workflows** 适合具有多个步骤的流程，这些步骤等待计时器或外部事件数小时或数天，必须经受住重新启动和部署，并且在失败或被取消时必须撤销已完成的步骤。它们有自己的并发限制、速率限制、优先级和时间表，一步仍然可以将繁重的工作交给 BullMQ 队列。

blocks.md: A workflow instance is a row in your application's database, so starting one can be part of the transaction that saves the order: pass the transaction to `start()` as its `transaction` option. The order and its fulfilment commit together or not at all. A job queue writes through its own connection (Redis, or BullMQ's own PostgreSQL pool), so saving an order and enqueueing its job are two writes, and a crash between them loses one. The same goes for signals: a webhook can update the order and wake its workflow in one transaction.
blocks.text: A workflow instance is a row in your application's database, so starting one can be part of the transaction that saves the order: pass the transaction to start() as its transaction option. The order and its fulfilment commit together or not at all. A job queue writes through its own connection (Redis, or BullMQ's own PostgreSQL pool), so saving an order and enqueueing its job are two writes, and a crash between them loses one. The same goes for signals: a webhook can update the order and wake its workflow in one transaction.
blocks.zh: 工作流实例是应用程序数据库中的一行，因此启动工作流实例可以是保存订单的事务的一部分：将事务传递给 `start()` 作为它的 `transaction` 选择。订单及其履行一起提交或根本不提交。作业队列通过自己的连接写入（Redis，或 BullMQ 自己的 PostgreSQL 池），因此保存订单和将其作业排队是两次写操作，它们之间的崩溃会丢失一次。信号也是如此：webhook 可以在一个事务中更新订单并唤醒其工作流。

blocks.md: The tutorial below shows where queues and sagas run out: code that continues after a durable wait ([Sleep for a week, then ask for a review](/reliability/workflows#sleep-for-a-week-then-ask-for-a-review)), an event racing a deadline ([Wait for the delivery webhook](/reliability/workflows#wait-for-the-delivery-webhook)), and compensation that survives a crash ([Let customer support cancel an order](/reliability/workflows#let-customer-support-cancel-an-order)).
blocks.text: The tutorial below shows where queues and sagas run out: code that continues after a durable wait (Sleep for a week, then ask for a review), an event racing a deadline (Wait for the delivery webhook), and compensation that survives a crash (Let customer support cancel an order).
blocks.zh: 下面的教程显示了队列和传奇在哪里耗尽：在持久等待后继续的代码（[Sleep for a week, then ask for a review](/reliability/workflows#sleep-for-a-week-then-ask-for-a-review)），一个与截止日期赛跑的事件（[Wait for the delivery webhook](/reliability/workflows#wait-for-the-delivery-webhook)），以及在崩溃中幸存的赔偿（[Let customer support cancel an order](/reliability/workflows#let-customer-support-cancel-an-order)).

blocks.md: Import `WorkflowsModule` once, in the root module, next to [`DrizzleModule`](/data/drizzle), which registers the Drizzle database that `@InjectDrizzle()` injects. Workflow classes are ordinary providers, so they go in `providers` next to the services they inject. This is the finished module: the workflows and the controllers it lists are written in the following sections, and the first provider is the package's PostgreSQL store, which [Keep workflows in your database](/reliability/workflows#keep-workflows-in-your-database) explains.

blocks.md: The `worker` runs inside your application process. It polls for due instances every second, and a local `start()` or `signal()` wakes it immediately. It claims due instances under a lease and renews the lease every third of `leaseDuration`. If the process dies, its instances are claimable again once the lease expires. Set `worker: false` on processes that should only start, signal and inspect workflows, such as API pods. A step gets 3 attempts by default, with a backoff that starts at 1 second and doubles up to 5 minutes. A `retry` option here changes that default.
blocks.text: The worker runs inside your application process. It polls for due instances every second, and a local start() or signal() wakes it immediately. It claims due instances under a lease and renews the lease every third of leaseDuration. If the process dies, its instances are claimable again once the lease expires. Set worker: false on processes that should only start, signal and inspect workflows, such as API pods. A step gets 3 attempts by default, with a backoff that starts at 1 second and doubles up to 5 minutes. A retry option here changes that default.
blocks.zh: 这个 `worker` 在您的应用程序流程中运行。它每秒钟轮询适当的实例，并在本地 `start()` 或者 `signal()` 立即唤醒它。它根据租赁要求到期，并每三分之一续租一次 `leaseDuration`.如果流程终止，一旦租约到期，其实例就可以再次索取。设置 `worker: false` 对于只应启动、发出信号和检查工作流的流程，例如 API 豆荚。默认情况下，一个步骤有 3 次尝试，后退从 1 秒开始，加倍，最多 5 分钟。一个 `retry` 此处的选项更改了默认值。

blocks.md: In `main.ts`, enable shutdown hooks. On `SIGTERM` the worker stops claiming, aborts the `signal` of running steps, waits up to `shutdownTimeout`, and hands the instances it stopped back to the store. Another process then picks them up at once instead of waiting for the lease.
blocks.text: In main.ts, enable shutdown hooks. On SIGTERM the worker stops claiming, aborts the signal of running steps, waits up to shutdownTimeout, and hands the instances it stopped back to the store. Another process then picks them up at once instead of waiting for the lease.
blocks.zh: 在 `main.ts`，启用关机挂钩。在 `SIGTERM` 工人停止索赔，中止 `signal` 运行步骤，等待 `shutdownTimeout`，并将它停止的实例交回存储。另一个过程会立即取走它们，而不是等待租赁。

blocks.md: Workflow instances, their journals, the signals they wait for and the signals sent live in a **store**. Until you register one, the module keeps them in memory: fine for a first run, but a restart loses every running order, and two processes don't share them.

blocks.md: On PostgreSQL, register the package's store, `PostgresWorkflowStore` from `@nestjs/workflows/postgres`. It runs its SQL through the database client your application already has, so it can join your transactions. It's an ordinary provider, registered once, in the root module, next to `WorkflowsModule`: both are application-wide. In `AppModule` above, it's the first provider: a factory that injects the Drizzle database and the `WorkflowStorage` registry, which the store registers itself with.

In AppModule above, it's the first provider: a factory that injects the Drizzle database and the WorkflowStorage registry, which the store registers itself with.
blocks.zh: 在 PostgreSQL 上，注册包的存储， `PostgresWorkflowStore` 来自 `@nestjs/workflows/postgres`.它运行它的 SQL 通过您的应用程序已经拥有的数据库客户端，因此它可以加入您的事务。它是一个普通的提供程序，在根模块中注册过一次，旁边 `WorkflowsModule`：两者都是广泛应用的。在 `AppModule` 上面，是第一个提供者：一个注入 Drizzle 数据库和 `WorkflowStorage` 注册表，商店用它来注册自己。

blocks.md: `fromDrizzle(db)` is the store's **executor**: it runs the store's statements through your Drizzle database, whichever driver it uses, such as `pg` or PGlite. `fromPg(pool)`, `fromTypeOrm(dataSource)`, `fromPrisma(prisma)` and `fromKysely(db)` do the same for a node-postgres pool, TypeORM, Prisma and Kysely. At startup, the module logs `WorkflowStorage: PostgresWorkflowStore`.

blocks.md: **The schema.** There's nothing to create for workflows: no tables, entities or Prisma models. The store keeps its tables in a schema of its own, `nest_workflows` (the `schema` option names another), and creates and migrates it itself. On MySQL, which has no schemas, they're tables of the connection's database, with the schema's name as their prefix: `nest_workflows_instances` and so on.

blocks.zh: **模式。**无需为工作流创建任何内容：没有表、实体或 Prisma 模型。商店把桌子放在自己的模式里，`nest_workflows`（`schema` 选项命名另一个），并创建和迁移它本身。在没有模式的 MySQL 上，它们是连接数据库的表，模式的名称作为前缀：`nest_workflows_instances` 等等。

blocks.md:
| Table | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `nest_workflows.instances` | Each workflow instance: its input, status, output or error, when it's due, and its lease |
| `nest_workflows.journal` | Each instance's recorded steps, sleeps, waits and compensations, with their results |
| `nest_workflows.waits` | The signals a suspended instance waits for |
| `nest_workflows.signals` | The signals sent, until `purge()` deletes the ones no instance can take any more |
| `nest_workflows.schedules` | The schedules, with their spec, state and next run |
| `nest_workflows.rate_limits` | The rate-limit windows, per workflow and key |
| `nest_workflows.migrations` | The versions of the store's schema applied |
blocks.zh:
| 桌子 | 它持有什么 |
| --- | --- |
| `nest_workflows.instances` | 每个工作流实例：它的输入、状态、输出或错误、何时到期以及它的租约 |
| `nest_workflows.journal` | 记录每个实例的步骤、睡眠、等待和补偿及其结果 |
| `nest_workflows.waits` | 挂起实例等待的信号 |
| `nest_workflows.signals` | 发送的信号，直到 `purge()` 删除实例不能再接受的内容 |
| `nest_workflows.schedules` | 时间表及其规格、状态和下一次运行 |
| `nest_workflows.rate_limits` | 每个工作流和关键的速率限制窗口 |
| `nest_workflows.migrations` | 应用的存储模式版本 |

blocks.md: They belong to the store: your migrations don't create them, and your own tables can't collide with them.

blocks.md: **Migrations.** The package ships the schema as versioned migrations, and the store applies them itself. With the `migrate` option, it applies the ones the schema hasn't had yet at startup, before the worker runs, in one transaction that holds an advisory lock: of several processes that start together, one migrates, and the others find nothing left to do. `migrate` defaults to `true`, except with `NODE_ENV=production`. So in development and in tests, the store creates its schema on the first start, and your migrations only create your own tables, here `orders`.

So in development and in tests, the store creates its schema on the first start, and your migrations only create your own tables, here orders.

blocks.md: With `migrate` off, a store whose schema is behind fails the startup with a `WorkflowSchemaError` that names these three ways, and fails every call the same way until the schema catches up, which it notices without a restart. Migrations only ever add tables, columns and indexes, so during a rolling deploy, the previous version of your application keeps running on the migrated schema. There are no down migrations.

Migrations only ever add tables, columns and indexes, so during a rolling deploy, the previous version of your application keeps running on the migrated schema. There are no down migrations.
blocks.zh: 和 `migrate` 关闭，模式背后的存储会使启动失败 `WorkflowSchemaError` 它命名了这三种方式，并以相同的方式失败每个调用，直到模式赶上，它注意到了这一点，而无需重新启动。迁移只添加表、列和索引，因此在滚动部署期间，应用程序的先前版本将继续在迁移的架构上运行。没有向下迁移。

blocks.md: **Transactions.** `start()` and `signal()` take your transaction as their `transaction` option: with Drizzle, the `tx` that `db.transaction()` hands its callback, as [Start it with the order](/reliability/workflows#start-it-with-the-order) shows. The store runs its statements on that transaction, so they commit or roll back with your writes. It refuses the database itself, whose statements would commit on their own, with a `TypeError` that says what to pass. With the other executors, pass a node-postgres client after `BEGIN` (not the pool), TypeORM's `EntityManager` from `dataSource.transaction()`, Prisma's interactive transaction client, or a Kysely transaction.
blocks.text: Transactions. start() and signal() take your transaction as their transaction option: with Drizzle, the tx that db.transaction() hands its callback, as Start it with the order shows. The store runs its statements on that transaction, so they commit or roll back with your writes. It refuses the database itself, whose statements would commit on their own, with a TypeError that says what to pass. With the other executors, pass a node-postgres client after BEGIN (not the pool), TypeORM's EntityManager from dataSource.transaction(), Prisma's interactive transaction client, or a Kysely transaction.
blocks.zh: **交易。**`start()` 和 `signal()` 将您的交易视为他们的 `transaction` 选项：带 Drizzle，这个 `tx` 那个 `db.transaction()` 递交其回调，如 [Start it with the order](/reliability/workflows#start-it-with-the-order) 显示。商店在该事务上运行其报表，因此它们会提交或回滚您的写入。它拒绝数据库本身，数据库的语句会自动提交 `TypeError` 上面写着要传递什么。与其他执行器一起，在之后传递 node-postgres 客户端 `BEGIN`（不是泳池），TypeORM 的 `EntityManager` 来自 `dataSource.transaction()`,Prisma 的交互式事务客户端，或 Kysely 事务。

blocks.md: **Isolation.** The store relies on READ COMMITTED, PostgreSQL's default isolation level: its statements race each other, and under a stricter level they would fail with serialization errors. At startup, it checks the database's `default_transaction_isolation`, and fails if it's stricter. A `signal()` in your transaction needs a READ COMMITTED transaction too, or its wake-ups could miss waits committed after the transaction's snapshot: it's refused with a `TypeError` otherwise.
blocks.text: Isolation. The store relies on READ COMMITTED, PostgreSQL's default isolation level: its statements race each other, and under a stricter level they would fail with serialization errors. At startup, it checks the database's default_transaction_isolation, and fails if it's stricter. A signal() in your transaction needs a READ COMMITTED transaction too, or its wake-ups could miss waits committed after the transaction's snapshot: it's refused with a TypeError otherwise.
blocks.zh: **隔离。**商店依靠 READCOMMITTEDPostgreSQL 的默认隔离级别：它的语句相互竞争，在更严格的级别下，它们会出现序列化错误。启动时，它会检查数据库的 `default_transaction_isolation`，如果更严格，就会失败。一个 `signal()` 在您的交易中需要 READCOMMITTED 事务，或者它的唤醒可能会错过事务快照后提交的等待：它被拒绝 `TypeError` 否则。

blocks.md: With Prisma, pass the client to `fromPrisma()`, and as `transaction`, the transaction client that `prisma.$transaction()` hands its callback. The store's own transactions wait up to 10 seconds for a connection and run for up to a minute, longer than Prisma's defaults: the second argument of `fromPrisma()` changes that, with `maxWait` and `timeout`. If your application signals in bursts, give its own transactions a longer `maxWait` too, since signals queue behind each other.

blocks.md:
- **The tables.** MySQL has no schemas inside a database, so the store keeps its tables in the connection's database, the one the URL's path names, and the `schema` option is the prefix of their names: `nest_workflows_instances`, `nest_workflows_signals` and so on, next to `nest_workflows_migrations` and `nest_workflows_locks`, which hold its versions and its locks.
- **Bounded keys.** Ids, names and keys are indexed columns of limited length. An instance id, a workflow or signal name, a signal's `key` and `id`, and a concurrency or rate-limit key hold 255 characters, a schedule id 230, and a step, sleep or wait name 512. `start()` and `signal()` reject a longer one with a `RangeError` before anything is written. Keys still compare exactly, as on PostgreSQL.
- **Your transactions.** `start()` and `signal()` with the `transaction` option work at REPEATABLE READ, MySQL's default, and at READ COMMITTED: the wake-up reads the waits with a locking read, which also sees those committed after your transaction's snapshot. Avoid SERIALIZABLE, where MySQL turns plain reads into locking ones: a `start()` in such a transaction would hold every signal up until the transaction ends.
- **Deadlocks.** MySQL breaks a deadlock by rolling back one of the transactions, with error 1213 (`ER_LOCK_DEADLOCK`). The store runs its own transactions again. In yours, the rollback also took your writes, so the error reaches your code: run the transaction again. A transaction that writes an order and then signals, while another one signals and then writes the same order, deadlocks that way.
- **Migrations.** MySQL commits each DDL statement on its own, so the migrations can't run in one transaction. The store and `npx @nestjs/workflows migrate` apply them one statement at a time, under a lock (`GET_LOCK()`), so processes that start together still migrate once, and a run that stopped halfway resumes where it stopped. The command line takes a `mysql://` URL and then needs `mysql2`, and `npx @nestjs/workflows sql --dialect mysql` prints the SQL. With your own tool, apply the statements in order, each once, one per call, as the TypeORM migration above does: for drizzle-kit, whose MySQL migrator sends one statement per breakpoint, add `--statement-breakpoints`.

blocks.zh:
- **表。** MySQL 在数据库中没有模式，因此存储库将其表保存在连接的数据库中，即 URL 的路径名，以及 `schema` 选项是他们名字的前缀：`nest_workflows_instances`,`nest_workflows_signals` 等等，旁边 `nest_workflows_migrations` 和 `nest_workflows_locks`，保存它的版本和锁。
- **有界键。** ID、名称和键是长度有限的索引列。实例 id、工作流或信号名称、信号的 `key` 和 `id` 和并发或速率限制键保存 255 个字符、调度 id 230 和步骤、休眠或等待名称 512。`start()` 和 `signal()` 拒绝一个较长的 `RangeError` 在任何东西被写出来之前。键仍然精确地比较，就像在 PostgreSQL 上一样。
- **您的交易。**`start()` 和 `signal()` 与 `transaction` 选项工作于 REPEATABLEREADMySQL 的默认值，并且在 READCOMMITTED：唤醒以锁定读取方式读取等待，这也会看到在您的事务快照之后提交的等待。避免 SERIALIZABLE，其中 MySQL 将普通读取转换为锁定读取：a`start()` 在这样的事务中，将保持每个信号直到事务结束。
- **死锁。** MySQL 通过回滚其中一个事务来打破死锁，出现错误 1213 (`ER_LOCK_DEADLOCK`)。商店再次运行自己的交易。在您的代码中，回滚也带走了您的写入，因此错误到达了您的代码：再次运行事务。一个事务写一个订单然后发出信号，而另一个事务发出信号然后写入相同的订单，这样就会陷入僵局。
- **迁移。**MySQL 提交每个 DDL 语句本身，因此迁移不能在一个事务中运行。商店和 `npx @nestjs/workflows migrate` 在锁下，一次应用一个语句（`GET_LOCK()`)，因此一起启动的进程仍然会迁移一次，而中途停止的运行会从停止的地方恢复。命令行采用 `mysql://` URL 然后需要 `mysql2`，和 `npx @nestjs/workflows sql --dialect mysql` 打印 SQL.使用您自己的工具，按顺序应用语句，每次调用一次，就像 TypeORM 上面的迁移确实如此：对于 drizzle-kit，其 MySQL 迁移器每个断点发送一条语句，添加 `--statement-breakpoints`.

blocks.md: Every side effect needs an idempotency key. A step runs **at least once**: if the process dies after the payment provider charged the card but before the result reached the journal, the step runs again. The engine hands each step an `idempotencyKey` that stays the same across attempts and processes (`<instance id>:<step name>`). Pass it to the system you call, and the effect happens once:

blocks.md: `ctx.step()` runs the function once and writes its result to the journal. Whenever the instance runs again (after a wait, a sleep or a crash), `run()` starts from the top and `charge-payment` returns the journaled charge without calling the payment provider. Results must be JSON-serializable, and they come back in their JSON form, on the first run too: a `Date` is a string. The return type says so (`Journaled<Charge>`), so TypeScript flags code that treats a journaled value as a live object.

blocks.md:
- **`retry`**: `attempts` counts the first attempt too, and `backoff` sets the wait before each retry: a `delay`, a growth `factor`, a `maxDelay` cap and optional `jitter`. A number is shorthand for the attempts, and `false` means a single attempt. A failed attempt parks the instance until the backoff has elapsed, so a retry survives a restart too. A `NonRetryableStepError`, such as a declined card, fails the step at once.
- **`compensate`**: registered when the step completes. If the workflow later fails or is cancelled, the compensations of completed steps run in reverse order. Each is journaled and retried like a step, with its own idempotency key. If `reserve-stock` fails because an item is out of stock, the charge is refunded. [Sleep for a week, then ask for a review](/reliability/workflows#sleep-for-a-week-then-ask-for-a-review) shows how to end this once the order is delivered.

blocks.zh:
- **`retry`**：`attempts` 也计算第一次尝试，`backoff` 设置每次重试前的等待时间：`delay`、增长 `factor`、`maxDelay` 上限和可选的 `jitter`。数字是尝试的简写，`false` 表示一次尝试。失败的尝试会暂停实例，直到回退过去，因此重试也会在重新启动后存活下来。`NonRetryableStepError`，如被拒绝的卡，会立即失败该步骤。
- **`compensate`**：步骤完成时注册。如果工作流稍后失败或被取消，则已完成步骤的补偿将以相反的顺序运行。每个都像一个步骤一样被记录和重试，有自己的幂等键。如果 `reserve-stock` 因为商品缺货而失败，费用将被退还。[Sleep for a week, then ask for a review](/reliability/workflows#sleep-for-a-week-then-ask-for-a-review) 显示订单交付后如何结束此操作。

blocks.md: Steps can also run in parallel. To reserve each item on its own, start one step per item and wait for them together. Each step has its own name, with the item's index in it, and so its own idempotency key and compensation:
blocks.text: Steps can also run in parallel. To reserve each item on its own, start one step per item and wait for them together. Each step has its own name, with the item's index in it, and so its own idempotency key and compensation:
blocks.zh: 步骤也可以并行运行。要单独预订每个项目，请从每个项目开始一步，一起等待它们。每个步骤都有自己的名称，其中包含项目的索引，因此也有自己的幂等键和补偿：

blocks.md: If one item is out of stock, its step fails, the others finish, and the compensations of the ones that completed run: the reservations are released, then the charge is refunded. Compensations run in the reverse order of the `ctx.step()` calls, whichever step finished first. The rest of the tutorial keeps the single `reserve-stock` step.

blocks.md: With `transaction`, the store creates the instance through the transaction your ORM handed the callback, so it commits with the order, or rolls back with it if anything later in the callback fails. The worker only ever sees committed instances: it picks this one up at its next poll after the commit. Pass the transaction, not the database, which the store refuses: `start()` without the option writes on its own, which is the dual write the option removes. With TypeORM, pass the transaction's `EntityManager`, and with Prisma, the transaction client, as [Keep workflows in your database](/reliability/workflows#keep-workflows-in-your-database) shows.

The worker only ever sees committed instances: it picks this one up at its next poll after the commit. Pass the transaction, not the database, which the store refuses: start() without the option writes on its own, which is the dual write the option removes. With TypeORM, pass the transaction's EntityManager, and with Prisma, the transaction client, as Keep workflows in your database shows.
blocks.zh: 和 `transaction` 存储通过您的事务创建实例 ORM 提交了回调，因此它会随订单提交，或者如果回调中的任何操作失败，它会随订单回滚。工作程序只看到提交的实例：它在提交后的下一次轮询中选择这个实例。传递存储拒绝的事务，而不是数据库：`start()` 没有选项会自行写入，这是选项删除的双重写入。和 TypeORM，传递事务的 `EntityManager`，并与 Prisma 事务客户端，作为 [Keep workflows in your database](/reliability/workflows#keep-workflows-in-your-database) 显示。

blocks.md: The instance id comes from the order id, which makes `start()` idempotent. Starting the same id with the same input returns the existing instance with `created: false`, and a different input throws `WorkflowIdConflictError`. A reconciliation job can call it again for an order without charging twice.

Starting the same id with the same input returns the existing instance with created: false, and a different input throws WorkflowIdConflictError. Set it in `run()` as the order moves on, and to `delivered` once the carrier has delivered it (in [Sleep for a week, then ask for a review](/reliability/workflows#sleep-for-a-week-then-ask-for-a-review)):

blocks.md: The status isn't journaled. Every execution replays `run()`, and with it the `setStatus()` calls, so each execution sets the status again on its way through, and a status set in a loop doesn't grow the journal. The workflow never reads it back, so nothing it decides depends on it. It's written with the instance's next write: when the next step starts, when the instance parks, or when it ends. So the endpoint shows `paid` while `reserve-stock` waits for a retry, and `awaiting-delivery` once the instance parks for the carrier. A status the workflow no longer changes stays, such as `awaiting-delivery` on a cancelled order: `status` tells what happened. A value that isn't JSON, or takes more than 16 KiB as JSON, fails the instance with a `TypeError`, and `undefined` clears the status. Each written change is emitted as a `custom-status` event.

blocks.md: `waitForSignal()` records the wait and parks the instance: its status becomes `suspended` and `wakeAt` is the deadline. No memory, timer or worker is held for those 3 days. It resolves with the signal's payload, typed as a `CarrierEvent`, or with `null` once the timeout passes. `ctx.fail()` then fails the instance, and the compensations run in reverse: the stock is released, then the charge is refunded. A `match` option filters the signals further by payload, such as `match: (event) => event.trackingNumber !== ''`; it runs again on every replay, so it must be a pure function of the payload.

blocks.md: `signal()` stores the signal with a correlation `key` and wakes the instances waiting for that signal and key. Keys match exactly, so the order id keeps one order's delivery from waking another, and a wait without a key only takes signals sent without one. Signals are durable. A webhook that arrives before the workflow reaches the wait still counts, and each signal is consumed at most once per instance, so the carrier's retries are harmless. They still store a signal each, unless you pass an `id`, such as the tracking number: a signal with the same name and `id` is stored once, and a repeat returns the first one's `signalId` with `created: false`. A delivery recorded after the deadline loses to the timeout, even if no worker was running when the deadline passed.

blocks.zh: `signal()` 用相关性存储信号 `key` 并唤醒等待信号和密钥的实例。密钥完全匹配，因此订单 id 防止一个订单的交付唤醒另一个订单，没有密钥的等待只接受没有密钥发送的信号。信号经久耐用。在工作流到达等待之前到达的 webhook 仍然算数，每个信号每个实例最多消耗一次，因此运营商的重试是无害的。它们仍然每个存储一个信号，除非你通过一个 `id`，例如跟踪号码：具有相同名称的信号和 `id` 存储一次，重复返回第一个 `signalId` 和 `created: false`.在截止日期之后记录的传递会失去超时，即使截止日期过去时没有工作人员在运行。

blocks.md: The controller answers `200` only after the transaction has committed. A delivery for an order the store doesn't know rolls back with a `404`, leaving no signal behind, and if the database fails, the carrier gets an error and delivers the webhook again. Signals sent in a transaction queue behind each other until it ends, so keep such transactions short. On PostgreSQL, the transaction must use the default READ COMMITTED isolation; the store refuses a stricter one, which could miss a wait registered while it ran. On MySQL, the default REPEATABLE READ works as well.

On MySQL, the default REPEATABLE READ works as well.
blocks.zh: 控制器应答 `200` 只有在事务提交之后。商店不知道的订单的交付会回滚 `404`，不会留下任何信号，如果数据库出现故障，运营商会收到错误并再次传递 webhook。在事务队列中一个接一个地发送信号，直到它结束，所以要保持这样的事务短。在 PostgreSQL 上，事务必须使用默认值 READCOMMITTED 孤立；商店拒绝更严格的一个，这可能会错过运行时注册的等待。在 MySQL 上，默认值 REPEATABLEREAD 也管用。

blocks.md: `ctx.signalWait()` and `ctx.timer()` only describe a condition, and `waitForAny()` waits for them together. It parks the instance once, with every signal it waits for and the earliest deadline, and resolves with the `key` of the condition that happened first and its `value`: a signal's payload, or `null` for a timer. Checking `key` narrows `value`, so after the two checks `delivery` is a `CarrierEvent`. A returned parcel fails the instance, and the compensations release the stock, which is back in the warehouse, and refund the charge. The status endpoint's `waitingFor` lists both signals while the instance waits.

It parks the instance once, with every signal it waits for and the earliest deadline, and resolves with the key of the condition that happened first and its value: a signal's payload, or null for a timer. Checking key narrows value, so after the two checks delivery is a CarrierEvent. A returned parcel fails the instance, and the compensations release the stock, which is back in the warehouse, and refund the charge. The status endpoint's waitingFor lists both signals while the instance waits.
blocks.zh: `ctx.signalWait()` 和 `ctx.timer()` 仅描述一种状况，并且 `waitForAny()` 一起等他们。它将实例停放一次，包括它等待的每个信号和最早的截止日期，并用 `key` 首先发生的情况及其 `value`：信号的有效载荷，或 `null` 为了计时器。检查 `key` 狭窄 `value` 所以两次检查之后 `delivery` 是一个 `CarrierEvent`.退回的包裹未能通过实例，赔偿会释放库存，库存回到仓库，并退还费用。状态端点的 `waitingFor` 在实例等待时列出两个信号。

blocks.md: The outcome is journaled as one entry under the wait's name, so every later execution gets the same winner. When several conditions are ready at once, the signal recorded first wins, whichever condition it matched. A signal sent after a timer's deadline doesn't count, as with `waitForSignal()`'s `timeout`, and timers count from when the wait is first reached. Only the winning signal is taken: a return reported after the delivery would stay for a later wait of the same instance. To wait for all of several signals instead, await several `waitForSignal()` calls with `Promise.all()`: each is journaled on its own, and the instance parks once for all of them. A child workflow can be a condition too, as [Start child workflows](/reliability/workflows#start-child-workflows) shows.

When several conditions are ready at once, the signal recorded first wins, whichever condition it matched. A signal sent after a timer's deadline doesn't count, as with waitForSignal()'s timeout, and timers count from when the wait is first reached. Only the winning signal is taken: a return reported after the delivery would stay for a later wait of the same instance. To wait for all of several signals instead, await several waitForSignal() calls with Promise.all(): each is journaled on its own, and the instance parks once for all of them. A child workflow can be a condition too, as Start child workflows shows.
blocks.zh: 结果被记录为等待名下的一个条目，因此每次以后的执行都会得到相同的获胜者。当几个条件同时准备就绪时，记录的信号首先获胜，无论它匹配哪个条件。在计时器截止日期之后发送的信号不算数，`waitForSignal()` 的 `timeout`，计时器从第一次到达等待开始计数。只获取获胜信号：在交付后报告的返回将保留到稍后等待同一实例。要等待所有几个信号，请等待几个 `waitForSignal()` 呼叫 `Promise.all()`：每一个都有自己的日志记录，实例为所有的日志记录一次。子工作流也可能是一个条件，如 [Start child workflows](/reliability/workflows#start-child-workflows) 显示。

blocks.text: Finish run() with the point of no return, a durable timer and the last step:
blocks.zh: 完成 `run()` 有了不归路，一个耐用的计时器和最后一步：

blocks.md: `ctx.sleep()` stores a wake-up time and parks the instance, like the wait. After 7 days, any worker resumes it: never early, and usually within a poll interval of the deadline. When it resumes, `run()` replays from the top: `charge-payment` and `await-delivery` return their journaled values, so `charge` and `delivery` are in scope a week later. A delayed job can't give you that continuation. To sleep until a point in time instead, pass an object with `until`, a `Date` or epoch milliseconds, computed from journaled values such as `ctx.now()`.
blocks.text: ctx.sleep() stores a wake-up time and parks the instance, like the wait. After 7 days, any worker resumes it: never early, and usually within a poll interval of the deadline. When it resumes, run() replays from the top: charge-payment and await-delivery return their journaled values, so charge and delivery are in scope a week later. A delayed job can't give you that continuation. To sleep until a point in time instead, pass an object with until, a Date or epoch milliseconds, computed from journaled values such as ctx.now().
blocks.zh: `ctx.sleep()` 存储唤醒时间并停放实例，就像等待一样。7 天后，任何工人都会恢复它：从不提前，通常在截止日期的投票间隔内。当它恢复时， `run()` 从顶部回放： `charge-payment` 和 `await-delivery` 返回它们的日志记录值，因此 `charge` 和 `delivery` 一周后就在范围内。一份延迟的工作不能给你这种延续。要睡眠到某个时间点，请传递一个对象 `until`, a `Date` 或历元毫秒，根据日志值计算，例如 `ctx.now()`.

blocks.md: `ctx.commit()` marks the point of no return. Once the parcel is delivered, refunding the charge would be wrong, whatever happens next. `commit()` discards the compensations registered so far. If the review email then fails for good, the instance ends as `failed` with the step's error, and nothing is refunded or released. A cancel past this point doesn't undo anything either. Only the steps after `commit()` register compensations that can still run. The commit point is journaled under its name, so it replays like a step, and the status endpoint lists it as `delivered`.

If the review email then fails for good, the instance ends as failed with the step's error, and nothing is refunded or released. A cancel past this point doesn't undo anything either. Only the steps after commit() register compensations that can still run. The commit point is journaled under its name, so it replays like a step, and the status endpoint lists it as delivered.
blocks.zh: `ctx.commit()` 标志着不归路。一旦包裹送达，无论接下来发生什么，退还费用都是错误的。 `commit()` 放弃迄今为止登记的赔偿。如果审核电子邮件永远失败，则实例结束为 `failed` 随着步骤的错误，没有任何东西被退款或释放。超过这一点的取消也不会撤销任何东西。只有后面的步骤 `commit()` 注册仍然可以运行的补偿。提交点记录在其名称下，因此它像步骤一样重放，状态端点将其列为 `delivered`.

blocks.md: A wait's `timeout` bounds one wait, and a step's `timeout` one attempt. To bound a whole instance, give the workflow a run timeout:
blocks.text: A wait's timeout bounds one wait, and a step's timeout one attempt. To bound a whole instance, give the workflow a run timeout:
blocks.zh: 等待 `timeout` 界限一等待，一步 `timeout` 一次尝试。若要绑定整个实例，请为工作流提供运行超时：

blocks.code: @Workflow('order-fulfilment', { timeout: '30d' })

blocks.md: The deadline is the instance's start plus the timeout, stored with the instance as its `deadline`, so it holds across restarts and deploys, and a parked instance wakes for it even when its sleep or wait would end later. Once it passes, the instance stops at its next `ctx` call (a step that is running finishes first), its compensations run, and it ends as `failed` with a `WorkflowTimeoutError`. Compensations aren't bound by the deadline. Here the wait gives up after 3 days and the sleep takes 7, so 30 days is a safety net. `start()` takes a `timeout` option too, which overrides the decorator's for that instance.
blocks.text: The deadline is the instance's start plus the timeout, stored with the instance as its deadline, so it holds across restarts and deploys, and a parked instance wakes for it even when its sleep or wait would end later. Once it passes, the instance stops at its next ctx call (a step that is running finishes first), its compensations run, and it ends as failed with a WorkflowTimeoutError. Compensations aren't bound by the deadline. Here the wait gives up after 3 days and the sleep takes 7, so 30 days is a safety net. start() takes a timeout option too, which overrides the decorator's for that instance.
blocks.zh: 截止日期是实例的开始加上超时，与实例一起存储 `deadline` 因此，它会在重新启动和部署期间保持不变，即使睡眠或等待稍后结束，停放的实例也会唤醒它。一旦它通过，实例就会在下一个实例停止 `ctx` 调用（正在运行的步骤首先结束），其补偿运行，并以 `failed` 用一个 `WorkflowTimeoutError` 赔偿不受最后期限的限制。在这里，等待 3 天后放弃，睡眠需要 7 天，所以 30 天是一个安全网。 `start()` 需要一个 `timeout` 选项也是，它覆盖该实例的装饰器的选项。

blocks.text: Add a cancel() route to OrdersController, and ConflictException and HttpCode to its @nestjs/common import. OrdersService.markCancelled() sets the order's status:

blocks.md: `cancel()` sets a flag. A parked instance wakes at once. A running one lets its current step finish and stops at its next `ctx` call. (A running instance in another process notices the flag on its next lease renewal, within a third of `leaseDuration`.) Either way, the compensations of the completed steps run in reverse, and the instance ends as `cancelled` with the reason as its error message. `cancel()` returns the instance with an `accepted` flag. It's `false` when the instance had already completed or failed, when it is already compensating a failure, or when a cancel or a terminate was already requested. A second cancel changes nothing, and the first reason is kept.

(A running instance in another process notices the flag on its next lease renewal, within a third of leaseDuration.) Either way, the compensations of the completed steps run in reverse, and the instance ends as cancelled with the reason as its error message. cancel() returns the instance with an accepted flag. It's false when the instance had already completed or failed, when it is already compensating a failure, or when a cancel or a terminate was already requested. A second cancel changes nothing, and the first reason is kept.
blocks.zh: `cancel()` 设置标志。一个停放的实例会立即唤醒。一个正在运行的人让它的当前步骤结束，并在下一个步骤停止 `ctx` 呼吁。（另一个进程中正在运行的实例会在其下一次租约续订时注意到该标志，时间为三分之一 `leaseDuration`.）无论哪种方式，完成步骤的补偿都是相反的，并且实例结束为 `cancelled` 原因是它的错误信息。`cancel()` 返回实例 `accepted` 旗。是 `false` 当实例已经完成或失败时，当它已经在补偿失败时，或者当已经请求取消或终止时。第二次取消不会改变任何事情，第一个原因被保留。

blocks.md: Once the carrier has reported the delivery, the route answers `409`, because support should start a return instead. The workflow doesn't rely on that check. A cancel that reaches it after `ctx.commit('delivered')` stops the review request and refunds nothing. A cancel it sees before it has consumed the delivery event still refunds, because it hasn't reached its point of no return yet.

A cancel that reaches it after ctx.commit('delivered') stops the review request and refunds nothing. A cancel it sees before it has consumed the delivery event still refunds, because it hasn't reached its point of no return yet.
blocks.zh: 一旦承运人报告了交付，路由就会响应 `409`，因为支持应该开始返回。工作流不依赖于该检查。之后到达的取消 `ctx.commit('delivered')` 停止审核请求，不退款。它在使用交付事件之前看到的取消仍然会退款，因为它还没有达到不可退货的地步。

blocks.md: What each status means
blocks.text: What each status means
blocks.zh: 每个状态意味着什么

blocks.md: An instance's `status` says what it's doing, and whether it needs you:
blocks.text: An instance's status says what it's doing, and whether it needs you:
blocks.zh: 实例的 `status` 说明它在做什么，以及它是否需要您：

blocks.md:
| Status | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pending` | Started, and not yet claimed by a worker. One that stays `pending` waits for a concurrency slot or room in a rate-limit window, or is of a version no running worker registers | Nothing while a limit holds it. Otherwise, deploy a worker with that version, or delete the instance |
| `running` | A worker holds its lease and executes it | Nothing. `cancel()` stops it at its next `ctx` call, and `terminate()` without compensating |
| `suspended` | Parked on a sleep, a wait or a retry's backoff, until `wakeAt` or a signal | Nothing. A signal or `cancel()` wakes it |
| `compensating` | Undoing its completed steps after a failure or a cancel | Nothing: it ends as `failed`, `cancelled` or `compensation_failed`. `terminate()` stops the undo |
| `completed` | Done, with the result of `run()` as its `output` | Nothing, until retention purges it |
| `cancelled` | Cancelled, after its compensations ran, or terminated without them (`error.name` is `WorkflowTerminatedError`). `error.message` is the reason | Nothing, until retention purges it |
| `failed` | A step gave up, `ctx.fail()` was called, the run timeout passed or the journal hit its limit, and then its compensations ran. Or a definition error, such as a deploy that broke replay, failed it without compensating | If no compensation ran, fix the cause and retry it. Otherwise it's done: its completed steps were undone |
| `compensation_failed` | An undo gave up halfway. `error` is the original failure, with the compensation's own error as `error.compensation` | Fix the cause, such as a warehouse API that was down, and retry it. Or finish the undo by hand and delete the instance |
blocks.zh:
| 状况 | 这意味着什么 | 怎么办 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pending` | 已经开始，但尚未被工人认领。一个留下来的 `pending` 在速率限制窗口中等待并发插槽或房间，或者是没有运行的工作人员注册的版本 | 只要有限制，什么都没有。否则，部署具有该版本的工作程序，或删除实例 |
| `running` | 工人持有租约并执行租约 | 没有。`cancel()` 在下一个停止 `ctx` 打电话，然后 `terminate()` 不补偿 |
| `suspended` | 停放在睡眠、等待或重试的后退上，直到 `wakeAt` 或信号 | 没有。信号或 `cancel()` 唤醒它 |
| `compensating` | 失败或取消后撤销已完成的步骤 | 无：它以 `failed`、`cancelled` 或 `compensation_failed` 结尾。`terminate()` 停止撤销 |
| `completed` | 完成，结果是 `run()` 作为它的 `output` | 什么都没有，直到保留清除它 |
| `cancelled` | 在其补偿运行后取消，或在没有它们的情况下终止（`error.name` 是 `WorkflowTerminatedError`）。`error.message` 是原因 | 什么都没有，直到保留清除它 |
| `failed` | 一步放弃，`ctx.fail()` 被调用，运行超时已过或日志达到其极限，然后其补偿运行。或者定义错误（例如中断重放的部署）使其失败而没有进行补偿 | 如果没有补偿运行，请修复原因并重试。否则它就完成了：它的完成步骤被撤销 |
| `compensation_failed` | 撤销中途放弃。`error` 是原始故障，补偿本身的误差为 `error.compensation` | 修复原因，如仓库 API 那是下来的，再试一次。或者手动完成撤消并删除实例 |

blocks.md: Retry, delete or terminate
blocks.text: Retry, delete or terminate
blocks.zh: 重试、删除或终止

blocks.md: `WorkflowClient` has the actions for the table's last column. Call them from a staff-only route or a script:
blocks.text: WorkflowClient has the actions for the table's last column. Call them from a staff-only route or a script:
blocks.zh: `WorkflowClient` 具有表最后一列的操作。通过员工专用路线或脚本呼叫他们：

blocks.md:
- **`retry()`** runs a `failed` instance again from its journal: completed steps return their results, the step that gave up gets its attempts back, and sleeps and waits the instance left behind start over. A deploy that broke replay is retried once the fixed code runs. It refuses an instance whose compensations ran, since resuming would build on undone work: start a new instance instead. An instance past its run timeout needs a new one, as the `timeout` option (counted from now), or `false` for none. A `compensation_failed` instance runs the compensations that didn't complete again, each with its attempts back, and ends as it would have: `failed` or `cancelled`.
- **`delete()`** removes a finished instance with its journal. An unfinished one needs the `force` option, and goes without running its compensations: use it for an instance no worker can run any more, such as one of a version you no longer deploy.
- **`cancel()`**, as above, stops an instance that is still running, and runs its compensations.
- **`terminate()`** stops an instance without running its compensations, for one whose undo mustn't or can't run, such as an order support has already refunded by hand. A parked instance stops at once, a running one at its next `ctx` call, and a compensating one after the compensation it's running. It ends as `cancelled`, with a `WorkflowTerminatedError` whose message is the reason (`Terminated.` without one). It's accepted after a `cancel()` too, which it replaces, and a `cancel()` after it is refused. Its children get their `parentClose`, as for any end.

blocks.zh:
- **`retry()`**运行 a `failed` 实例再次从它的日志中：完成的步骤返回它们的结果，放弃的步骤恢复它的尝试，并休眠并等待留下的实例重新启动。一旦修复的代码运行，就会重试中断重放的部署。它拒绝一个补偿运行的实例，因为恢复将建立在未完成的工作之上：而是启动一个新的实例。运行超时的实例需要一个新的实例，因为 `timeout` 选项（从现在开始计算），或 `false` 没有。一个 `compensation_failed` 实例再次运行未完成的补偿，每个补偿都有自己的尝试，并按原样结束： `failed` 或者 `cancelled`.
- **`delete()`**删除已完成的实例及其日志。未完成的需要 `force` 选项，并且不运行其补偿：将其用于没有工作人员可以再运行的实例，例如您不再部署的版本之一。
- **`cancel()`**，如上所述，停止仍在运行的实例，并运行其补偿。
- **`terminate()`**停止实例而不运行其补偿，对于撤销不能或不能运行的实例，例如订单支持已经手动退款。一个停放的实例立即停止，一个正在运行的实例立即停止 `ctx` 调用，并在补偿运行后进行补偿。结尾是 `cancelled`，用一个 `WorkflowTerminatedError` 谁的信息是原因（`Terminated.` 没有）。它被接受后 `cancel()` 它也取代了它，以及 `cancel()` 被拒绝之后。它的孩子得到他们的 `parentClose`，至于任何一端。

blocks.md: `retry()` and `delete()` throw a `WorkflowStateError`, whose `status` is `409`, for a status where they make no sense, and when another change to the instance races them. A retry is journaled as `$retry:1`, `$retry:2` and so on, with the status and error it retried, and both actions are emitted, as `workflow-retried` and `workflow-deleted`.

Run it every night, on one instance of your application, with `@Cron()` from `@nestjs/schedule` and `@OnOneInstance()` from [`@nestjs/locks`](/reliability/locks):

blocks.md: Limit how many run at once
blocks.text: Limit how many run at once
blocks.zh: 限制一次运行的数量

blocks.md: A worker runs every due instance it has room for. Three options decide what runs, and in what order, across every worker: a concurrency limit, a rate limit and a priority. The fulfilment sets the first two in `@Workflow()`:
blocks.text: A worker runs every due instance it has room for. Three options decide what runs, and in what order, across every worker: a concurrency limit, a rate limit and a priority. The fulfilment sets the first two in @Workflow():
blocks.zh: 一个工人运行它有空间的每一个到期的实例。三个选项决定了在每个工作者之间运行什么以及以什么顺序运行：并发限制、速率限制和优先级。实现将前两个设置为 `@Workflow()`：

blocks.md: **Concurrency.** `concurrency` caps how many instances run at once: a `limit` for the workflow, or a `limit` per key with a `key` function, here the customer's id. An array takes one of each. An instance holds a slot only while an execution runs it, compensations included, not while it sleeps or waits: a limit protects what the steps call, and an order parked for days holds up nobody. A process that crashes frees its slots once its leases expire. Instances past a limit stay due and wait for a slot, most overdue first, and a full key is passed over, so one busy customer never holds back another's order. The key is computed from the input when the instance starts, and `start()`'s `concurrencyKey` option sets another, for a workflow whose limit has a key.
blocks.text: Concurrency. concurrency caps how many instances run at once: a limit for the workflow, or a limit per key with a key function, here the customer's id. An array takes one of each. An instance holds a slot only while an execution runs it, compensations included, not while it sleeps or waits: a limit protects what the steps call, and an order parked for days holds up nobody. A process that crashes frees its slots once its leases expire. Instances past a limit stay due and wait for a slot, most overdue first, and a full key is passed over, so one busy customer never holds back another's order. The key is computed from the input when the instance starts, and start()'s concurrencyKey option sets another, for a workflow whose limit has a key.
blocks.zh: **并发性**`concurrency` 限制一次运行的实例数量：a`limit` 对于工作流，或 `limit` 每个键带有 `key` 函数，这是客户的 id。一个数组取每一个。一个实例只在执行运行它时保留一个插槽，包括补偿，而不是在它睡眠或等待时：限制保护步骤调用的内容，停放几天的订单不会阻止任何人。一旦租约到期，就会崩溃并释放其位置。超过限制的实例保持到期并等待一个插槽，大多数先过期，并且一个完整的密钥被传递，因此一个忙碌的客户永远不会拖延另一个客户的订单。当实例启动时，根据输入计算密钥，并且 `start()` 的 `concurrencyKey` 选项设置另一个选项，用于限制具有键的工作流。

blocks.md: **Rate limits.** `rateLimit` caps how many executions start per window: `max` per `duration` for the workflow, or per key with a `key` function, which `start()`'s `rateLimitKey` option overrides. Every execution counts, the first one and each resumption after a sleep, a signal, a retry's backoff or a cancel, because each can call what the limit protects. The fulfilment sends the payment provider one request per execution at most, so this caps its requests, and the executions that send none too. A window opens with the first execution after the previous one ended, and admits `max` executions until it closes, so two windows back to back can admit twice `max` within one `duration`. Say the payment provider allows 20 requests a second: allow 10.

Every execution counts, the first one and each resumption after a sleep, a signal, a retry's backoff or a cancel, because each can call what the limit protects. The fulfilment sends the payment provider one request per execution at most, so this caps its requests, and the executions that send none too. A window opens with the first execution after the previous one ended, and admits max executions until it closes, so two windows back to back can admit twice max within one duration. Say the payment provider allows 20 requests a second: allow 10.
blocks.zh: **费率限制。** `rateLimit` 限制每个窗口开始执行的次数： `max` 每 `duration` 对于工作流，或每个键 `key` 函数，其中 `start()`'s `rateLimitKey` 选项覆盖。每次执行都很重要，第一次执行和睡眠后的每次恢复、信号、重试的回退或取消都很重要，因为每次执行都可以调用限制保护的内容。履行每次执行最多向支付提供者发送一个请求，因此这限制了它的请求，也限制了不发送任何请求的执行。在前一个执行结束后，随着第一次执行而打开一个窗口，并允许 `max` 执行直到它关闭，所以两个窗口背靠背可以允许两次 `max` 在一个 `duration`.假设支付提供者每秒允许 20 个请求：允许 10 个。

blocks.md: **Priorities.** `start()`'s `priority` option decides what is claimed first: the lowest priority, then the most overdue. It's an integer from 1 to 2,097,151, and instances started without one go before every prioritized one. Express orders go first:

blocks.md: Since instances without a priority go first, once orders have one, other work needs one to go after them: the invoice batch's schedule gives it 10, in [Run workflows on a schedule](/reliability/workflows#run-workflows-on-a-schedule). An instance keeps its priority for every execution, and children inherit their parent's. Priorities are strict: a steady stream of express orders holds the standard ones back. `@StartOn()` takes the same option, as [With CQRS](/reliability/workflows#with-cqrs) shows.

blocks.md: Limits come from the highest registered version of the workflow and apply to all its versions, and each process applies the limits of the code it runs, so deploy a change to them everywhere. Claims never admit more than the limits allow, but can admit less for a moment: workers polling at the same time can take a few polls to fill a short window, and with both a concurrency key and a rate-limit key, a candidate that one kind of key passes over waits for the next claim. Claims also sort the due instances by priority, which the index on `wake_at` doesn't give them: cheap while few instances are due, noticeable with a large backlog. `drain()` stops when nothing left can start.

blocks.md: Shipping grows: book the carrier's pickup, cancel it if the order is undone, then wait for the delivery or the return. It's a process of its own, with its own steps, retries and status, so give it a workflow of its own, and run it as a **child** of the fulfilment:

blocks.zh: 运输增长：预订承运人的提货，如果订单被取消，取消，然后等待交货或退货。它是一个自己的过程，有自己的步骤、重试和状态，所以给它一个自己的工作流程，并将其作为实现的**子**来运行：

blocks.md: `CarrierClient` is a stand-in for the carrier's booking API, which, like the payment provider, answers a repeated idempotency key with the first booking. In the fulfilment, the child takes the place of the wait:
blocks.text: CarrierClient is a stand-in for the carrier's booking API, which, like the payment provider, answers a repeated idempotency key with the first booking. In the fulfilment, the child takes the place of the wait:

blocks.code:
// Starts the shipment, and waits for it to end: its delivery, or a ChildWorkflowFailedError.
const delivery = await ctx.executeChild(ShipmentWorkflow, order);

blocks.md: Register `ShipmentWorkflow` and `CarrierClient` as providers, next to the fulfilment. The carrier's webhook doesn't change: it signals the order's id, and the shipment is now the instance waiting for it.

blocks.zh: 登记 `ShipmentWorkflow` 和 `CarrierClient` 作为提供者，紧邻履行。承运人的 webhook 没有改变：它发出订单 id 的信号，装运现在是等待它的实例。

blocks.md:
- **`ctx.executeChild()`** starts the child and waits for its end. Both are journaled, as `$child:<id>` and `$result:<id>`, so a replay gets the same child back instead of starting another, and the fulfilment parks in the meantime. `ctx.startChild()` only starts it, and returns a handle: its `result()` waits for the child, and the handle is a condition of `waitForAny()`, to race the child against a timer or a signal.
- **Ids.** A child's id defaults to its parent's id, the workflow's name and a count of that workflow's children in this run, such as `order-71e1973d/shipment#1`. Give children started from parallel branches an `id` option derived from your data, so that a replay, which can reach them in another order, finds each one.
- **Failures.** If the child fails, is cancelled or is terminated, `executeChild()` throws a `ChildWorkflowFailedError`, with its `status` and its error as `cause`. Left uncaught, it fails the fulfilment like any error: a returned parcel fails the shipment, whose compensation cancels its booking, and then the fulfilment, whose compensations refund the charge and release the stock. Catch it to try something else, such as another carrier.
- **`parentClose`** decides what happens to a child that is still running when its parent ends or starts compensating: `'cancel'`, the default, cancels it, and its compensations run; `'terminate'` stops it without them; `'abandon'` leaves it running. When support cancels the order, the shipment is cancelled with it, and the pickup with the shipment.
- A child inherits its parent's priority, unless `startChild()` gets one, and takes `concurrencyKey` and `rateLimitKey` options as `start()` does. `getStatus()` with the `children` option lists an instance's children, each with its `parentId`, and `list()` pages through them by `parentId`.

- **`ctx.executeChild()`**启动子程序并等待其结束。两者都有日志记录，如 `$child:<id>` 和 `$result:<id>` 因此，重播会让同一个孩子回来，而不是启动另一个孩子，同时实现公园。`ctx.startChild()` 只启动它，并返回一个句柄：它 `result()` 等待孩子，句柄是 `waitForAny()` 让孩子与计时器或信号赛跑。
- **Ids.**子的 id 默认为其父的 id、工作流的名称和本次运行中该工作流的子的计数，例如 `order-71e1973d/shipment#1` 给从平行分支开始的孩子一个 `id` 选项从您的数据中派生出来，以便重播可以以不同的顺序到达他们，找到每一个。
- **失败。**如果子失败、被取消或被终止，`executeChild()` 将抛出一个 `ChildWorkflowFailedError`，其 `status` 和错误为 `cause`。如果没有被发现，它就会像任何错误一样失败履行：退回的包裹会失败运输，其赔偿会取消其预订，然后履行，其赔偿会退还费用并释放库存。抓住它尝试其他东西，比如另一个载体。
- **`parentClose`** 决定当父母终止或开始补偿时仍在奔跑的孩子会发生什么：`'cancel'`，默认值，取消它，它的补偿运行；`'terminate'` 没有他们就停下来；`'abandon'` 让它运行。当支持取消订单时，货件也会随之取消，提货也会随之取消。
- 子代继承其父代的优先权，除非 `startChild()` 获得优先权，并像 `start()` 一样选择 `concurrencyKey` 和 `rateLimitKey` 选项。带有 `children` 选项的 `getStatus()` 列出了一个实例的子实例，每个子实例都有它的 `parentId`，并通过 `parentId` 列出了 `list()` 页。

- `signal` is aborted on shutdown, on a lost lease and on those timeouts. Pass it to your I/O.

blocks.md: Every worker whose code declares the schedule starts its occurrences, and each occurrence starts one instance, however many workers there are: its id is the schedule's id and the occurrence's time, such as `monthly-invoices@2026-10-01T06:00:00.000Z`. The `input` function receives the occurrence, its schedule's `id` and its time `at`, and so does the instance, as `ctx.schedule`, which is `null` for an instance started otherwise.

blocks.zh: 代码声明调度的每个 worker 都启动它的实例，每个实例启动一个实例，无论有多少个 worker：它的 id 是调度的 id 和实例的时间，如 `monthly-invoices@2026-10-01T06:00:00.000Z`.这 `input` 函数接收事件，其调度的 `id` 时间到了 `at` 实例也是如此，因为 `ctx.schedule`，这是 `null` 对于以其他方式开始的实例。

blocks.md:
- **When.** `cron` takes 5 fields, or 6 with the seconds first, `every` a fixed interval, and `rrule` an RFC 5545 recurrence rule. Times are wall-clock times in `tz`, UTC by default, so the batch starts at 02:00 in New York before and after the clocks change. When the clocks go back, a local time that occurs twice runs once, the first time, so an hourly schedule skips the second pass of the repeated hour. When they go forward, a time that doesn't exist still runs, as much later as the clocks jumped: 02:30 runs at 03:30. `every` takes no `tz`: it repeats a fixed interval whatever the time zone. `startAt`, `endAt` and `limit` bound a schedule.
- **`missed`** says what happens to occurrences no worker was up to start, during a deploy or an outage. `'skip'`, the default, starts one only if a worker finds it within a minute of its time; `'once'` starts the latest of them; `'all'` starts each of them, the latest 100 at most, and needs `overlap: 'allow'`. The occurrences it passes over are reported in a `schedule-skipped` event.
- **`overlap`** says what an occurrence does while an instance the schedule started is unfinished: `'skip'`, the default, passes it over, with a `schedule-skipped` event; `'allow'` starts it anyway; `'cancel-previous'` cancels the running one; `'buffer-one'` starts it once the running one ends.

blocks.zh:
- **何时。**`cron` 取 5 个字段，或先取 6 个字段，`every` 固定间隔，以及 `rrule` 安 RFC5545 递归规则。时间是挂钟时间 `tz`,UTC 默认情况下，批处理在时钟变化前后的纽约 02:00 开始。当时钟倒转时，出现两次的本地时间第一次运行一次，因此每小时时间表跳过重复时间的第二次通过。当他们前进时，一个不存在的时间仍然运行，就像时钟跳动一样晚：02:30 运行在 03:30。`every` 不接受 `tz`：无论时区如何，它都会重复固定的间隔。`startAt`,`endAt` 和 `limit` 有时间表。
- **`missed`** 表示在部署或停机期间，如果没有工作人员可以启动，会发生什么情况。`'skip'`，默认情况下，只有当工人在一分钟内找到它时，才会启动一个；`'once'` 开始其中最新的一个；`'all'` 启动它们中的每一个，最多最新的 100 个，需要 `overlap: 'allow'`。它传递的事件在 `schedule-skipped` 事件中报告。
- **`overlap`**表示当计划启动的实例未完成时，实例执行的操作：`'skip'` 默认值，将其传递给 `schedule-skipped` 事件；`'allow'` 无论如何都要开始；`'cancel-previous'` 取消正在运行的；`'buffer-one'` 运行结束后启动它。

blocks.md: A declared schedule belongs to the code, also while a rolling deploy runs the old and the new code side by side. Each process saves the schedules that its workflows declare when it starts, and confirms them every minute while its worker runs. A process leaves a schedule as it is while another process confirms it, if its own code doesn't declare it or a newer version of the workflow declares it differently. Once no process has confirmed it for five minutes, a process deletes a schedule that its code doesn't declare, whether or not it runs the schedule's workflow, and replaces another declaration with its own. So an old pod that restarts mid-rollout leaves alone the schedules that the new code adds or a new version changes, a schedule that a deploy drops goes about five minutes after the last process of the old code stopped, also when the deploy removes its workflow, and a rollback brings the old declaration back.

blocks.zh: 声明的计划属于代码，而滚动部署并排运行新旧代码。每个进程保存其工作流在启动时声明的时间表，并在其工人运行时每分钟确认这些时间表。如果一个进程自己的代码没有声明它，或者工作流的较新版本以不同的方式声明它，则进程保留它，而另一个进程确认它。一旦五分钟内没有进程确认它，进程就会删除其代码没有声明的计划，无论它是否运行计划的工作流，并用自己的声明替换另一个声明。因此，在中间部署重新启动的旧 pod 不会留下新代码添加或新版本更改的时间表，部署删除的时间表会在旧代码的最后一个进程停止后大约五分钟消失，也会在部署删除其工作流时消失，回滚会将旧声明带回来。

blocks.md: Processes of other code on the same database, such as the workers of other workflows, also delete a schedule when no worker whose code declares it has run for five minutes, as while those workers are scaled to zero. The next process whose code declares it saves it again as it starts, and the schedule starts over: from its next occurrence, unpaused, with its runs counted from zero.

blocks.md: `WorkflowClient.schedules`, also injectable as `WorkflowSchedules`, handles schedules at runtime. `trigger('monthly-invoices')` starts an occurrence now, whatever `overlap` says and even while the schedule is paused, with its time as `at`. `pause()` stops the occurrences until `resume()`, which starts again from the first one after now. `preview()` returns the next occurrences, in epoch milliseconds, and `get()` and `list()` read the schedules. A schedule that isn't in the code, such as one per customer, is saved with `upsert()`, and `remove()` deletes it, leaving the instances it started running:

A schedule that isn't in the code, such as one per customer, is saved with upsert(), and remove() deletes it, leaving the instances it started running:

blocks.md: Wait for a result
blocks.text: Wait for a result

blocks.md: Most callers start a workflow and move on. Some need its result: an accountant who wants a month's invoices now, before the schedule renders them, calls a route that renders them and answers with the count. `startAndWait()` starts the instance and waits for it to end:
blocks.text: Most callers start a workflow and move on. Some need its result: an accountant who wants a month's invoices now, before the schedule renders them, calls a route that renders them and answers with the count. startAndWait() starts the instance and waits for it to end:
blocks.zh: 大多数调用者开始工作流程并继续前进。有些人需要它的结果：一个会计师现在想要一个月的发票，在时间表呈现它们之前，调用一个呈现它们的路由，并用计数来回答。`startAndWait()` 启动实例并等待其结束：

blocks.md:
- `startAndWait()` is `start()`, then `result()`, which waits for an instance to end and resolves with its output. For an id that has an instance already, it waits for that one, so the accountant calling the route again, while the batch runs or after it ended, gets the same batch. The wait's options are the fourth argument: the third one's `timeout` stays the instance's run timeout.
- Past the wait's `timeout`, in wall-clock time rather than the module's clock, it rejects with `WorkflowResultTimeoutError`, and the instance keeps running: the route answers `202`. A `signal` option stops the wait when it's aborted, as when the caller goes away.
- On shutdown, a wait lasts while the worker finishes its running steps, up to `shutdownTimeout`, so an instance that ends meanwhile still answers with its result. Then the wait rejects with an `Error`, before Nest closes the HTTP server, and the route answers at once, here with a `500`, instead of holding up the shutdown until its wait's `timeout`.
- An instance that failed, was cancelled or terminated rejects with a `WorkflowFailedError`, whose `status` says how it ended and whose `cause` is its error. Here, that's a `500`.
- `result()` waits for an instance by its id, such as the one `trigger()` started, whichever process runs it. `startAndWait()` refuses the `transaction` option, since the instance only exists once your transaction commits: call `start()` in the transaction, and `result()` after the commit.

Here, that's a 500. result() waits for an instance by its id, such as the one trigger() started, whichever process runs it. startAndWait() refuses the transaction option, since the instance only exists once your transaction commits: call start() in the transaction, and result() after the commit.
blocks.zh:
- `startAndWait()` 是 `start()`,然后 `result()`，它等待实例结束并使用其输出进行解析。对于已经有实例的 id，它会等待该实例，因此会计师在批处理运行时或结束后再次调用路由，会得到相同的批处理。等待的选项是第四个论点：第三个论点 `timeout` 保持实例的运行超时。
- 过了等待 `timeout` 在挂钟时间而不是模块的时钟中，它拒绝 `WorkflowResultTimeoutError`，实例继续运行：路由响应 `202`. A `signal` 选项在等待中止时停止等待，例如当呼叫者离开时。
- 在关机时，在工人完成其运行步骤时，将持续等待，直至 `shutdownTimeout`，所以同时结束的实例仍然用它的结果来回答。然后等待拒绝 `Error`,之前 Nest 关闭 HTTP 服务器，路由立即响应，这里有一个 `500`，而不是推迟关机直到它等待 `timeout`.
- 失败、被取消或终止的实例拒绝使用 `WorkflowFailedError`，谁的 `status` 说它是如何结束的以及谁的 `cause` 是它的错误。这里，那是一个 `500`.
- `result()` 按 id 等待实例，如 `trigger()` 启动，无论哪个进程运行它。`startAndWait()` 拒绝 `transaction` 选项，因为实例仅在您的事务提交时存在：call`start()` 在交易中，以及 `result()` 提交后。

blocks.md: The journal is keyed by name, so step, sleep and wait names are a contract with every instance that is still running. The name is also part of the idempotency key.
blocks.text: The journal is keyed by name, so step, sleep and wait names are a contract with every instance that is still running. The name is also part of the idempotency key.
blocks.zh: 日志是按名称键入的，因此步骤、睡眠和等待名称是与每个仍在运行的实例的契约。名称也是幂等键的一部分。

blocks.md: Suppose you rename `charge-payment` to `charge-card` and deploy. An order that was waiting for the carrier resumes, finds no `charge-card` entry in its journal, and would charge the card again, under a key the payment provider has never seen. Before the first new step of an execution runs, the engine checks that the code reached every step in the journal. Here it didn't, so the instance fails without charging:

blocks.zh: 假设您重命名 `charge-payment` 二 `charge-card` 并部署。等待运营商恢复的订单，没有找到 `charge-card` 在其日记账中记录，并将在支付提供者从未见过的密钥下再次向卡收费。在执行的第一个新步骤运行之前，引擎检查代码是否到达了日志中的每一步。这里没有，所以实例在不充电的情况下失败：

blocks.code:
Instance "order-6d0f8c06" of workflow "order-fulfilment@1" does not match its journal:
"charge-payment", "reserve-stock", "await-delivery" were recorded by an earlier run but not
reached before the new step "charge-card". A deployed change renamed, removed or reordered steps.
Ship such changes as a new version (@Workflow(name, { version })) and keep the old class
registered until its instances finish.

blocks.md: Rules for workflow code
blocks.text: Rules for workflow code
blocks.zh: 工作流代码规则

blocks.md: `run()` executes again from the top every time an instance resumes. Code between steps runs on every execution, so it must make the same decisions each time:
blocks.text: run() executes again from the top every time an instance resumes. Code between steps runs on every execution, so it must make the same decisions each time:
blocks.zh: `run()` 每次实例恢复时，从顶部再次执行。步骤之间的代码在每次执行时运行，因此每次都必须做出相同的决定：

blocks.md:
- Put anything that touches or reads the outside world in a step: HTTP calls, database reads and writes, feature flags.
- Outside steps, use `ctx.now()`, `ctx.random()` and `ctx.uuid()` instead of `Date.now()`, `Math.random()` and `randomUUID()`. They're journaled.
- In `run()`, only `await` `ctx` operations and pure computation. Never wait on a real timer.
- Step, sleep and wait names must be unique within a run. In a loop, add the index to the name, such as `remind-1` and `remind-2`. Give children started from parallel branches an `id` of their own.
- Don't call `ctx` methods inside a step's function. The function runs once and replays only see its result, so the engine fails the instance when a step calls `ctx`. Throw a `NonRetryableStepError` from a step instead of calling `ctx.fail()` there.
- If you catch errors in `run()`, rethrow what you don't handle. `isWorkflowInterrupt()` identifies the engine's control flow. The engine doesn't depend on it: after a swallowed interrupt no step runs, `commit()` throws again, and a cancel still cancels. But `finally` blocks run at every suspension, so keep side effects out of them.
- `Promise.all()` over steps is fine, and a step in the same `Promise.all()` as a sleep or wait starts after it. `Promise.race()` and `Promise.any()` are not replay-safe.
- Inputs, step results and signal payloads must be JSON-serializable. A `Date` comes back as a string, on the first run and on every replay, and the `Journaled` types of results and payloads say so.
- Keep no per-run state on `this`: one instance of the class serves every order.

blocks.zh:
- 把任何接触或读取外部世界的东西放在一个步骤中：HTTP 调用、数据库读写、功能标志。
- 在外部步骤中，使用 `ctx.now()`、`ctx.random()` 和 `ctx.uuid()` 代替 `Date.now()`、`Math.random()` 和 `randomUUID()`。他们被记录下来了。
- 在 `run()`，仅 `await``ctx` 运算和纯计算。永远不要等待真正的计时器。
- 步骤、睡眠和等待名称在运行中必须是唯一的。在循环中，将索引添加到名称中，例如 `remind-1` 和 `remind-2` 给从平行分支开始的孩子一个 `id` 他们自己的。
- 不要打电话 `ctx` 步骤函数中的方法。该函数运行一次，并且只回放它的结果，因此当一个步骤调用时，引擎会使实例失败 `ctx`.扔一个 `NonRetryableStepError` 从一步而不是呼叫 `ctx.fail()` 那里。
- 如果在 `run()` 把你处理不了的东西扔回去。`isWorkflowInterrupt()` 标识发动机的控制流。引擎不依赖于它：在吞咽中断之后，没有步骤运行，`commit()` 再次抛出，取消仍然取消。但 `finally` 每个悬架上都有块，所以要避免副作用。
- `Promise.all()` 超过步骤是好的，在同一个步骤中 `Promise.all()` 因为睡眠或等待之后开始。`Promise.race()` 和 `Promise.any()` 不适合重播。
- 输入、步进结果和信号有效载荷必须为 JSON-可序列化。一个 `Date` 在第一次运行和每次重播时都以字符串的形式返回，并且 `Journaled` 结果和有效载荷的类型是这样说的。
- 保持无运行状态 `this`：类的一个实例服务于每个订单。

blocks.md: Two things make workflow tests fast and deterministic:
blocks.text: Two things make workflow tests fast and deterministic:

blocks.md:
- Every timestamp the engine uses (deadlines, retry times, lease expiry and `ctx.now()`) comes from the module's `clock`. A `ManualWorkflowClock` only moves when you call `advance()`.
- With the worker disabled, nothing runs in the background. `WorkflowWorker.drain()` runs every due instance until none is left that can start, and starts the occurrences of schedules that the clock has passed. The clock starts on 1 January 2026 at 00:00 UTC, so a test that moves it by days also starts the invoice batch's first occurrence, at 07:00 UTC.

blocks.md: With CQRS
blocks.text: With CQRS
blocks.zh: 和 CQRS

blocks.md: If your application follows the [CQRS recipe](/recipes/cqrs), command handlers publish events, and event handlers and sagas react to them. They react in memory: an event published just before the process stops never reaches them, and a saga that waits for a second event forgets the first one on a restart. The `@nestjs/workflows/cqrs` entry point lets the events themselves start and signal workflows, durably, while your code keeps executing commands and publishing events. It works with `@nestjs/cqrs` 11 and later, registered with `CqrsModule.forRoot()` as in the recipe.

The @nestjs/workflows/cqrs entry point lets the events themselves start and signal workflows, durably, while your code keeps executing commands and publishing events. It works with @nestjs/cqrs 11 and later, registered with CqrsModule.forRoot() as in the recipe.

blocks.md: `@StartOn()`'s `id` is required. It derives the instance id from the business key, as `start()` does, so an event published twice finds the instance the first one started. It also takes `start()`'s `priority`, `concurrencyKey` and `rateLimitKey`, each as a value or a function of the event: here, express orders go first, as before. `@SignalOn()`'s `id` is optional, and becomes the signal's `id`: a delivery event published again, say for the carrier's retried webhook, stores no second signal. `input` defaults to the event itself, and a signal's `payload` too. TypeScript checks the input against `run()` and the payload against the signal's type. The events are plain classes, such as `OrderPlacedEvent` with a `readonly order: Order` constructor parameter.
