blocks.md:
OnGatewayInit Requires the afterInit() method, which receives the library-specific server instance as an argument.
OnGatewayConnection Requires the handleConnection() method, which receives the library-specific client socket instance as its first argument.

blocks.title: Warning
blocks.md: Nest doesn't wait for an async `handleConnection()` to finish before it handles the client's messages, so the hook isn't a gate: messages that arrive before it disconnects the client are still handled. To reject a client before any of its messages are handled, use connection-level middleware instead: socket.io's `server.use()` in `afterInit()`, or, with `WsAdapter`, a `verifyClient` function in the `@WebSocketGateway()` options.

blocks.md: Request-scoped gateways
blocks.text: Request-scoped gateways
blocks.zh: 请求范围网关

blocks.md: Starting with NestJS v12, gateways support [request-scoped](/fundamentals/injection-scopes) providers. Nest creates a new instance of every request-scoped dependency per connected socket. That instance lives as long as the connection does, so it can safely hold per-connection state.
blocks.text: Starting with NestJS v12, gateways support request-scoped providers. Nest creates a new instance of every request-scoped dependency per connected socket. That instance lives as long as the connection does, so it can safely hold per-connection state.
blocks.zh: 从 NestJSv12，网关支持 [request-scoped](/fundamentals/injection-scopes) 供应商。Nest 为每个连接的套接字创建每个请求范围依赖项的新实例。该实例的寿命与连接的寿命一样长，因此它可以安全地保持每个连接状态。

blocks.zh: 将插座本身注入 `REQUEST` 令牌，就像你注入 HTTP 请求到请求范围 HTTP 供应商：

blocks.md: The gateway then injects it like any other provider:
blocks.text: The gateway then injects it like any other provider:
blocks.zh: 然后，网关像其他提供者一样注入它：

blocks.md: Because the scope is tied to the connection rather than to a single message, the `sequence` counter above increments across every message received on that socket, while a second client gets its own independent instance. Nest tears the request-scoped instances down when the socket disconnects.
blocks.text: Because the scope is tied to the connection rather than to a single message, the sequence counter above increments across every message received on that socket, while a second client gets its own independent instance. Nest tears the request-scoped instances down when the socket disconnects.
blocks.zh: 因为作用域绑定到连接而不是单个消息，所以 `sequence` 对该套接字上接收的每条消息进行计数，而第二个客户端获得自己的独立实例。Nest 当套接字断开连接时，拆卸请求范围内的实例。

blocks.title: Notice
blocks.md: As with HTTP, request-scoped providers add per-connection instantiation overhead. Use the default singleton scope unless you need per-connection state.
blocks.text: As with HTTP, request-scoped providers add per-connection instantiation overhead. Use the default singleton scope unless you need per-connection state.
blocks.zh: 和 HTTP，请求作用域提供程序会增加每个连接的实例化开销。除非需要每个连接状态，否则使用默认的单例作用域。

chapters.title: Pipes
chapters.summary: There is no fundamental difference between regular pipes and WebSocket pipes.

blocks.md: There is no fundamental difference between [regular pipes](/pipes) and WebSocket pipes. The only difference is that instead of throwing `HttpException`, you should throw `WsException`. Only a `WsException` reaches the client with its own message. Any other exception, including the `BadRequestException` that the built-in validation pipes throw by default, is reported to the client as `'Internal server error'`.
blocks.text: There is no fundamental difference between regular pipes and WebSocket pipes. The only difference is that instead of throwing HttpException, you should throw WsException. Only a WsException reaches the client with its own message. Any other exception, including the BadRequestException that the built-in validation pipes throw by default, is reported to the client as 'Internal server error'.
blocks.zh: 之间没有根本区别 [常规管道](/pipes) 和 WebSocket 管道。唯一的区别是，不是扔 `HttpException`，你应该扔 `WsException`.只有一个 `WsException` 用自己的消息到达客户端。任何其他例外情况，包括 `BadRequestException` 默认情况下，内置验证管道抛出的数据将报告给客户端 `'Internal server error'`.

chapters.title: Overview
chapters.summary: In addition to traditional (sometimes called monolithic) application architectures, Nest natively supports the microservice architectural style of development.

blocks.md: In addition to traditional (sometimes called monolithic) application architectures, Nest natively supports the microservice architectural style of development. Most of the concepts discussed elsewhere in this documentation, such as dependency injection, decorators, exception filters, pipes, guards, and interceptors, apply equally to microservices. Wherever possible, Nest abstracts implementation details so that the same components can run across HTTP-based platforms, WebSockets, and microservices. This section covers the aspects of Nest that are specific to microservices.
blocks.text: In addition to traditional (sometimes called monolithic) application architectures, Nest natively supports the microservice architectural style of development. Most of the concepts discussed elsewhere in this documentation, such as dependency injection, decorators, exception filters, pipes, guards, and interceptors, apply equally to microservices. Wherever possible, Nest abstracts implementation details so that the same components can run across HTTP-based platforms, WebSockets, and microservices. This section covers the aspects of Nest that are specific to microservices.
blocks.zh: 除了传统（有时称为单片）应用程序体系结构之外，Nest 本地支持微服务架构开发风格。本文档其他地方讨论的大多数概念，如依赖注入、装饰器、异常过滤器、管道、防护和拦截器，同样适用于微服务。只要有可能，Nest 抽象实现细节，以便相同的组件可以跨 HTTP-基于平台、WebSockets 和微服务。本节涵盖 Nest 这些是特定于微服务的。

blocks.md: In Nest, a microservice is fundamentally an application that uses a different **transport** layer than HTTP.
blocks.text: In Nest, a microservice is fundamentally an application that uses a different transport layer than HTTP.
blocks.zh: 在 Nest 中，微服务基本上是使用与 HTTP 不同的**传输**层的应用程序。

blocks.md: Nest supports several built-in transport layer implementations, called **transporters**, which are responsible for transmitting messages between different microservice instances. Most transporters natively support both **request-response** and **event-based** message styles. Nest abstracts the implementation details of each transporter behind a canonical interface for both styles. This lets you switch from one transport layer to another (e.g., to take advantage of the reliability or performance features of a particular transport layer) without changing your application code.
blocks.text: Nest supports several built-in transport layer implementations, called transporters, which are responsible for transmitting messages between different microservice instances. Most transporters natively support both request-response and event-based message styles. Nest abstracts the implementation details of each transporter behind a canonical interface for both styles. This lets you switch from one transport layer to another (e.g., to take advantage of the reliability or performance features of a particular transport layer) without changing your application code.
blocks.zh: Nest 支持几个内置的传输层实现，称为**transporters**，它们负责在不同的微服务实例之间传输消息。大多数传输程序本机支持**请求-响应**和**基于事件**的消息样式。Nest 抽象了两种样式的规范接口背后每个传输程序的实现细节。这允许您从一个传输层切换到另一个传输层（例如，利用特定传输层的可靠性或性能特征），而无需更改应用程序代码。

The options object is specific to the chosen transporter. The TCP transporter exposes the properties described below. For other transporters (e.g., Redis or MQTT), see the relevant chapter for a description of the available options.

host Connection hostname
port Connection port
retryAttempts Number of times the server tries to listen again after it closes unexpectedly (default: 0)

serializer Custom serializer for outgoing messages
deserializer Custom deserializer for incoming messages

Message and Event Patterns
blocks.text: Message and Event Patterns
blocks.zh: 消息和事件模式

blocks.md: Microservices recognize both messages and events by **patterns**. A pattern is a plain value, e.g., a literal object or a string. Patterns are automatically serialized and sent over the network along with the data portion of a message. This way, message senders and consumers can coordinate which requests are consumed by which handlers.
blocks.text: Microservices recognize both messages and events by patterns. A pattern is a plain value, e.g., a literal object or a string. Patterns are automatically serialized and sent over the network along with the data portion of a message. This way, message senders and consumers can coordinate which requests are consumed by which handlers.
blocks.zh: 微服务通过**模式**识别消息和事件。模式是纯值，例如文字对象或字符串。模式被自动序列化，并与消息的数据部分一起通过网络发送。这样，消息发送者和消费者可以协调哪些请求由哪些处理程序消费。

blocks.md: Request-response
blocks.text: Request-response
blocks.zh: 请求-响应

blocks.md: The request-response message style is useful when you need to **exchange** messages between services. It ensures that the service has actually received the message, without requiring you to implement an acknowledgment protocol manually. However, request-response isn't always the best fit. For example, streaming platforms that use log-based persistence, such as [Kafka](https://docs.confluent.io/3.0.0/streams/) or [NATS JetStream](https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream), are optimized for a different set of challenges, more aligned with the event messaging paradigm (see [event-based messaging](/microservices/basics#event-based) for more details).
blocks.text: The request-response message style is useful when you need to exchange messages between services. It ensures that the service has actually received the message, without requiring you to implement an acknowledgment protocol manually. However, request-response isn't always the best fit. For example, streaming platforms that use log-based persistence, such as Kafka or NATS JetStream, are optimized for a different set of challenges, more aligned with the event messaging paradigm (see event-based messaging for more details).
blocks.zh: 当您需要在服务之间**交换**消息时，请求-响应消息样式非常有用。它确保服务实际上已经接收到消息，而不需要您手动实现确认协议。然而，请求响应并不总是最合适的。例如，使用基于日志的持久性的流平台，例如 [Kafka](https://docs.confluent.io/3.0.0/streams/) 或者 [NATS JetStream](https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream)，针对一组不同的挑战进行了优化，更符合事件消息传递范例（参见 [基于事件的消息传递](/microservices/basics#event-based) 更多详情）。

blocks.md: To enable the request-response message type, Nest creates two logical channels: one for transferring data and another for waiting for incoming responses. For some underlying transports, like [NATS](https://nats.io/), this dual-channel support is provided out of the box. For others, Nest compensates by creating separate channels manually, which can introduce some overhead. If you don't need the request-response message style, consider using the event-based method instead.

For others, Nest compensates by creating separate channels manually, which can introduce some overhead. If you don't need the request-response message style, consider using the event-based method instead.

blocks.md: To create a message handler based on the request-response paradigm, use the `@MessagePattern()` decorator, which is imported from the `@nestjs/microservices` package. Use this decorator only within [controller](/controllers) classes, as they serve as the entry points for your application. The Nest runtime ignores it in providers.

In such cases, the overhead of maintaining two channels for request-response is unnecessary.

blocks.md: A client Nest application can exchange messages with, or publish events to, a Nest microservice using the `ClientProxy` class. blocks.md: Request-scoping
blocks.text: Request-scoping

blocks.md: If you come from a different programming language background, it may be surprising that in Nest, most things are shared across incoming requests. This includes the database connection pool, singleton services with global state, and more. Node.js doesn't follow the request/response multi-threaded stateless model, in which each request is processed by a separate thread. As a result, using singleton instances is **safe** for your applications.

As a result, using singleton instances is safe for your applications.

blocks.md: Tracing a request across services
blocks.text: Tracing a request across services
blocks.zh: 跨服务跟踪请求

blocks.md: Timeouts tell you that a call failed to come back in time. They don't tell you *where* the time went, and in a system of five services talking over TCP, NATS, and Kafka, that is the question that matters. A gateway request that takes 3 seconds might spend 2.9 of them in a downstream service that nobody suspected, while each service's own logs show that everything looked fine.

A gateway request that takes 3 seconds might spend 2.9 of them in a downstream service that nobody suspected, while each service's own logs show that everything looked fine.

blocks.text: TLS support
blocks.zh: TLS 支持

blocks.md: When communicating outside of a private network, encrypt the traffic. The TCP transporter has built-in support for TLS, based on Node's [TLS](https://nodejs.org/api/tls.html) module, which lets you encrypt communication between microservices and their clients.

chapters.title: Redis
chapters.summary: The Redis transporter implements the publish/subscribe messaging paradigm and uses the Pub/Sub feature of Redis.

blocks.md: The [Redis](https://redis.io/) transporter implements the publish/subscribe messaging paradigm and uses the [Pub/Sub](https://redis.io/topics/pubsub) feature of Redis. Published messages are categorized in channels, without the publisher knowing which subscribers (if any) will receive them. Each microservice can subscribe to any number of channels, and a single message can be received by multiple subscribers. Messages exchanged through channels are **fire-and-forget**: if a message is published and no subscriber is interested in it, the message is removed and can't be recovered. As a result, there is no guarantee that a message or event is handled by at least one service.
blocks.text: The Redis transporter implements the publish/subscribe messaging paradigm and uses the Pub/Sub feature of Redis. Each microservice can subscribe to any number of channels, and a single message can be received by multiple subscribers. Messages exchanged through channels are fire-and-forget: if a message is published and no subscriber is interested in it, the message is removed and can't be recovered. As a result, there is no guarantee that a message or event is handled by at least one service.
blocks.zh: [Redis](https://redis.io/) 传输器实现发布/订阅消息范例，并使用 Redis 的 [Pub/Sub](https://redis.io/topics/pubsub) 特性。发布的消息被分类到频道中，发布者不知道哪些订阅者（如果有的话）会收到它们。每个微服务可以订阅任意数量的信道，并且单个消息可以由多个订户接收。通过渠道交换的消息是**一笔勾销**：如果发布了一条消息，没有订阅者对它感兴趣，消息就会被删除，无法恢复。因此，不能保证消息或事件由至少一个服务处理。

chapters.title: MQTT
chapters.summary: MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) is an open source, lightweight messaging protocol optimized for low latency.

blocks.md: [MQTT](https://mqtt.org/) (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) is an open source, lightweight messaging protocol optimized for low latency. It provides a scalable and cost-efficient way to connect devices using a **publish/subscribe** model. A communication system built on MQTT consists of the publishing server, a broker, and one or more clients. The protocol is designed for constrained devices and for low-bandwidth, high-latency, or unreliable networks.

The protocol is designed for constrained devices and for low-bandwidth, high-latency, or unreliable networks.
blocks.zh: [MQTT](https://mqtt.org/)（消息队列遥测传输）是一种开源、轻量级的消息传递协议，针对低延迟进行了优化。它提供了一种使用**发布/订阅**模型连接设备的可扩展且经济高效的方式。建立在 MQTT 由发布服务器、代理和一个或多个客户端组成。该协议是为受限设备和低带宽、高延迟或不可靠网络设计的。

chapters.title: NATS
chapters.summary: NATS is a simple, secure, and high-performance open source messaging system for cloud native applications, IoT messaging, and microservices architectures.

blocks.md: [NATS](https://nats.io) is a simple, secure, and high-performance open source messaging system for cloud native applications, IoT messaging, and microservices architectures. The NATS server is written in Go, and client libraries are available for dozens of major programming languages. NATS supports both **At Most Once** and **At Least Once** delivery. It runs anywhere, from large servers and cloud instances to edge gateways and Internet of Things devices.
blocks.text: NATS is a simple, secure, and high-performance open source messaging system for cloud native applications, IoT messaging, and microservices architectures. The NATS server is written in Go, and client libraries are available for dozens of major programming languages. NATS supports both At Most Once and At Least Once delivery. It runs anywhere, from large servers and cloud instances to edge gateways and Internet of Things devices.
blocks.zh: [NATS](https://nats.io) 是一个简单、安全、高性能的开源消息传递系统，适用于云原生应用程序、物联网消息传递和微服务架构。这个 NATS 服务器是用 Go 编写的，客户端库适用于几十种主要的编程语言。NATS 支持**最多一次**和**至少一次**交付。它可以在任何地方运行，从大型服务器和云实例到边缘网关和物联网设备。

blocks.md: For the [request-response](/microservices/basics#request-response) message style, the NATS transporter doesn't use the built-in NATS [Request-Reply](https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/reqreply) API. Instead, the client publishes a "request" on a given subject with the `publish()` method and a unique reply subject name. Responders listen on that subject and send responses to the reply subject. Reply subjects are routed back to the requester dynamically, regardless of the location of either party.

Reply subjects are routed back to the requester dynamically, regardless of the location of either party.

blocks.md: For the [event-based](/microservices/basics#event-based) message style, the NATS transporter uses the built-in NATS [Publish-Subscribe](https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/pubsub) mechanism. A publisher sends a message on a subject, and every active subscriber listening on that subject receives the message. Subscribers can also register interest in [wildcard](#wildcards) subjects. This one-to-many pattern is sometimes called fan-out.

chapters.summary: RabbitMQ is an open-source, lightweight message broker that supports multiple messaging protocols.

blocks.md: [RabbitMQ](https://www.rabbitmq.com/) is an open-source, lightweight message broker that supports multiple messaging protocols. It can be deployed in distributed and federated configurations to meet high-scale, high-availability requirements, and it is one of the most widely deployed message brokers, used by small startups and large enterprises alike.

blocks.md: Message acknowledgement

blocks.md: To make sure a message is never lost, RabbitMQ supports [message acknowledgements](https://www.rabbitmq.com/confirms.html). The consumer sends an acknowledgement back to tell RabbitMQ that a particular message has been received and processed, and that RabbitMQ is free to delete it. If a consumer dies (its channel is closed, its connection is closed, or the TCP connection is lost) without sending an ack, RabbitMQ assumes the message wasn't fully processed and re-queues it.

The consumer sends an acknowledgement back to tell RabbitMQ that a particular message has been received and processed, and that RabbitMQ is free to delete it. If a consumer dies (its channel is closed, its connection is closed, or the TCP connection is lost) without sending an ack, RabbitMQ assumes the message wasn't fully processed and re-queues it.
blocks.zh: 为了确保消息永远不会丢失， RabbitMQ 支架 [消息确认](https://www.rabbitmq.com/confirms.html).消费者发送确认回来告诉 RabbitMQ 特定消息已被接收和处理，以及 RabbitMQ 可以随意删除。如果消费者死亡（其通道关闭、连接关闭或 TCP 连接丢失）而没有发送 ack， RabbitMQ 假设消息未被完全处理并重新排队。

chapters.summary: Kafka is an open source, distributed streaming platform with three key capabilities:.

blocks.md: [Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/) is an open source, distributed streaming platform with three key capabilities:

blocks.md:
- Publish and subscribe to streams of records, similar to a message queue or enterprise messaging system.
- Store streams of records in a fault-tolerant durable way.
- Process streams of records as they occur.

- 以容错持久的方式存储记录流。
- 在记录流发生时处理它们。

blocks.md: Message pattern
blocks.text: Message pattern
blocks.zh: 消息模式

blocks.md: The Kafka microservice message pattern uses two topics for the request and reply channels. The `ClientKafkaProxy.send()` method sends messages with a [return address](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/ReturnAddress.html) by associating a [correlation id](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/CorrelationIdentifier.html), reply topic, and reply partition with the request message. This requires the `ClientKafkaProxy` instance to be subscribed to the reply topic and assigned to at least one partition before sending a message.
blocks.text: The Kafka microservice message pattern uses two topics for the request and reply channels. The ClientKafkaProxy.send() method sends messages with a return address by associating a correlation id, reply topic, and reply partition with the request message. This requires the ClientKafkaProxy instance to be subscribed to the reply topic and assigned to at least one partition before sending a message.
blocks.zh: 这个 Kafka 微服务消息模式为请求和回复通道使用两个主题。这个 `ClientKafkaProxy.send()` 方法发送消息 [返回地址](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/ReturnAddress.html) 通过关联一个 [相关性 id](https://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/CorrelationIdentifier.html)，回复主题，并使用请求消息回复分区。这需要 `ClientKafkaProxy` 在发送消息之前，要订阅回复主题并分配给至少一个分区的实例。

blocks.md: As a result, you need at least one reply topic partition for every running Nest application. For example, if you run 4 Nest applications but the reply topic has only 3 partitions, 1 of the Nest applications will fail when it tries to send a message.
blocks.text: As a result, you need at least one reply topic partition for every running Nest application. For example, if you run 4 Nest applications but the reply topic has only 3 partitions, 1 of the Nest applications will fail when it tries to send a message.
blocks.zh: 因此，每次运行至少需要一个回复主题分区 Nest 应用。例如，如果运行 4Nest 应用程序，但回复主题只有 3 个分区，其中 1 个 Nest 当应用程序试图发送消息时，它将失败。

blocks.md: When new `ClientKafkaProxy` instances launch, they join the consumer group and subscribe to their respective topics. This triggers a rebalance of the topic partitions assigned to the consumers in the group.
blocks.text: When new ClientKafkaProxy instances launch, they join the consumer group and subscribe to their respective topics. This triggers a rebalance of the topic partitions assigned to the consumers in the group.
blocks.zh: 新的时候 `ClientKafkaProxy` 实例启动后，他们加入消费者组并订阅各自的主题。这将触发分配给组中消费者的主题分区的重新平衡。

blocks.md: Normally, topic partitions are assigned using the round-robin assigner, which assigns topic partitions to a collection of consumers sorted by consumer names that are randomly set on application launch. However, when a new consumer joins the consumer group, it can be positioned anywhere within that collection. Pre-existing consumers positioned after the new consumer can then be assigned different partitions, and those consumers lose the response messages of requests sent before the rebalance.
blocks.text: Normally, topic partitions are assigned using the round-robin assigner, which assigns topic partitions to a collection of consumers sorted by consumer names that are randomly set on application launch. However, when a new consumer joins the consumer group, it can be positioned anywhere within that collection. Pre-existing consumers positioned after the new consumer can then be assigned different partitions, and those consumers lose the response messages of requests sent before the rebalance.
blocks.zh: 通常，使用循环分配器分配主题分区，循环分配器将主题分区分配给按应用程序启动时随机设置的消费者名称排序的消费者集合。然而，当一个新的消费者加入消费者组时，它可以被定位在该集合中的任何位置。位于新消费者之后的预先存在的消费者然后可以被分配不同的分区，并且那些消费者丢失在再平衡之前发送的请求的响应消息。

blocks.md: To prevent `ClientKafkaProxy` consumers from losing response messages, Nest uses a built-in custom partition assigner. During a rebalance, it lets each existing consumer keep the reply partition it was previously assigned, and distributes the remaining partitions among the other consumers.
blocks.text: To prevent ClientKafkaProxy consumers from losing response messages, Nest uses a built-in custom partition assigner. During a rebalance, it lets each existing consumer keep the reply partition it was previously assigned, and distributes the remaining partitions among the other consumers.
blocks.zh: 防止 `ClientKafkaProxy` 防止消费者丢失响应消息，Nest 使用内置的自定义分区分配器。在重新平衡期间，它允许每个现有消费者保留其先前分配的回复分区，并将剩余分区分配给其他消费者。

blocks.md: Regular expression patterns
blocks.text: Regular expression patterns
blocks.zh: 正则表达式模式

blocks.md: KafkaJS supports subscribing to topics by regular expression. Starting with NestJS v12, you can pass a `RegExp` directly to `@MessagePattern()` or `@EventPattern()`. Nest preserves the pattern, forwards it to the KafkaJS `subscribe()` call, and falls back to regular expression matching when resolving a handler for an incoming topic.

Nest preserves the pattern, forwards it to the KafkaJS subscribe() call, and falls back to regular expression matching when resolving a handler for an incoming topic.
blocks.zh: KafkaJS 支持通过正则表达式订阅主题。从 NestJSv12 开始，您可以将 `RegExp` 直接传递给 `@MessagePattern()` 或 `@EventPattern()`。Nest 保留模式，将其转发到 KafkaJS`subscribe()` 调用，并在解析传入主题的处理程序时返回到正则表达式匹配。

blocks.md: This subscribes the handler to every topic matching the expression (`hero.kill.dragon`, `hero.rescue.villager`, and so on) without registering each one explicitly. Use `context.getTopic()` to find out which topic delivered the message.
blocks.text: This subscribes the handler to every topic matching the expression (hero.kill.dragon, hero.rescue.villager, and so on) without registering each one explicitly. Use context.getTopic() to find out which topic delivered the message.
blocks.zh: 这会将处理程序订阅与表达式匹配的每个主题（`hero.kill.dragon`,`hero.rescue.villager` 等等）而无需显式注册每个。使用 `context.getTopic()` 找出哪个主题传递了信息。

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: Regular expression patterns are a Kafka-specific capability; other transporters continue to match patterns by exact value. Nest resets `lastIndex` before matching, so global (`/g`) and sticky (`/y`) expressions do not produce stateful misses.
blocks.text: Regular expression patterns are a Kafka-specific capability; other transporters continue to match patterns by exact value. Nest resets lastIndex before matching, so global (/g) and sticky (/y) expressions do not produce stateful misses.

blocks.md: Incoming
blocks.text: Incoming
blocks.zh: 传入

blocks.md: Nest receives incoming Kafka messages as objects with `key`, `value`, and `headers` properties whose values are of type `Buffer`. Nest parses these values by converting the buffers into strings. If a string is "object-like" (i.e., it starts with a curly brace or a square bracket), Nest attempts to parse it as JSON, except for the `kafka_correlationId`, `kafka_replyTopic` and `kafka_replyPartition` headers it routes replies with, which are always kept as strings. The `value` is then passed to the associated handler.
blocks.text: Nest receives incoming Kafka messages as objects with key, value, and headers properties whose values are of type Buffer. Nest parses these values by converting the buffers into strings. If a string is "object-like" (i.e., it starts with a curly brace or a square bracket), Nest attempts to parse it as JSON, except for the kafka_correlationId, kafka_replyTopic and kafka_replyPartition headers it routes replies with, which are always kept as strings. The value is then passed to the associated handler.
blocks.zh: Nest 接收传入 Kafka 消息作为对象 `key`, `value`，和 `headers` 其值为类型的属性 `Buffer`. Nest 通过将缓冲区转换为字符串来解析这些值。如果字符串是“类对象”的（即，它以大括号或方括号开头）， Nest 尝试将其解析为 JSON，除了 `kafka_correlationId`, `kafka_replyTopic` 和 `kafka_replyPartition` 它路由回复的头，这些头总是以字符串的形式保存。这个 `value` 然后传递给关联的处理程序。

blocks.md: Nest does not decode a message larger than 16 MiB after decompression, counting its key, its headers and, unless `parser.keepBinary` is set, its value. It logs and skips the message, so that its offset is committed, and a `ClientKafkaProxy` fails the request that such a reply answers. To change the limit, set the `parser.maxMessageSize` option.

blocks.zh: Nest 不对解压缩后大于 16 MiB 的消息进行解码，计算其密钥、报头，除非 `parser.keepBinary` 设置，其值。它记录并跳过消息，以便提交其偏移量，并且 `ClientKafkaProxy` 此类回复应答的请求失败。要更改限制，请设置 `parser.maxMessageSize` 选择。

blocks.md: Nest serializes outgoing Kafka messages before publishing events or sending messages. Serialization applies to the arguments passed to the `ClientKafkaProxy` `emit()` and `send()` methods, and to the values returned from a `@MessagePattern()` method. It "stringifies" values that are not strings or buffers by using `JSON.stringify()` or the `toString()` prototype method.

Serialization applies to the arguments passed to the ClientKafkaProxy emit() and send() methods, and to the values returned from a @MessagePattern() method. It "stringifies" values that are not strings or buffers by using JSON.stringify() or the toString() prototype method.

Header values must be of type `string` or `Buffer`, and a message can carry at most 10,000 of them, an array value counting once per item. blocks.md: Retriable exceptions
blocks.text: Retriable exceptions
blocks.zh: 可追溯例外

blocks.md: As with other transporters, unhandled exceptions are automatically converted to a "user-friendly" format. However, in some edge cases you might want to bypass this mechanism and let the `kafkajs` driver consume exceptions instead. Throwing an exception while processing a message instructs `kafkajs` to **retry** it (redeliver it), which means that even though the message (or event) handler was triggered, the offset won't be committed to Kafka.

However, in some edge cases you might want to bypass this mechanism and let the kafkajs driver consume exceptions instead. Throwing an exception while processing a message instructs kafkajs to retry it (redeliver it), which means that even though the message (or event) handler was triggered, the offset won't be committed to Kafka.
blocks.zh: 与其他传输程序一样，未处理的异常会自动转换为“用户友好”格式。但是，在某些边缘情况下，您可能希望绕过此机制并让 `kafkajs` 相反，驱动程序消耗异常。在处理消息时抛出异常指示 `kafkajs` **重试**它（重新传递它），这意味着即使消息（或事件）处理程序被触发，偏移量也不会提交给 Kafka.

blocks.md: Nest handles a message as a request only when it carries the `kafka_correlationId` and `kafka_replyTopic` headers that `ClientKafkaProxy.send()` adds. Any other message, such as one written by a producer other than Nest, is handled as an event, even when it reaches a `@MessagePattern()` handler: its unhandled exceptions are retriable, and the next message of the partition is only processed once the stream the handler returns completes. For topics that other producers write to, make sure message handlers return streams that complete, and handle the messages they cannot process instead of throwing, unless these should be redelivered.

blocks.md: This filter retries processing a Kafka event up to a configurable number of times. When an exception occurs, it republishes the message to the same topic with an incremented `retry-count` header, then commits the current offset. chapters.title: gRPC
chapters.summary: gRPC is a modern, open source, high-performance RPC framework that can run in any environment.

blocks.md: [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-node) is a modern, open source, high-performance RPC framework that can run in any environment. It connects services in and across data centers, with pluggable support for load balancing, tracing, health checking, and authentication.
blocks.text: gRPC is a modern, open source, high-performance RPC framework that can run in any environment. It connects services in and across data centers, with pluggable support for load balancing, tracing, health checking, and authentication.
blocks.zh: [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-node) 是一个现代的、开源的、高性能的 RPC 可以在任何环境中运行的框架。它连接数据中心内部和数据中心之间的服务，支持负载平衡、跟踪、运行状况检查和身份验证。

blocks.md: Like many RPC systems, gRPC is based on defining a service in terms of functions (methods) that can be called remotely. For each method, you define the parameters and return types. Services, parameters, and return types are defined in `.proto` files using Google's open source, language-neutral protocol buffers mechanism.
blocks.text: Like many RPC systems, gRPC is based on defining a service in terms of functions (methods) that can be called remotely. For each method, you define the parameters and return types. Services, parameters, and return types are defined in .proto files using Google's open source, language-neutral protocol buffers mechanism.
blocks.zh: 像许多人一样 RPC 系统，gRPC 是基于根据可以远程调用的函数（方法）来定义服务。对于每个方法，您可以定义参数和返回类型。中定义了服务、参数和返回类型 `.proto` 使用 Google 开源、语言中立的文件 协议缓冲区机制。

blocks.md: With the gRPC transporter, Nest uses `.proto` files to dynamically bind clients and servers, which makes remote procedure calls straightforward to implement and serializes and deserializes structured data automatically.
blocks.text: With the gRPC transporter, Nest uses .proto files to dynamically bind clients and servers, which makes remote procedure calls straightforward to implement and serializes and deserializes structured data automatically.
blocks.zh: 与 gRPC 运输机，Nest 使用 `.proto` 文件动态绑定客户端和服务器，这使得远程过程调用可以简单地实现，并自动序列化和反序列化结构化数据。

blocks.md: Nest applications can act as gRPC clients, consuming services defined in `.proto` files. You access remote services through a `ClientGrpc` object, which you can obtain in several ways.

blocks.md: The preferred technique is to import the `ClientsModule`. Use its `register()` method to bind a package of services defined in a `.proto` file to an injection token, and to configure the service. The `name` property is the injection token. For gRPC services, use `transport: Transport.GRPC`. The `options` property is an object with the same properties described in [Options](/microservices/grpc#options) above.

blocks.md: `GrpcExceptionFilter` also handles `RpcException`. blocks.md: Metadata is information about a particular RPC call in the form of a list of key-value pairs, where the keys are strings and the values are typically strings but can be binary data. Metadata is opaque to gRPC itself: it lets the client provide information associated with the call to the server, and vice versa. Metadata may include authentication tokens, request identifiers and tags for monitoring purposes, and data information such as the number of records in a data set.

chapters.title: Custom transporters
chapters.summary: Nest provides a variety of transporters out of the box, as well as an API for building custom transport strategies.

blocks.md:
Nest provides a variety of **transporters** out of the box, as well as an API for building custom transport strategies.
Transporters let you connect components over a network using a pluggable communications layer and a simple application-level message protocol (see the [full article](https://dev.to/nestjs/integrate-nestjs-with-external-services-using-microservice-transporters-part-1-p3)).
blocks.text: Nest provides a variety of transporters out of the box, as well as an API for building custom transport strategies. Transporters let you connect components over a network using a pluggable communications layer and a simple application-level message protocol (see the full article).
blocks.zh:
Nest 提供了各种开箱即用的**传输器**，以及用于构建自定义传输策略的 API。
Transporters 允许您使用可插拔通信层和简单的应用程序级消息协议（参见 [全文](https://dev.to/nestjs/integrate-nestjs-with-external-services-using-microservice-transporters-part-1-p3)）通过网络连接组件。

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md:
Building a microservice with Nest doesn't necessarily mean you must use the `@nestjs/microservices` package. For example, if you want to communicate with external services (e.g., other microservices written in different languages), you may not need all the features provided by the `@nestjs/microservices` library.
If you don't need the decorators that let you define subscribers declaratively (`@EventPattern` or `@MessagePattern`), running a [standalone application](/application-context) and managing connections and channel subscriptions manually is enough for most use cases, and gives you more flexibility.

如果您不需要允许您声明式定义订阅者的装饰器（`@EventPattern` 或者 `@MessagePattern`），运行一个 [独立应用](/application-context) 手动管理连接和频道订阅对于大多数用例来说已经足够了，并为您提供了更大的灵活性。

chapters.title: Pre-request hooks
chapters.summary: Pre-request hooks are functions that run before all enhancers (guards, interceptors, and pipes) on every invocation of a pattern handler.

blocks.md: Pre-request hooks are functions that run before all enhancers (guards, interceptors, and pipes) on every invocation of a pattern handler. They are the microservices equivalent of HTTP middleware: a place to establish per-request context that must be visible to guards and the rest of the pipeline.
blocks.text: Pre-request hooks are functions that run before all enhancers (guards, interceptors, and pipes) on every invocation of a pattern handler. They are the microservices equivalent of HTTP middleware: a place to establish per-request context that must be visible to guards and the rest of the pipeline.
blocks.zh: 预请求钩子是在每次调用模式处理程序时运行在所有增强器（防护、拦截器和管道）之前的函数。它们相当于微服务 HTTP 中间件：建立每个请求上下文的地方，该上下文必须对守卫和管道的其余部分可见。

blocks.title: Hint
blocks.md: The `PreRequestHook` interface is exported from the `@nestjs/common` package.
blocks.text: The PreRequestHook interface is exported from the @nestjs/common package.
blocks.zh: 这个 `PreRequestHook` 接口从 `@nestjs/common` 包装。

blocks.md: Hooks run at the start of the following sequence:
blocks.text: Hooks run at the start of the following sequence:
blocks.zh: 钩子在以下序列的开头运行：

blocks.code:
Incoming message
  └─ Pre-request hooks  (registration order)
       └─ Guards
            └─ Interceptors
                 └─ Pipes
                      └─ Handler

blocks.md: Exceptions thrown inside a hook are caught by the same wrapper that covers the rest of the pipeline, so your existing [exception filters](/microservices/exception-filters) handle them without extra configuration.
blocks.text: Exceptions thrown inside a hook are caught by the same wrapper that covers the rest of the pipeline, so your existing exception filters handle them without extra configuration.
blocks.zh: 抛入钩子中的异常会被覆盖管道其余部分的相同包装器捕获，因此您现有的 [异常筛选器](/microservices/exception-filters) 无需额外配置即可处理它们。

blocks.md: Binding hooks
blocks.text: Binding hooks
blocks.zh: 捆扎钩

blocks.md: Register hooks on the microservice instance with the `registerPreRequestHook()` method, before the microservice is initialized (i.e., before calling `app.listen()` or `app.init()`). Hooks registered after initialization are ignored, and Nest logs a warning. Multiple calls accumulate hooks in registration order.
blocks.text: Register hooks on the microservice instance with the registerPreRequestHook() method, before the microservice is initialized (i.e., before calling app.listen() or app.init()). Hooks registered after initialization are ignored, and Nest logs a warning. Multiple calls accumulate hooks in registration order.
blocks.zh: 在微服务初始化之前（即，在调用 `app.listen()` 或 `app.init()` 之前），使用 `registerPreRequestHook()` 方法在微服务实例上注册挂钩。初始化后注册的钩子将被忽略，Nest 会记录警告。多个调用按注册顺序累积挂钩。

blocks.md: Each hook receives an `ExecutionContext` and a `next` function. Calling `next()` advances to the next hook or, when no hooks remain, to the guard → interceptor → pipe → handler pipeline. The hook must return an `Observable`: either the one produced by `next()`, or one that wraps it.
blocks.text: Each hook receives an ExecutionContext and a next function. Calling next() advances to the next hook or, when no hooks remain, to the guard → interceptor → pipe → handler pipeline. The hook must return an Observable: either the one produced by next(), or one that wraps it.
blocks.zh: 每个钩子接收一个 `ExecutionContext` 和一个 `next` 功能。呼叫 `next()` 前进到下一个挂钩，或者当没有挂钩时，前进到防护→拦截器→管道→处理器管道。钩子必须返回一个 `Observable`：由 `next()` 或者包裹它的。

blocks.title: Warning
blocks.md: If a hook doesn't call `next()`, the handler never runs. This is the same contract as HTTP middleware.
blocks.text: If a hook doesn't call next(), the handler never runs. This is the same contract as HTTP middleware.
blocks.zh: 如果钩子不叫 `next()` 处理程序从不运行。这是同一份合同 HTTP 中间件。

blocks.title: Note
blocks.md: In a [hybrid application](/faq/hybrid-application), `connectMicroservice()` initializes the connected microservice immediately (unless you pass `deferInitialization: true` in its second argument), so hooks registered on the returned instance afterward are not applied.
blocks.text: In a hybrid application, connectMicroservice() initializes the connected microservice immediately (unless you pass deferInitialization: true in its second argument), so hooks registered on the returned instance afterward are not applied.
blocks.zh: 在一个 [混合应用](/faq/hybrid-application),`connectMicroservice()` 立即初始化连接的微服务（除非通过 `deferInitialization: true` 在它的第二个参数中），因此不应用随后在返回的实例上注册的钩子。

blocks.md: To build your NestJS application, compile your TypeScript code into JavaScript. This process generates a `dist` directory containing the compiled files. Build your application by running the following command:
blocks.text: To build your NestJS application, compile your TypeScript code into JavaScript. This process generates a dist directory containing the compiled files. Build your application by running the following command:
blocks.zh: 要构建您的 NestJS 应用程序，请将您的 TypeScript 代码编译成 JavaScript。此过程生成包含编译文件的 `dist` 目录。运行以下命令构建应用程序：

blocks.code: $ npm run build

blocks.md: This command typically runs `nest build` under the hood, which is a wrapper around the TypeScript compiler with some additional features (such as copying assets). If you have a custom build script, you can run it directly. For Nest CLI monorepos, pass the name of the project to build as an argument (`npm run build my-app`).

blocks.md: After a successful compilation, you should see a `dist` directory in your project root containing the compiled files, with `main.js` as the entry point. If you have any `.ts` files in the root directory of your project (and your `tsconfig.json` is configured to compile them), they are compiled into the `dist` directory as well, which changes the directory structure: instead of `dist/main.js`, you get `dist/src/main.js`. Keep that in mind when configuring your server.

blocks.md: NODE_ENV=production
blocks.text: NODE_ENV=production
blocks.zh: NODE_ENV=生产

blocks.md: While there's technically no difference between development and production in Node.js and NestJS, it's good practice to set the `NODE_ENV` environment variable to `production` when running your application in a production environment, because some libraries in the ecosystem behave differently based on this variable (e.g., enabling or disabling debugging output).
blocks.text: While there's technically no difference between development and production in Node.js and NestJS, it's good practice to set the NODE_ENV environment variable to production when running your application in a production environment, because some libraries in the ecosystem behave differently based on this variable (e.g., enabling or disabling debugging output).
blocks.zh: 虽然从技术上讲，开发和生产之间没有区别 Node.js 和 NestJS，设置 `NODE_ENV` 环境变量到 `production` 在生产环境中运行应用程序时，因为生态系统中的一些库根据此变量的行为不同（例如，启用或禁用调试输出）。

blocks.md: You can set the `NODE_ENV` environment variable when starting your application:
blocks.text: You can set the NODE_ENV environment variable when starting your application:
blocks.zh: 您可以设置 `NODE_ENV` 启动应用程序时的环境变量：

blocks.code: $ NODE_ENV=production node dist/main.js

blocks.md: Running your application
blocks.text: Running your application
blocks.zh: 运行您的应用程序

blocks.md: To run your NestJS application in production, use the following command:
blocks.text: To run your NestJS application in production, use the following command:
blocks.zh: 运行您的 NestJS 在生产中应用，请使用以下命令：

blocks.code: $ node dist/main.js # Adjust this based on your entry point location

blocks.md: This command starts your application, which listens on the port passed to `app.listen()` (`3000` in newly generated projects, unless the `PORT` environment variable is set). Make sure your deployment platform routes traffic to that port.

blocks.md: Alternatively, you can use the `nest start` command. It is a wrapper around `node dist/main.js`, with one key difference: it runs `nest build` before starting the application, so you don't need to run `npm run build` manually.

blocks.md: Health checks
blocks.text: Health checks
blocks.zh: 健康检查

blocks.md: Health checks are essential for monitoring the health and status of your NestJS application in production. With a health check endpoint, you can regularly verify that your app is running as expected and respond to issues before they become critical.
blocks.text: Health checks are essential for monitoring the health and status of your NestJS application in production. With a health check endpoint, you can regularly verify that your app is running as expected and respond to issues before they become critical.

blocks.md: In NestJS, you can implement health checks with the **@nestjs/terminus** package, which supports checks for database connections, external services, and custom indicators.

blocks.md: Logging
blocks.text: Logging
blocks.zh: 伐木作业

blocks.md: Logging is essential for any production-ready application. It helps you track errors, monitor behavior, and troubleshoot issues. In NestJS, you can manage logging with the [built-in logger](/application/logger), or opt for external libraries if you need more advanced features.
blocks.text: Logging is essential for any production-ready application. It helps you track errors, monitor behavior, and troubleshoot issues. In NestJS, you can manage logging with the built-in logger, or opt for external libraries if you need more advanced features.
blocks.zh: 日志记录对于任何生产就绪的应用程序都是必不可少的。它可以帮助您跟踪错误、监控行为和解决问题。在 NestJS，您可以使用 [内置记录器](/application/logger)，或者如果需要更高级的功能，可以选择外部库。

blocks.md: Best practices for logging:
blocks.text: Best practices for logging:
blocks.zh: 日志记录的最佳实践：

blocks.md:
- Log errors, not exceptions: Focus on logging detailed error messages to speed up debugging and issue resolution.
- Avoid sensitive data: Never log sensitive information such as passwords or tokens.
- Use correlation IDs: In distributed systems, include unique identifiers (like correlation IDs) in your logs to trace requests across services.
- Use log levels: Categorize logs by severity (e.g., `info`, `warn`, `error`), and disable debug or verbose logs in production to reduce noise.
blocks.text: Log errors, not exceptions: Focus on logging detailed error messages to speed up debugging and issue resolution. Avoid sensitive data: Never log sensitive information such as passwords or tokens. Use correlation IDs: In distributed systems, include unique identifiers (like correlation IDs) in your logs to trace requests across services. Use log levels: Categorize logs by severity (e.g., info, warn, error), and disable debug or verbose logs in production to reduce noise.
blocks.zh:
- 记录错误，而不是异常：专注于记录详细的错误消息，以加快调试和问题解决。
- 避免敏感数据：切勿记录密码或令牌等敏感信息。
- 使用关联 ID：在分布式系统中，在日志中包含唯一标识符（如关联 ID），以跟踪跨服务的请求。
- 使用日志级别：按严重程度对日志进行分类（例如，`info`,`warn`,`error`），并在生产中禁用调试或详细日志，以减少噪声。

blocks.md: For distributed applications, a centralized logging service such as Elasticsearch, Loggly, or Datadog is very useful. These tools offer log aggregation, search, and visualization, making it easier to monitor and analyze your application's performance and behavior.

blocks.md: Observability

blocks.md: Health checks and logs tell you whether the application is up; they don't tell you which route got slower after the last deploy, which class is burning the time, or which line threw. For that, instrument the application with [NestJS Observe](https://www.observe.nestjs.com/ 'NestJS Observe'), our official observability platform: install the `@nestjs/observe` SDK, pass an API key, and requests, jobs, errors, logs, and traces start streaming to a dashboard with no manual span wiring or collector to run.

blocks.md: Scaling up or out
blocks.text: Scaling up or out
blocks.zh: 放大或缩小

blocks.md: Scaling your NestJS application effectively is crucial for handling increased traffic and ensuring optimal performance. There are two primary strategies for scaling: **vertical scaling** and **horizontal scaling**. Understanding both helps you design your application to manage load efficiently.
blocks.text: Scaling your NestJS application effectively is crucial for handling increased traffic and ensuring optimal performance. There are two primary strategies for scaling: vertical scaling and horizontal scaling. Understanding both helps you design your application to manage load efficiently.
blocks.zh: 扩展您的 NestJS 有效的应用程序对于处理增加的流量和确保最佳性能至关重要。缩放有两种主要策略：**垂直缩放**和**水平缩放**。了解这两者有助于您设计应用程序以有效地管理负载。

blocks.md: **Vertical scaling**, often referred to as "scaling up", involves increasing the resources of a single server to improve its performance. This could mean adding more CPU, RAM, or storage to your existing machine. Key points to consider:
blocks.text: Vertical scaling, often referred to as "scaling up", involves increasing the resources of a single server to improve its performance. This could mean adding more CPU, RAM, or storage to your existing machine. Key points to consider:
blocks.zh: **垂直扩展**，通常被称为“扩展”，涉及增加单个服务器的资源以提高其性能。这可能意味着增加更多 CPU,RAM，或存储到您现有的计算机。需要考虑的要点：

blocks.md:
- Simplicity: Vertical scaling is generally simpler to implement since you only need to upgrade your existing server rather than manage multiple instances.
- Limitations: There are physical limits to how much you can scale a single machine. Once you reach the maximum capacity, you may need to consider other options.
- Cost-effectiveness: For applications with moderate traffic, vertical scaling can be cost-effective, as it reduces the need for additional infrastructure.
blocks.text: Simplicity: Vertical scaling is generally simpler to implement since you only need to upgrade your existing server rather than manage multiple instances. Limitations: There are physical limits to how much you can scale a single machine. Once you reach the maximum capacity, you may need to consider other options. Cost-effectiveness: For applications with moderate traffic, vertical scaling can be cost-effective, as it reduces the need for additional infrastructure.
blocks.zh:
- 简单性：垂直扩展通常更容易实现，因为您只需要升级现有的服务器，而不是管理多个实例。
- 限制：单台机器的扩展范围有物理限制。一旦达到最大容量，您可能需要考虑其他选项。
- 成本效益：对于中等流量的应用程序，垂直扩展可能具有成本效益，因为它减少了对额外基础架构的需求。

blocks.md: Example: If your NestJS app is hosted on a virtual machine and you notice that it's running slowly during peak hours, you can upgrade the VM to a larger instance with more resources, typically by selecting a larger instance type in your provider's dashboard.
blocks.text: Example: If your NestJS app is hosted on a virtual machine and you notice that it's running slowly during peak hours, you can upgrade the VM to a larger instance with more resources, typically by selecting a larger instance type in your provider's dashboard.
blocks.zh: 例如：如果你的 NestJS 应用程序托管在虚拟机上，您注意到它在高峰时段运行缓慢，您可以升级 VM 到具有更多资源的更大实例，通常是通过在提供者的仪表板中选择更大的实例类型。

blocks.md: **Horizontal scaling**, or "scaling out", involves adding more servers or instances to distribute the load. This strategy is widely used in cloud environments and is essential for applications expecting high traffic. Benefits and considerations:
blocks.text: Horizontal scaling, or "scaling out", involves adding more servers or instances to distribute the load. This strategy is widely used in cloud environments and is essential for applications expecting high traffic. Benefits and considerations:
blocks.zh: **水平扩展**或“扩展”涉及添加更多服务器或实例来分配负载。这种策略在云环境中广泛使用，对于期望高流量的应用程序来说是必不可少的。好处和注意事项：

blocks.md:
- Increased capacity: By adding more instances of your application, you can handle a larger number of concurrent users without degrading performance.
- Redundancy: The failure of one server doesn't bring down your entire application, because traffic can be redistributed among the remaining servers.
- Load balancing: To manage multiple instances effectively, use load balancers (like Nginx or AWS Elastic Load Balancing) to distribute incoming traffic evenly across your servers.
blocks.text: Increased capacity: By adding more instances of your application, you can handle a larger number of concurrent users without degrading performance. Redundancy: The failure of one server doesn't bring down your entire application, because traffic can be redistributed among the remaining servers. Load balancing: To manage multiple instances effectively, use load balancers (like Nginx or AWS Elastic Load Balancing) to distribute incoming traffic evenly across your servers.
blocks.zh:
- 容量增加：通过添加更多应用程序实例，您可以在不降低性能的情况下处理更多并发用户。
- 冗余：一台服务器的故障不会导致整个应用程序瘫痪，因为流量可以在其余服务器之间重新分配。
- 负载平衡：要有效地管理多个实例，请使用负载平衡器（如 Nginx 或 AWS 弹性负载平衡）将传入流量均匀分布在您的服务器上。

blocks.md: Example: For a NestJS application experiencing high traffic, you can deploy multiple instances of your app in a cloud environment and use a load balancer to route requests, ensuring that no single instance becomes a bottleneck.
blocks.text: Example: For a NestJS application experiencing high traffic, you can deploy multiple instances of your app in a cloud environment and use a load balancer to route requests, ensuring that no single instance becomes a bottleneck.
blocks.zh: 例如：对于一个 NestJS 应用程序遇到高流量，您可以在云环境中部署应用程序的多个实例，并使用负载平衡器来路由请求，确保没有单个实例成为瓶颈。

blocks.md: Containerization technologies like [Docker](https://www.docker.com/) and container orchestration platforms such as [Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io/) make this process straightforward. You can also use cloud-specific load balancers like [AWS Elastic Load Balancing](https://aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/) or [Azure Load Balancer](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/services/load-balancer/) to distribute traffic across your application instances.
blocks.text: Containerization technologies like Docker and container orchestration platforms such as Kubernetes make this process straightforward. blocks.md: Some other tips
blocks.text: Some other tips
blocks.zh: 其他一些提示

blocks.md: Keep these additional tips in mind when deploying your NestJS application:
blocks.text: Keep these additional tips in mind when deploying your NestJS application:
blocks.zh: 部署时，请记住这些附加提示 NestJS 应用：

blocks.md:
- **Security**: Protect your application from common threats such as SQL injection and XSS. See the chapters in the "Security" category, such as [Helmet](/security/helmet) and [CORS](/security/cors), for details.
- **Monitoring**: Use monitoring tools like [Prometheus](https://prometheus.io/) or [New Relic](https://newrelic.com/) to track your application's performance and health. Cloud providers and Mau may offer built-in monitoring services (such as [AWS CloudWatch](https://aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/)).
- **Do not hardcode environment variables**: Avoid hardcoding sensitive information like API keys, passwords, or tokens in your code. Use environment variables or a secrets manager to store and access these values securely.
- **Backups**: Regularly back up your data to prevent data loss in case of an incident.
- **Automate deployments**: Use CI/CD pipelines to automate your deployment process and ensure consistency across environments.
- **Rate limiting**: Implement rate limiting to prevent abuse and protect your application from DDoS attacks. See the [rate limiting](/security/rate-limiting) chapter for details, or use a service like [AWS WAF](https://aws.amazon.com/waf/) for advanced protection.

blocks.md: Dockerizing your application
blocks.text: Dockerizing your application
blocks.zh: Dockerization 您的应用程序

blocks.md: [Docker](https://www.docker.com/) is a platform that uses containerization to let developers package applications along with their dependencies into a standardized unit called a container. Containers are lightweight, portable, and isolated, which makes them ideal for deploying applications in various environments, from local development to production.
blocks.text: Docker is a platform that uses containerization to let developers package applications along with their dependencies into a standardized unit called a container. Containers are lightweight, portable, and isolated, which makes them ideal for deploying applications in various environments, from local development to production.
blocks.zh: [Docker](https://www.docker.com/) 是一个使用容器化的平台，让开发人员将应用程序及其依赖项打包到一个称为容器的标准化单元中。容器重量轻、便携且隔离，这使得它们非常适合在从本地开发到生产的各种环境中部署应用程序。

blocks.md: Benefits of Dockerizing your NestJS application:
blocks.text: Benefits of Dockerizing your NestJS application:
blocks.zh: 码头化的好处 NestJS 应用：

blocks.md:
- Consistency: Docker ensures that your application runs the same way on any machine, eliminating the "it works on my machine" problem.
- Isolation: Each container runs in its own isolated environment, preventing conflicts between dependencies.
- Scalability: You can scale your application by running multiple containers across different machines or cloud instances.
- Portability: Containers move between environments without changes, so you can deploy your application on different platforms.
blocks.text: Consistency: Docker ensures that your application runs the same way on any machine, eliminating the "it works on my machine" problem. Isolation: Each container runs in its own isolated environment, preventing conflicts between dependencies. Scalability: You can scale your application by running multiple containers across different machines or cloud instances. Portability: Containers move between environments without changes, so you can deploy your application on different platforms.
blocks.zh:
- 一致性：Docker 确保您的应用程序在任何机器上都以相同的方式运行，消除了“它在我的机器上工作”的问题。
- 隔离：每个容器在自己的隔离环境中运行，防止依赖项之间的冲突。
- 可伸缩性：您可以通过在不同的机器或云实例上运行多个容器来扩展您的应用程序。
- 可移植性：容器在环境之间移动而无需更改，因此您可以在不同的平台上部署应用程序。

blocks.md: To install Docker, follow the instructions on the [Docker website](https://www.docker.com/get-started). Once Docker is installed, create a `Dockerfile` in your NestJS project. It is a text file that contains the instructions Docker uses to build your container image.
blocks.text: To install Docker, follow the instructions on the Docker website. Once Docker is installed, create a Dockerfile in your NestJS project. It is a text file that contains the instructions Docker uses to build your container image.
blocks.zh: 要安装 Docker，请按照 [Docker website](https://www.docker.com/get-started) 上的说明进行操作。安装 Docker 后，在您的 NestJS 项目中创建一个 `Dockerfile`。它是一个文本文件，包含 Docker 用于构建容器映像的说明。

blocks.md: Here's a sample `Dockerfile` for a NestJS application:
blocks.text: Here's a sample Dockerfile for a NestJS application:
blocks.zh: 这是一个样本 `Dockerfile` 对于一个 NestJS 应用：

blocks.code:
# Use the official Node.js image as the base image
FROM node:24

# Set the working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy package.json and package-lock.json to the working directory
COPY package*.json ./

# Install the application dependencies
RUN npm install

# Copy the rest of the application files
COPY . .

# Build the NestJS application
RUN npm run build

# Expose the application port
EXPOSE 3000

# Command to run the application
CMD ["node", "dist/main"]

chapters.title: Standalone apps
chapters.summary: There are several ways to mount a Nest application.

blocks.md: There are several ways to mount a Nest application. You can create a web app, a microservice, or a bare Nest **standalone application** (without any network listeners). A standalone application is a wrapper around the Nest **IoC container**, which holds all instantiated classes. Through the standalone application object, you can obtain a reference to any existing instance from any imported module. This lets you take advantage of the Nest framework anywhere, including scripted **CRON** jobs. You can even build a **CLI** on top of it.

chapters.title: Overview
chapters.summary: The Nest CLI is a command-line tool that helps you initialize, develop, and maintain Nest applications.

blocks.md: The [Nest CLI](https://github.com/nestjs/nest-cli) is a command-line tool that helps you initialize, develop, and maintain Nest applications. It scaffolds projects, serves them in development mode, and builds and bundles them for production. It also embodies best-practice architectural patterns to encourage well-structured applications.
blocks.text: The Nest CLI is a command-line tool that helps you initialize, develop, and maintain Nest applications. It scaffolds projects, serves them in development mode, and builds and bundles them for production. It also embodies best-practice architectural patterns to encourage well-structured applications.
blocks.zh: 这个 [Nest CLI](https://github.com/nestjs/nest-cli) 是一个命令行工具，可帮助您初始化、开发和维护 Nest 应用。它支架项目，以开发模式为它们服务，并构建和捆绑它们用于生产。它还体现了最佳实践架构模式，以鼓励结构良好的应用程序。

blocks.md: Installation
blocks.text: Installation
blocks.zh: 安装

blocks.md: **Note**: This guide uses [npm](https://docs.npmjs.com/downloading-and-installing-node-js-and-npm) to install packages, including the Nest CLI. You can use another package manager if you prefer. npm offers several ways to control how your OS command line resolves the `nest` binary. Here, we install it globally with the `-g` option. This is convenient, and it is the approach the rest of the documentation assumes. Keep in mind that when you install **any** npm package globally, you are responsible for making sure you run the correct version. It also means that all your projects run the **same** version of the CLI. A reasonable alternative is the [npx](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/latest/docs/lib/content/commands/npx.md) program built into the npm CLI (other package managers have similar features), which ensures that you run a **managed version** of the Nest CLI. For more information, consult the [npx documentation](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/latest/docs/lib/content/commands/npx.md) or your DevOps team.

blocks.md: Once the CLI is installed, you can invoke its commands from your OS command line through the `nest` executable. To list the available commands, run:
blocks.text: Once the CLI is installed, you can invoke its commands from your OS command line through the nest executable. To list the available commands, run:

blocks.md: To create, build, and run a new Nest project in development mode, go to the folder that should contain your new project and run the following commands:

blocks.md: Project structure
blocks.text: Project structure
blocks.zh: 项目结构

blocks.md: When you run `nest new`, Nest creates a new folder and populates it with a boilerplate application. You can keep working in this default structure and add new components as described throughout this documentation. We refer to the project structure generated by `nest new` as **standard mode**. Nest also supports an alternate structure for managing multiple projects and libraries, called **monorepo mode**.
blocks.text: When you run nest new, Nest creates a new folder and populates it with a boilerplate application. You can keep working in this default structure and add new components as described throughout this documentation. We refer to the project structure generated by nest new as standard mode. Nest also supports an alternate structure for managing multiple projects and libraries, called monorepo mode.
blocks.zh: 当你跑步时 `nest new`,Nest 创建一个新文件夹，并用样板应用程序填充它。您可以继续在此默认结构中工作，并按照本文档中所述添加新组件。我们指的是由 `nest new` 作为**标准模式**。Nest 还支持用于管理多个项目和库的替代结构，称为**monorepo 模式**。

blocks.md: The two modes differ only in how the **build** process works (monorepo mode simplifies build complexities that can arise in monorepo-style project structures) and in built-in [library](/cli/libraries) support. All other Nest features, and this documentation, apply equally to both. You can switch from standard mode to monorepo mode at any time, so you can safely defer this decision while you're still learning Nest.
blocks.text: The two modes differ only in how the build process works (monorepo mode simplifies build complexities that can arise in monorepo-style project structures) and in built-in library support. All other Nest features, and this documentation, apply equally to both. You can switch from standard mode to monorepo mode at any time, so you can safely defer this decision while you're still learning Nest.
blocks.zh: 这两种模式的区别仅在于**构建**过程的工作方式（monorepo 模式简化了 monorepo 风格的项目结构中可能出现的构建复杂性）和内置 [图书馆](/cli/libraries) 支持。所有其他 Nest 特性和本文档同样适用于两者。您可以随时从标准模式切换到单回购模式，因此您可以在学习期间安全地推迟此决定 Nest.

blocks.md: You can use either mode to manage multiple projects. The following table summarizes the differences:
blocks.text: You can use either mode to manage multiple projects. The following table summarizes the differences:
blocks.zh: 您可以使用任一模式来管理多个项目。下表总结了差异：

blocks.md:
| Feature                                                    | Standard Mode                                                      | Monorepo Mode                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Multiple projects                                          | Separate file system structure                                     | Single file system structure                               |
| `node_modules` & `package.json`                            | Separate instances                                                 | Shared across monorepo                                     |
| Default compiler                                           | `tsc`                                                              | rspack                                                     |
| Compiler settings                                          | Specified separately                                               | Monorepo defaults that can be overridden per project       |
| Lint and formatter config files                           | Specified separately                                               | Shared across monorepo                                     |
| `nest build` and `nest start` commands                     | Target defaults automatically to the (only) project in the context | Target defaults to the **default project** in the monorepo |
| Libraries                                                  | Managed manually, usually via npm packaging                        | Built-in support, including path management and bundling   |
blocks.zh:
| 特征 | 标准模式 | 单存储模式 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| 多个项目 | 独立文件系统结构 | 单文件系统结构 |
| `node_modules`&`package.json` | 单独的实例 | 跨 monorepo 共享 |
| 默认编译器 | `tsc` | rspack |
| 编译器设置 | 单独指定 | 每个项目可以覆盖的 Monorepo 默认值 |
| Lint 和格式化程序配置文件 | 单独指定 | 跨 monorepo 共享 |
| `nest build` 和 `nest start` 命令 | 目标自动默认为上下文中的（仅）项目 | 将默认目标设置为 monorepo 中的 **默认项目** |
| 文库 | 手动管理，通常通过 npm 打包 | 内置支持，包括路径管理和捆绑 |

blocks.md: See [Workspaces](/cli/monorepo) and [Libraries](/cli/libraries) for more detail to help you decide which mode suits you best.
blocks.text: See Workspaces and Libraries for more detail to help you decide which mode suits you best.
blocks.zh: 看 [Workspaces](/cli/monorepo) 和 [Libraries](/cli/libraries) 了解更多详细信息，帮助您决定哪种模式最适合您。

blocks.md: CLI command syntax
blocks.text: CLI command syntax
blocks.zh: CLI 命令语法

blocks.md: All `nest` commands follow the same format:
blocks.text: All nest commands follow the same format:
blocks.zh: 全部 `nest` 命令遵循相同的格式：

blocks.code: nest commandOrAlias requiredArg [optionalArg] [options]

blocks.md: For example:
blocks.text: For example:
blocks.zh: 例如：

blocks.code: $ nest new my-nest-project --dry-run

blocks.md: Here, `new` is the _commandOrAlias_; its alias is `n`. `my-nest-project` is the _requiredArg_. If you don't supply a _requiredArg_ on the command line, `nest` prompts for it. The `--dry-run` option has the short form `-d`. The following command is therefore equivalent to the one above:
blocks.text: Here, new is the _commandOrAlias_; its alias is n. my-nest-project is the _requiredArg_. If you don't supply a _requiredArg_ on the command line, nest prompts for it. The --dry-run option has the short form -d. The following command is therefore equivalent to the one above:
blocks.zh: 这里，`new` 是_commandOrAlias_；它的别名是 `n`。`my-nest-project` 是_requiredArg_。如果您没有在命令行上提供 _requiredArg_，`nest` 会提示它。`--dry-run` 选项的简称为 `-d`。因此，以下命令等同于上面的命令：

blocks.code: $ nest n my-nest-project -d

blocks.md: Most commands, and some options, have aliases. Run `nest new --help` to see them.
blocks.text: Most commands, and some options, have aliases. Run nest new --help to see them.
blocks.zh: 大多数命令和一些选项都有别名。运行 `nest new --help` 去看他们。

blocks.md: Command overview
blocks.text: Command overview
blocks.zh: 命令概述

blocks.md: Run `nest <command> --help` for any of the following commands to see its options. See the [CLI command reference](/cli/usages) for a detailed description of each command.
blocks.text: Run nest --help for any of the following commands to see its options. See the CLI command reference for a detailed description of each command.
blocks.zh: 运行 `nest <command> --help` 对于以下任何命令，请查看其选项。参见 [CLI 命令参考](/cli/usages) 有关每个命令的详细描述。

blocks.md:
| Command    | Alias | Description                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `new`      | `n`   | Scaffolds a new _standard mode_ application with all the boilerplate files it needs to run.    |
| `generate` | `g`   | Generates and/or modifies files based on a schematic.                                          |
| `build`    |       | Compiles an application or workspace into an output folder.                                    |
| `start`    |       | Compiles and runs an application (or the default project in a workspace).                      |
| `add`      |       | Imports a library that has been packaged as a **nest library**, running its install schematic. |
| `upgrade`  | `update` | Upgrades an existing project to the latest NestJS major version.                               |
| `deploy`   |       | Deploys your application to the cloud, powered by [Mau](https://mau.nestjs.com/).              |
| `info`     | `i`   | Displays information about installed Nest packages and other useful system information.        |
blocks.zh:
| 命令 | 别名 | 描述 |
| ---------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `new` | `n` | 用运行所需的所有样板文件搭建一个新的_standard mode_应用程序。 |
| `generate` | `g` | 基于原理图生成和/或修改文件。 |
| `build` | | 将应用程序或工作区编译成输出文件夹。 |
| `start` | | 编译并运行应用程序（或工作区中的默认项目）。 |
| `add` | | 导入已打包为**嵌套库**的库，运行其安装原理图。 |
| `upgrade` | `update` | 将现有项目升级到最新项目 NestJS 主要版本。 |
| `deploy` | | 将您的应用程序部署到云，由 [Mau](https://mau.nestjs.com/) 提供支持。 |
| `info` | `i` | 显示有关已安装的信息 Nest 软件包和其他有用的系统信息。 |

blocks.md: Requirements
blocks.text: Requirements
blocks.zh: 要求

blocks.md: The CLI binary itself runs on **Node.js v20.11 or later**, but the schematics behind `nest new`, `nest generate`, and `nest upgrade` (`@nestjs/schematics`) require **Node.js v22.22.3+, v24.15+, or v26+**. Running a Nest application has a lower floor (see [Node.js requirements](/migration-guide#nodejs-requirements) in the migration guide). If you generate code on the machine you develop on, use the latest active LTS release.
blocks.text: The CLI binary itself runs on Node.js v20.11 or later, but the schematics behind nest new, nest generate, and nest upgrade (@nestjs/schematics) require Node.js v22.22.3+, v24.15+, or v26+. Running a Nest application has a lower floor (see Node.js requirements in the migration guide). If you generate code on the machine you develop on, use the latest active LTS release.
blocks.zh: 这个 CLI 二进制文件本身在**上运行 Node.jsv20.11 或更高版本**，但后面的原理图 `nest new`,`nest generate`，和 `nest upgrade`(`@nestjs/schematics`) 要求**Node.jsv22.22.3+、v24.15+或 v26+**。运行一个 Nest 应用程序具有较低的楼层（参见 [Node.js requirements](/migration-guide#nodejs-requirements) 在迁移指南中）。如果在开发的计算机上生成代码，请使用最新的活动 LTS 释放。

blocks.md: The Nest CLI also requires a Node.js binary built with [internationalization support](https://nodejs.org/api/intl.html) (ICU), such as the official binaries from the [Node.js download page](https://nodejs.org/en/download). If you encounter ICU-related errors, check that your binary meets this requirement:

blocks.zh: NestCLI 还需要一个用 [国际化支持](https://nodejs.org/api/intl.html)（ICU）构建的 Node.js 二进制文件，如 [Node.js download page](https://nodejs.org/en/download) 中的官方二进制文件。如果遇到与 ICU 相关的错误，请检查您的二进制文件是否满足以下要求：

blocks.code: node -p process.versions.icu

blocks.text: If the command prints undefined, your Node.js binary has no internationalization support.

chapters.title: Workspaces
chapters.summary: Nest has two modes for organizing code:.

blocks.md: Nest has two modes for organizing code:
blocks.text: Nest has two modes for organizing code:
blocks.zh: Nest 有两种组织代码的模式：

blocks.md:
- **standard mode**: suited to individual, project-focused applications that have their own dependencies and settings and don't need to optimize for sharing modules or for complex builds. This is the default mode.
- **monorepo mode**: treats code artifacts as part of a lightweight **monorepo**, and may be more appropriate for teams of developers and/or multi-project environments. It automates parts of the build process to make it easy to create and compose modular components. It promotes code reuse, makes integration testing easier, makes it easy to share project-wide artifacts such as lint rules and other configuration policies, and is easier to use than alternatives such as Git submodules. Monorepo mode uses the concept of a **workspace**, represented in the `nest-cli.json` file, to coordinate the relationships between the components of the monorepo.
blocks.text: standard mode: suited to individual, project-focused applications that have their own dependencies and settings and don't need to optimize for sharing modules or for complex builds. This is the default mode. monorepo mode: treats code artifacts as part of a lightweight monorepo, and may be more appropriate for teams of developers and/or multi-project environments. It automates parts of the build process to make it easy to create and compose modular components. It promotes code reuse, makes integration testing easier, makes it easy to share project-wide artifacts such as lint rules and other configuration policies, and is easier to use than alternatives such as Git submodules. Monorepo mode uses the concept of a workspace, represented in the nest-cli.json file, to coordinate the relationships between the components of the monorepo.
blocks.zh:
- **标准模式**：适用于单个、以项目为中心的应用程序，这些应用程序有自己的依赖关系和设置，不需要针对共享模块或复杂的构建进行优化。这是默认模式。
- **monorepo 模式**：将代码工件视为轻量级**monorepo**的一部分，可能更适合开发人员团队和/或多项目环境。它自动化了构建过程的一部分，使创建和组装模块化组件变得容易。它促进了代码重用，使集成测试更容易，使共享项目范围的工件（如 lint 规则和其他配置策略）变得容易，并且比 Git 子模块等替代方案更容易使用。Monorepo 模式使用**工作区**的概念，如 `nest-cli.json` 文件，以协调 monorepo 组件之间的关系。

blocks.md: Virtually all of Nest's features are independent of your code organization mode. The **only** effect of this choice is how your projects are composed and how build artifacts are generated. All other functionality, from the CLI to core modules to add-on modules, works the same in either mode.
blocks.text: Virtually all of Nest's features are independent of your code organization mode. The only effect of this choice is how your projects are composed and how build artifacts are generated. All other functionality, from the CLI to core modules to add-on modules, works the same in either mode.
blocks.zh: 几乎所有 Nest 的功能与代码组织模式无关。这种选择的**唯一**影响是您的项目是如何组成的，以及如何生成构建工件。所有其他功能，从 CLI 从核心模块到附加模块，两种模式下的工作方式都相同。

blocks.md: You can also switch from **standard mode** to **monorepo mode** at any time, so you can delay this decision until the benefits of one approach or the other become clearer.
blocks.text: You can also switch from standard mode to monorepo mode at any time, so you can delay this decision until the benefits of one approach or the other become clearer.
blocks.zh: 您也可以随时从**标准模式**切换到**单一回购模式**，因此您可以推迟此决定，直到一种或另一种方法的好处变得更加明显。

blocks.md: Standard mode
blocks.text: Standard mode
blocks.zh: 标准模式

blocks.md: When you run `nest new`, Nest creates a new **project** using a built-in schematic. Nest does the following:
blocks.text: When you run nest new, Nest creates a new project using a built-in schematic. Nest does the following:
blocks.zh: 当你跑步时 `nest new`,Nest 使用内置原理图创建新的**项目**。Nest 执行以下操作：

blocks.md:
1. Creates a new folder named after the `name` argument you pass to `nest new`.
2. Populates that folder with the default files of a minimal Nest application. You can examine these files in the [typescript-starter](https://github.com/nestjs/typescript-starter) repository.
3. Adds files such as `nest-cli.json`, `package.json`, and `tsconfig.json` that configure the tools for compiling, testing, and serving your application.
blocks.text: Creates a new folder named after the name argument you pass to nest new. Populates that folder with the default files of a minimal Nest application. You can examine these files in the typescript-starter repository. Adds files such as nest-cli.json, package.json, and tsconfig.json that configure the tools for compiling, testing, and serving your application.
blocks.zh:
1. 创建一个以传递给 `nest new` 的 `name` 参数命名的新文件夹。
2. 用最小值的默认文件填充该文件夹 Nest 应用。您可以在 [typescript-starter](https://github.com/nestjs/typescript-starter) 仓库。
3. 添加文件，例如 `nest-cli.json`,`package.json`，和 `tsconfig.json` 配置用于编译、测试和服务应用程序的工具。

blocks.md: From there, you can modify the starter files, add new components and dependencies (e.g., `npm install`), and develop your application as described in the rest of this documentation.
blocks.text: From there, you can modify the starter files, add new components and dependencies (e.g., npm install), and develop your application as described in the rest of this documentation.
blocks.zh: 从那里，您可以修改启动器文件，添加新的组件和依赖项（例如，`npm install`)，并按照本文档其余部分所述开发应用程序。

blocks.md: Monorepo mode
blocks.text: Monorepo mode
blocks.zh: 单存储模式

blocks.md: To enable monorepo mode, start with a _standard mode_ structure and add **projects**. A project can be a full **application** (which you add to the workspace with `nest generate app`) or a **library** (which you add with `nest generate library`). We discuss these project types below. The key point for now is that the **act of adding a project** to an existing standard mode structure **converts it** to monorepo mode. Let's look at an example.
blocks.text: To enable monorepo mode, start with a _standard mode_ structure and add projects. A project can be a full application (which you add to the workspace with nest generate app) or a library (which you add with nest generate library). We discuss these project types below. The key point for now is that the act of adding a project to an existing standard mode structure converts it to monorepo mode. Let's look at an example.

blocks.md: This command generates a project skeleton, including the standard `src` and `test` folders from the [typescript starter](https://github.com/nestjs/typescript-starter).
